EMS personnel examined Jessen. Primary and secondary evaluations indicated that he had sustained fatal injuries.

incidents.name: East Slide Rock Ridge
incidents.fire: East Slid Rock Ridge Wildland Fire Use
incidents.summary: A natural ignition inside a wilderness area is managed as a wildland fire use action. Fourteen days later the fire crossed the maximum manageable area boundary and was converted to a suppression fire. This Wildland Fire Use Review examines actions and policies surrounding this event with suggestions for policy remediations and planning for future wildland fire use actions
incidents.quote: A common problem in wildland fire use incidents with unanticipated outcomes is unrealistic, indefensible maximum manageable areas (MMAs). The East Slide Rock Ridge WFU strategy had an indefensible MMA boundary to the north, based on a land allocation imaginary line (the wilderness boundary) rather than a defensible topographic feature or fuel break.

incidents.name: Smitty Fire Aircraft Accident Fatalities
incidents.summary: On September 1, 2008, about 1810 Pacific daylight time, N4235T, a Lockheed SP2H airplane, was destroyed after impacting terrain following a loss of power and loss of control about 2 miles northwest of the Reno/Stead (4SD) Airport, Reno, Nevada.
incidents.quote: The witness reported watching the airplane takeoff, and at an elevation estimated to be between 100 to 300 feet above the ground, he observed the left jet engine emitting flames, followed by the left wing being engulfed in flames. The witness further reported that about 2 seconds later the airplane entered a left wing down attitude before impacting terrain and bursting into flames.

incidents.name: Rattle Fire Snag Incident
incidents.summary: Just after felling a snag that threatened the fire line a faller is struck by a second snag. This High Reliability Organizing Review looks at the factors that were involved leading up to the faller to be struck.
incidents.quote: ...swamper-2 looked down to give the all clear on the radio and before the swamper-2 could key his radio, he looked up and saw a snag fall, landing directly on top of the faller-2 and only missing the swamper by about a foot. Faller-2 was not hit by the tree he was cutting, he was hit by a small snag from approximately 40 feet within the interior of the fire.

incidents.name: Pole Creek
incidents.summary: Dedicated resources for patrolling and monitoring did not occur throughout the entirety of the burn. Resources used for patrolling and monitoring continued as ignition resources on a different location within the project area. This resulted in an area of the blackline that was out of sight of ignition resources and resultedin an escape which eventually consumed approximately 550 acres.
incidents.quote: There was consensus amongst the team and the local unit that “fire is fire”meaning whether it is blacklining, prescribed burning or a wildland fire. Agreement was reached that once “fire is put on the ground” all rules of fire management apply.

incidents.name: Jay Fire ATV Rollover
incidents.summary: Two members of a VFD were following a dozer into a fire. While descending a steep hil the six-wheel ATV rolled over.
incidents.quote: The descent was very rocky and uneven and the flattened oak brush concealed a depression in the trail. The right front wheel of the ATV went into this depression and that coupled with the momentum of driving down the steep incline and the weight of the passengers caused the ATV to roll over to the right. The driver was able to extricate himself but the passenger remained pinned until the driver and three other firefighters were able to roll the ATV off of the individual.

incidents.name: Wizard Fire
incidents.summary: A preoccupation with ignition of a new unit (Highway 20 Project, unit #25) occurred. No plan was established for multi-ignition prescribed burn operations, which lead to focus on the next ignition of the Highway 20 Project Unit #25 and missing the patrol and mop-up phases of Unit #61. The Acting FMO, Fuels Specialist, and Fuels Technician, discussed plans for the next day, but no operational plan was formalized, nor were crews briefed related to Unit 61 AND Unit 25. The fire on Unit 61 escaped the containment lines on the day after ignitions, resulting in a wildfire declaration.
incidents.quote: The Patrol plan is vague. The burn plan speaks to the day of the burn, but not to the following days during the patrol portion of the burn. The burn plan mentions the untreated forest land along the north boundary. The Mop-up shift plan was not utilized for the day after the ignition phase of the burn.

incidents.name: Sacramento Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: Officer Falconer was working on a fire line with the Globe Wildland Fire Crew while fighting the Sacramento Fire in the vicinity of Lake Havasu City. Falconer complained of feeling dizzy and after sitting, collapsed from a cause still to be reported. Other officer and inmate firefighters responded immediately to provide emergency medical assistance and made every effort to revive Falconer. Sun City paramedics were summoned to the scene and initiated basic life support measures. Officer Falconer was subsequently transported to the Colorado River Medical Center in Needles, California for emergency medical treatment, where at 1445hrs he was pronounced dead.
incidents.quote: Falconer complained of feeling dizzy and after sitting, collapsed.

incidents.name: Indian Run
incidents.summary: The Indian Run Prescribed Fire Facilitated Learning Analysis examines the planning and events leading up to a wildfire declaration through a lens of High Reliability Organizing.
incidents.quote: “Don’t tell the ID Team/District Ranger you can do things that you can’t. Make sure the project boundaries are defendable."

incidents.name: Chalk Fire Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: On October 3rd, 2008, at approximately 1940 hrs., a Strike Team made up of 4 BDF engines and 1BLM engine were traveling from the ICP to their night shift assignment. While in a curve, the right rear wheels of Engine #56 ran off the roadway and caught a four to six inch drop between the asphalt and shoulder. The driver attempted to correct the situation, resulting in the engine veering across theroad, hitting a dirt embankment and rolling over on the left hand side of the road. The engine landed on the passenger side. The five crew members were treated on scene and transported by ground ambulance to Mee Memorial Hospital in King City, CA. All crew members were treated and released with minor injuries.
incidents.quote: San Bernardino National Forest (BDF) Engine #56, with five crew members, drifted off the right hand side of a paved two lane road and causing the engine to veer across the two lane road, hit an embankment and roll over.

incidents.name: Committee Drive Fire Engine Burnover 2008
incidents.summary: On October 7, 2008, at approximately 1230 hours, the local Fire Department personnel initial-attacked the Committee Drive Fire. Estimated size at initial attack was 5 acres. Given the fire's forward spread and progression into denser timber, a request was made for four mutual aid engines. Upon their arrival, Engine C was staged for structure protection closer to the origin, while the other three units (engines D, E, and F) were directed to go to the tower site. At approximately 1330 hours, a wind shift occurred, causing the fire to make a run toward the vicinity of three of the mutual aid engines. While trying unsuccessfully to restart the pump for spraying, Engine F’s motor stalled out and could not be restarted. The fire spread to Engine F’s site and started to engulf it. The Fire Department personnel at the scene and engines D and E retreated to a safety zone near the tower site--resulting in no personal injuries, but a total loss of Engine F.

incidents.name: Quarling Eagles
incidents.fire: Quarling Eagles Prescribed Fire/NF5 Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: This escaped prescribed fire examines two prescribed fires declared wildfires. The Quarling Eagle prescribed fire, a timber sale purchaser conducted burn, highlights tensions between timber sale contract requirements and fire management prescribed burn requirements. The NF5 prescribed fire, an agency ignited fire, was declared wild after 54 days for various reasons, even though the fire had not escaped the unit boundary.
incidents.quote: When preparing the complexity analysis for a burn plan it may be appropriate to document that the ignition phase of a burn rates as Complex, but also include that follow up patrol activities may rate as Intermediate.

incidents.name: Greenthin
incidents.summary: A fall prescribed fire on the edge of a Ranger District, GACC boundary, and State line escapes at night despite staffing above the burn plan requirements.
incidents.quote: Before the burn and during the afternoon, crews were chattering about tree top winds, concerns with mid-slope holding, receptive fuel bed (“the fuels crunched when walked upon”), an engine crew noted “We are going to suck smoke.”

incidents.name: Union Chapel VFD Accident
incidents.summary: Firefighter John C. Myers passed away from injuries received in a motor vehicle accident while working at the scene of an outdoor grass fire.
incidents.quote: Myers was traveling south on County Road Wesley, when his son, Firefighter Juston Myers, also working the fire, was heading north on CR Wesley. Juston crossed left of center on the narrow gravel road in heavy smoke obstructed conditions and collided head on with the fire department vehicle his father was driving.

incidents.name: Mannford Oklahoma Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: Nearly a dozen hours after the grass firefight had begun, firefighter Adams collapsed and stopped breathing at approximately 2200hrs while he was backing his fire apparatus along the side of Hwy 51. Adams was assisted by other responders but succumbed to his injury and was pronounced at the scene.

incidents.name: Mallard Slough Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The Mallard Slough Prescribed fire was ignited on March 13, 2009, on the Camas National Wildlife Refuge in southeast Idaho. The prescribed fire's objective was to consume 95–100% of the dead materials in 13 medium-(30’ x 30’)-size machine piles. These piles consisted of branch and bowl wood from nearby Russian olive trees that were removed as part of a hazard fuels reduction project. On March 21st, these piles apparently still had some residual heat that spread out of the piles and started a grass and brush fire that subsequently burned 172 acres on the Refuge.

incidents.name: Christian Creek
incidents.summary: On April 9, 2009, North Carolina Division of Forest Resources (NCDFR) personnel responded to the Christian Creek Fire. The fire was contained at approximately three acres. The next morning, three NCDFR personnel returned to the fire to determine “mop-up” requirements. At approximately 0950 hours, lightning struck the ground near the firefighters as they were patrolling the fireline. One firefighter was knocked to the ground and another reported feeling some tingling in his shoulder area. All three individuals were transported to Mission Memorial Hospital in Asheville, North Carolina with non-life threatening injuries. By 1230 hours that day, they were evaluated for injuries and released .

incidents.name: East Encerrito Prescribed Fire 2009
incidents.summary: During the second day of East Encerrito Prescribed Fire operations, an unexpected wind shift and change in fire behavior forced the Fire Effects Monitor (FEMO) Trainee to make a hasty retreat to a safety zone. The FEMO trainee narrowly avoided serious injury and entrapment from a rapidly moving head fire, due in part to a timely warning and situational awareness.

incidents.name: Nugget Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The prescribed fire was declared an escaped fire and the largest of the spots was contained at 42 acres at the end of the first operational shift (day of ignition).
incidents.quote: During ignition operations, several spot fires occurred, one of which grew rapidly. In attempt to contain this spot fire, additional resources were ordered, including air tankers.

incidents.name: Farm Flats Proficiency Jump
incidents.summary: One jumper fell from the tree or “burned out.” He sustained injuries that required a medivac, by helicopter, from the jump spot to the closest emergency facility. The five smokejumpers who experienced “hard landings” were assessed at the medical facility.
incidents.quote: Five individuals did experience “hard landings,” and one smokejumper landed in a tree.

incidents.name: Palomar IHC Carrier Accident
incidents.summary: There was no injury to drivers or passengers in either vehicle.
incidents.quote: When the other vehicle driver lost control, the vehicle began hitting guard rails on both sides of the road, impacted the crew carrier’s front left bumper, fender, and tire, and ended up resting on the other side of the south bound lane of the highway.

incidents.name: Red Rock Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The fire exceeded the capability of the Ranger District and Forest requiring conversion to a wildfire.
incidents.quote: A planned 206-acre prescribed underburn, to reduce hazardous fuel loadings and re-introduce fire into the wilderness.

incidents.name: Freeman Reservoir Fatality
incidents.summary: On June 26, 2009, Brett Stearns, Engine Captain of Little Snake Field Office (LSFO) Engine 1613, was fatally injured as a result of traumatic injury incurred during a tree felling training exercise. This injury was directly caused by a section of tree that broke away from the main trunk during a felling demonstration and struck Mr. Stearns in the head and back.
incidents.quote: A warning was shouted and Team 4 Trainer, still holding the saw, was able to take approximately three steps toward his escape route before he was struck in the head and the backside of his body.

incidents.name: Logging Slash Fire Fuel Tank Ignition
incidents.summary: At approximately 1857 hours on July 9, 2009, while supporting a water pumping operation, a member of the Idaho City Interagency Hotshot Crew was burned while working on the Logging Slash Fire in interior Alaska. The IHC crewmember was assigned the operation of a Mark 3 pump to support a water pumping function utilizing a folda­tank and Mark 3 pump. During a routine check of the fuel supply the liquid and vapors were ignited. The resulting flash fire burned the crew member. A designated medevac helicopter from an adjacent fire was dispatched while medical personnel on scene began treatment of the injured crew member and prepared him for transport. The injured crew member was rapidly transported to a Fairbanks hospital and after an evaluation by physicians, was transferred to a Seattle burn center. The crew member was moved from the Intensive Care Unit to the regular burn ward where his condition continued to improve.
incidents.quote: During a routine check of the fuel supply, when the crew member opened the Jerry can (fuel tank), flammable liquid and vapors spewed from the container and were ignited.

incidents.name: White Fire
incidents.summary: Two firefighters received injuries, one with a possible broken collarbone (X-ray showed badly bruised) and the second firefighter received a broken arm and two lacerations to the head (fifteen stitches) when his hardhat was knocked off and he fell to the ground.
incidents.quote: While working a lightning fire, in very steep terrain, two firefighters on the ground were injured when a heli-tanker water drop of 400 gallons missed its target.

incidents.name: Willow Helibase Rappel Fatality
incidents.summary: On July 21, 2009, Thomas David Marovich, Jr. a Rappeller from the Chester Helitack Crew attached to the Lassen National Forest sustained fatal injuries from an un-arrested descent during a proficiency rappel just southeast of the Willow Creek Helibase.
incidents.quote: "We are all a version of TJ. We are all a version of his crew that day. We do work involving risk. We practice and perform life-dependent critical tasks over and over. Proficiency rappels were intended to prevent just this kind of accident and it happened anyway."

incidents.name: Backbone Fire Helicopter Crash
incidents.summary: On July 17, 2009, about 1510 Pacific daylight time, a Croman SH-3H, N613CK, collided with terrain at a heliwell site near the Willow Creek Hellibase, Willow Creek, California. On the accident flight, pilot 1 stated that the helicopter had taken on 400 to 450 gallons of water, which was the same amount as previous flights. As he applied power, the helicopter started to climb clear of the heliwell. He stated that as the snorkel came out of the water, the other pilot (pilot 2) warned the pilot 1 of a droop in rotor RPM several times. Pilot 1 said that he stopped applying power, and started to move forward. He tried to drop the load, but was not sure that he actually activated the dump switch. Witnesses observed the left main landing gear make contact with the heliwell. The helicopter rolled after ground contact, and came to rest on its left side. Both pilots survived the accident.
incidents.quote: Witnesses observed the left main landing gear make contact with the heliwell.

incidents.name: Whiskey Fire
incidents.summary: Three employees provided medical attention to the employee and later assisted in loading employee “A” on to the helicopter and they took him to the Hospital.
incidents.quote: About a step into it, the ground gave way and employee “A” ended up falling down the hill into his secondary escape route. In the process his knee got twisted and dislocated his knee cap 2-3 inches to the right of his knee.

incidents.name: Mill Flat Fire
incidents.summary: By the time the smoke cleared the following morning, all the residents of the town had been evacuated, six homes were destroyed or severely damaged and several other buildings and corrals were significantly burned.
incidents.quote: The Mill Flat Fire which had been managed since July 25, 2009 rapidly burned out of the Pine Valley Wilderness on the Dixie National Forest in southern Utah moving down hill towards the town of New Harmony.

incidents.name: Little Grass Valley
incidents.summary: The employee was treated and released but ordered to remain off work pending further medical examinations.
incidents.quote: One of the employees cut a small tree that fell and struck another employee. The employee that was hit by the tree was injured and required a Medivac flight to an area hospital.

incidents.name: Dry Creek Complex
incidents.summary: On Friday, August 21, 2009, at approximately 1200 hours, three Type 6 engines, an ATV w/firing device and one firefighter on foot were assigned to a burn-out and holding operation in an indirect firefighting strategy to hold a fireline in advance of a wildland fire. The fire behavior was changing rapidly with severe increases in rates of spread. The Captain in one of the holding engines attempted to yell out the window of the engine to tell two firefighters on the ground to get into the engine. However, they were unable to hear this order. There was no attempt to call them on the radio. They ran east on the road, jumped a fence and ran into a vineyard. The Engine Captain was unable to move the vehicle until the fire had completely surrounded it and then passed by. The Captain, not knowing where the two firefighters were located, radioed that he had lost two firefighters. Hearing that communication, the firefighters radioed that they had left and were OK.

incidents.name: Bull Run Snag Fatality
incidents.summary: A falling snag may have been knocked over by the rotor-wash of the CH-47 helicopter being used for the eradication.
incidents.quote: Steve Uptegrove was part of a forest crew assisting the Baker County Narcotics Enforcement Team with the eradication of an illegal marijuana garden on national forest lands south of Unity, Oregon.

incidents.name: Klamath Hotshots Rollover
incidents.summary: One crew member with significant injuries was transported to a hospital in Chico, CA and admitted for treatment. The rest of the crew sustained minor to moderate injuries and were transported to a hospital in Red Bluff, CA and treated then released.
incidents.quote: Eight personnel from the Klamath Hotshots, Klamath National Forest, were involved in a vehicle accident on Highway 99 near Los Molinos, CA.

incidents.name: Big Meadow Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The Big Meadow Prescribed Fire was an 89-acre subunit of the Foresta Complex Prescribed Fire Plan. On August 26, 2009, after planning and preparing the prescribed fire unit, Yosemite National Park personnel began implementation of the project. At 1015 hours a test fire was initiated and results were within prescription parameters. The Go/No Go Checklist was approved and ignition of the unit continued. Soon after, multiple spot fires occurred outside of prepared firelines which included several burning snags. Personnel on scene were unable to contain the spot fires and the Burn Boss declared the prescribed burn a wildfire at 1210 hours.
incidents.quote: The prescription was followed, but it was inadequate.

incidents.name: Station Fire Fatalities
incidents.summary: On the afternoon of Sunday, August 30, 2009, at approximately 1645 hours, a County of Los Angeles Fire Department, Camp Superintendant (Fire Captain) and Camp Foreman (Fire Fighter Specialist) were involved in a single vehicle accident near Los Angeles County Fire Camp 16 (near Mt. Gleason).
incidents.quote: At approximately 1630 hours, Camp 16 began experiencing an ember shower due to the unstable air and tremendous energy release that lifted massive amounts of ignited fire brands into the atmosphere.

incidents.name: Station Fire
incidents.summary: The study reviewed the past practice of using helicopters in support of night firefighting, which agencies are currently doing night operations, what technology is available today, mission definition and qualification, risk assessment for the candidate helicopter night missions, effectiveness and utilization of night water drops and cost estimates.
incidents.quote: The Chief of the Forest Service has initiated a national assessment of night flying operations. The Forest Service stopped these operations in the early 1980’s due to night flying accidents that resulted in fatalities.

incidents.name: Silver Fire Hit by Water Drop
incidents.summary: The entire snag was knocked down by the drop and fortunately the crewmember was not struck directly by the entire snag.
incidents.quote: Three crewmembers got behind a tree to shield themselves, when a piece of a 16” DBH cedar snag hit one of the crewmembers on the wrist, fracturing it.

incidents.name: Silver Fire Run Over by Vehicle
incidents.summary: The firefighter was taken by ambulance to the local hospital and later transferred to a trauma center, remaining there for a month.
incidents.quote: At that time he saw a sleeping bag in the headlights and realized a person in the sleeping bag was seriously injured after being struck by the tire of the water truck.

incidents.name: Woody Ridge Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: Both of the injured employees were treated and released that day, though both continued to experience some symptoms more than a week later.
incidents.quote: Seconds after that call and concerned for their own safety, the firefighters retreated toward what they believed would be a safer area back toward the main fire. During their retreat, they were hit by a brief but intense pulse of convective heat. Both firefighters suffered airway injuries.

incidents.name: Lava Point Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On October 3, 2009, the Zion Fire Management Program was planning to burn a 45-acre unit prior to a cold front's frontal passage. The decision was made to black line the unit's south boundary prior to the frontal passage and then burn the remainder of the unit after the front had passed. At 1100, hours a test fire was initiated. At 1230 hours, it was determined that results were within prescription parameters and met the resource objectives. After 2 spot fires could not be contained the Burn Boss requested that the contingency resources, which were not on scene, be dispatched to support operations. The next day, with two uncontrolled spot fires and a forecasted cold front passage with high winds and no means to pay for assisting interagency resources, the Burn Boss declared the prescribed burn a wildfire at 0840 hours.
incidents.quote: The Go/No Go Checklist was approved and ignition of the unit continued. After progressing a quarter mile, multiple spot fires occurred outside of the identified unit. Firing operations were halted. Even so, personnel on scene were unable to contain the spot fires.

incidents.name: Sheep Fire
incidents.summary: A private passenger vehicle pulled onto Hwy 138 and into the traffic lane of E-4699. When the operator of E-4699 applied the brakes, the engine lost traction with the road surface. The loss of traction resulted in the engine striking a bridge abutment and causing major damage to the front end of the vehicle.
incidents.quote: Use of seat belts prevented serious injuries to personnel on the engine.

incidents.name: Mi-Wok Ranger District Rx Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The firefighter received 1st, 2nd, and 3rd degree burns to the right leg. The firefighter was transported to a local medical clinic for treatment, referred to UC Davis Burn Center, and was released.
incidents.quote: The firefighter unknowingly dripped fuel from these two torches onto his pant leg. When the firefighter walked past a burning pile, his pant leg ignited.

incidents.name: Lynn Hollow Tree Incident
incidents.summary: On Saturday, November 07, 2009, the Firestorm Wildland Fire Suppression Crew (FWFS), a contract fire fighting company, was working in Great Smoky Mountains National Park. The FWFS crew was tasked with “prepping” the Lynn Hollow drainage for a planned prescribed burn. The FWFS crew of 15 and one National Park Service employee arrived at the worksite, briefed as to the day’s work assignments, and began work at 0830 hours. At approximately 1305 hours he was struck by a large chestnut oak limb. The patient was treated and released from Blount Memorial with soft tissue injuries to his back and shoulder with instructions not to return to work for three days. He also sustained minor cuts and abrasions to his face, neck, and upper back.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1305 hours, the faller was felling two beetle-kill snags that were leaning against a large limb approximately 45 feet above ground level on a healthy Chestnut Oak. The faller's cut on the first pine went as planned. As the faller's second pine began to fall in the intended direction, he began to egress along his planned route and was struck by a large chestnut oak limb that had been broken by the second beetle-kill pine as it fell.

incidents.name: Twin Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: One of these spots became established beyond the capacity for control by ground forces resulting in an escape and a subsequent conversion to wildfire.
incidents.quote: Several spots occurred outside of the burn unit that afternoon. The next morning more spots were found east of the burn unit in heavy fuels and relatively inaccessible terrain.

incidents.name: Big Roundtop Fire Powerline Incident
incidents.summary: A Campbell County fire crew contained a 25‑acre fire on November 18, 2009, when a dead poplar snag near high‑voltage power lines snapped unexpectedly as the dozer operator attempted to move it, striking two power lines and causing dangerous arcing and flames. The Incident Commander ordered the operator to remain still until the lines were de‑energized, after which utility personnel removed the tree and forestry staff completed mop‑up once the area was safe.
incidents.quote: The trunk of the tree burst into flame where it made contact with the 2 lines. The scene felt like a fireworks display

incidents.name: Dark Ridge Tree Felling Incident
incidents.summary: On November 29, 2009, a Big South Fork FirePro crewmember was felling a snag­-topped hickory tree on the Cumberland Gap National Historic Park boundary in preparation for a prescribed burn. The Cumberland Gap Wildland Fire Module Supervisor noticed that the tree was not falling as expected and moved to the tree to assist with placing wedges. The tree then broke free and pivoted, falling against the Wildland Fire Module Supervisor--pinning him to the ground. Crew members immediately radioed for assistance and began cutting and removing the tree. Local EMS was transported to the scene, where the injured employee was stabilized and taken to a waiting helicopter for transport to the University of Tennessee Trauma Center for definitive care.

incidents.name: Driving Accident CNF
incidents.summary: The government vehicle then traveled straight down the side of the hill and came down to rest on its side. The three firefighters reported that they suffered no injuries.
incidents.quote: A vehicle came into their lane causing the Forest Service driver to take evasive action. Once correction was made they entered “Dead Man’s Curve” came out of it and saw another vehicle coming down hill.

incidents.name: Feather River RX Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The firefighter was transported to a burn center for treatment.
incidents.quote: During operations one firefighter suffered second-degree burns to his right leg covering approximately three percent of his body.

incidents.name: Windsong Prescribed Fire Review
incidents.summary: The slopover was contained within the first burning period and was not declared a wildfire.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service prescribed fire near the town of Custer, South Dakota, spread onto Forest and Private Lands.

incidents.name: Great Divide Escape RX
incidents.summary: At approximately 1100, the RXB3 is contacted by aerial patrol and notified that the prescribed fire escaped Unit 2 and upon growing in size, is declared a wildfire by noon.
incidents.quote: The [now]minimal staffing and distance between this unit and the others provides some challenge in containing the minor spread of the fire beyond its original control lines.

incidents.name: Fletcher Escaped RX
incidents.summary: No structures were lost, however 212 acres of private land were involved in the Road 39 wildfire.
incidents.quote: On April 8, 2010, the Fletcher Block 2 (Fletcher burn), a 2466 acre prescribed fire, was ignited on the Poteau/Cold Springs Ranger District of the Ouachita National Forest.

incidents.name: Birthday Fire
incidents.summary: A firefighter was struck by a hazard tree on April 19, 2010 at approximately1800 p.m. Mountain Standard Time during wildland fire suppression operations while assigned to the Birthday Fire located on the Bureau of Indian Affairs Crow Agency in South Central Montana. The firefighter was transported by air ambulance to Billings, Montana for treatment of injuries received.
incidents.quote: The firefighter was struck in the back while retreating.

incidents.name: Cooter's Bog Escape Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The wildfire eventually burned 132 acres of pine plantation before being brought under control by on-site and contingency resources.
incidents.quote: After completion of the firing phase of prescribed burn operations, a pine snag caught fire and threw embers outside of control lines, causing a spot fire in a pine plantation on adjacent private lands.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Swamper Injury LP NF
incidents.summary: The FEO received a laceration to his right index finger, requiring four stitches.
incidents.quote: The FEO reached into to Sage Brush to assist the sawyer by pulling brush and made contact with the tip of the saw.

incidents.name: Shultz Fire
incidents.summary: All three did escape to a safe area without any injury however some minor damage was done to vehicles due to heat.
incidents.quote: Three individuals' escape route was compromised without their knowledge. As the incident developed from single tree and group torching into a sustained crown run the individuals which were in three separate vehicles were forced to utilize their escape route.

incidents.name: Carson Hole Parachute Landing Injury
incidents.summary: The injuries sustained include a fractured left fibula and a sprained right ankle.
incidents.quote: On July 3, 2010, at 12:54 PM, a Bureau of Land Management smokejumper was injured during initial response of the Carson Hole Wildland Fire.

incidents.name: Meadow Creek APA
incidents.summary: The seriousness of her injuries (fractured pelvis and three broken ribs) was not fully understood by Shannon or her supervisor for nearly two weeks after the accident. Word of this accident did not reach fire managers on the White River National Forest for almost a month.
incidents.quote: As she looked up in the direction of the sound, she made a split second decision that saved her life; Shannon launched off the log. Branches of the 60 foot tall, 12-inch Douglas-fir caught her in mid-air, twirled her around, and slammed her onto the rocky stream bed 5 feet below.

incidents.name: Bear Fire Exposure
incidents.summary: A post incident military safety team discovered an expended canister of CS gas in the area where firefighters experienced a strange smell with metallic or bitter taste. The ICT4(T) declared a Mass Casualty Incident (MCI) and all ten were transported via air and ground ambulance to two local hospitals for evaluation and treatment.
incidents.quote: During initial attack of the Bear Incident ten firefighters, including the incident commander left the fireline complaining of nausea, vomiting, headache and extreme fatigue.

incidents.name: Sand 2 Incident
incidents.summary: It was not until a day later when the Firefighter returned home and visited a medical facility, that it was determined he had suffered burns on his feet.
incidents.quote: The Firefighter began to feel heat through his boots and would from time to time back off to allow some cooling to take place and then step back into the ash to work again.

incidents.name: Stove Scald Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The firefighter was treated for and released with 1st degree burns to the back of hands, face and neck, and 1st to 2nd degree burns to the face and chest.
incidents.quote: The scalding burn occurred when boiling coffee grounds and water splashed onto the firefighter’s chest, face, neck and hands as he was reaching to turn off the stove.

incidents.name: Trail Peak Fire Excertion
incidents.summary: Hospital Patient assessed by doctor and diagnosed to have an imbalance of electrolytes and physical exhaustion.
incidents.quote: At approximately 2015, a Firefighter was incapacitated due to over exertion and an electrolyte imbalance, causing severe cramping of the legs, mild vision and disorientation problems, during initial response of the Trail Peak Fire

incidents.name: Constantia Fire
incidents.summary: The fire fighter was working on a tree torching near the line, fell and received minor burns to the left hand due to not wearing gloves.
incidents.quote: A crewmember of the Diamond Mountain Hotshots was injured while working on the Constantia Incident.

incidents.name: Snake Bite Incident
incidents.summary: A crew assigned to the McDonald Incident made the decision to sleep in an area of slightly rolling terrain located off of the main access road approximately 1.8 miles east of the Incident Base. The crew parked their vehicle off a “two track” and dispersed into an area approximately 50 feet behind their vehicle. Tents were not used, the crew choosing to sleep on ground cloths in their sleeping bags. At approximately 2300, approximately one hour after “bedding down,” a poisonous snake crawled into the sleeping bag of a crew member as they slept. After awaking to the movement, the crew member received multiple bites on the thigh while removing the snake from their sleeping bag.
incidents.quote: Tents were not used, the crew choosing to sleep on ground cloths in their sleeping bags.

incidents.name: Arkansas Forestry Commission Tractor Transport Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: Forest Ranger Christopher Wayne Adams worked a fire scene on the morning of August 2, 2010. His activities consisted of plowing lines around a previous fire to assure containment. Once this was completed, Forest Ranger Adams was assigned to drive a tractor trailer truck hauling a D5 Caterpillar plow. As Forest Ranger Adams approached a curve in the road, he lost control of the vehicle; it left the roadway and overturned. Forest Ranger Adams was trapped in the cab of the truck and was pronounced dead at the scene. Forest Ranger Adams was wearing his seatbelt at the time of the crash.

incidents.name: Morton Fire Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: Both firefighters received first responder emergency medical care within moments and Advanced Life Support care within 20 minutes of their request for assistance.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1612 hours the personnel from Water Tender 99 reported via radio that their vehicle had rolled down an embankment and requested help.

incidents.name: Deer Park Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: After landing, the helicopter tipped backwards onto its tail boom, rendering the helicopter and medivac spot unusable for the medical evacuation. A second medivac spot was created, and an agency contracted helicopter was used to medivac the patient and medical personnel to the Deer Park helibase.
incidents.quote: While walking up the ridgeline on roughly a 35% slope, the lookout stumbled and reached towards the rocks to steady his balance. This caused an approximately 200 pound boulder to slide free which rolled and pinned the lookout against other rocks. The lookout radioed back to the crew that he had sustained a possible femur fracture.

incidents.name: Patrol Motorcycle Accident
incidents.summary: He suffered a crushed L-5 vertebrate and a realignment of his L-4 and L-3.
incidents.quote: A Fire Prevention Technician rode his motorcycle over an embankment and came to rest approximately 60 feet from the roads edge in a rock pile.

incidents.name: Assault at Remote Work Station
incidents.summary: On August 18, 2010 at approximately 1445, a U.S. Forest Service Prevention Patrol employee (Patrol 21) was working alone completing paperwork at East Fork, a remote station. An unknown male knocked on the door asking to use the telephone. Upon entry, the male attacked the employee for no apparent reason by striking him in the head, knocking him to the floor, and continued to kick the employee while unconscious. Somehow, the employee was able to use the cordless station phone to make a 911 call, which went to the local Los Angeles County (LACO) Sheriff’s Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) station. The LACO sheriff relayed the information to LACO Fire. That information was sent via a Mobile Data Terminal to the Angeles National Forest Emergency Operations Center (EOC). The EOC staff immediately dispatched the closest Forest Service engine to the East Fork station.
incidents.quote: Upon entry, the male attacked the employee for no apparent reason by striking him in the head, knocking him to the floor, and continued to kick the employee while unconscious.

incidents.name: Davis 5 Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: An additional spot fire that had not been staffed started torching trees and rapidly became established beyond the capacity for control by ground forces resulting in an escape and a subsequent conversion to wildfire.
incidents.quote: One of the spot fires made a run of about 20 acres before lying down.

incidents.name: Banner Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: The firefighter was diagnosed with a concussion, soft tissue damage and slight swelling, and was released later that day to recover at home.
incidents.quote: While brushing out a highway right‐of‐way outside the fire perimeter, a firefighter from a Type II hand crew was hit on the right side of hard hat and on right side of forehead by a small diameter leaning snag.

incidents.name: Phoenix Fire
incidents.summary: The resulting injury was a deep tissue wound of 1.5 inches, requiring eight sutures.
incidents.quote: During one of the swings to drive the wedge, the axe hit the edge of wedge which was bottomed out and bounced back.

incidents.name: Jesse Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: Injuries sustained include two broken vertebrae, a sprained ankle and a torn MCL in the knee.
incidents.quote: At 1127 hours, while constructing line around the fire perimeter, a sawyer was struck by a dead fork of a subalpine fir located within the fire.

incidents.name: Near Mid Air FLA
incidents.summary: The pilot of one of the aircraft took immediate evasive action and once separation had been obtained, discussion about the event occurred over the radio.
incidents.quote: Towards the end of the operational day, two aircraft came within an estimated 200-300 feet of each other.

incidents.name: Bullards Fire
incidents.summary: Firefighter receives 1st aid and awaits ground transport then later on at hospital received 10 stitches.
incidents.quote: Firefighter impacted by dawgs while hiking with the chainsaw, cut above right elbow .

incidents.name: Pyramid Butte FLA
incidents.summary: The crewmember was released from the hospital Intensive Care Unit after being treated for a skull fracture and internal bleeding.
incidents.quote: A Warm Springs IHC crewmember was struck by a large rock that caused considerable personal injury.

incidents.name: Scotts Chapel Road Fatality
incidents.summary: At approximately 1138 hours on September 7, 2010 a KDF Forest Ranger Technician engaged in fire suppression activities was struck in the head by a snag that had fallen and rolled downhill over a small bluff and struck the employee in the head. The employee was knocked out and sustained a serious head injury, fractured hip, bruises, and a 2nddegree leg burn on his calves from the burning snag.
incidents.quote: The crew spent the next 90 minutes assisting with providing aid to the injured firefighter, moving him to the road, and helping his transport to the hospital by Life Flight.

incidents.name: Bald Angel FLA
incidents.summary: The driver escaped through the driver’s side window after the cab filled with water and suffered a few bumps and bruises.
incidents.quote: When in reverse, the engine suddenly regained traction, jolted back and to the left resulting in the rear wheels sliding towards the reservoir. The engine rolled over into the reservoir in approximately four feet of water coming to rest on its passenger side and roof.

incidents.name: Crandall Felling Accident
incidents.summary: The AFEO was evacuated by air to West Park Medical Center, evaluated, treated for four broken spinous processes and released two days later.
incidents.quote: An Assistant Fire Engine Operator (AFEO) was struck and pinned to the ground by a tree he was cutting near the Crandall Ranger Station.

incidents.name: Long Fire Engine Damage
incidents.summary: Members of the engine crew returned from the fire line and extinguished the fire. Two firefighters used the pump, hose and water from the burning engine to suppress the fire.
incidents.quote: Several firefighters on the incident watched the apparatus burning as they attempted to contact the engine crew via radio communications.

incidents.name: McArthur Fire Department Engine Water Tank Rupture Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Ryan Neil Seitz and other firefighters from Ohio responded to a group of wildland fires in Eastern Ross County, Ohio. Firefighter Seitz was staffing a brush truck. The water tank on the brush truck failed under pressure and Firefighter Seitz was struck in the chest by a piece of the tank. He was killed as a result of trauma and was pronounced dead at the cene.

incidents.name: Atlantic Volunteer Fire Rescue Company Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter William Harold "Hal" Clark and the members of his department were assisting with wildland fires in New Church, VA. Firefighter Clark operated a 300 foot 1-1/2-inch hoseline on the fire for approximately 35 minutes. Firefighter Clark became ill while working the incident. He was treated at the scene and taken to the hospital. He was pronounced dead at the hospital as the result of a heart attack.

incidents.name: Lynn VFD Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On September 24, 2010, Firefighter Ronald W. Stephan responded to a mutual-aid wildland fire. By 1620 hours, his department was back in service. The next morning, Firefighter Stephan suffered a heart attack while working on his farm. EMS was called at 0950 hours. Firefighter and EMS responders provided CPR and ALS-level care. Their efforts were not successful and Firefighter Stephan was pronounced dead due to a heart attack.

incidents.name: Breaks 1 Escaped RX
incidents.summary: The next morning—because crews could not safely construct direct handline around the spots—an assessment of opportunities for containment indicated that spot fire spread could not be halted before the end of the next burning period and was then declared a wildfire.
incidents.quote: Due to strong winds, very rugged terrain, reduced visibility, and fire located below the holding crew positions, the Burn Boss and District fire managers deemed it unsafe to attack the spot fires that evening.

incidents.name: Sacramento Metro Fire District Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter James Carlyle Saunders and other firefighters from his fire department controlled a wildland fire that occurred near a local golf course. Firefighters were in the process of mopping up when Firefighter Saunders became ill. He was treated by firefighters and transported by ambulance to the hospital. Firefighter Saunders suffered a heart attack and died on October 7, 2010.

incidents.name: Columbia Fire Dept Hit by Vehicle Fatality 2010
incidents.summary: Firefighter Chance Hyatt Zobel and his engine company were dispatched to a fire in the median of a local highway. When his company and another engine arrived on the scene, they positioned their apparatus in a shielding position to protect firefighters from traffic. As Firefighter Zobel and other firefighters were extinguishing the fire, a two-vehicle crash occurred on the highway behind the apparatus. The crash caused one of the vehicles to slide between the guardrail and one of the engines. The vehicle entered the fire scene and struck Firefighter Zobel and another firefighter. Both firefighters were transported to the hospital. Firefighter Zobel died due to traumatic injuries.

incidents.name: Figueroa
incidents.summary: The Burn Boss determined that assigned resources would not be able to contain the fire and declared an escape at 2142 hours.
incidents.quote: At 2100 hours, a spot fire was detected outside the line on the northeast corner of the unit. This spot grew to 2 acres and progressed uphill within the project area.

incidents.name: California Department of Corrections Crew Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On November 23, 2010, an SUV crossed the centerline and collided head-on with a CDC inmate crew carrier, killing inmate firefighter Fernando Sanchez.

incidents.name: Greer Escaped RX Review
incidents.summary: Within the hour, the patrol unit began receiving text messages and voicemails inquiring about a large volume of smoke visible from Springerville east of the burn unit, and was later declared an escape and renamed the Turkey Fire.
incidents.quote: The Greer Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) Prescribed Fire was ignited north of Greer and west of Springerville, Arizona. Multiple units within the Greer WUI burn plan were implemented over the next several weeks.

incidents.name: North Carolina Firefighter Fatality
incidents.summary: Chief Barbour responded to a woods fire on 01/29/2011. The following day (within 24 hours), Barbour experienced chest pains and was transported to Wake Med in Raleigh, NC. Chief Barbour was treated at the hospital but never recovered from his injury and passed away just before midnight on 02/04/2011.
incidents.quote: Wilson's Mills Fire and Rescue Firefighter Fatality

incidents.name: Smoky Hill Wind Farm Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: A privately conducted prescribed burn escaped control, and Lincoln County authorities were notified of a wildfire. The fire spread quickly, eventually reaching 400 acres, and requiring the response of 120 firefighters operating 45 pieces of fire apparatus and supporting equipment. All 7 fire departments in Lincoln County were committed, and assisted by another 5 VFD’s from Ellsworth County. During initial suppression efforts, two firefighters in a brush truck (type 6 engine) experienced vehicle difficulties and became disabled in front of the fire, and subsequently sustained serious burns.
incidents.quote: They were unable to find immediate access to the burned area, and for reasons as-yet unknown, their engine stalled. They got out, and were almost immediately overrun by the head fire. They ran laterally out of the head fire, back towards where they had come from, which placed them in unburned fuel on one flank of the fire.

incidents.name: Bear Meadows Stop Work FLA
incidents.summary: The event was simply that an employee, over a period of time, came to realize a project he was working on was unsafe; not just for a person at his own skill level, but for anyone. Eventually the employee spoke up. After some initial surprise and organizational inertia, the project was reviewed by outside experts. The employee’s perceptions were validated and the project was suspended.
incidents.quote: “Individual chainsaw operators have the obligation to say “NO” and walk away from any situation they determine to be an unacceptable risk.” Forest Service Health and Safety Code Handbook

incidents.name: Unity Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: Upon leaving the scene of an outdoor fire and while returning to quarters, Firefighter Wilkes and another firefighter stopped at a convenience store to fill their apparatus with fuel. After entering the inside of the convenience store, Firefighter Wilkes suffered a medical emergency and passed away. The nature and cause of Firefighter Wilkes’ injury is still to be determined.

incidents.name: McCormick Highway Fire
incidents.summary: On February 21, 2011 multiple volunteer fire departments responded to a grass fire in Lincoln County. The first engine on the scene arrived within 6 minutes of the dispatch. The fire ignited (Cause-Machine Use) in an active hay field approximately 100 yards behind a structure. Structure protection was immediately established adjacent to the fire’s point of origin. Most containment efforts on the fire were unsuccessful as the fire spread exceeded engine/knocker capabilities. A volunteer fireman arriving to support the efforts of a fire knocker located near the head of the fire had to relocate his van from the threatening fire. Shortly after relocating the van and sizing the area up, he started approaching the area of the fire knocker on foot. As wind shifted intermediately, the spread of the fire exceeded his ability to escape the fire’s path. The fireman was burned (Approximately 26% of his body) while escaping to his van
incidents.quote: As wind shifted intermediately, the spread of the fire exceeded his ability to escape the fire’s path. The fireman was burned (Approximately 26% of his body) while escaping to his van

incidents.name: Westport Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: Several hours after participating in a training exercise related to wildland fire incidents, Fire Chief Stock passed away from a heart attack he suffered while at his residence.
incidents.quote: Westport Volunteer Fire Department Fatality

incidents.name: Shrimp Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Three tractor plows retreated to the black when fire behavior picked up on the Shrimp Fire. In the short time it took to turn one of the plows around, the operator was burned.
incidents.quote: The operator received flash burns to the eyes and some 1st degree burns to the eye lids. The operator’s neck shroud and other PPE likely prevented other burns.

incidents.name: Tar Heel Fire Department MVA Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Hunsinger while responding to a brush fire call was driving his personal vehicle (Mazda 3) to the fire department when he went off the road for an unknown reason, then overcorrected turning back into oncoming traffic, and was struck broadside by a minivan. Firefighter Hunsinger died at the scene. The driver of the minivan suffered minor injuries.
incidents.quote: Tar Heel Volunteer Fire Department Fatality

incidents.name: County Road U Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: The victim was riding in one of two fire department brush trucks that became stuck in sand. The four fire fighters abandoned their apparatus and walked southeast towards the nearest road to escape the fire. Approximately 300 yards from the apparatus, the fire fighters became separated due to poor visibility.
incidents.quote: He was found lying face down with severe burns to his feet, chest, arms, hands, and head but was alert and coherent.

incidents.name: 323 Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Simmons died while fighting a 3000 acre brush fire. While seeking safety from an area being overrun by flames during wildland firefighting operations, Firefighter Simmons passed away from “blunt force trauma consistent with being struck by a vehicle” based on information from the Tarrant County medical examiner.
incidents.quote: Volunteer Fire Fighter Dies and 5 Volunteer Fire Fighters are Injured during Wildland Urban Interface Fire.

incidents.name: Chittenden Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: The emergency room Doctor felt the laceration was not caused by the tree but was caused by the hard hat, yet he received multiple stitches.
incidents.quote: After getting hit with the tree Sam’s first thought was to get back to work and finish the project. He noticed there was something on his neck. Marvin looked at it and realized Sam was bleeding and had a scalp laceration.

incidents.name: Bull Fire Entrapment FLA
incidents.summary: An incident helicopter transported the injured firefighters to the Tucson hospital. . They were referred to the burn center in Phoenix and also released from the center that same day.
incidents.quote: After the two helitack members lit a backfire, they ran downhill away from H-3 and the fire, and then ran back to the helispot, dodging through the flames carrying their fire shelters in their hands. Both firefighters received burns.

incidents.name: Acadian Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Once the ambulance arrived the medical crew treated the LEO for first degree burns to the hands and a quarter size second degree burn to the right elbow. The LEO then returned to LE&I duties after being treated and did not require additional medical treatment.
incidents.quote: As the LEO was running towards the road he called the IC on the radio and informed the IC that he had received burns to his hands and arms.

incidents.name: Fiddlers Island Road Firing Operation Incident
incidents.summary: As the main fire continued burning to the west towards Buck Island, the decision was made for all resources to withdraw to the Strange Island Staging Safety Zone. No injuries to personnel or damage to equipment was reported.
incidents.quote: The decision was made to conduct a strategic firing operation in advance of the head of the fire and hold it on the east side of the road.

incidents.name: Horseshoe 2 Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: The two lookouts eventually take refuge in a stone building where LO1 eventually needed stiches in his hand after punching through a window to gain entry.
incidents.quote: Lookout 2 (LO2) and LO1 are both moving rapidly—believing that their lives are in danger. As they descend on the east side of the ridge, the fire makes a rapid uphill push on the west side that runs toward the lookout position that they had just abandoned.

incidents.name: Kay Currie Rd Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Goins was found burned and expired within a forest / brush fire near his own residence. The Texas Forest Service personnel were responding to the report of the fire. Apparently a Texas Forest Service spotter plane investigating the fire report saw and contacted the Angelina County Sheriff’s Office when they noticed a body on the ground. Exact details of the cause of death are unknown at this time and an autopsy has been ordered by the County Sheriff.
incidents.quote: Huntington Volunteer Fire Department Fatality

incidents.name: Hastings Fire Tree Incident
incidents.summary: After initial treatment the crew member was flown to Providence Hospital in Anchorage for additional tests and treatment. He was released from the hospital on 06/17 and later released for travel to his home unit.
incidents.quote: While conducting mop-up operations, a member of the ZigZag IHC was struck by a tree.

incidents.name: Blue Ribbon Fire Fatalities
incidents.summary: The Type 3 Tractor/Plow unit became stumped in a Hardwood cut-over dry swamp. One of the Type 2 Tractor/Plow units came to assist and became hung up in the process as well. With the fire approaching, the two operators left their units on foot and both were overtaken by fire shortly after where they both perished.
incidents.quote: Crews were unaware that there was more than one cutover (dry) pond.

incidents.name: Engine 30 Vehicle Fire
incidents.summary: In June 2011, a Type 6 engine suffered driveline failure while traveling on I-10 near Buckeye, AZ en route to a severity assignment. Flying driveline parts ignited a vehicle and grass fire; the crew safely discharged extinguishers and removed fuel cans before the engine was consumed.
incidents.quote: The passenger noticed driveline parts flying out behind the vehicle—that started a wildfire. The driver pulled the engine into the median and quickly exited.

incidents.name: Debris Fire Near Miss
incidents.summary: A near-miss incident that occurred in the CALFIRE Riverside Unit. The incident resulted in power lines falling narrowly missing an engine and where two CAL FIRE/Riverside County Fire Department Type I Fire Engines sustained damage from radiant heat during the suppression of a debris fire that threatened structures.

incidents.name: Las Conchas Rock Injury
incidents.summary: The patient was immediately evaluated by fireline EMT’s with the decision made to transport him via short-haul helicopter due to the nature of the injury and steep terrain where the crew was located.
incidents.quote: The first boulder, the size of a “Volkswagen Beetle”, was successfully avoided but another rock, measuring 2’ x 2’, hit the crewmember pinning him to the ground.

incidents.name: Crew Carrier Rollover 2011
incidents.summary: A hot shot crew carrier was returning to quarters after completing a recon for possible lightning strikes, left the roadway (Mt. Emma Road), and rolled down an embankment, coming to rest on the driver’s side. All nine crew members were transported to four local hospitals for evaluation and treatment. Seven crew members were released by 0500 on July 5, 2011 and two were admitted for further evaluation and treatment at USC Medical Center.

incidents.name: McCuen Fire LLR
incidents.summary: After arrival to ICP, the crew showered and changed cloths in the school facilities. Further evaluation from the Raton Fire Department/Haz-Mat response Team determined there was no threat and they were all cleared.
incidents.quote: A Type 2 crew comprised of USFS/NPS employees from Montana witnessed flames exiting the fire hose which they were utilizing for mop up.

incidents.name: CR 337 Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: On July 7, 2011 at approximately 1550 hours, crewmembers from the Bonneville IHC were performing cold trailing operations after completing hand fireline construction in Division A of the CR 337 Fire. This location is approximately 5 miles northwest of Mineral Wells, in Palo Pinto County, Texas. Weather conditions were very hot, with afternoon temperatures exceeding 105 degrees Fahrenheit. Without exhibiting any noticeable signs of distress, crewmember Caleb Hamm lost consciousness and stopped breathing. Initial efforts to restore breathing were unsuccessful.
incidents.quote: About 20 minutes before the accident, the Bonneville Assistant Superintendent stopped and talked to Hamm for a couple of minutes and said he was completely lucid and did not appear to be fatigued.

incidents.name: Las Conchas Vehicle Burn Damage
incidents.summary: Engine 2 Captain experienced a sunburn like sensation on his left ear and face and smoke inhalation, which developed into a cough. Two days later, Engine 2 Captain was taken to a second hospital for a second evaluation because his cough persisted.
incidents.quote: They had no place to go with the fire increasing in intensity. It was at this point that he felt the radiant heat on the left side of his face and experienced smoke inhalation.

incidents.name: Engine 5442 Drive Shaft Failure
incidents.summary: At approximately 1100 hours on July 10, 2011, the front drive shaft on Bureau of Land Management Southern Nevada District Fire Engine 5442 broke and separated from the vehicle. The vehicle was travelling at approximately 60 miles per hour on US 95 near Las Vegas, Nevada. This failure caused severe damage to the engine, totaled one and moderately damaged three other privately owned vehicles that were travelling in the vicinity of the accident. No injuries occurred.

incidents.name: Steel Fire Hit By Log
incidents.summary: The firefighter was transported by an agency helicopter to the hospital and diagnosed with a dislocated collar bone and broken shoulder. The firefighter was treated and released with plans to see an orthopedic surgeon for shoulder surgery.
incidents.quote: A crewmember of an initial attack crew on the Steel Fire in Idaho was struck—and carried downhill—by a chunk of rolling log.

incidents.name: Diamond Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: The Fort Apache Helitack and Fort Apache Hotshots were dispatched as Initial Attack resources and were flown to a helispot located on a ridge top on Patty Butte near the fire start. Terrain in the area is steep and rocky with a dense woodlands fuel type. Following completion of a handline around the approximately 35 acre fire all resources hiked back up to the helispot (spike camp). As resources returned to helispot, the Incident Commander determined that one firefighter was not accounted for and initiated a search to locate the missing firefighter. The firefighter was in possession of a handheld radio and attempts to contact him throughout the evening were not successful. After several sweeps of the area, law enforcement from local, county and state agencies were requested to assist with the search efforts. Search efforts continued throughout the night until the missing firefighter was found deceased at 6:18 am.
incidents.quote: Diamond Fire Fatality

incidents.name: Chainsaw Stopped By Chaps
incidents.summary: A firefighter/Sawyer Class “A” was working with a crew on a thinning project located in a thick mixture of vegetation (Fir, Oak), located on a slight slope. No injuries incurred.
incidents.quote: The moving chain cut through the first three layers of materiel but was stopped by the fibers before it could cut into his leg.

incidents.name: Perry Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: Captain King reportedly stopped breathing while fighting a grass and abandoned structure fire and received CPR and ALS treatment, he started breathing again at the scene and was taken to a hospital in Oklahoma City where he died. Weather conditions (heat) are being considered a contributing factor but the cause remains undetermined at this time.
incidents.quote: Perry Fire Department Fatality

incidents.name: Carrying Chainsaw Injury
incidents.summary: In August 2011, a sawyer carrying an un-sheathed chainsaw on his shoulder lost balance slightly, causing the chain to cut his neck. The sawyer suffered a neck laceration requiring stitches.
incidents.quote: As the firefighter was proceeding to his next cut he lost his balance slightly as he was hiking, bringing the chain on chainsaw in contact with his neck.

incidents.name: Coal Canyon Fire Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: During initial attack, the Incident Commander formulated a plan: use hose lay and hand line to work up from the heel on the right flank, use the helicopter to make bucket drops along the left flank. As additional resources arrived, the IC, perceiving the increasing complexity, requested a type 3 organization through dispatch. Shortly after, as fire behavior increased and compromised an egress route, fire entrapped and overran firefighters attempting escape. One firefighter died, two received serious burns, and two received minor burns.
incidents.quote: As fire behavior increased and compromised an egress route out of the fire area, the fire entrapped and overran firefighters attempting escape.

incidents.name: Coal Canyon Fire Entrapment Fatality 2011
incidents.summary: On August 11, 2011, at approximately 1330, U.S. Forest Service, South Dakota State, and Volunteer Fire Department personnel responded to a fire in Coal Canyon on the Black Hills National Forest, South Dakota. During initial attack, the Incident Commander formulated a plan: use hose lay and hand line to work up from the heel on the right flank, use the helicopter to make bucket drops along the left flank. As additional resources arrived, the IC, perceiving the increasing complexity, requested a type 3 organization through dispatch. Shortly after, as fire behavior increased and compromised an egress route, fire entrapped and overran firefighters attempting escape. Firefighter Trampus Haskvitz died, two others received serious burns, and two received minor burns. Two firefighters were entrapped in the engine; one remained entrapped and died; the other escaped. The third firefighter, who was overrun by fire while on foot, was transported to a Greeley, Colorado Burn Center.

incidents.name: Coal Canyon Fire 320 Road Entrapment 2011
incidents.summary: August 12, during burnout operations on Division Zulu, firefighters experienced a sudden increase in fire behavior and were forced to implement entrapment avoidance procedures that resulted in no injuries to personnel. During the event a crew vehicle caught on fire and sustained significant damage to the rear of the vehicle.
incidents.quote: Just after 1500, the wall of flames crests the ridge. Fire behavior is explosive and erratic with over 100 foot flame lengths. Several fire whirls are generated as the burnout meets the main fire. The winds are strong enough to blow one crewmember’s hardhat off. The Crew Boss suddenly realizes that the operation has now shifted from an offensive tactic of burning out ahead of the fire, to a defensive tactic of firing out good black for the crew to step into if necessary.

incidents.name: Peter's Ridge FLA
incidents.summary: At 1757, the injured jumper was transferred to the local medical evacuation ship, and successfully transported to the hospital where he was treated.
incidents.quote: At 1345, dispatch was notified that there was an injured smokejumper in need of medical attention on the Peter’s Ridge incident, but that it was not life threatening.

incidents.name: Jones Creek ATV Rollover
incidents.summary: The operator was able to jump off of the ATV as it began to roll. No individuals were injured in this incident.
incidents.quote: They began driving through a narrow switchback along the trail when the first ATV’s right front tire nudged a rock on the right side of the trail causing the ATV to slide to the left of the trail and the edge to give way. The ATV then proceeded to roll down a steep drainage approximately 80 feet.

incidents.name: Snow Gate Tree Incident
incidents.summary: His injuries consisted of a broken scapula, two broken ribs, two fractured vertebrae and a sprained ankle.
incidents.quote: During the initial attack phase, a firefighter was struck by a burning snag during line construction activities.

incidents.name: Motor Fire Log Bucking Incident
incidents.summary: All five people suffered bumps and bruises. One person suffered cuts to the head and twisted a knee (person who tried to stop log from rolling).
incidents.quote: During direct fireline construction on an active portion of the Motor wildfire a sawyer on a type 2IA Handcrew partially bucked a log that when stepped on by a fellow firefighter caused it to break free and roll down hill and hit 4 people.

incidents.name: ATV Fatality
incidents.summary: While operating at the scene of an outdoor fire, Firefighter Meyers passed away from injuries sustained when, according to state police, he lost control of the ATV he was operating and crashed into the front of a Texas Parks and Wildlife pickup truck at a roadway intersection.

incidents.name: Salt Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: At the same time, the tractor of a dozer transport was burned over and a lowboy trailer on a second transport was damaged. No injuries were sustained.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1800 hours a dozer operator and transport driver deployed a fire shelter during operations in support of the Salt Fire.

incidents.name: Nasty Fire Hoist
incidents.summary: He had only recently discovered that he was allergic to bee stings several weeks prior when he had an anaphylactic reaction and was rushed to the hospital for treatment.
incidents.quote: At 1550, the squad boss trainee from squad 2 called the crew boss on the radio and announced that squad 2’s squad boss had been stung by a bee.

incidents.name: Mother Lode Fire
incidents.summary: The eight firefighters moved away from the fire area and cleared a landing zone. They were successfully evacuated from the fire.
incidents.quote: After the crew shuttle and gear back haul was complete, five helitack and three rappellers were forced to evacuate the helispot; fire activity picked up significantly.

incidents.name: Rock Creek RX Entrapment
incidents.summary: The crewmember was transported to an emergency room at the local hospital and then to a regional burn center, where he spent two days and one night and was released after treatment for second degree burns on his hands and face.
incidents.quote: During the entrapment, he had deployed his shelter, run through an actively burning area to reach the road and sustained first and second degree burns to his hands, face and legs.

incidents.name: Pagami Creek Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Four others deployed fire shelters on a small island. Two others were picked up by floatplane, just as the approaching fire changed course. All survived without major injury.
incidents.quote: Shortly before noon, eight forest personnel were fleeing from fire. Two abandoned their canoe and sought refuge in the lake, sharing a single fire shelter.

incidents.name: Ozena Lightning Strike Injuries
incidents.fire: Mount Pinos Ranger District Lightning Plan
incidents.summary: Evaluation from medical personnel found the chief complaints were: tingling in arms, dizziness, disoriented, burned hair on arms, headache, and feeling strange.
incidents.quote: The engine operator was momentarily blinded by the flash. Within seconds he was able to focus and observed his Captain and crew on the ground.

incidents.name: WCT Compartment Syndrome
incidents.summary: After day two of major leg pain, the employee was diagnosed with “Compartment Syndrome.” The condition required surgery to remove dead tissue in the patient’s lower left leg.
incidents.quote: On lap 10¾ (out of 12 total laps), one individual collapsed and complained of leg pain.

incidents.name: Schoolhouse Chainsaw Injury
incidents.summary: On September 23, 2011 at 1300 hours, an inmate firefighter suffered a serious thigh laceration from a chainsaw kickback in Redwood National Park, California. Attempting to push a pinched tree off a saw bar, the sawyer throttle triggered a rotational kickback into the helper, who lacked saw PPE.
incidents.quote: The inmate firefighter sustained a serious deep laceration to his upper left thigh region.

incidents.name: Crystal Lake Tree Felling
incidents.summary: The instructor who was struck by the tree was evaluated and released the same night, the sawyer was uninjured.
incidents.quote: As the team was escaping from the felling tree the instructor was hit by a large branch of the tree and suffered 36 stitches to the ear area and six stitches to the back of the head.

incidents.name: Davies Creek Ridge Heli-Mission FLA
incidents.summary: The crash resulted in no injuries but was, nevertheless, a very serious accident.
incidents.quote: On a remote mountain top on the Tongass National Forest, a helicopter overturned with a Forest Service employee and a contract pilot onboard.

incidents.name: Chihuahua3 Firefighter Collapse
incidents.summary: On Oct 2, 2011, an inmate firefighter with Puerta La Cruz Crew 3 collapsed with heat illness during mop-up on the Chihuahua3 Fire in San Diego County. Contributory factors included pre-incident dehydration, light meals, and concurrent OTC/prescription medications for poison oak; she was medevacked via Mercy Air.
incidents.quote: After approximately two hours on the fire line, one Fire Crew Member (FCM) collapsed on the fire line presenting an altered level of consciousness.

incidents.name: Lower Sheep RX Escape
incidents.summary: Following policy, a wildfire was declared on the morning of October 3. Eventually, an area of about 100 acres of National Forest land was burned outside of the planned burn block.
incidents.quote: Spot fires outside of the northern edge of this burn started in the afternoon, and while initial efforts to contain these spot fires were successful, subsequent spot fires continued to spread on a steep, forested slope.

incidents.name: Alice Lake Canoe Incident
incidents.summary: As a result, three firefighters were totally immersed in cold water and exposed to hypothermic conditions for a period of approximately 25 minutes until they were rescued by floatplane.
incidents.quote: An incident occurred that resulted in a motorized canoe being swamped in the middle of a large lake within the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness.

incidents.name: Prospect Rock ATV FLA
incidents.summary: The rider jumped off to the left, striking his shoulder on the ground, sustaining a broken collarbone.
incidents.quote: Before reaching the top of the grade, the ATV began to tip over backwards after striking a rock with a front tire.

incidents.name: SQF Tree Cutting Injury
incidents.summary: The employee turned away as the tree made contact to his back causing a contusion and scrapes to his posterior left upper quadrant with immediate loss of breath. He was taken to the emergency room of the hospital where we was placed on light duty for 6 weeks.
incidents.quote: As the second cut was being made, the bind released and one end of the 10” tree swung towards the employee.

incidents.name: Truck Rolls Down Hill
incidents.summary: Employees on scene verified that the vehicle was still in gear and the brake set after it had impacted the tree. There were no injuries.
incidents.quote: The truck rolled off the edge and downhill approx. 10-15 feet. The center of the tailgate impacted an oak tree. From the time the employees exited the vehicle to the time it rolled was between 10-20 seconds.

incidents.name: California RX Wind Event
incidents.summary: By December 7th, the wind event had abated. No Forest Service prescribed fire escapes were reported and wildland fires within these forest’s DPA’s were controlled.
incidents.quote: In late November and early December of 2011, the Pacific Southwest Region experienced a significant high wind event, which challenged National Forests that had ongoing prescribed fires.

incidents.name: Corte Madera Ranch VMP Burn Helicopter Incident
incidents.summary: At approximately 1015 hours, Copter 10 arrived over the southwest edge of the burn plot and was instructed via radio to use rotor wash to put some wind on a specific area of the perimeter to help get the fire established in the standing vegetation. Copter 10 approached from the southwest, facing due north, as they neared the area burning. Copter 10 hovered approximately 40 feet west of the fireline and 40 feet above ground level (AGL), for approximately 40-60 seconds. During the hover maneuver, the ground fire intensity in the windrows increased dramatically, from estimated vertical flame lengths of 5-10 feet to horizontal flame lengths in excess of 35-40 feet, igniting standing vegetation and resulting in a growing fire towards the interior of the burn plot.
incidents.quote: San Diego County Sheriff’s helicopter Copter 10 recieved heat/fire damage, while assisting CAL FIRE and San Diego County Fire Authority ground resources on the Corte Madera Ranch Vegetation Management Program (VMP) burn in southeast San Diego County.

incidents.name: Training Hike Fatality
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, January 4, 2012, at approximately 3:45 PM, near the conclusion of a crew training hike, a 54 year old Inmate Firefighter Trainee collapsed. The injured Inmate Firefighter Trainee was transported by ambulance to a local hospital where he was later pronounced dead.
incidents.quote: Shortly thereafter, the Training Crew Swamper advised the Fire Captain that the trainee's condition was getting worse. The Fire Captain reassessed the trainee and noticed his level of consciousness had deteriorated. Several minutes later the trainee became unconscious and pulseless. CPR was initiated immediately by the Training Crew Swamper and the Fire Captain.

incidents.name: Lawler Retardant Avoidance Area FLA
incidents.summary: “I couldn’t see the drops, so no; I couldn’t tell how far the drift was”.
incidents.quote: “My [avoidance area] map was not with me, it was at my office to add the new map inserts which included the new avoidance area.”

incidents.name: Forest Health Piles Escape RX
incidents.summary: As the fire began to spread by means of spotting from log-to-log, the burn team worked diligently to contain the spots. Buffeted by wind gusts in excess of 35 mph during the afternoon and evening, the fire burned approximately 3.5 acres of private property.
incidents.quote: As the threeperson burn team completed ignition around noon, the relative humidity dropped rapidly while brisk westerly winds developed.

incidents.name: Apple Incident Airtanker Drop Injury
incidents.summary: A Fire Apparatus Engineer assigned to an engine was approximately 50’-60’ downhill from the ridgeline near the flank of the fire. The FAE acknowledged the notification of incoming air drops. An air tanker then came over the ridge and began its drop run . The FAE saw the air tanker at the last second and discarded his tool but was unable to get into the proper safety position for the drop. He was struck by the drop causing him to roll approximately 50’-60’ feet down the steep slope.
incidents.quote: A Helitack Fire Captain was acting as a lookout and notified all personnel operating in the area that airtankers were about to make air drops.

incidents.name: Apalachicola Unit 208 Escape
incidents.summary: It escaped containment and was declared the Grand Bay Fire on February 12, 2012.
