incidents.quote: The Burn Unit 208 Rx was completed on the Wakulla Ranger District of the Apalachicola National Forest on January 28, 2012.

incidents.name: Southern Region Prescribed Fire Review
incidents.summary: In addition to the local review, the Southern Region took this opportunity to assign a Review Team to assess the current drought conditions as they relate to prescribed fire control difficulties. The Review Team documented local and regional measures being implemented by fire managers and Line Officers to mitigate elevated risk associated with drought conditions. In addition, the Review Team assessed other escapes and near misses and the degree to which the Southern Region has adopted a "learning culture" and "shared risk management" in the prescribed fire program.
incidents.quote: The burn was ignited on Jan. 28. The project’s objectives were achieved and the burn had remained within the unit, exhibiting little activity. Sometime between the evening of Feb. 12 and the morning of the Feb. 13, strong winds and low RH caused smoldering organic soils to flareup and burn into an adjacent swamp.

incidents.name: Work Capacity Test Heart Attack
incidents.summary: Approximately 100-meters short of the 2.5 mile marker of the work capacity test, one of the participants suddenly fell forward and landed face down on the pavement. The medic was approximately 100-meters in front of the victim and was at the victim’s side within seconds. The medic assessed the situation and immediately called for assistance on the radio. The medic advised that the victim was in “full arrest.” CPR was started immediately and 911 dispatch was notified via the 800 MHz radio. The medic hooked up an AED and intubated the victim.
incidents.quote: Had the established protocols not been in place, had the medic not been on scene, had there not been good communication established, and had the employees of Prophetstown State Park not managed this situation correctly the victim would have died.

incidents.name: Drip Torch Malfunction RLS
incidents.summary: We were on a large wildfire yesterday where we needed to do a significant burnout and one of our drip torches would not flow fuel. It acted clogged, but when we disassembled, air flowed freely through every part. When we grabbed it yesterday, the fuel tube was slightly loose in the brass disk/cap, so it was hand tightened. Disassembled, everything flowed, but assembled, it wouldn't work.
incidents.quote: When did you last test your drip torches?

incidents.name: Lower North Fork Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The Lower North Fork Prescribed Fire Project, located south of Conifer, Colo., is part of a large scale restoration effort on Denver Water property. Colorado State Forest Service (CSFS) planned the project to consist of six units. The 50 acre Unit 4A is one of the units identified for prescribed fire application following mastication treatments. On Thursday, March 22, 2012, Unit 4A was ignited according to plan. Ignition was completed by 2000 that evening. On Friday, March 23, crews worked to secure the burn and by the end of the day, the prescribed fire was put into patrol/monitor status. To this point in time operations were completed according to the plan with no problems. On Monday March 26, 2012, a three-­person crew was monitoring the Unit during a “red flag warning”. At approximately 1315 winds carried a stream of ground level embers across the established prescribed fire control line. At 1430 it was converted to a wildfire.
incidents.quote: A complex series of winds resulted in two spot fires outside control lines that were quickly contained by mop­‐up/ patrol personnel on scene. The crew responded to a third spot fire at 1340 located approximately 1500 feet southeast down the control line from the two earlier contained spot fires. The new spot fire quickly became established and it exceeded the capacity for control by ground forces resulting in an escape and subsequent conversion to a wildfire at 1430.

incidents.name: Cottonwood Escaped Prescribed Fire FLA
incidents.summary: Three and one half hours after igniting a successful test burn, the Burn Boss declared the Cottonwood Prescribed Burn to be a wildfire and assumed his new role as Incident Commander (IC).
incidents.quote: Light winds blew across the fireline and carried flying embers into the surrounding old-growth chaparral, landed in dry tinder, and sprang into a spot fire located outside the project boundary.

incidents.name: Camp 14 PT Fatality
incidents.summary: Upon returning to Fire Camp 14, it was determined that the Captain had not returned and a search operation was immediately initiated. The Captain was found on the hiking trail in cardiac arrest at approximately 1055 hours. Rescue efforts were initiated and additional resources were requested through Dispatch.
incidents.quote: On April 3, 2012, a Fire Captain working as a fire crew supervisor, suffered cardiac arrest while participating in a routine morning physical training hike with his crew. The Captain was pronounced dead at the hospital.

incidents.name: Crowl Road Fire Burnover
incidents.summary: The initial responding dozer/plow units (Jax-53 and Jax-57) became stuck in a wet area. Jax-53 became stuck first and Jax-57 came to assist. After an unsuccessful attempt to free Jax-53, Jax-57 also became stuck. As the fire was encroaching, the firefighters made the decision to leave the units on foot, taking their fire shelters with them. Neither firefighter had their portable radio and as a result, communications were lost for approximately 15 minutes until the two firefighters were found by Clay County Fire Department Personnel after making their way to safety. There were no injuries as a result of this event; however, substantial damage was caused to the internal engine of Jax-53.
incidents.quote: On April 7, 2012 from approximately 1555 hours to 1610 hours, two Florida Forest Service firefighters were involved in a burnover while operating enclosed cab medium dozer/plow units to suppress a wildfire.

incidents.name: Wyoming County Dept Firefighter Fatality
incidents.summary: Other firefighters in the vehicle were able to get control of the truck and bring it to a safe stop. Longo was treated and transported to the hospital but passed away from his injury several days later.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Longo was driving a squad truck to the fire station to pick up a brush truck in response to a grass fire when he suffered a fatal stroke.

incidents.name: Expedition Fire Burned Dozer
incidents.summary: The fire plow itself sustained no damage resulting from either fire. The operator was not injured.
incidents.quote: During initial attack operations an engine compartment fire in a tractor/plow unit thatwas building line resulted in a total loss of the equipment.

incidents.name: Coyote Basin Chainsaw Injury
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, May 9, 2012 at approximately 1845 hrs, a BLM engine crewmember (Swamper) was injured during suppression operations on a mutual aid fire with Moffat County. During the construction of saw line Swamper reached to deflect falling brush from hitting the sawyer. In the motion his right leg made contact with the bar of the chainsaw.
incidents.quote: The swamper, standing just below and to the left noticed the falling oak, and in an attempt to protect the sawyer, stepped uphill and reached to deflect the brush.

incidents.name: Gladiator Fire Near Miss
incidents.summary: While disengaging, the three crewmembers made the decision to discard tools and line gear due to poor visibility, smoky conditions, steep terrain and a perceived imminent threat to life. After discarding their line gear the three crew members continued up the handline with fire shelters, hand tools, and PPE to the safety zone uninjured.
incidents.quote: While conducting a firing operation, three members of a Type II IA Handcrew retreated along their escape route towards their identified safety zone due to an increase in fire behavior and a shift in wind direction.

incidents.name: Snake Bite LA County
incidents.summary: The Fire Crew Supervisor gave the crew their assignment to clear grass and brush from the roadside and conducted a safety briefing with the crew. At approximately 1115 hours a crewmember was bitten by a rattlesnake while swinging his McLeod in the grass.
incidents.quote: During a reflexive attempt to remove the rattlesnake from his finger with his left hand, the snake bit his left middle finger.

incidents.name: Minden P2V Landing Incident
incidents.summary: After circling the airfield and several unsuccessful attempts to get the left main gear to extend, the pilots declared an emergency and used emergency procedures to configure the aircraft for landing. The were no injuries to the pilot or co-pilot.
incidents.quote: A Lockheed P2V-7 made an emergency landing at Minden-Tahoe Airport, Minden, Nevada.

incidents.name: White Rock Air Tanker Fatalities
incidents.summary: Both pilots were fatally injured. The airplane was substantially damaged by impact forces and a post crash fire.
incidents.quote: A Lockheed P2V-7, N14447 (using call sign Tanker 11), collided with mountainous terrain while conducting firefighting operations 20 miles north of Modena, Utah.

incidents.name: Box Creek Escaped RX
incidents.summary: A few days later the fire had burned an additional 668 acres and had exceeded the project area. Managers determined that they would not be able to control the fire outside the project area by the end of the next burning period and declared a wildfire at 2200 on June 4.
incidents.quote: The fire spotted out of the test fire stand. By the time nightfall had stopped the fire’s spread, it had covered an area of approximately 194 acres, moving roughly one mile from the test fire site.

incidents.name: Sunflower Felling Incident
incidents.summary: At about 30 feet away, he glances over his right shoulder—to see the tree coming at him. Before he can reach the road at the end of his escape route, he is struck in the head with a glancing blow on the right side of his hard hat, followed by a strike to the right arm.
incidents.quote: “I had this feeling come over me, like something was going to happen.”

incidents.name: Montezuma Fire Rollover Fatality
incidents.summary: One passenger was pronounced dead on the scene. The driver and other passenger were taken to the Sells Hospital with non-life threatening injuries and were later released.
incidents.quote: At approximately 8:00 AM this morning, three firefighters working on the Montezuma Fire currently burning in the Baboquivari Mountains west of Tucson, were involved in a single vehicle rollover while en route to the fire.

incidents.name: 257 Fire Rhabdo RLS
incidents.summary: He was flown to a Level 1 trauma center where he was diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis (Rhabdo).
incidents.quote: A Hotshot captain was scouting line when he eventually decided to hike back to the crew vehicles. But the cramps became worse and eventually necessitated a medical evacuation.

incidents.name: Arizona Strip Heat Stroke
incidents.summary: Upon completion of the PTR one of the crew members began to express that he was feeling poorly. The crew member was assisted back to one of the module vehicles at which time his condition appeared to deteriorate.The crew member was driven to the hospital and admitted for treatment. Upon examination the attending physician determined that the crew member had developed heat stroke and was treated accordingly.
incidents.quote: On June 15, 2012 crew members from two modules were in a structured group physical training run (PTR) on the Virgin River bike trail in St.George,Utah.

incidents.name: Compartment 7 Escaped RX
incidents.summary: A couple days later, the District Ranger, DFMO, and Burn Boss take a reconnaissance flight over fire: fire is now 2800 acres and was converted to a wildfire.
incidents.quote: A reconnaissance flight was conducted at the end of the day after ignitions. Aerial observations indicated all control lines were holding and no other issues were noted.

incidents.name: North Schell Escaped RX
incidents.summary: Once the ignition area began to grow in intensity, short-range spotting started to occur, spreading fire brands below the main fire—encouraging downhill fire spread. Southwest winds continued to increase and encourage downhill fire spread until the RX was declared a wildfire days later.
incidents.quote: The prescription called for high-intensity crown fire to consume the fir trees. A test fire was conducted on June 9 using hand-ignition in an isolated stand about 20 acres in size.

incidents.name: Poco Fire Dozer Incident
incidents.summary: Finding only minor superficial damages, the dozer was started, removed from the site inspected for damage and transported back to the home unit for further assessment and repair.
incidents.quote: Due to rapidly escalating fire activity in steep terrain, the Dozer Operator and the Heavy Equipment Boss Trainee abandoned the Forest Service agency dozer.

incidents.name: Circle Meadow RX Hit By Snag Injury
incidents.summary: “I looked up, saw the snag falling in my direction, and instinctively lunged back and to the left. The snag hit somewhere behind and below me,” recalls the Resource Advisor. The “pole-sized” snag fell and hit the large log. The top several feet of the snag broke off. This broken section was three to four inches in diameter and two to three feet long. When the Resource Advisor sat up, he realized there was a problem with his ankle. His foot was twisted at an odd angle. To both crewmembers, it looked like the tree had struck the Resource Advisor and sent him tumbling down the hill. One of the crewmembers called out and asked if he was OK. There was not an immediate response. Eventually, the Resource Advisor said that he had a broken ankle.
incidents.quote: Someone yelled: “Tree!” (Everyone agrees that someone yelled it, but no one can remember doing it.)

incidents.name: Clay Springs Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: An engine burn over occurred during initial attack, on the Clay Springs fire, a 107,000 acre fire, reported June 27, 2012 at 14:15 hours, south of Oak City, Utah. The driver suffered second degree burns on his left arm and on both ears. The first nozzle man suffered second degree burns on his entire face, arms, left hand, buttocks and back of his right leg. The second nozzle man also suffered second degree burns to part of his face, elbow, buttocks and backs of both legs. His nomex pants were burned to a brown color down the backs of his legs. After transport to the local hospital in Delta, UT, the two nozzle men were flown by helicopter to the burn center in the University of Utah Medical Center in Salt Lake City Utah. The driver declined treatment at the burn center and received care from the local hospital.

incidents.name: Battery Caused Engine Fire
incidents.summary: The engine operator turned to see flames coming from the back of the engine. He pulled over and started to throw things off the engine, including: cots, ice chest, and gas can. But the fire wouldn’t stop until a responsive crewmember—from the crew transport vehicle responded with a 10-pound chemical fire extinguisher—and put out the fire. Upon arrival, Safety Officer Mervin Lent noted fire scars on the engine bed, water tank, and gas can. He asked the engine operator to replace all the equipment back onto the engine—in their original positions prior to the fire. It was determined that while driving down the dirt road, the cover had bounced off the battery. The cot then made repeated contact with the battery terminal and the gasoline can. This created two small openings in the gas can allowing fumes and liquid gas to escape from the tank and ignite from the arching.
incidents.quote: Several crewmembers were waving and yelling: “Stop! You’re on fire!”

incidents.name: White Draw Fire MAFFS Fatalities
incidents.summary: "Additionally, I find by the preponderance of evidence, the failure of the White Draw Fire Lead Plane aircrew and Air Attack aircrew to communicate critical operational information; and conflicting operational guidance concerning thunderstorm avoidance, substantially contributed to the mishap."
incidents.quote: "I find by clear and convincing evidence the cause of the mishap was MPl, MP2, MN and ME's inadequate assessment of operational conditions, resulting in the MA impacting the ground after flying into a microburst."

incidents.name: Engine Tire Blowout RLS
incidents.summary: The engine immediately pulled to the left. But the driver was able to safely negotiate the engine to the right shoulder of the road.
incidents.quote: While traveling at a speed of 62 mph, with three firefighters on board, the left front tire on this Type 4 Engine blows out.

incidents.name: Unit 233 RX Entrapment
incidents.summary: The firefighter shook out his shelter but did not enter it. No injuries were sustained.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1620 hours a firefighter from the firing team became entrapped and removed his fire shelter from its case during firing operations.

incidents.name: Salmon Challis NF UTV Accident
incidents.summary: When the UTV hit the transition between two surfaces, where there was also a small dip in the surface, it began to tip to the driver’s side. The crew member instinctively stuck his leg out of the UTV to the ground, to help prevent the UTV from tipping. The rollbar hit the crew member's lower leg.
incidents.quote: The crew member got out of the tipped UTV and did not immediately realize that he had been injured, until he looked down and saw that his left foot was sticking out at an odd angle.

incidents.name: Flat Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: The five engine crewmembers were able to make it to safety with no injuries.
incidents.quote: “I went into survival mode.” “30 feet from the road, our path to the road was blocked by heat and flame.”

incidents.name: Lighthouse Fire Tree Felling RLS
incidents.summary: While working in a cottonwood stand, a Class C Faller began to prepare to fall a tree by bucking out logs in the escape route. The sawyer decided to take a second look at the tree to be felled and perceived small cracks they had not previously noticed. The tree suddenly began to break, and personnel moved away from the area. From a safe distance they watched the tree fail and crash to the ground.
incidents.quote: Then I noticed that the charred bark pattern had a different pattern—hairline cracks like a cracked pane of glass. Before my eyes, the black hairline cracks gave way and grew to reveal white, unburned wood underneath. I knew that the tree was about to fall.

incidents.name: Engine Night Driving RLS
incidents.summary: After the vehicle came to rest, the driver set the air brake, shut off the engine, and exited the vehicle.
incidents.quote: Due to low visibility, the driver didn’t see see that the bank had a cut back. The front driver’s side wheel went over the edge

incidents.name: Forest Incident Heat Injuries
incidents.summary: Two hours after initial dispatch, two firefighters experienced a heat related illness. Approximately two hours later, a third firefighter experienced signs and symptoms of a heat related illness. By 8:00 P.M., a total of five firefighters were treated for heat related illnesses. Two of the firefighters were transported to local hospitals via air ambulance, one by ground, and the remainder treated and released at scene.
incidents.quote: On Saturday, July 21, 2012 at approximately 10:11 am, CAL FIRE units were dispatched to a vegetation fire near the community of Guinda in north western Yolo County. During the initial attack operations, multiple firefighters experienced heat related signs and symptoms.

incidents.name: Ash Creek Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The dozer was working with two hotshot personnel trying to flank a section of the fire that had slopped over control lines when the wind direction changed pushing the fire towards the dozer.
incidents.quote: A dozer operator sustained burns on his face, nose, ear and the right hand while working directly on the fire’s edge.

incidents.name: Ash Creek Fire ATV Accident
incidents.summary: The DIVS was traveling up a dozer line when the ATV rolled backward, flipping over the top of him. Injuries included a broken clavicle and crack/bruised ribs.
incidents.quote: The DIVS on the most active part of the fire rolled an ATV while scouting the fire line.

incidents.name: Penn Fire POV Collision/Firefighter Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter was hit or run over by a vehicle on the Penn fire.

incidents.name: Turkey Incident Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: A CAL FIRE Prevention Officer was responding to the Turkey Incident on Whitesbridge Avenue, a two lane road near the community of Mendota. While attempting to gain access to the Incident, the Officer slowed and activated his rear facing amber lights. As the Officer was turning left onto the dirt access road his vehicle was struck by a civilian driver attempting to pass in the oncoming lane.
incidents.quote: Whitesbridge Avenue is heavily traveled daily by vehicles traveling from Mendota to Fresno California.

incidents.name: Mustang Fire Near Miss
incidents.summary: A few hours later, the four firefighters arrived at the LZ and called for a pick up.
incidents.quote: Seconds later, an independent crown fire swept through the canopy within the burned area and cut off egress to the ridge to the potential helispot for the ICT5(T).

incidents.name: Tree Felling Accident Solar Panel
incidents.summary: On the second tree the sawyer had a procedure in place, felling the tree upslope and away from the pump house, similar to that of the first tree. All the cutting was done from the uphill/ opposite side of the pump house. The tree had a slight lean in the desired direction although the majority of the limb weight was towards the pump house. With the tree being alive and green this added more weight than anticipated. The sawyer anticipated that the tree would begin to start falling, which didn’t happen since the weight of the limbs was pulling in a different direction. The sawyer continued cutting through the back cut and eventually through the majority of the holding wood. Once the holding wood was severed the weight of the limbs broke the remainder of the holding wood and the tree fell towards the pump house and solar panels on top.
incidents.quote: The sawyer felled the first tree in the desired direction, using a conventional face cut and then back cut.

incidents.name: Chips Fire Asbestos Hazard Mitigation
incidents.summary: The decision was made to stop the retrieval of suppression equipment (hose, pumps, tools) in the serpentine areas.
incidents.quote: A geologic map of the serpentine rock areas confirmed that some dozer and hand lines were constructed in these areas.

incidents.name: Elbow Pass Camp Illness
incidents.summary: An additional four cases were reported for a total of seven individuals. There was no evidence that the virus was ever spread through the kitchen or food, as all cases were directly tied to person-to-person contact. No additional cases were reported after the 7th, and all individuals that were sickened recovered within 24 hours of showing signs of infection.
incidents.quote: Samples from those sickened were sent to a lab, two of which ultimately tested positive for Norovirus G1.

incidents.name: Chips Fire Helicopter Rotor Blade Strike
incidents.summary: "The need to get water closest to the fire just isn't that great."
incidents.quote: A T1 helicopter experienced a main rotor-blade strike while descending into a new dip site.

incidents.name: Klamath Engine MVA
incidents.summary: "After the certified mechanic and I did a damage assessment investigation, we found the only damage was the petcock on the bottom of the pump was broken off."
incidents.quote: While enroute from one incident to another incident, the engine in the strike team hit a piece of the road that caused the back end to slide off the road.

incidents.name: Lanes Fire Water Tender Runaway Rollover
incidents.summary: A private water tender assigned to the Lanes Fire was involved in a solo vehicle accident near the intersection of Auberry Road and Beal Road within Fresno County. CAL FIRE personnel responded to the accident location where they found the water tender overturned, approximately 219 feet below Beal Road. The driver was not injured and the vehicle sustained major damage
incidents.quote: While the driver was outside of the vehicle, the unoccupied water tender rolled away from the driver, over an embankment and overturned several times.

incidents.name: Steep Corner Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: The cause of this accident was that a green cedar tree, weakened by fire, fell and struck a firefighter in the head. It fell with a force far greater than the design limits of any hardhat could withstand.
incidents.quote: “Snag falling!” Kerry yells as he sees a tree across the creek falling toward them. Everyone scatters; some firefighters run downhill while Kerry and Anne run uphill.

incidents.name: Wye Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: While a firing operation was in progress a spot fire occurred. A hand crew attempted to suppress the spot fire; however, the firing operation was unsuccessful due to fire behavior. While retreating to their safety zone, an inmate firefighter assigned to the hand crew sustained first degree burns to his face.

incidents.name: Buck Incident Air Tanker Drop Injury
incidents.summary: At the time of incident, the crewmembers were scouting on foot to determine the best access to their assignment. As they turned to walk back to the engine, the Fire Apparatus Engineer and one Firefighter were struck from behind and knocked to the ground by the force of the retardant released by a passing air tanker. The Crewmembers involved did not see or hear the air tanker until moments prior to impact.
incidents.quote: A CAL FIRE/Riverside County Fire Department type III fire engine and two of the three crewmembers, were struck by retardant dropped from a CAL FIRE air tanker.

incidents.name: Buck Incident Fatality
incidents.summary: While California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation Officers were waking up the crews to prepare them for the day’s assignment, an inmate firefighter was discovered to be unresponsive. The officers immediately called 911 from a cell phone. The call was transferred to the CAL FIRE/Riverside County Fire Department Emergency Command Center (ECC). The ECC then notified the Buck Fire Communications Unit of the emergency. The ECC dispatched an Advanced Life Support Ambulance to the scene.
incidents.quote: Evaluation and testing was performed at the local hospital to evaluate for dehydration and it was determined there was no dehydration or rhabdomyolysis.

incidents.name: Chips Fire Felling Injury
incidents.summary: The faller received 18 staples in the back of his head and was released the same day.
incidents.quote: The faller walked around the tree to retrieve his falling axe and began using it to remove a small portion of the wedge section still left in the undercut. He struck this small section four times and on the fifth strike a limb fell vertically striking the faller’s hard hat.

incidents.name: North Pass Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: The fire was running their direction from the south side burning over one of the engines while concurrently entrapping another engine forcing the crew to shelter-in-vehicle on the same dozer line. There were no injuries.
incidents.quote: In the late afternoon hours; the “bewitching hour,” as one strike team leader called it; embers from a burning oak tree, located in the black, spotted across the line and ran to the ridge top.

incidents.name: Trinity Ridge West Bucking Injuries
incidents.summary: Two injured firefighters sustained minor injuries and the third injured firefighter was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation and was released that same day.
incidents.quote: Three Bonneville Hotshot crewmembers were injured when a 24”dbh 40‘ long downed log broke free during bucking operations and rolled 40’ downhill towards three crewmembers, and one received blunt force trauma to the chest.

incidents.name: Bagley Fire Tree Strike Injury
incidents.summary: The patient received staples to the head lacerations and required surgery to repair a broken should blade. The water tender did receive major damage to the front of the vehicle.
incidents.quote: It was determined the cause of the debris was a snag that fell well interior, then hit a green tree that ended up falling at the draft site, resulting in the impact with the water tender and then eventually striking the day driver.

incidents.name: Trinity Ridge Driving Incident
incidents.summary: Once he feels everything is all right he gets out of the vehicle and calmly radios back to ICP that there had been an accident but no injuries.
incidents.quote: Glass suddenly materializes all over him, tree limbs smash and go flying by and the vehicle comes to a slow stop.

incidents.name: Mustang Fire Rollover
incidents.summary: He recalls being pulled out of his pickup with people telling him he had rolled his vehicle and then he can remember being in the ambulance as he was transported to the hospital.
incidents.quote: On one particular corner, the dust was heavy in the air and the sun was at the perfect angle that as the last engine rounded the corner the sun shot straight into George’s eyes.

incidents.name: North Pass Fire Rotor Blade Strike
incidents.summary: After shut down was complete, the pilots inspected the main rotor-blade damage and noted that all 5 main blades incurred damage to the trailing edge about 18” inboard from the tip.
incidents.quote: As the water was released, the Second-in-Command heard/felt the blades strike the tree and immediately called for power and to pull up. As the Pilot-in-Command initiated a climb-out from the site, the pilots noted a “lateral shudder” in the aircraft.

incidents.name: Trinity Ridge Fire - 1st Degree Burn
incidents.summary: Upon arrival at ICP in the morning he went to the Medical Unit and was sent to a nearby hospital for examination.
incidents.quote: Kurt is unsure if it was the extreme heat or hot rocks or a combination of both but when the water hit the stump hole it erupted with a shower of “sludge”. This mixture of hot mud and water hit his ungloved hand (which was holding the hose) and he immediately felt pain.

incidents.name: Likely Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, September 5, 2012, at about 11:27 AM, two CAL FIRE Handcrews were dispatched from Intermountain Conservation Camp #22 on an initial attack assignment to a vegetation fire south of Likely, California. At approximately 2:00 PM, the lead handcrew was constructing direct handline when the fire behavior suddenly increased during a wind shift. As the majority of the crew retreated into the black, three inmates found their escape route blocked by the advancing flame front. The inmates passed through the flame front into the black where they sustained first degree and some minor spots of second degree burns to their faces. The inmate firefighters were transported via ground ambulance to Modoc Medical Center where they were treated and released for minor burns.
incidents.quote: The lead handcrew was constructing direct handline when the fire behavior suddenly increased during a wind shift.

incidents.name: Bagley Fire Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: The driver suffered no injuries and was wearing his seatbelt.
incidents.quote: After driving the water tender over a log and causing the water to start shifting, this caused the water tender to roll onto its passenger side, and come to rest on the side of the road.

incidents.name: Engine Burned on Flint Canyon Fire
incidents.summary: At approximately 1840 hours, E3462 from the Idaho Falls District Bureau of Land Management (BLM) was overtaken by flames and destroyed while engaged in fire operations on the Flint Canyon Fire near Rockland, Idaho. E3462 was a total loss. No injuries resulted from this incident.
incidents.quote: While the crew was engaged in fire suppression efforts, a crew member spotted smoke in the vicinity of the engine.

incidents.name: Brush 18 Engine Fire
incidents.summary: Div W radioed to Operations and relayed that there was an engine engulfed in flames on his division, there were no injuries, and everyone was safe and accounted for.
incidents.quote: As the crewmember with the saw set it down in the black, he turned around to find fire on the ground on the east side of the truck.

incidents.name: Mustang Fire Security Rollover
incidents.summary: He slowly pulled himself out of the vehicle and checked for injuries and was later examined by a paramedic and made notifications.
incidents.quote: The vehicle almost came to a stop, Shawn had a brief thought of “Thank Goodness” and then the vehicle slowly tilted to the right and rolled over.

incidents.name: Scotts Fire Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: A private water tender assigned to the Scotts Fire was involved in a solo vehicle accident. The water tender was driving on a dirt road and left the road above a steep gully. The water tender went over an embankment and overturned.
incidents.quote: As the driver approached the turn, he was talking on his cellular phone.

incidents.name: North Pass Driving Incident
incidents.summary: The crew was traveling in a crew-cab pickup with 5 crew members in the truck. There were a few vehicles ahead of the truck, as well as a few behind them. There was a lot of dust in the air from the crew’s vehicle. The crew representative stated that it appeared certain areas of the road had received less dust abatement than others. The driver of the vehicle stated that the vehicle was traveling 5-10 mph andthey had their seatbelts on. They slowed down due to a cattle guard and a sun/shade transition. Theythen accelerated forward and estimated there was 5-10 feet of visibility. The driver missed the corner ahead and the truck went over the edge. He applied the brakes the whole time but the hill was so steep they did not stop the truck.
incidents.quote: The roads in the area have many sharp corners, and heavy fire traffic during the incident made them very dusty.

incidents.name: Halstead Fire Sepsis
incidents.summary: Jim was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), where he stayed for two days and was later released.
incidents.quote: Jim had been diagnosed with pneumonia and sepsis, and was suffering from septic shock. The doctor’s assessment was that the blood poisoning was caused by pneumonia.

incidents.name: Wenatchee Complex Cardiac Arrest Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Chris Seelye, under contract with the USDA Forest Service, suffered a medical emergency while battling the Wenatchee Complex Fire. Firefighter Seelye was treated by incident medical personnel and rushed to a nearly hospital where he passed away later that evening.
incidents.quote: Chris knew what he was doing and he died doing what he loved. The world is short a great man

incidents.name: Gold Pass Fire Snag Incident RLS
incidents.summary: After the area had been snagged by three sawyers, a firefighter was told to mop-up the top of the fire below the road. As he was working the top lateral, he was struck from behind by the top of a four-inch DBH snag. In pain and shaken, the firefighter walked to the top of the road under his own power. He reported the incident to the Incident Commander. He complained of a headache, pain in his left forearm, and feeling a little nauseated.
incidents.quote: The snag hit his hardhat—knocking it off—and struck his left forearm. The force of the impact knocked the firefighter to the ground.

incidents.name: Dagsboro VFD Driving Fatality
incidents.summary: Dagsboro Volunteer Fire Department was dispatched for an outside fire in a wooded area on East Clogg Drive just outside town limits.
incidents.quote: While en route to Station 73 in a personal vehicle, Junior Firefighter Townsend was fatally injured in a motor vehicle crash.

incidents.name: Pole Creek Bucket Extraction
incidents.summary: Believing the TFLD’s position was being compromised by a change in fire behavior, the pilot encouraged the TFLD to climb into the helicopter bucket and flew him to a safe location approximately one-half mile away from the fire edge.
incidents.quote: As the pilot hovered and watched the speed of the fire coming toward the TFLD, the pilot said “I’m going to suggest something to you and I hope you do it. I want you to get in the bucket.”

incidents.name: Milepost 66 Ropes Incident
incidents.summary: Crew member #2 was bleeding and had some deformity on the left side of his face. After he made it to the Highway, medical transport ensued and Crew member #2 was admitted to the Hood River County Hospital and later referred to Oregon Health Science University hospital for a more complete evaluation.
incidents.quote: Crew member #2 said, “I just got hit by a rock.” Crew member #3 called out to #2 a little later, “are you OK?”, received no response and started moving toward #2.

incidents.name: Saddle Rx Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter was injured while black lining a burn unit that contained a significant amount of blowdown.
incidents.quote: One of the individuals crawled over some blowdown with his driptorch, felt heat on his pants, and looked down to see that his lower left pant leg was on fire.

incidents.name: Wetmore Fire
incidents.summary: While assisting in evacuation of civilians in the Greenwood subdivision, a Battalion Chief, Captain, and several civilians dispersed throughout five vehicles were forced to take refuge in a safe area while the head of the fire passed by them. The safe area was situated on a gravel county road, surrounded by light fuels consisting of overgrazed pastures and isolated pockets of heavier fuels consisting of Ponderosa Pine and Pinion-Juniper.
incidents.quote: Weather conditions during the initial attack on Tuesday afternoon were clear skies, temps 75+ degrees with southwest winds 40-45 mph with gusts to 70 mph.

incidents.name: Spur Fire Stump Hole Incident
incidents.summary: The Fire Crew Captain with the help of another Crewmember dragged the incapacitated firefighter through the flame front into the black. The Captain received a superficial 1st degree burn from radiant heat to the left side of his face during the process of moving the firefighter.
incidents.quote: Just as the Captain has called his sawyers back, his attention is diverted. Crewmember 1, wearing his hard hat, trips and falls into a large stump hole from a previous fire.

incidents.name: Six Rivers Pile Burning Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A crew member suffered burns to the neck, ear, and face after accidentally falling into a burning hand-pile during a prescribed burn operation. Immediate response by the team included first aid and a swift transport to the hospital. Lessons learned emphasized the importance of safety protocols, pre-burn planning, and medical readiness. Recommendations included enhancing protective equipment and communication strategies to improve emergency response in such scenarios.
incidents.quote: The crew member immediately attempted to stand up while encountering heavy smoke and the helpless feeling of being unable to push themselves out of the pile.

incidents.name: Marbleyard Snag Incidents FLA
incidents.summary: The firefighter was assessed on scene by his co-workers and taken to the hospital for further evaluation. The firefighter was treated and released to full duty.
incidents.quote: The 8” dbh, 45’ tall locust snag became entangled in the tops of two other trees pulling them down on top of him slightly reducing the direct impact to his hard hat.

incidents.name: Haudenschild Driving Fatality
incidents.summary: Haudenschild was reportedly not wearing seat restraints and passed away at the scene of blunt force trauma due to the motor vehicle crash.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Haudenschild died from injuries sustained when the fire apparatus he was operating crashed as he was responding to a reported grass fire.

incidents.name: Washington Township FD Water Tender Rollover Fatality
incidents.summary: On November 11, 2012, a 26-year-old male volunteer fire fighter was killed when the tanker he was driving crashed en-route to a grass fire.
incidents.quote: He boarded the tanker and left the station with lights and siren activated. The apparatus crashed approximately five miles from the department. The Victim was ejected and suffered fatal injuries. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

incidents.name: Taos Crew Carrier Rollover
incidents.summary: One BLM employee and one USFS employee received serious, potentially life-threatening injuries. The USFS employee was transported by ambulance to the hospital in Taos, New Mexico. The BLM employee incurred an extended hospital stay, while the USFS employee was released two days following the incident.
incidents.quote: A loss of control occurred; the crew carrier began to roll and the passenger side front corner of the apparatus body (crew compartment) slammed into the asphalt. Next, the apparatus pitched forward, toppled end over end, and came to rest on the driver’s side on the east side of the highway.

incidents.name: Structure Firefighter Timothy Jansen Fatality
incidents.summary: Jansen was on the first fire apparatus to arrive at scene and was standing outside the vehicle when he was hit. Firefighter Jansen was taken to St. Joseph's Hospital in Breese, where he passed away from his injuries.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Jansen was struck and killed by a fire truck at the scene of a house fire.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Training Tree Injury
incidents.summary: At approximately 1340 hours, a Florida Forest Service Firefighter was struck in the head by a segment of a nearby dead snag that was connected, by vines, to the top of the tree that was being felled. The segment that fell and inflicted injury was approximately 20 feet long and 8 inches in diameter. FFS Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) were on scene and treated the Firefighter for head injuries, multiple abrasions and numbness to his right side. The Firefighter was rapidly airlifted to Bayonet Point Medical Center where he received surgery to fuse two vertebrae in his neck and was treated for a concussion and fractured orbital socket.
incidents.quote: As the Lookout observed this chain of events occurring, he noticed the snag behind them beginning to fall and gave a shout of warning to the crew located within the fall zone.

incidents.name: Pack Test Compartment Syndrome
incidents.summary: “‘Compartment Syndrome’ can lead to ‘Rhabdomyolysis,’ the breakdown of muscle fibers resulting in the release of muscle contents (myoglobin) into the bloodstream. These releases can cause multiple symptoms and, if left undiagnosed, can lead to kidney and muscle damage, and in rare cases, results can be fatal.”
incidents.quote: Due to the severity of the pain associated with this condition, it was difficult for Edward to walk. He says he could only “crawl around on the floor.”

incidents.name: Cowles Bog Tree Accident
incidents.summary: Firefighter A (injured firefighter) had finished cutting his third tree of the day and was in the process of “bucking it” when another tree north of where he was sawing, unexpectantly uprooted and fell. This tree struck Firefighter A across his shoulder knocking him to the ground. It was later determined his face had struck the edge of the chainsaw cowling between the chain brake and the handle. This resulted in a fracture of his nose, right eye orbit, and T-1 vertebrae.
incidents.quote: A 31-year old Wildland Firefighter was struck by a falling tree.

incidents.name: Schnepp Fatality
incidents.summary: A short time after fighting a brush fire Sunday evening, February 24, Firefighter Schnepp passed away from a cause still to be determined.

incidents.name: Makay Island NWR Fatality
incidents.summary: fMorrison was treated by fellow responders on scene and en route to a hospital where he passed away from his injury.
incidents.quote: Fire Chief Morrison was operating at the scene of a brush fire when he collapsed from an apparent heart attack.

incidents.name: Broz Driving Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Broz passed away from injuries sustained when his personally owned vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree while he was responding to an outdoor fire in the Francis Beidler Forest. Broz was reported to have been wearing seat restraints at the time of the accident.
incidents.quote: A volunteer firefighter was killed when his personally owned vehicle left the roadway and struck a tree while he was responding to a fire in the Francis Beidler Forest.

incidents.name: Scheuerer Fatality
incidents.summary: The accident apparently happened after the wind shifted causing heavy smoke from the controlled burn to reduce visibility on the road where Scheuerer was present. Firefighter Scheuerer did not survive the injuries he sustained when struck by the vehicle.
incidents.quote: While conducting a controlled burn in Hunterdon County with the New Jersey Forest Fire Service, Firefighter Scheuerer was struck and killed by a vehicle driven by a civilian.

incidents.name: Pasture 3B Escaped RX
incidents.summary: The escape rapidly progressed, assisted by topography, drought conditions, and increased winds. Additional resources were called to respond to the escaped fire. The Pasture 3B RX was declared a wildfire, renamed to Pautre fire, and burned a total of 10,679 acres.
incidents.quote: This was the first burn of the season and a test fire was initiated after the passing of a small rainy cell that morning.

incidents.name: Merritt Island Engine Accident
incidents.summary: At approximately 15:00, both engines were attempting to turn left into an entrance gate along the highway. Both engines slowed and used their left turn signal. As the Merritt Island engine was turning left, a civilian vehicle passed the trailing National Park Service engine and struck the Merritt Island engine on the driver’s side front fender, tire and bumper area of the engine. The driver of the Merritt Island engine said he looked in all mirrors prior to turning and never saw the civilian vehicle attempting to pass. No injuries occurred as a result of the accident.
incidents.quote: While patrolling and doing area familiarization for crews detailed to the Complex, a National Park Service Type VI engine was following a Merritt Island Type VI engine en route to the Beeline Units of the St. Johns NWR along State Rd 407.

incidents.name: Summit Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Firefighter 2 turned and crouched to shield himself away from the heat and flames. Simultaneously, he quickly moved into the burned area which was only a few feet away. After he retreated into the burned area, he met up with firefighter 1 and the engine. The captain told them they had less than a quarter tank of water left and that they needed to leave to get water. While they were getting water at a nearby hydrant off the fire line, firefighter 1 noticed the injuries to firefighter 2’s face and notified the captain. The captain made the notification to his fire line supervisor who in turn requested a medical response.
incidents.quote: During the operation, firefighter 2 observed that fire had crossed the dozer line approximately 300 feet behind the engine.

incidents.name: Springs Fire Fall
incidents.summary: While climbing up the bank, the firefighter began to slip in the duff layer. He reached out and grabbed a root from the tree. The root broke under the weight of the FEMT causing him to slide approximately 10 feet down the bank on his hands and feet, facing the bank. When he reached the bottom of the bank he was off balance and fell striking his head on a rock.
incidents.quote: The FEMT chose the steeper route without the poison oak.

incidents.name: Monument Springs Fatality
incidents.summary: After a little more than one hour from the time of the Crewmember’s collapse, resuscitation efforts were halted under the order of the physician with medical control.
incidents.quote: While on a hike in the Sacramento Mountains, a Crewmember from a Type 6 Engine collapsed and became unresponsive while ascending a hill in the Monument Canyon drainage.

incidents.name: Cactus Fire Rotor Strike
incidents.summary: "On May 6, 2013, a helicopter's tail rotor struck a prickly pear cactus while hovering to reposition a 100-foot longline on the Cactus Fire. No structural damage or vibration resulted; after inspection by an aircraft maintenance inspector, the helicopter was cleared to resume operations.
incidents.quote: The pilot was not comfortable with how close the line was to the skid and lifted the helicopter up about three feet in order to reposition. During this time the tail rotor made contact with a prickly pear cactus.

incidents.name: Belle Fourche Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On May 8, 2013 the Belle Fourche prescribed burn was declared an escaped prescribed burn and converted to a wildfire. During the implementation phase of this prescribed fire, two separate incidents occurred which were contributory to the escaped prescribed burn. Early in the operational shift of May 7th, a UTV and rider were involved in a vehicle tip-over. Also on May 7th, a power line was a scorched and caused the loss of power to the National Monuments upper pumping station, which contributed to damaging the Monuments waterlines.
incidents.quote: The Belle Fourche Prescribed Fire unit is a 325 acre landscape-scale prescribed burn located within the boundaries of Devils Tower National Monument (DETO), designed to reduce the woody fuel load as well as maintain the native grass ecosystem.

incidents.name: Stump Springs Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: A declaration was made once winds picked up, jackpot fuels started throwing embers and the contingency resources couldn't keep up.
incidents.quote: One of the igniters, laying fire along the edge, noted that the wick on his torch was extinguished by a gust of wind, stating aloud, “my wick just blew out”.

incidents.name: Thompson Ridge Medical
incidents.summary: Crewmember stated he had been off psychotropic medications for 4 days because he forgot them at home. His history included:schizophrenia, anxiety disorder, and “Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder” (ADHD). Crewmember said his anxiety was triggered by another crew member’s comment and he was now having difficulty controlling his anger. He stated that he felt like: “I could hit that guy”.
incidents.quote: There was a concern that the crewmember wanted a box cutter to hurt himself and others.

incidents.name: Saddleback Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighters on scene started CPR and called for emergency evacuation. Luke was transported by helicopter to the nearest hospital in Alturas. Despite all efforts to resuscitate him, he did not survive.
incidents.quote: Redding Smokejumper Luke Sheehy was struck by a falling portion of a tree while constructing a fire line on the Saddle Back Fire in the Modoc National Forest, South Warner Wilderness.

incidents.name: Streeter Medical Incident
incidents.summary: The patient was treated and remained in the hospital for approximately a week, with the Forest Service providing a rotation of support, including personnel in leadership positions.
incidents.quote: The EMT reported that the patient “felt like he wasn’t getting enough air and that he thought he was having a heart attack because of his medical history and the tightness he was feeling in his chest.

incidents.name: Big Meadow Medevac
incidents.summary: Prompt action by members of two hotshot crews, as well as fire line paramedics that arrived minutes later, contributed to the successful resuscitation of the firefighter. An Automated External Defibrillator (AED) was used on site to resuscitate the firefighter. Fellow crewmembers then transported the firefighter to the nearest helispot just as the requested medevac helicopter arrived on scene. The firefighter was then transferred to the medical flight crew and taken to a cardiac care hospital in Denver, Colorado.
incidents.quote: Early on the morning of Sunday, June 16, a member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) walking with his crew from spike camp to the fireline collapsed due to sudden cardiac arrest.

incidents.name: ATV Flip Over
incidents.summary: During post initial attack fire patrol, as the ATV operator is ascending a 25% slope—in the black interior of the fire—one front tire hits a burned sage stump. The ATV’s left front end pops up—causing the ATV to flip-over backward. The operator is able to leap out of the way of the falling ATV—avoiding personal injury.
incidents.quote: ATV Flip-Over

incidents.name: PT Rhabdo and Heat Injury
incidents.summary: While participating in 3-mile physical training run, a firefighter began to have trouble breathing approximately ¾ ways through. The individual slowed to a walk and was accompanied by his Crew Supervisor. After a few minutes, the firefighter seemed to get a second wind and sprinted to complete the run. Afterwards the firefighter was observed to be pale and became unresponsive. He was sat down in the shade while the crew immediately began cooling procedures and administered oxygen. Park medics responded and the individual was transported by ambulance and life flight to a hospital in Fresno, California.
incidents.quote: Firefighter has been diagnosed with exhaustive heat stroke which has led to rhabdomylosis. He remains in critical, but stable, condition.

incidents.name: Helicopter Bucket Strikes
incidents.summary: Helicopters at this elevation with this density altitude have less performance than at lower elevations. The variable wind direction and speed severely hamper aviation activities.
incidents.quote: Within two days there were two bucket strikes on the West Fork Complex.

incidents.name: Yarnell Hill Fire Entrapment Fatalities
incidents.summary: They were members of the Granite Mountain IHC, hosted by the Prescott Fire Department. One crewmember was separated from the crew earlier that day and was not at the deployment site.
incidents.quote: Nineteen firefighters died on the Yarnell Hill Fire in central Arizona after deploying fire shelters.

incidents.name: All-Terrain Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: While on a fire assignment, a Task Force Leader scouting between trails and roads was operating an ATV. As he traveled off the road he began traversing across a rocky, wooded sloped area. Suddenly, the left front tire went up on a rock as the right front tire went down into a depression. The ATV started a very slow rollover to the front right and the operator simply stepped off the ATV, which caused him to fall backwards hitting his head--which was protected by a D.O.T-endorsed helmet--on a tree. No vehicle damage or injury occurred.
incidents.quote: I was operating the ATV slowly and intermittently applying the hand brakes.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Vapor Lock
incidents.summary: The fuel ignited and “flashed” causing minor burns to the sawyer’s right arm, right side of neck, and right ear.
incidents.quote: A sawyer was injured when gas from a Stihl MS460 chainsaw fuel tank ignited after the sawyer opened the fuel cap to release excess pressure in the tank.

incidents.name: Minidoka Ranger District Heat Stroke FLA
incidents.summary: After spending three nights in a hospital, the individual was released for several weeks to fully recover.
incidents.quote: While participating in daily physical training, a fire/fuels crewmember suffered heat stroke during a 3.2 mile run.

incidents.name: Hardee Fatality
incidents.summary: Assistant Fire Chief Hardee responded to a brush fire late in the evening of July 6th, 2013. Upon return from the response, Hardee complained of having a headache and then departed the station and returned home. Early the next morning, Chief Hardee failed to respond on another emergency call. His wife noticed he was seriously ill and contacted 911 Fire/EMS for a possible stroke. Chief Hardee was transported to Grand Strand Hospital in Myrtle Beach where surgery was performed that day. Assistant Fire Chief Hardee succumbed to his CVA injury and passed away around 0200hrs on the morning of July 9th.
incidents.quote: Assistant Fire Chief Hardee succumbed to his CVA injury and passed away.

incidents.name: Chariot Dozer Entrapment
incidents.summary: A dozer operator experiencing sudden mechanical power loss built an emergency safety zone and survived an advancing fire front with helicopter water drops.
incidents.quote: The operator maintained constant communication with the Dozer Strike Team Leader which allowed coordination of four water drops from a Type 1 helicopter onto D3341's position.

incidents.name: Pardee Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighters, qualified as Emergency Medical Technicians, provided immediate care. To reach emergency medical responders, additional firefighter personnel and local landowners joined efforts to carry the Contract Dozer Operator up steep and rugged terrain. Despite best efforts, emergency medical personnel were unable to resuscitate the Contract Dozer Operator. The coroner’s report determined the cause of death was “severe Coronary Artery Disease.”
incidents.quote: The victim, Dennis Long, was engaged in downhill line construction during initial attack. The DOZB found the victim pale and unresponsive and began CPR.

incidents.name: Utah Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: Multiple people were involved and slightly injured, but all were transported to the hospital and were released.
incidents.quote: A T1 water tender lost their gear and brakes while coming down a steep hill, swerving to hit an erratic driver who was coming head-on, fish tailed, and rolled the tender.

incidents.name: Engine Patrol Incident
incidents.summary: The driver then secured the scene by dumping the water from the tank, putting the park brake on, hooking the winch cable to an upslope tree, and called for assistance.
incidents.quote: After several days of thunderstorms and on detection patrol, an engine pulled over to allow ATV's to pass when they slid off the road.

incidents.name: Nut Hill Tree Incident
incidents.summary: The adjacent firefighters did an initial check of the injured firefighter’s vital signs, state of consciousness, and looked for spinal or neck injuries. The firefighter never lost consciousness and was then tranported to the hospital.
incidents.quote: It was around 2200 when one of the forks at the top of the snag broke and fell approximately 45 feet striking a firefighter in the head, shoulder and back, knocking the firefighter to the ground.

incidents.name: Tassajara Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: There was some concern about the local hospital being a small facility, not a trauma center and not known to have surgeons on site. On this particular day, there was a touring surgeon at the hospital who happened to be a hand specialist.
incidents.quote: The puller slipped, fell, and his hand grazed the tip of the running saw as it cut through the log.

incidents.name: IHC Packout
incidents.summary: The crew activated the medical plan and constructed a makeshift splint and backboard and began carryout operations to a nearby trail. From the trail, a litter with wheel was used to complete the carryout back to the evacuation point.
incidents.quote: After approximately five minutes of line construction, a crewmember slipped and twisted his knee.

incidents.name: Northern Pueblos WCT Fatality
incidents.summary: Emergency Medical Personnel on scene monitoring WCT participants, immediately initiated CPR, and other lifesaving protocol with assistance from Agency Staff. The patient was transported to the Espanola Hospital four miles away, where he was pronounced deceased.
incidents.quote: At approximately 39 minutes into a Work Capacity Test (WCT) an individual collapsed within 400 yards from completion of the WCT.

incidents.name: Incident 398 Tree Strike Fatality
incidents.summary: One faller was killed instantly and the other faller was knocked to the ground, breaking both shoulder blades.
incidents.quote: The fallers were at the base of the 64" DBH tree, but had not yet begun cutting the tree, when the top portion with several green limbs attached broke away from the main tree and fell on the contract fallers.

incidents.name: Aspen Fire Dozer Entrapment
incidents.summary: While working on the main Aspen Fire, constructing dozer line, a new start below where they were working casued the module to flee to the safety zone.
incidents.quote: Dozer and Dozer Boss Narrowly Escape Sudden Fire

incidents.name: Falls Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: While he suffered 2nd degree burns he did not have deep tissue damage. The doctors told him that his wet feet had increased the intensity of the burn because steam, in contrast to dry heat, causes significantly more damage.
incidents.quote: Around 2300 he hiked three miles back to his engine. Upon arrival he realized his feet were really hurting “worse than ever before” and after he took his boots off the swelling was immediate and his boots could not be put back on.

incidents.name: Rock Close Call
incidents.summary: After approximately six hours of firefighting, a large boulder rolled down the hill towards the Helitack Fire Captain (FC). The FC took refuge behind a tree and sustained injuries to his arm while taking evasive actions.
incidents.quote: Crew members began yelling, “Rock!”

incidents.name: Runaway Engine FLA
incidents.summary: The STEN began to slow his vehicle allowing the engine to creep up to it until contact was made adn then he began to apply his brakes gently, bringing the brakeless engine to a full stop.
incidents.quote: The AFEO began to downshift, and when applying the brakes, he then noticed that the brakes were not working nor were the dashboard gauges.

incidents.name: Big Windy Fire Water Tender Fatality
incidents.summary: Night operational period resources had completed their fireline work assignments and were released to travel back to the Incident Command Post at approximately 0700. The route from the fireline to the highway is a narrow, winding, paved mountain road with a steep downhill grade for approximately 3 miles. Toward the bottom of the downgrade, the water tender impacted a cut bank next to the road and rolled onto its top. An advanced life support ambulance with a paramedic on board, was called and reached the scene within 7minutes. The paramedic on scene pronounced the driver deceased.
incidents.quote: Toward the bottom of the downgrade, the water tender impacted a cut bank next to the road and rolled onto its top.

incidents.name: Dozer Cab Fire
incidents.summary: When the Dozer Operator began to back down the dozer line for a different travel route, the passenger compartment began to rapidly fill with smoke. The Dozer Operator exited the passenger compartment and was able to use the dozer’s fire extinguisher in an effort to suppress the fire. Additional fire extinguishers from Dozer 3140 and Dozer 3540 were used to help suppress the fire inside the passenger compartment of Dozer 3341. The operator compartment was totally damaged and there was significant damage to the engine compartment.
incidents.quote: CAL FIRE Dozer experienced a fire within the passenger compartment of the dozer.

incidents.name: Engine 492 Rollover
incidents.summary: At the time of the accident all three members of Engine 492 were wearing their seatbelts. Use of seatbelts and the integrity of the engine cab are likely the principal reasons for the survivability of this accident.
incidents.quote: Engine 492 rolled over a few times before coming to rest on its wheels (up-right).

incidents.name: 187 Fire Hazard Tree
incidents.summary: "I’m not going to make the same mistake of exposing personnel to working around burning snags just to contain a fire, I’ll search for another alternative to get the job done."
incidents.quote: Having chainsaw approval when you request it, rather than a day later can make a difference between a hazardous tree and a tree too hazardous to fall.

incidents.name: Grassy Mountain Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: A contractor employee was found unresponsive by a Bureau ofLand Management engine crew. The BLM employees check vitals and found the contractor had no pulse and was not breathing. CPR was administered, life flight was immediately requested. CPR continued until life flight arrived. Life flight personnel administered care until the patient was pronounced deceased.
incidents.quote: A contractor Transport operator was found unresponsive and later was pronounced deceased.

incidents.name: Grizzly Fire Tree Fall Injury
incidents.summary: After 5-hours, the injured TFLD(T) made it to the hospital and released that night.
incidents.quote: The top of a large green white fir 40" DBH had fallen and hit the TFLD(T).

incidents.name: Beaver Creek Cardiac Arrest
incidents.summary: Local EMS unit administered three more shocks; pulse was regained and the patient was transported via ambulance to Life Flight.
incidents.quote: The Planning Section Chief witnessed a member of the camp crew constructing a yurt “go down.”

incidents.name: Green Ridge Short Haul
incidents.summary: A fireline EMT from the same crew was present and the “9 Line” protocol was followed, indicating a level of severity of red. Within five minutes a local area Advanced Life Support ambulance was enroute to the designated drop point with a 20 minute ETA.
incidents.quote: A handcrew member had difficulty breathing after inhaling hot smoke while working a spot fire.

incidents.name: Cog Fire ATV
incidents.summary: During the right turn and side-slope travel, the operator proceeded slowly with his right knee on the seat and left foot on the left ATV peg for more control. The ATV contacted a sagebrush plant approximately two feet in height whichcaused the ATV to begin tipping downhill. The operator noticed that the ATV was about to rollover. He pushed the ATV away from himself and landed on the uphill side of the ATV. The ATV rolled approximately 92 feet downhill and came to a stop on its own. The ATV sustained damage, but the operator, as well as bystanders, did not suffer any injuries.
incidents.quote: During the afternoon of August 18, 2013, a fire started in a drainage bottom that was terrain-driven with multiple structures in the area. As the fire continued to spread up drainage and over ridgelines to the east.

incidents.name: Lost Lake Chainsaw Kickback
incidents.summary: The firefighter was evaluated by on-site EMTs, treated on scene, and transported to a hospital with a non-life threatening injury.
incidents.quote: The firefighter had felled a tree and was in the initial stages of ‘low stumping’ when a violent chainsaw ‘kickback’ occurred causing the injury.

incidents.name: Howard Fire Bridge Collapse
incidents.summary: The driver was placed on a backboard and transported by pickup, ambulance and eventually Life Flight helicopter to a hospital where he was diagnosed with a fractured sacrum.
incidents.quote: The Driver, who was not wearing his seatbelt, remembers trying to “climb out of the UTV” as it slid off the right side of the bridge.

incidents.name: Little Fire
incidents.summary: The crew later reported that this simple amenity of cool water to share, along with the effectiveness of using the shelters as a shield from the radiant heat and smoke, greatly increased the morale of everyone.
incidents.quote: In under 2 hours, Div-A and crew will learn the value of adaptability and resilience in the face of breathtaking challenges.

incidents.name: Nabob Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: The contract crew was rehabilitating a fire line by pulling brush back over fireline that connected with the Pacific Crest Trail. The crew had just taken a lunch break when the firefighter collapsed. EMT’s on scene and multiple other EMS resources attempted to revive the firefighter and were unsuccessful.
incidents.quote: A firefighter from a contract Type 2 hand crew collapsed and died on the Nabob incident on Sunday.

incidents.name: Kelley Fire Medevacs (1 of 2)
incidents.summary: A crewmember from the IHC was injured by a falling snag and was extricated from a remote area of the fire with the aid of an interagency helicopter and crew, trained and equipped for “short haul”.
incidents.quote: During the early assessment of the extent of injuries, the crew “sprayed the injured firefighter with a “Fedco” (a backpack pump), in an effort to keep the fire off him.”

incidents.name: Corral Complex Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: While watering roads, a Type 2 Support Water Tender lost control along a sharp corner and steep section of Big Hill road, 1 mile east of state route 96. The water tender went over the embankment approx. 200 ft. The Driver was found outside the vehicle with multiple injuries. The driver was medevac’d to Mercy Medical Center in Redding California.
incidents.quote: Major Damage to Water Tender

incidents.name: Kelley Fire Medevacs (2 of 2)
incidents.summary: An agency medevac transport of the victim from an unimproved helispot was executed.
incidents.quote: The firefighter was beginning to feel fatigued and weak. A medical emergency/incident was declared for a victim of dehydration.

incidents.name: Schoolhouse Mesa Fatality
incidents.summary: A State Search & Rescue operation was ordered that night they lost commo and took over the search around midnight. His body wasn't found until a week later.
incidents.quote: The ATV then rolled over, hit a tree, and settled back on him. The ATV rear cargo rack landed on his neck, impacting just below his helmet. He died instantly.

incidents.name: Weiser Complex Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: Analysis of the scene later would show 7 points where the dozer hit the ground on its way down. Two hours later the operator, after extraction and Medivac, was in a hospital.
incidents.quote: The dozer rolled 310 feet downhill, coming to rest near a large snag 450 feet below the road.

incidents.name: Grizzly Bear Encounter
incidents.summary: Hearing my yell, from about 100-feet behind me, my other crewmembers started yelling frantically. By the time I got the spray out and was ready to deploy it on the bear, it was quickly turning around about 25-feet down the hill from me.
incidents.quote: “I looked up to see a 450-500 pound Grizzly coming at me very quickly . . .”

incidents.name: Kelley Fire ATV Accident
incidents.summary: The West Fork Kelley Creek ATV Trail #038 is a narrow one-way trail with few areas available to turn out. The local forest has identified travel regulations at the trailhead designating single uphill travel only. Upon scouting the trail, the Division Supervisor (DIVS) realized that the trail would be a valuable asset. However, good communications would be necessary to mitigate the one-way only travel on the trail. The DIVS asked the Safety Officer (SOF2(t)) assigned to the division to sign the trailhead with a sign requiring operators of ATVs to call out on the tactical frequency assigned to the division and announce which way they were traveling.
incidents.quote: On September 3, 2013 at approximately 1600 a Polaris Sportsman 550 EPS AVT was totaled when it rolled down a steep slope on Division Delta of the Kelley Fire near Featherville, Idaho.

incidents.name: Rim Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The firefighter is initially diagnosed with a 5-6 percent Body Surface Area second degree burn of the left lower extremity. After five hours in the ER, he is admitted to a hospital room upstairs.
incidents.quote: On the third day on the fire, while mopping-up, he steps into a stump hole full of hot ash. His left leg sinks up to his knee. Because he was a State employee...the patient advocate support is the bigger story.

incidents.name: SRF Truck Rollover
incidents.summary: The driver was found by another agency module with no noticeable injuries.
incidents.quote: The vehicle went over the embankment approx. 80 ft. striking a large tree.

incidents.name: Tree on Vehicle
incidents.summary: The tree struck the vehicle’s driver’s-side roof—leaving a small dent.
incidents.quote: "As I was felling the final tree in my section (3-inch DBH/30-feet tall), a white Subaru Outback stopped in the direct path of the falling tree."

incidents.name: Smith Prairie Smokejumper Fatality
incidents.summary: On September 27, 2013, at about 1230, BLM smokejumper Mark Urban was fatally injured when his parachute did not open for reasons that have yet to be determined.
incidents.quote: A BLM smokejumper validating the functionality of a safety device and the jump procedures was fatally injured when his parachute canopy failed to deploy.

incidents.name: Finger Lakes NF RX Lessons
incidents.summary: The consequence of the malfunctioning terra torch wand, in combination with the placement of the face shroud, was that RXCM #1 sustained a 2nd degree burn on his nose. Evidently the burn injury wasn’t fully communicated until two days later. Although RXCM #1 felt the radiant heat on his face, “I thought it was similar to a sun burn,” and didn’t think much of it.
incidents.quote: The first RXCM pair was given a briefing by a qualified Terra Torch Operator (TTOP). RXCM #1 was holding the terra torch burn wand and RXCM #2 was assisting with the hose and coordinating terra torch pump operations.

incidents.name: Washington State Hazard Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: An Airway Heights prison inmate died while clearing land for the state Department of Natural Resources after a timber harvest.

incidents.name: Staph Infection
incidents.summary: The TFLD-T underwent surgery the following day and continued on intravenous antibiotics in the hospital. The strain of his staph infection could not be determined from a culture. After four days and nights in the hospital, he was released on the fifth day and sent home with two broad-spectrum antibiotics.
incidents.quote: The lesion was lanced. He was given oral antibiotics and referred to see an ENT specialist the next day. The following morning, the TFLD-T's entire face was severely swollen. He could barely open his eyes.

incidents.name: Powerline on Engine
incidents.summary: A line dropped on the unoccupied engine before crew could move it. The vehicle sat with an energized line on top of it for about 3 hours until the power company arrived and de-energized the line.
incidents.quote: As soon as they arrived, thick black smoke was rising above the small canyon community. Their initial report was, “two structures fully involved” they parked their engine and engaged.

incidents.name: Stanza Tree Strike
incidents.summary: After five days of felling operations, an experienced C faller was injured while felling an 8" diameter by 50' tall Madrone snag.
incidents.quote: "I saw the tree break off the stump before it was intended to"

incidents.name: Winkles Fatality
incidents.summary: Winkles was treated by fellow responders at the scene then transported to the hospital where he passed away.
incidents.quote: Fire Chief Winkles suffered an apparent heart attack while working at the scene of an accidental grass fire that spread to and destroyed a nearby residence.

incidents.name: Arkansas Forestry Commission Aircraft Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: Following almost two weeks of searching for a missing single-engine Cessna 210 Centurion, Civil Air Patrol located the crash site and a National Guard helicopter crew confirmed that the pilot, Jake Harrell, was deceased and likely killed upon impact. Harrell, an experienced pilot, went missing while flying a regularly scheduled fire detection flight throughout west Arkansas. Investigation into the fatal incident continues by local, state, and federal (NTSB) authorities.
incidents.quote: A pilot doing aerial reconnaisance for the Arkansas Forestry Commission was killed after striking trees on a ridge during a low cloud day.

incidents.name: Hilton Fatality
incidents.summary: According to officials, the cause of the fire is under investigation and may have been intentionally set in several locations.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Hilton suffered a fatal heart attack while fighting an outdoors fire that was threatening homes in the area.

incidents.name: Skull Incident
incidents.summary: The crew was assigned to a brush clearing project along a narrow county road. During chipping operations, a vehicle passed through traffic controls and struck the inmate crew member. The inmate was treated for multiple injuries at the scene and transported by ground ambulance to Sutter Amador Hospital. The inmate was then transported by air ambulance to San Joaquin General Hospital in Stockton, CA.
incidents.quote: On Thursday, February 6, 2014, at approximately 1355 hours, a member of Vallecito Crew 2 was struck by a private vehicle.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Cut to Wrist
incidents.summary: On February 13, 2014, at approximately 1200 hours, a CAL FIRE inmate Firefighter was operating a chainsaw and sustained a laceration to the top of his left wrist. The inmate was transported by ground ambulance to a local hospital for treatment.
incidents.quote: As the inmate was slipping downhill with the chainsaw, the chainsaw rolled inverted causing the throttle to be engaged by the inmate's right hand.

incidents.name: Jerry Campbell Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Campbell reported feeling unwell to his supervisor. EMS responders were called and found that Firefighter Campbell was suffering a heart attack.

incidents.name: Engine Bin Damage
incidents.summary: While using Engine 641 for supporting lighters, an individual climbs onto back of engine to get torch fuel mix—crossing over the engine’s plumbing and accidentally opening the number 3 pre-connect valve. This unintentional action charges 100 feet of 1 1/2” hose in Bin #4 on this Type 6 Engine.
incidents.quote: The Engine Operator hears a loud bang noise and sees that engine compartment #4 is busted at the welds of the compartment.

incidents.name: Mollere Fatality Pack Test
incidents.summary: Fellow firefighters on scene initiated a medical assessment and found Mollere in cardiac arrest. The EMTs and Paramedics began advanced life support immediately on scene. Lieutenant Mollere was transported to the Payson Regional Medical Center where resuscitative efforts continued until he passed away.
incidents.quote: While performing a Wildland Pack Test, Lieutenant Mollere collapsed on the Payson High School track.

incidents.name: Wyoming WCT Fatality
incidents.summary: Fire Crew Supervisor Drake, a career employee of Wyoming State Forestry Division, supervised and trained inmates called “Smoke Busters,” well-respected teams utilized to fight wildland fires and complete many other associated projects on both federal and state lands.
incidents.quote: Fire Crew Supervisor Ted Drake passed away from a reported heart attack while participating in a work capacity test for red card certification, part of the wildland fire qualification system used by federal and most state wildland fire management agencies.

incidents.name: Emmett Ridges Smokejumper Accident
incidents.summary: A BLM Boise Great Basin smokejumper incurred two broken femurs when he experienced a hard landing during a routine refresher parachute jump.
