This was the second jump of the day at the same location. The jump spot was located along an open ridgeline in an area commonly used for training jumps.
incidents.quote: A smokejumper had a hard landing on a routine practice jump. The ground crew advised the jumpship, Jumper 49, to call a Life Flight helicopter to evacuate the injured jumper.

incidents.name: PT Rhabdo
incidents.summary: This is the story/chronology of a 29-year-old engine captain, who—during morning PT a few weeks ago—thinks he is having severe heat cramps. Fortunately, he decides to go to the hospital—where he is diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis (“Rhabdo”). The engine captain’s immediate treatment in the ER prevents his kidneys from completely shutting down. Now, almost four weeks later, he’s still on light duty, is experiencing pain and dizziness, and is not sure when he will be fully recovered.
incidents.quote: “I would describe the pain as someone wrenching your thighs in a vice while someone else hits them with a baseball bat.”

incidents.name: Wichita Mountains NWR UTV Flammable Debris
incidents.summary: Our fire staff decided to add a small work light on the rear of our 2011 6x6 Polaris Ranger. When they removed the plastic floor panel to aid in pulling the new wire, they found that the entire compartment underneath the floor panel was completely full of cured grass, sticks, and other dead vegetation. It would be very easy for an external ignition source to light the accumulated material—causing a fire that would be extremely hard to access and put out.
incidents.quote: Removing Combustible Debris Beneath Floor Plates on Polaris Rangers.

incidents.name: Short Haul Coordination
incidents.summary: Confusion arose when ground forces on a fire expected a medical evacuation of an injured fire fighter to be implemented using short-haul. The cooperator chose to complete the mission using a hover exit/entrance method instead.
incidents.quote: The ground personnel did not expect a hover maneuver and were unfamiliar with the protocols of the cooperator.

incidents.name: Heat Transfer Burn Injury
incidents.summary: As is normal with many districts, the militia model was being implemented: fire-qualified employees from other units were coming to assist with the burn. About an hour after ignition began, a Firefighter sustained a third-degree burn injury between her knee and boot on her inner left leg.
incidents.quote: "My leg was pink and white, had some discoloration, and it hurt a bit, but it was nothing extreme. I had no idea it was that bad, so I told the other burners I was okay and kept on burning."

incidents.name: Cocos Fire Lower Extremity Burn Injury
incidents.summary: At approximately 1300 hour’s winds increased, with an increase of fire activity; including some spotting. In order to improve the margin of safety personnel choose to enter the black and walk back to their engines. The engine crews traveled across a finger to shorten the walking distance to the engines. Within their walking path some areas had thick ash and some “jackpots” were also present. As the Firefighters approached the engines, some personnel noticed heat convecting through the soles of their boots. Once they returned to their engines the Firefighters observed their boot soles had delaminated, rendering the boots out of service. One Firefighter suffered first and second degree burns to his/her feet. The injured Firefighter was treated at the scene and transported to the University of California San Diego burn center where he/she was examined, treated and released.
incidents.quote: As the Firefighters approached the engines, some personnel noticed heat convecting through the soles of their boots.

incidents.name: South Meadow Creek Simulation
incidents.summary: This was a full scale, real time emergency response simulation exercise. The simulation coordinator chose to end the simulation after two unplanned aviation related incidents occurred.
incidents.quote: The firefighters and emergency personnel involved in this simulation were not aware that this is a test.

incidents.name: Helitack IA Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Copter 104 was providing mutual aid to the City of Vallejo Fire Department at the time of the incident. The crew from Copter 104 was initiating direct fireline attack on a flank of the fire, when the firefighter stepped into a depression in the ground with the left foot, causing a loss of balance. The firefighter then fell forward contacting the ground with the left hand and right knee and during this process; the firefighter sustained first and second degree burns to the left hand, both feet and the right knee. Simultaneously a patch of brush, approximately two feet in front of the firefighter, flared up causing first and second degree burns to the firefighters face.
incidents.quote: On May 24, 2014, at approximately 1620 hours a CAL FIRE firefighter from Copter 104, of the Sonoma/Lake/Napa Unit, sustained serious burn injuries while fighting a wildland fire.

incidents.name: Badger Fire
incidents.summary: The crewmember working along the fire perimeter was navigating a steep terrain constriction near the top of the mesa, when he was struck by a large boulder. Fellow crew members respond immediately, taking decisive action. The patient was assessed by an EMT and the decision was made to transport by air.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1010 hrs. on Saturday, May 24th, 2014, an incident occurred on the Badger Fire, BLM Phoenix District, Arizona

incidents.name: Sled Springs Rhabdo Incident During PT
incidents.summary: With less than a quarter of a mile (of a total of 4 miles) to go in the run, crewmember begins to lose coordination. Two crew members assist him to the finish and help him sit down. He refuses care and his speech is slurred. Eventually being treated for shock with vitals quickly dimineshing, the crewmemebr is taken to the hospital and on the 3rd day, is diagnosed with Rhabdo.
incidents.quote: During a crew "bump run", a crewmember starts acting intoxicated.

incidents.name: Hunter Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: The fire crew was working in very steep terrain using hand tools and chain saws. The saw team was actively cutting thick brush when the crew sawyer struck the left arm of the puller with the chain saw resulting in an 18 inch laceration to the puller’s left arm.
incidents.quote: On May 27, 2014, at approximately 0500 hours, an inmate fire crew was assigned to hand line construction on Division Z. The fire crew was working in very steep terrain using hand tools and chain saws.

incidents.name: Skunk Fire Tire Failure
incidents.summary: At approximately 0645 on 06/05/2014 chase truck U3665 returning from the Skunk Fire was involved in a vehicle accident. U3665 had two BLM employees, public vehicle 9175 had one occupant and public vehicle 905 had one occupant; no injuries were reported at the scene and no persons required first aid or medical assistance at the incident.
incidents.quote: At approximately 0645 on 06/05/2014 chase truck U3665 returning from the Skunk Fire was involved in a vehicle accident.

incidents.name: NV VFD Training Fatality
incidents.summary: Garcia was treated at the scene and then transported to the Northern Nevada Medical Center in Sparks, Nevada, where he succumbed to his injury.
incidents.quote: Assistant Fire Chief Garcia was participating in wildland fire training when he collapsed from an apparent heart attack.

incidents.name: IHC Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: During the drive back to the station, the EMT notified the captain that the crewmember's cramps were getting worse. The superintendent and captain realized they were not going to be able to transport the crewmember, and that immediate action was required.
incidents.quote: "Hey Cap. I'm calling it [The crewmember] needs to go to the hospital." - EMT rendering aid

incidents.name: Pole Creek Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: Due to a miscommunication between the Burn Boss and one of the firing teams, the firing pattern was not completed as originally intended, producing very active fire behavior and spotting more than a half mile in front of the fire. Ignition operations ceased as fire personnel focused on locating and controlling spot fires. Two days later, due to concerns of the fire spreading to a timber sale located north of the fire and the need for additional resources, the Burn Boss made the decision to declare the prescribed burn a wildfire.
incidents.quote: The Pole Creek Prescribed burn, located on the Bridger-Teton NF on the Kemmerer RD, was declared a wildfire June 10, 2014.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Fuel Geyser
incidents.summary: Prior to this event, the saw team filled-up their saw just before taking lunch. While on their lunch break, the saw had been set down in the sun. After lunch, the saw team was unable to start the saw. While troubleshooting the problem, the crew member held the saw at waist height and opened the saw’s fuel cap. That’s when the pressurized fuel from the tank sprayed out—into the crew member’s face and eyes.
incidents.quote: The high temperature (98 degrees) caused the fuel to expand within the saw’s fuel tank.

incidents.name: ATV Loading - Six Rivers NF
incidents.summary: The ATV’s frame landed on his helmet, shattering it, and the shards of plastic caused many facial wounds.
incidents.quote: The Superintendent of a Handcrew sustained facial lacerations and received many stitches to wounds on his face after an ATV rolled back on top of him while attempting to load it into the back of a pickup truck by riding it up a ramp.

incidents.name: San Juan Fire Fuels Treatment Effectiveness
incidents.summary: The fire’s forward spread was largely halted by the end of the second day—despite continued high winds—in large part due to the success of burnout operations in areas where previous thinning and prescribed burning had occurred.
incidents.quote: Overall, the fuel treatments that were encountered by this fire performed as designed by reducing fire intensities. This allowed firefighters to work in a safer environment where their suppression efforts could be successful.

incidents.name: Monticello Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: On July 6, 2014, at approximately 1320 hours, a CAL FIRE dozer was operating on Division M of the Monticello Incident. The dozer was working sidehill, constructing fire line in steep terrain. The dozer became unstable and rolled at least two times coming to rest on its tracks in a small drainage below. The operator sustained a head injury and a possible loss of consciousness. Fire line personnel immediately responded to assist and treat the operator. A CAL FIRE helicopter performed a hoist rescue. The operator was transferred to a waiting medevac helicopter and was transported to a trauma center for evaluation. The operator was released from the hospital later that evening.
incidents.quote: A CAL FIRE dozer constructing fire line in steep and rugged terrain rolled over several times, causing injury to the operator and damage to the dozer.

incidents.name: Pacific Southwest Aviation Lessons Learned
incidents.summary: The two aircraft had been supporting the Nicholls Fire on the Sequoia National Forest with retardant drops, and were returning to load at the Air Attack Base.
incidents.quote: A Legacy Airtanker and a NextGen Airtanker that came within 400 feet of each other while approaching the Porterville Airport.

incidents.name: Vehicle Fire Response MVA
incidents.summary: At approximately 1830 hours on July 13, 2014, a CAL FIRE Model 34 engine, on cover assignment from out of the Unit, was dispatched to a vehicle fire. The fire was a threat to nearby vegetation on Highway 101 just south of Howard Forest Headquarters. The engine was turning left onto Highway 101, southbound, from the Howard Forest Headquarters driveway. As the engine crossed the northbound lane it was struck by a northbound POV. The POV struck the engines driver side rear duals. The POV sustained major front end damage, and the driver suffered leg and ankle injuries.
incidents.quote: The CAL FIRE engine immediately circled and parked off the roadway, and the crew provided treatment to the driver of the POV. The driver of the POV was transported by ambulance to a local hospital and released later that evening.

incidents.name: Rock Ridge Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A county engine was assisting the BLM on the four-acre Rock Ridge wildfire which was started by lightning on July 13 in sage and juniper. The county engine crew was assigned to support mop-up operations on the morning of July 14. At approximately 1130 hours a firefighter from the county engine sustained bums to the forearm and leg and was transported by medivac helicopter from the fire area to the University of Utah Bum Center.
incidents.quote: Recently, a wildland firefighter was seriously burned while operating a saw in hot ash when fuel spilled from a Stihl chainsaw onto the saw chaps,

incidents.name: Holroyd Park Tree Incident
incidents.summary: While standing in the green and thinking he was safely out of range from the burning snags, the sawyer lookout held his post while the sawyer removed other snags. What felt like mere moments later, one of those snags finally lost its battle against bug and burn, and fell directly toward his position. With no time to respond, he was struck on the right side of his hardhat.
incidents.quote: A firefighter was struck and injured by a dead lodgepole pine tree that fell during initial attack.

incidents.name: Quaking Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: The firefighter was knocked to the ground sustaining injuries and was assessed on scene by several EMTs. Crews packaged and transported the injured firefighter by NPS rescue helicopter to the South Rim Helibase, Grand Canyon NP, at which point the firefighter was transferred to a medivac helicopter for air transport to Flagstaff Medical Center for evaluation.
incidents.quote: While preparing a section of containment line for firing/holding operations, a fire fighter was struck by a snag being felled by another firefighter.

incidents.name: Bully Fire Tree Incident
incidents.summary: An IHC crewmember was struck across the back and head by a fire weakened tree while fighting a wildland fire. The crew member remained conscious and felt tingling in his hands. Due to mechanism of injury coupled with pain in the crew member’s back and leg, C-Spine precautions were immediately initiated where he was transported to a a helibase via a hoist ship, then transported to a hospital by ground ambulance.
incidents.quote: An incident in which a federal hotshot crewmember was struck by a 10-12 in inch diameter, “A” size, fire weakened tree while performing hand-line construction.

incidents.name: Richfield Fire Engine Loss
incidents.summary: BLM resources engaged the southwest corner of the fire utilizing direct attack. At approximately 1215 hours BLM discovered that a Richfield RFD engine was attempting to engage the northeast corner of the fire was stuck and needed assistance. A type four BLM engine attempted to assist the Richfield RFD engine however the Richfield engine was wedged on a large rock and the fire was spreading towards the disabled engine. The RFD crew was unable to get the engine unstuck or protect the equipment before it was engulfed by the fire. The RFD crew withdrew to a nearby safety zone and was uninjured.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1138 hours on 07/16/2014 a rural type 4 fire engine from the Richfield, Idaho Rural Fire Department (RFD) responded to a fire reported to be on private land approximately 5 miles Southwest of Richfield, Idaho along highway 26.

incidents.name: Skyline Road Engine Accident
incidents.summary: As Engine 38 approaches fire # 73, FF1 observes smoke several hundred feet off the right side of the road, as the engine passes a dirt road that leads towards the fire. A split second later FF1 turns to FF2 and asks, “was that our road”. At that time FF2 is looking at the map and responds back and says “I think so”. Engine 38 drifts off the road, and FF1 tries to steer the engine back on to the road, however the weight of the vehicle and the extremely poor condition of the road prevent a recovery. The engine travels about 100 feet then jumps back on to the road. As soon as the vehicle gets back on the road FF1 over-corrects the steering which causes Engine 38 to roll once and land upright on the Westside of the Skyline 42 road. The crash resulted in injuries to FF1 (broken collar bone) and injuries to FF2 (neck and spinal injuries).
incidents.quote: On July 18, 2014 at approximately 1400 Pacific Daylight Time a Type 4 wildland fire engine with two personnel aboard was enroute to the 73 fire on an initial attack response. The engine experienced a rollover accident while enroute to the fire.

incidents.name: IHC Rhabdo
incidents.summary: An IHC crewmember, after three days of a standard PT routine, then assigned to a fire, noticed urinie getting darker, and muscle soreness (not extreme). Admitted to a hospital and an overnight stay, he continued IV rehydration and oral fluids. His CK levels had only fallen to about 63,000 (normal levels are 50-200). For the next four days, he remained in the hospital with IV treatment and continued to drink water. When his CK levels reached14,000, the doctor determined that—considering his age and fitness—he could be released to the care of his primary care physician in Denver. He is flown home to continue recovery and regular testing.
incidents.quote: The next morning, his urine is still very dark. Concerned, he mentions this to a crew EMT. The EMT immediately reports this to the foreman and superintendent, who suspect rhabdomyolysis.

incidents.name: VLAT Ground Incident
incidents.summary: During a last minute taxi pattern change from the marshaller, the VLAT struck the stair truck/stand. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) determined this was not an accident.
incidents.quote: During Retardant Loading operations the following ground incident occurred at an Airtanker Base (ATB) where a Very Large Airtanker (VLAT) struck air stairs during egress from the retardant loading pit.

incidents.name: Citadel Jump Spot
incidents.summary: On July 21, 2013, at 1230, Jumper 49 with eight Smokejumpers was ordered to the Citadel Fire (HR0D) on Craig BLM. After standard smokejumper operations, the fire activity increased and the para-cargo in the jump spot was burned up by the fire. Smokejumpers were able to salvage their jumper gear. No injuries were sustained.
incidents.quote: The downhill pulse of the fire—with no real indicators such as increased wind speeds or T-storms—caught the smokejumpers by surprise.

incidents.name: Anderson Water Tender Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: The Montana Highway Patrol said the driver of the other truck, a brush truck, missed a turnoff en route to the fire and was making a U-turn when Anderson crashed into him. The water tender (tanker) truck driven by Anderson tipped on its side and Anderson had to be extricated from the wreck. He was then transported to the hospital by ambulance where he died several weeks later.
incidents.quote: A Water Tender was involved in a motor vehicle accident with a brush truck while responding to a grass fire. The water tender operator, Cheif Dave Anderson died several weeks after the collision.

incidents.name: Bully Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: Approximately two-thirds of a mile east of Cloverdale Road they encountered west bound a tractor trailer in their lane. The operator of the tractor trailer made an abrupt right turn steering movement to avoid a head on collision with U-2438. The dump style 40 foot trailer, loaded with debris, jackknifed. The tractor trailer hit the south guardrail, tipped, on its driver side and continued to slide westbound blocking all lanes of traffic. The driver of U-2438 braked and moved to the right as far as possible. The tractor sideswiped the driver side of the U-2438 behind the cab and the nose of the dump trailer impacted U-2438 head on.
incidents.quote: A CAL FIRE utility providing logistical support collided with a tractor trailer. Minor injuries occurred to two CAL FIRE firefighters. No injuries were reported by the civilian commercial vehicle operator. The CAL FIRE utility vehicle and trailer of the commercial vehicle sustained extensive damage.

incidents.name: Warm Springs Agency MVA
incidents.summary: After the accident, the Forest Service employee was treated at the scene and released. The other driver was detained by law enforcenemt. At the time of the 24-hour preliminary report (July 26, 2014) the accident was still under investigation by local law enforcenment.
incidents.quote: Severity resources for IA were involved in an accident invloving one other vehicle.

incidents.name: Carlton Complex Bambi Bucket Snag
incidents.summary: The pilot continued to make additional water drops with the top of the tree tangled in the bucket, apparently not knowing that this tree-snag incident had occurred. It is believed that military Black Hawk helicopter pilots cannot see their buckets. They therefore rely on their crew to spot the bucket. In addition, military pilots don’t often use fire buckets on their ships. That’s why it’s important that both air and ground crews share a responsibility to maintain situation awareness during these operations.
incidents.quote: A National Guard Black Hawk helicopter making water drops hard-snagged his Bambi Bucket in the top of a tree.

incidents.name: Fir Grove
incidents.summary: The Fir Grove fire, discovered at 1304 hours MST on Sunday, July 28, started from a lightning strike north of Gooding, Idaho on the west side of highway 46. Response to the incident included multiple air and ground resources. At approximately 1645 hours, a photographer from the Times-News in Twin Falls, Idaho took a photo of a firefighter who was helping to conduct a burn out operation on the Fir Grove fire. As a High Reliability Organization (HRO) the Twin Falls District recognized what appeared to be a questionable act of a firefighter jumping through or over flames on a Twin Falls BLM fire. Throughout the LLR, additional HRO principles were identified.
incidents.quote: “A firefighter jumped through a wall of flame Sunday night after lighting a back burn on Highway 46.”

incidents.name: Launch Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: While helping transport firefighters across Fourmile Lake by boat, the firefighter went for a "walk" while waiting for supplies and other firefighters to load onto the boat. After a bit of time, an official Missing Persons Protocol was activated and was later found on some rocks where the individual sustained a fatal wound after a fall.
incidents.quote: Firefighter sustains a fatal injury from a fall.

incidents.name: Carlton Complex Bucket Drop
incidents.summary: Due to a miscommunication between ground resources and the helicopter pilot, a water drop was dropped in an area that was not "clear" resulting in live trees getting snapped/uprooted and hitting the CRWB. Fortunately, there were only minor injuries.
incidents.quote: On the Carlton Complex, southwest of Twisp, Wastington, three firefighters had a close call with a helicopter bucket drop.

incidents.name: Tree Felling Lessons Learned
incidents.summary: A felling team sized up a 30" diameter, 60' tall sugar pine snag. They determined the tree needed to be felled downhill. Once it fell, the tree continued down the steep slope. Hearing the warning shouts from above, a fire crewmember left the area of parked pickup trucks on the road below the tree-felling operation. The sliding log smashed the parked pickup, causing major damage. There were no injuries.
incidents.quote: “Don’t be complacent, speak up when you see something that may comprise safety”

incidents.name: Logging Unit Medevac RLS
incidents.summary: After the Firefighter passed out the first time, he regained consciousness again but this time was clenching his throat, had increased difficulty breathing, and elevated heart rate. The on scene EMT suspected a cardio issue and the Firefighter was transported by Life Flight helicopter to the local hospital.
incidents.quote: While working on a remote steep section of line, a Firefighter passed out while hiking to the assigned section of line.

incidents.name: Oregon Gulch Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: At approximately 0300 hours, the crew took a break on the fire line. The crew took their break on a piece of dozer line which was at the bottom of a slope that the crew had been working. A crew member went to the middle of the dozer line, removed their gloves and partially removed their web gear to sit down on the line. Within minutes of sitting down the firefighter was struck by a burning log about 2 feet long by 6 inches in diameter. The log had rolled down the slope to the dozer line. The burning log impacted the firefighter on the right side igniting components of the web gear. The firefighter suffered a serious burn to the hand while trying to pat out the flames of the web gear.
incidents.quote: A CAL FIRE engine crew was assigned to Division U on the Oregon Gulch fire burning in the Siskiyou Unit. The crew was assigned to mop up activity in their division.

incidents.name: French Fire Night Time Hoist Extraction
incidents.summary: A sawyer cutting brush ahead of line construction effort was struck by an 8” diameter piece of woody debris. As crewmembers rushed to the downed firefighters aid, he was found to be semi-conscious with a visible laceration to the head.
incidents.quote: A large snag within the black fell parallel to the fire pe-rimeter, hit adjacent trees, and caused a shrapnel effect of flying woody debris that hit a sawyer.

incidents.name: Near Midair Helicopter Collision
incidents.summary: While returning to the helibase outside the TFR for fuel, the helicopter sees another Type 1 helicopter at his 2:30 position. The other helicopter is approximately 20 feet lower in altitude, 200 yards away—and rapidly closing. During the immediate hard bank, the only thing he can see is the belly of the other helicopter—located about 75 feet away in the 90-degree bank.
incidents.quote: “I banked hard left, as hard as the ship would go over. As I looked back at him, all I saw was her white belly—and I can tell you, she is missing 3 rivets on the belly.”

incidents.name: South Fork Complex Heavy Equipment Rollover
incidents.summary: After pushing the limits of the equipment on a piece of steeper ground, extending the boom below grade to get "the last little piece", the road gave way causing the Hydro-Ax to slowly role over, which resulted in no injuries.
incidents.quote: “I told myself, make one more cut then call the HEQB to let him know we are pushing the limits of this machine.”

incidents.name: Faller Hit by Tree Shrapnel
incidents.summary: After making his backcut on the snag, the tree jumped, the faller ran and was then knocked to the ground by an 8-foot 6-inch section of the tree top (5-7 inch diameter). The wind was knocked out of him. Three other pieces of the top landed in the cutting area and on the faller’s escape route.
incidents.quote: A falling module with almost 30 years experience together, took down a snag where the top fell out and resulted in a cracked rib, a chipped disc, a bruised lung, in addition to contusions and abrasions on the faller.

incidents.name: Lost Ridge Fire
incidents.summary: The two individuals got turned around and required to firefighters to hike in late at night to bring them overnight gear, food and water. All hiked out the next morning with no injuries.
incidents.quote: Two militia firefighters from the local District became disoriented regarding their location while conducting an evacuation of trails and campsites being threatened by a nearby fire.

incidents.name: Fifteen Cent Lake Fire Rollover
incidents.summary: Skid #2 started to adjust the back end of the skidgine to be fully pointed downhill when several rocks kicked loose and rolled out from under the rear tires. This action changed the ordination and angle of Skid #2, jarring it toward the front right tire (the downhill side)—causing Skid #2 to rollover. Skid #2 rolled five times before coming to rest on its right side, approximately 200 feet down slope. When Skid #2 stopped rolling, the operator immediately jumped out of the skidgine, under his own power, and ran clear of the machine—thinking it might roll again.
incidents.quote: “I am so glad I had my seatbelt on and an “Oh S***” handle to hang on to. All I was thinking was keep your hand and feet inside the vehicle at all times. The last thing I wanted to do was lose an arm.” Skid #2 Operator

incidents.name: Beaver Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: The fire front was advancing into their site, flying embers shot at them like a fierce hail storm. A hot ember landed on HEQB (T)’s neck and he let out a yell. He then put his phone into his pocket. DIVS-C and HEQB (T) started to deploy their shelters beside DIVS C’s truck—to use it as a heat shield.
incidents.quote: As DIVS-C drove down the dozer line, he was feeling okay about the situation—until about halfway down the line when he noticed the downhill crown run that was following him. He later reflected that, in that instant, he got the sick feeling that: “This isn’t gonna be a good deal.”

incidents.name: Dusty Road Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: As the driver pressed on the brakes to slow the vehicle to navigate the turn and to see better through the dust, the vehicle began to vibrate and shake as it floated across the washboards toward the outside of the road where it came to rest on a tree.
incidents.quote: The vehicle slid along the tree and came to a stop. If it wasn’t for the tree, the truck could have gone off the road and down the steep slope—approximately 30-50 feet to the bottom.

incidents.name: Tonahutu Fire Dead and Down Mitigations RLS
incidents.summary: Crews encountered high tree fall rates at low wind speeds and encountered challenges in developing a medical egress route through the dense, dead-and-down jackstraw. Beetle kill stability changes over time. Many studies suggest it reaches its peak in approximately five to eight years. Crews working on the Tonahutu Fire were in a stand that was most likely reaching its peak of instability.
incidents.quote: During initial attack and subsequent extended attack in 10-year-old beetle-killed lodgepole on the Tonahutu Fire.

incidents.name: South Cle Elem Ridge
incidents.summary: While bucking out a large log, the round broke free, but instead of the log rolling to either side, the log slid down the 60-70 percent slope—with force pinching and dragging the sawyer. At the same time, the uphill portion snagged the Squad Leader who was trying to scramble out of the way.
incidents.quote: The downhill portion of the ponderosa pine broke free of the main bole, pinching and dragging the Sawyer.

incidents.name: Bald Sisters Fire
incidents.summary: The Firefighter stood and looked up just as the top of the tree struck her on the back between the spine and the right shoulder blade. The Firefighter was knocked to the ground by the combination of the steep slope and the force of the tree strike.
incidents.quote: A firefighter was bending over to pick up some limbs from one of the previously cut trees when she heard a yell: “Look out!”

incidents.name: Johnson Bar Fire Tree Incident
incidents.summary: While conducting line prep for a burnout, a small 4" DBH tree was felled and hit a crewmember.
incidents.quote: “I felt the tree hit my hard hat, and at first I didn’t think that it had caused any harm”

incidents.name: Grand Wash Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: During the course of the FLA process, it was discovered that different people had different definitions of what constituted an “Incident within and Incident”. The IC stated that, to him, this situation did not meet that threshold. A need to clarify expectations was discussed, and plans were made to have that conversation in the future.
incidents.quote: “My whole goal was to get [CRWB (t)] to the truck, get some AC, and put him on an I.V.”—EMT

incidents.name: Freedom Fire
incidents.summary: After the injury, the sawyer walked out and eventually was transported to the ER via ambulance where he received surgery from a laceration on his shoulder, from the saw he tried to ditch as he was tumbling, that was 14 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm deep—exposing the clavicle bone.
incidents.quote: After a violent kickback and a tumble down the steep terrain, the sawyer looked down to see blood gushing out of his wound from his neck/shoulder area.

incidents.name: Raccoon Prescribed Fire Equipment Loss
incidents.summary: On August 20th BICY Fire Personnel were conducting a prescribed fire in Raccoon point. At approximately 14:45 Fire Buggy 2 erupted in flames on the passenger side. Flames engulfed the decking and the passenger seat. The operator was able to grab his radio and get off the buggy moments before his seat and side of the buggy were completely on fire. The buggy was a complete loss and burned rapidly to the ground. It is believed the fire occurred near or around the fuel tank.
incidents.quote: The Preserve’s swamp buggy fleet has been stood down, pending an inspection of each buggy’s fuel system; buggy operations will resume as inspections are completed and corrective action taken as needed.

incidents.name: Monroe Fire Heat Damaged ATV
incidents.summary: After helping a dozer construct line around a spot fire, the HEQB boss realized the fire had creeped and burnt into his ATV. Upon realizing the tire was on fire, he grabbed the e-brake (conduction/convection burn) to move it into the dozer line, later realizing he had 2nd degree burns.
incidents.quote: “I looked up the hill, saw smoke and thought – Oh #%&$!”

incidents.name: Hillside Fire Electircal Shock
incidents.summary: Approximately two hours into suppression activities two fire department personnel, a firefighter II-paramedic and a volunteer reserve firefighter received an electrical shock from an unknown power source, resulting in minor injuries.
incidents.quote: On the evening of August 28, 2014, while assigned to a vegetation fire, two fire department personnel were injured when they came in contact with an unknown electrical energy source.

incidents.name: Deception Complex
incidents.summary: As the forwarder came over the bump and made the turn, the load of logs began oscillating and tilted to the downhill side, where the forwarder laid over, causing no injuries to the operator or the equipment.
incidents.quote: As the load of logs slowly tilted more, gravity took over and pulled the entire machine onto its side.

incidents.name: 790 Fire Hit by Tree RLS
incidents.summary: The crewmember felt fine, but later was showing signs of nausea, a contusion was beginning to show, some dizziness, and slight head pain behind the eyes. Because they were a contract crew, there were issues of taken him to the hospital from camp.
incidents.quote: A sawyer on a Type 2 IA crew was injured by a tree that had been fallen by another crewmember.

incidents.name: Bridge Fire Vehicle Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: While driving on the dirt road, the FC and WTO stopped to have a conversation with a strike team leader. The STEN approached the driver’s window of the utility vehicle and engaged in a conversation with the FC, at which time the FC put the utility vehicle into park. Approximately 50 feet away from the utility vehicle, an engine crew from the strike team was using a reel line to actively mop up a large fire damaged cedar tree. The FC and the STEN heard the firefighters in the area yell, “Tree, Tree, Tree.” None of them knew which direction the tree was falling; the STEN hunched down near the driver’s side door. Once the STEN determined the tree was falling in their direction the STEN then retreated toward the rear of the utility vehicle. While the STEN retreated to the rear of the utility vehicle, the FC put the utility vehicle in reverse to move out of the way of the falling tree.
incidents.quote: On Sunday September 7, 2014, at approximately 2100 hours, a CAL FIRE utility vehicle was struck by a falling tree within the fire perimeter causing major damage to the utility. The two occupants of the vehicle were uninjured.

incidents.name: Lodgepole Bucking Injury
incidents.summary: After the incident occured from bucking the pine tree, the employee made it to the hospital and the injuries sustained were an approximately six-inch deep laceration to his wrist and lower forearm area, and a fracture to the left lower leg bone.
incidents.quote: After the first bucking cut from the butt-end, the tree immediately sprung back and struck his lower legs, just above his boot tops. After “coming to” he realized that his chainsaw was still running and that his left forearm and wrist was resting upon the idling chainsaw.

incidents.name: Meadow Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: After a short time of being engaged, the saw team working with Squad One begins size-up of a burning snag located along the fire's edge. Next, due to safety concerns with this snag, overhead working in the area instructs the saw team to disengage the area of the snag. A short time later, while the saw team worked in the area, the burning snag cuts loose—on its own—at the base. The upper portion of the snag delivers a direct blow to a saw team member’s back and shoulder—knocking him to the ground. The injured individual remains conscious as his saw partner removes the portion of the tree that remained on top of him.
incidents.quote: The injured individual remains conscious as his saw partner removes the portion of the tree that remained on top of him.

incidents.name: Black Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On Saturday September 13, 2014, at approximately 1625 hours, a rapidly moving wildland fire burned over two local agency Type III engines and one CAL FIRE utility vehicle; destroying one of the two engines and the utility. The second engine sustained significant heat damage. Two local agency fire personnel suffered minor injuries, and were treated and released at a local medical facility. During the same fire run, firefighters on a CAL FIRE engine having to take refuge in a structure. The CAL FIRE engine sustained minor damage. The engine operator suffered minor injuries and was treated and released at a local medical facility.
incidents.quote: All of the structures along the ridge were threatened.

incidents.name: King Fire Entrapment CAL FIRE
incidents.summary: After deployement, the group was told a second fire front was coming and probably not survivable. So they exited their shelters, and ran with them using the shelters as shields to a safer location.
incidents.quote: Erratic fire behavior caused a Fire Captain, a dozer operator and ten inmates to deploy shelters.

incidents.name: Blackwater Ag Tractor Accident
incidents.summary: On September 16, 2014, at approximately 1351 hours, Forestry Technician (Fire) James Tod Adams, while using an agricultural tractor equipped with a side mounted boom axe mower to clear a fire break on the JD Tract of Blackwater NWR in Cambridge, Maryland, sustained personal injury to his lower right leg as the result of a log penetrating the cab through the lower left portion of the front windshield of the tractor.
incidents.quote: Tractor Accident Resulting in Injury to Service Personnel and Damage to Government Property

incidents.name: Tract 17 Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The moderate-complexity prescribed fire was conducted on a 60-acre grassland unit of the refuge to reduce hazardous fuel loadings and provide quality browse for ducks, geese, and other waterfowl. During blacklining operations, fire crept undetected across a wetline at the test fire location. The escaped fire grew quickly and exceeded the capabilities of on-site resources, eventually burning a total of 410 acres before being controlled by on-site and contingency resources.
incidents.quote: On September 17, 2014, a prescribed burn implemented by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) on Sacramento National Wildlife Refuge (NWR) escaped control lines and was declared a wildfire.

incidents.name: King Fire Entrapment USFS
incidents.summary: Meanwhile, on the Bridge… The DIVS felt he had two options: stay in the vehicle on the bridge or hike down to the river. The DIVS makes the decision to use the river as his Safety Zone and ride out the flame front in the river, under a rock.
incidents.quote: All that can be made out is “… trapped… bridge…” For the next hour, multiple attempts to contact DIVS are made by different resources—including Air Attack—all with no response.

incidents.name: Freezeout Ridge Fire Snag Incident
incidents.summary: He was extracted by emergency longline extraction, then flown to a hospital. The firefighter reached definitive medical care in a timely way, and survived the event.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on a remote wildland fire was struck by a snag as he was walking toward a work area. His injuries were severe and life threatening, and included skull and facial fractures, broken arms, and temporary loss of consciousness.

incidents.name: Hutton Fatality
incidents.summary: While working an outdoor fire call along Highway 165 South near the Pine Tree Boat Landing on Lake Wallace, Assistant Fire Chief Hutton fell ill and passed away from a nature and cause of injury still to be reported.

incidents.name: Dog Rock Fire Air Tanker Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: Witnesses reported seeing the accident, and one of them provided a video that was taken from a vantage point along a mountain trail that was above Tanker 81's flightpath. The video revealed that while on approach, Tanker 81 struck trees with its left wing. Following the impact with the trees, the airplane entered a descending left roll, and it then impacted on the top of an approximate 800-ft-tall rock cliff. A fire erupted during the impact, the airplane fragmented, and the main wreckage was projected over the cliff and scattered over a wide river valley below the cliff face.
incidents.quote: A CAL FIRE S-2T air tanker impacted a tree and crashed killing the pilot on the Dog Rock Fire.

incidents.name: Interstate 25 Tire Blowout
incidents.summary: A fire module from Saguaro National Park was driving on I-25 in Colorado, returning from an assignment to Rocky Mountain National Park. Near Castle Rock, CO, one of the vehicles, a Ford F-550, experienced a tire blowout. The vehicle was towed and there were no injuries.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1100, Bravo Truck, traveling 75 mph in the center lane of three-lane Interstate 25, experienced a left front tire blow out.

incidents.name: Upper Lyons RX Shelter Deployment
incidents.summary: Crews were burning off of a handline when a combination of factors aligned to cause several spot fires in heavy fuels outside the unit. These spot fires burned together to form multiple slopovers. A decision was made to suspend ignition until an assessment of the slopovers could be completed. At approximately that same time, a firefighter who was hiking up the fireline became entrapped due to intense heat and dense smoke. As a result, this firefighter deployed their fire shelter on the handline.
incidents.quote: During a RX burn operation, a firefighter lost control of his surroundings and was forced to deploy his shelter after his escape route was compromised.

incidents.name: Waterman Complex Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: Driving, Water Tender Incident or Accident
incidents.quote: Waterman Complex Water Tender Rollover

incidents.name: Sanders Fatality
incidents.summary: Sanders was treated immediately at the station by fellow responders and transported to Jane Phillips Hospital in Bartlesville, Oklahoma, and then on to St. Johns Hospital in Tulsa where he died January 29th from a stroke.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Sanders became ill and collapsed at the firehouse while responding to a grass fire call.

incidents.name: Compartment 65 Prescribed Fire Firing Operation
incidents.summary: As fire behavior increased near I, the fire was able to climb into the yaupon with the help of the needle-drape. As the fire behavior increased, stronger in-flow winds lifted the fire into the canopy which was composed of pole sized pine. The crown fire crossed the parish road into saw timber sized pine…the surface fire quickly followed. The understory had a very heavy load of needle-draped yaupon; this portion of C-65 has not been burned for a very long period due to the close proximity of a residence.
incidents.quote: A thorough briefing was conducted in the Work Center at 0900 on January 29. Resources depart and reported to assigned areas. The test fire was started at 1030 and resources began burning out base lines. Weather conditions were near what was expected.

incidents.name: Roy's Pig RX Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Burn Injury, Firing, Prescribed Fire, Burn Injury
incidents.quote: Roy's Pig RX Burn Injury

incidents.name: Drip Torch Leg Burn 2
incidents.summary: The firefighter had fired approximately one-half of the mile-long wet line when he became entangled in a thick patch of yaupon holly and vines. As the firefighter “crashed” his way through the thicket, the vines kept pulling the torch behind him. This resulted in ignited fuel being poured onto his right Nomex pant leg several times, he reached down to “pat” out the flames.
incidents.quote: “A burn injury is like cooking a steak. Once you remove the steak from the grill it keeps cooking until the meat is cooled down. I knew I needed to cool it down. So after I jumped in the creek to put the flames out, I stayed in the water to cool it.” The Injured Firefighter

incidents.name: UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: V1 started teetering from right to left. When the vehicle’s right tires finally touched the ground—because they were spinning at a rapid rate of speed—the wheels grabbed the ground quickly and V1 teetered to the right. The momentum made V1 roll to the right and do one complete revolution, landing back upright on its wheels. All three members unbuckled and got out of V1 to check on each other and to check out V1. There were no injuries to the firefighters nor damage to V1.
incidents.quote: The momentum made V1 roll to the right and do one complete revolution, landing back upright on its wheels.

incidents.name: Drip Torch Leg Burn 1
incidents.summary: Fire fighters carrying drip torches were igniting a unit using a dot firing technique in order to create a flanking fire, and one of them became entangled in green briar vines. While attempting to untangle, the fire fighter’s Nomex pants caught on fire. The result was a 5” x 6” burn on the back of the fire fighter’s left calf.
incidents.quote: While this is not a new concern for firefighters, it continues to cause issues.

incidents.name: Kisatchie NF Tree Strike
incidents.summary: Once the backcut was started, the Smokejumper used a wedge to push the snag over. The top of the snag cleared the closest green tree but encountered the branches from the second green tree. The snag broke approximately 25 feet above the stump. The top portion of the snag slingshot back towards the stump. The Smokejumper, after wedging the snag over, moved nearly straight back from the stump and watched the snag. As the snag broke and the top came back at the Smokejumper, he moved further away and roughly 45 degrees from the stump. The Smokejumper was struck by the top of the snag.
incidents.quote: On February 26, 2015, a module of four Smokejumpers were operating chainsaws in a burn unit on the Kisatchie National Forest. At 1510, a Smokejumper was struck in the head by a falling snag.

incidents.name: Pack Test Close Call
incidents.summary: Medical Emergency, Training, Health and Fitness, Medical or Exertion or Heat
incidents.quote: Pack Test Close Call

incidents.name: Bonner Fatality
incidents.summary: While on duty at Alma Helitack Base in Santa Clara County, California, Pilot Bonner was found deceased inside of his barracks from a cardiac related nature of fatal injury.

incidents.name: Prescribed Fire UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: Driving, ATV or UTV Accident
incidents.quote: RX UTV Rollover

incidents.name: Pile Burn Mop up RLS
incidents.summary: On March 20 the Trabuco Ranger District of the Cleveland National Forest implemented a pile burn along the South Main Divide Road. While this Rx burn was cut short due to unfavorable winds, many of the piles were ignited before the operation was cancelled. During the burn, the opportunity to utilize two different mop-up techniques side-by-side was applied. One pile was checked using water. The other was allowed to burn completely while being “stoked” using hand tools.
incidents.quote: Pile Burning Mop-Up Options

incidents.name: Engine Strikes Tree
incidents.summary: An engine pulled over to let a vehicle pass and when the engine resumes course, its passenger-side wheels are in the road ditch, which is soft due to previous rains. The airbags did not deploy.
incidents.quote: After traveling approximately 200 feet attempting to get out of the ditch, the vehicle suddenly regains traction and goes across the roadway—where it strikes a tree.

incidents.name: DeSoto Prescribed Fire Helicopter Accident Fatalities
incidents.summary: The acknowledgement of these flight conditions in agency guides likely affects the deliberate acceptance of a “low and slow” profile as necessary for the accomplishment of the mission. Over a period of time (4+ decades), confidence and acceptability of the flight parameters strengthens with each successful mission, along with a slight departure from the awareness of the hazards associated with the flight profiles.
incidents.quote: The PSD operator recalled they “were flying along 25-to-30 feet above the highest tree…things were going really well,” and they were nearly through the first bag of balls when he heard two alarm warning buzzers go off simultaneously or nearly so followed immediately by the pilot stating, “We lost power,” and FIRB saying, “We’re going in; we’re going in.”

incidents.name: Big Cypress Pack Test Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: It was the injured employee’s first attempt at an arduous level Pack Test. Although experiencing severe pain in his shins by the first ¼ mile, the injured employee elected to complete the course. After the pain in his shins intensified over the next 30–45 minutes, the injured employee accepted transportation to a local hospital which was approximately 40 minutes away. After recognizing that the injured employee’s symptoms might be associated with rhabdomyolysis FIRE personnel that had accompanied the employee to the hospital suggested this to the attending physician, who began tests for rhabdomyolysis via blood and urinalysis samples. After reviewing his blood test results the next morning, he was urged by his doctor to admit himself to the same hospital so that he could be placed under supervised care until his blood tests indicated his levels were returning to normal. He was treated and released 72 hours later to his primary care physician without further complications.
incidents.quote: The “Pack Test Rhabdomyolysis Incident” occurred within Big Cypress National Preserve (BICY) on March 31, 2015. One collateral duty BICY FIRE employee was afflicted with an illness called rhabdomyolysis after attempting a Work Capacity Test

incidents.name: CAL FIRE Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: The training bureau was providing a C234 Intermediate Firing Methodsclass with approximately 22 students from MVU. The class was completed at approximately 1700 hours, and all of the students and equipment were released. At approximately 1800 hours, a CAL FIRE fire apparatus engineer (FAE1), who was a student in the class, returned to their assigned fire station to complete their regular shift. At approximately 1930 hours, FAE1 experienced muscle fatigue and cramping in both arms. FAE1 was evaluated by a physician the following morning at Sharp Rees Stealy occupational medicine. FAE1 was admitted to Palomar Hospital and was subsequently treated for rhabdomyolysis.
incidents.quote: FAE Suffered from Rhabdomyolysis

incidents.name: Phoenix BLM Work Capacity Test Incident
incidents.summary: The WCT administator determined the individual was not going to be able to complete the test in the allotted time and the test was stopped. The administrator soon realized the individual ws experiencing labored breathing and severe lower leg cramps. The individual was immediately moved to a shady spot and provided hydration. The on scene EMT was notified and began assessing the individual's vital signs. The EMT decided the best practice would be to transport the individual by ambulance to the nearest hospital.
incidents.quote: Phoenix BLM Work Capacity Test Incident

incidents.name: Farm Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: On April 13th 2015 at approximately 2005 hrs, a firefighter from the BLM Canyon Country District suffered 1st and 2nd degree burns around the entire circumference of his calves and a small burn on his left wrist when he fell in a stump hole on the Farm Fire near the town of Green River Utah. The accident occurred at dusk and the area the firefighter was working in was covered in white ash and had burned very intensely.
incidents.quote: Realizing he had burned his legs, the firefighter immediately walked over to the Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) to report his injury.

incidents.name: Cold Brook Escaped RX / UTV Accident
incidents.summary: The escaped prescription fire was declared a wildfire, During the wildfire suppression actions, a Utility-Terrain-Vehicle (UTV) with an operator and passenger, tipped over. The two individuals were not injured and escaped safely, but the UTV was immediately overrun by the wildfire and declared a total loss. The loss of the equipment classifies this incident as a “Wildland Fire Accident”.
incidents.quote: On Monday, April 13, 2015 the Cold Brook Prescribed Fire, at Wind Cave National Park, South Dakota, escaped prescription.

incidents.name: Araujo Fatality
incidents.summary: Inmate Firefighter Araujo suffered a heart attack while engaged in a training exercise on the Morongo Indian Reservation near Banning, California. Araujo succumbed to his injury after being airlifted to a base camp where he was treated by CAL FIRE and Riverside County Fire Department medics.
incidents.quote: Training exercise results in Fatality

incidents.name: Light Duty Work Capacity Test
incidents.summary: On April 14, 2015, a Forest employee participated in the light duty work capacity test (a one-mile walk with no pack). During the test, the employee experienced pain in the lower legs believed to be “shin splints”. At a clinic the next day, the clinician consulted with the regional medical center and advised him to immediately proceed to the emergency room. His spouse drove him two and one-half hours to the regional medical center where he was positively diagnosed with compartment syndrome and underwent emergency surgery.
incidents.quote: "Reality hit when the doctor said they were going to slice my leg open."

incidents.name: Blacks Creek Smokejumping Accident
incidents.summary: At 1158 on April 15, 2015 an accident occurred during a BLM smokejumper parachute training mission south of Boise, Idaho. The accident occurred when the smokejumper involved landed in strong winds while his main canopy was misaligned with the wind line. The misalignment caused the smokejumper to experience a hard landing. The smokejumper sustained a broken right humerus, dislocated right shoulder, with structural damage to the right shoulder, and a fractured rib upon landing.
incidents.quote: On April 15th, three loads of jumpers were scheduled to do their first refresher jumps of the year. This was the second jump refresher session for the Great Basin Smokejumpers for 2015.

incidents.name: Tree Bind Broken Leg
incidents.summary: While clearing out roads and cutting downed trees after a significant wind event, the dozer swamper got his vehicle stuck in a bind of a 7” tree. With the assistance from the dozer to help remove the vehicle, the tree bind increased, so the swamper used a chainsaw to release the tension on the log. Upon examination by the ER physician it became evident the sweeping motion of the tree released with enough force to break both the tibia and fibula in three places.
incidents.quote: Approximately half way through the release cut, the “top” violently snapped from a side bind striking the individual in the left shin just below the knee, swept him off his feet and carried him approximately 6 feet backwards.

incidents.name: Mud Lake Complex FLA
incidents.summary: The management of the Mud Lake Complex is a success story.For Big Cypress National Preserve and its fire managers, getting their firefighters to shift their way of thinking from the “old”—full suppression on every wildfire to the “new”—full control on some fires, confine/contain on others—will be an ongoing challenge. It could very well take a generation of firefighters to fully change the way in which they look at and manage fire on the landscape. The Mud Lake Complex proved to be an important step forward in this ongoing evolution. This incident will now provide many future lessons for the Preserve—as well as for any fire management program.
incidents.quote: “I was constantly going back and forth internally asking myself if we are doing the right thing. I tried to stay focused on the strategy in place and reminded myself of three things: Patience, Perseverance, and Fortitude.” J.D. Lee, Acting Superintendent Big Cypress National Preserve

incidents.name: Double Diamond Fire Review
incidents.summary: “At 1615 I came over the crest of the hill and saw fire crossing the road, I expected it to slow down but the pulse never quit. I knew direct attack would be unsuccessful and we needed to start evacuations immediately.” -Taskforce Leader
incidents.quote: On May 11th 2014, Mother’s Day, at 15:59 a call came in to the Hutchinson County Emergency Operations Center (EOC) about a wildfire in Fritch Texas. Twelve hours later 368 structures were destroyed.

incidents.name: Deschutes NF Work Capacity Test Incident
incidents.summary: On May 13th, 2015, the Deschutes National Forest administered a Work Capacity Fitness Test (light, moderate and arduous Pack Test, from now on referred to as “Pack Test”) in the Bend metro area. The incident that unfolded highlights the work the local unit did to prepare for medical emergencies, and may offer some ideas to other units around the country.
incidents.quote: Things happen. You just can’t foolproof everything.

incidents.name: Back Creek Fire Electrical Burn
incidents.summary: On May 15, 2015 a firefighter received electrical injuries during mop-up operations while walking near a sagging and energized power line. His injuries were severe and life threatening, and included electrical burns of the shoulder, arm and both feet. Electricity arced through his body entering through his shoulder and exiting through both feet to the ground. The firefighter was treated on site by a fire line EMT. He was extracted from the fire on a backboard, transported to a community hospital by ambulance, and later life-flighted to a level one trauma and burn center.
incidents.quote: "When we found that bear, the whole thing changed. If we had not found that bear, students would have never come over there.”

incidents.name: Boise NF Work Capacity Test Incident
incidents.summary: At approximately 09:45 the WCT began. Course monitors checked in with the WCT administrator as participants passed their spots at the ¼ mile and ½ mile. At approximately 10:10 employee was approximately 50 yards from the start point/turn around on his second lap. The WCT administrator and EMT noticed that the employee was struggling. The EMT ran to the employee and took his pack test vest off and made a quick assessment that the employee needed help. The EMT loaded the employee into his work truck and took him to the local Cascade ER.
incidents.quote: Upon further evaluation at the Boise hospital, it was determined that the employee had suffered a heart attack.

incidents.name: Willow Peak Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter received serious burns after gasoline sprayed out of a chainsaw gas tank and ignited. The saw became hot during saw operations so the firefighter had set it aside to cool for a few minutes. After it would not restart, he opened the fuel tank. A “fuel geyser” erupted from the tank.
incidents.quote: A “Fuel Geyser” Erupts from Chainsaw Tank.

incidents.name: Fuels Project Brush Cutter Injury
incidents.summary: While clearing vegetation during a recent fuel reduction project in this area of the Park, a seasonal Forestry Technician is injured when he unknowingly hits a discarded crab trap—which was obscured by vegetation—with the brush cutter he’s operating. A piece of the crab trap is propelled into the Forestry Technician’s right upper arm. He is unaware of the extent of his injury until an X-ray reveals the embedded debris in his arm.
incidents.quote: He shuts off the brush cutter and removes his Nomex shirt to find a small puncture wound that is bleeding slightly on his right upper arm.

incidents.name: Burn Injury through Nomex
incidents.summary: During live fire training at a local military base, two engine modules were engaged in mobile attack with a firefighter at the front of each engine using a 25-foot length of hose attached to the front bumper discharge. (See photo on right.) Both module leaders were nearby providing oversight to the operations and had nearly hooked the head of the fire when two firefighters received burn injuries to their elbows.
incidents.quote: Neither firefighter initially knew they had been burned—but later experienced discomfort and blistering on their elbows.

incidents.name: CAL FIRE Academy Dozer Accident
incidents.fire: CAL FIRE Heavy Fire Equipment Operator (HFEO) Academy #41
incidents.summary: On June 3, 2015, an HFEO academy was being held in conjunction with a Vegetation Management Program (VMP) treatment in TCU. At approximately 1800 hours, a CAL FIRE bull dozer (D3140) operated by a cooperating agency employee was constructing a dozer line downhill. Measurements taken using a clinometer indicate slopes of 20 and 45 percent along the dozer line. The dozer operator was the second in line of two dozers, improving a dozer line under the supervision of an adjunct instructor. During this operation, D3140 became unstable while stuck on a rock. The dozer rolled one and one quarter times downhill and came to rest on D3140’s right side. The operator suffered a small contusion above the right brow and a laceration on the right forearm requiring nine sutures. The operator didn’t suffer any loss of consciousness.
incidents.quote: Heavy Fire Equipment Operations Academy #41 Dozer Accident

incidents.name: Wyoming Work Capacity Test
incidents.summary: An employee taking the arduous Work Capacity Test experienced an asthma attack that resulted in difficulty breathing. The patient was transported via ambulance to the local medical clinic and then to the St. Johns Hospital in Jackson for further evaluation and monitoring.

incidents.name: Buenos Aires WCT Fatality
incidents.summary: At approximately 0800 hours on June 6, 2015, a 31 year old Student Conservation Association (SCA) employee, Veteran Fire Corps crewmember, collapsed 200 yards from the finish line while participating in the Wildland Firefighter Work Capacity Test. Medical care was immediately rendered by on-site, local EMS including the utilization of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). The individual was loaded in the Ambulance, which had been staged on-site for the test, within 5 minutes of his collapse and transported to an Advanced Care Facility.
incidents.quote: A Wildland Firefighter collapsed with a medical emergency 200 yards from the finish line while participating in the Wildland Firefighter Work Capacity Test.

incidents.name: Dry Creek Fire Chainsaw Near Miss
incidents.summary: After hiking approximately 30 minutes into the fire, the sawyer attempted to start the chainsaw. The saw sputtered a few times but did not stay running. The sawyer turned the saw tank upright to check the fuel level in the saw. The sawyer estimates he was approximately 11 feet down slope from the fire's smoldering edge. When the sawyer opened the saw cap, an immediate burst of fuel sprayed out of the tank under pressure.
incidents.quote: When the sawyer opened the saw cap, an immediate burst of fuel sprayed out of the tank under pressure.

incidents.name: Idaho BLM Physical Training Fatality
incidents.summary: Fire Operations Supervisor Sonner collapsed after he and his fire crew finished physical training at the Hammett Guard Station, Idaho. Fellow firefighters initiated medical treatment on scene but Sonner succumbed to a nature and cause of fatal injury still to be reported.
incidents.quote: An Idaho BLM firefighter had a fatal medical event after completing Physical Training run.

incidents.name: UTV Training Accident
incidents.summary: During an ATV/UTV training, two students were operating a Polaris Ranger XP 900 over the training course and struck a rock causing he UTV to roll over. No injuries were reported. Both trainees were wearing seat belts, helmets and all required PPE. Damage to the rear end and tailgate are visible and additional inspection may reveal more damage. The Safety Officer is conducting a Review and will get an inspection of the UTV. A 72 hour report will be generated.
incidents.quote: On June 12, 2015 at approximately 1500 two BLM fire and aviation employees who were participating in a training session for UTV and ATV operation were involved in an accident involving a UTV.

incidents.name: Cattail Fire UTV Destroyed
incidents.summary: As the Firefighters put the UTV in gear, it died. They restarted the UTV and placed it in gear only for it to die again. At this point, the firefighters decided to abandon the UTV and leave the area on foot.
incidents.quote: During burnout operations two Firefighters experienced a shift and increase in the winds, then decided to jump into the UTV to leave the area, when the UTV decided to not work.

incidents.name: Seed Orchard Run Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: Medical providers initially were not sure what his diagnosis was, and several days into his care his medical status started to worsen. He was transferred to a larger medical center for more specialty care and the preliminary diagnosis has been heat illness. The FF has some degree of kidney and liver failure and the future of that is not known. As of the date of this report, he continues to receive advanced medical care for the conditions that led to this incident.
incidents.quote: After a few days of showing heat related symptoms during normal workdays during a less strenuous PT run, a Firefighter started to wobble and his condition declined rapidly until he was unconscious.

incidents.name: Aggie Creek Fire Chainsaw Fuel Geyser
incidents.summary: One of the saw teams started up their saw (Stihl MS460) and noticed that the saw ran sluggish and was not wrapping out as usual. The sawyer stepped back from the fires black edge and opened the cap to visually inspect the fuel tank when a fuel geyser happened. The tank was 3/4 full of fuel. The sawyer was sprayed in fuel on his nomex shirt, gloves, and his face. The sawyer was wearing BUGZ goggles at the time this happened and suffered fuel to the eyes. The sawyer was treated with eye flushing by the crew EMT and a CA-1 was also filled out and filed with SMIS as precautionary measure. The Sawyer did not suffer any injury and there was no fire as result of the fuel geyser.
incidents.quote: Chainsaw fuel geyser incident

incidents.name: Case Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: On Friday, July 3, 2015, at approximately 1835 hours, an 18.8 inch diameter oak tree limb fell onto a Tulare Unit firefighter I (FF1) and two Mountain Home fire crew inmates (IM1 and IM2) FF1, IM1 and IM2 were mopping up a wildland fire ignited by lightning. FF1 was pinned under the limb and suffered major injuries; IM1 and IM2 suffered minor to moderate injuries. FF1 was air lifted to Community Regional Medical Center (CRMC) trauma center in Fresno with major traumatic injuries. IM1 and IM2 were air lifted to a landing zone and transferred to ground ambulances and transported to a local hospital. They were treated and released back to CDCR.
incidents.quote: Firefighter and Fire Crew Inmate Injuries

incidents.name: Burn Injury Follow Up
incidents.summary: On July 11 while conducting ignition operations on a prescribed fire, one of the firefighters stopped igniting for a short period of time during which a patch of short grass flamed up behind the firefighter. The flames briefly grazed the leg of the firefighter’s pants—burning the calf of the firefighter’s right leg. Four days later, the employee showed another employee the burn, at which point it was brought to the supervisor’s attention. During the period between when the burn occurred and it was made known to the supervisor, the employee had been caring for the burn without medical supervision. The employee was taken to a medical care facility to have the burn examined. It was determined to be a second degree burn. The employee was given care instructions and was able to return to normal duties that same day.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Continues Ignitions—Unaware of the Extent of the Burn

incidents.name: Stanislaus NF Type 3 Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: The Engine had just left town after breakfast to rendezvous with the STEN for the AM briefing. As the engine traveled through a intersection, a previously unseen SUV suddenly tried to pass the engine on the right. Quickly running out of pavement, the SUV—now in the dirt shoulder—turned into the engine, hitting it in the right front wheel.
incidents.quote: "I must have blacked out because the next thing I remember was waking up not knowing where I was … I went for the door… all I saw was dirt and glass...I could hear a gurgling sound as if it were water or possibly fuel… and a Firefighter screaming."

incidents.name: Drone Interferes with Initial Attack
incidents.summary: As I crest the ridge, I only have a shallow drainage to cross—in which the fire has established itself just below me and is making a strong push towardthe homes. At that moment, emergency traffic airs over command frequency that all aircraft have been grounded due to a drone sighted in the fire area. As the fire advances, I make eye contact with the property owner across the drainage.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1430 hours, a report is radioed to Dispatch of a 1/4-acre vegetation fire located directly behind our Mill Creek Fire Station. Stepping outside the office, my swamper and I see heavy smoke to the north of the compound. We quickly make our way to the transport to off-load the dozer and engage the fire.

incidents.name: Blasting Hazard Tree
incidents.summary: Three Class C Fallers looked at the tree. All agreed hand felling was not an option, they declined the falling operation. Due to these concerns, blasting was suggested as an option. After a short discussion with the Duty Officer, an order was placed for a regional blasting team. Given the lack of urgency or potential for fire spread, the order was placed for the morning of day 4—two days later—to allow for adequate preparation.
incidents.quote: While the advantage to this explosive is that it is very unlikely to ignite the surrounding vegetation on fire, it’s effectiveness at blasting trees was unknown.

incidents.name: Gregg Creek Broken Leg / Extraction
incidents.summary: “Hole.” “Hold?” “No! Hole!” Mica said as he turned to clarify. He turned back around and took a long step to avoid the identified hazard. Even so, he felt his right leg drop into the hole—which was partially obscured by foliage. His left leg bent at an unnatural angle as he fell into a hole much larger than he had perceived. This wasn’t good. He was in an extreme amount of pain, hours up the trail on a steep slope. It was getting dark. Everyone knows the next best option is to order a short-haul helicopter for the morning. As soon as it is light, sawyers go to work improving the helispot and the short-haul helicopter is able to extract Mica.
incidents.quote: Due to concerns over safety for everyone on the fire—especially considering the snags in the area—the decision to abort the hoist operation is made. As the helicopter flies away, the firefighters feel a surprising sense of relief.

incidents.name: Medevac Problems with Tree Strike Injury
incidents.summary: At 1623 hours—approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes from the initial injury—the light helicopter lands on the fire and drops off the backboard. The on-scene Medic packages the patient while the Zone Helicopter isenroute. The Zone Helicopter retrieves the injured patient and arrives back in Galena at 1715 hours along with the on-scene Medic and a liaison (a member of the patient’s home crew from Boise, Idaho). The air ambulance is there waiting for them.
incidents.quote: This helicopter responds—under the assumption that this is a request for a medical transport, not medevac—and arrives on the fire without a backboard.

incidents.name: Lowell Fire Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: Three U.S. Forest Service firefighters were scouting the division in the immediate vicinity of three CAL FIRE engine crews who were patrolling the fire’s edge. The firefighters observed an increase in fire activity below their location. A decision was made by all firefighters to relocate themselves and their equipment to a safer area. As they attempted to relocate, they were overrun by fire. Four firefighters suffered burn injuries, two utility vehicles were destroyed and one engine was damaged.
incidents.quote: On July 26, 2015, at approximately 1620 hours, two CAL FIRE and two U.S. Forest Service firefighters suffered burn injuries while battling the Lowell Fire.

incidents.name: Cold Trailing Burn Injury
incidents.summary: During cold trailing operations on the Bitter Creek Fire, the crewmember was assigned to grid for hot spots along the heel of the fire.The heel of the fire was located within the steep slopes and rocky terrain of the Little Bitter Creek drainage. While cold trailing, the firefighter lost his footing and fell forward, attempted to catch himself, and put his right ungloved (for cold trailing) hand into a hot ash pit.
incidents.quote: Cold trailingpresents a challenge because hands are exposed to potential burns.

incidents.name: Frog Fire Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: On the evening of July 30, 2015, Engine Captain Dave Ruhl was entrapped and killed while scouting on foot during initial attack of the Frog Fire on the Modoc National Forest
incidents.quote: Casey and Alex waited at the heel of the fire, feeling frustrated that Dave wasn’t there yet. They couldn’t raise him on the radio. Where was Dave?

incidents.name: Scale Fire Retardant Drop
incidents.summary: Both crew members received minor injuries (burns) as a result of the incident. The firefighter's injuries were evaluated in the field; one crew member was transported by ground to a regional medical center for further evaluation and released that day.
incidents.quote: During IA operations,two engine crew members were directly hit by a retardant drop from an Airtanker.

incidents.name: Watson Butte Smokejumper Injury
incidents.summary: The second jumper hit the ground hard 5-7 feet behind the seated jumper and went into a right side roll. Strong momentum carried the jumper forward. In the process of rolling,he ran into his jump partner. This collision was described as being “just like a football hit”—the right side of his helmet and right shoulder smashed into the other jumper’s back.
incidents.quote: The Life Flight medics told the injured smokejumper in flight they were thoroughly impressed with the level of his care and packaging.

incidents.name: Pacific Southwest Wire Strike Incident
incidents.summary: After filling the tank, the helicopter initiated forward flight and began climbing and accelerating out of the reservoir and towards the fire. The pilot did not see the unmarked black communication wire and silver cable, and collided with the wires at about 50 knots and 50 ft. AGL.
incidents.quote: A Bell 205A-1, made an emergency landing after striking a communication wire that stretched across San Gabriel Reservoir on the Angeles National Forest.

incidents.name: Cabin Fire Main Rotor Strike
incidents.summary: The crew performed a precautionary landing in a field located approximately 10 minutes away from the dip site. The Helicopter Manager was notified of the situation via cell phone. After shut down was complete, the pilots inspected the main rotor blade damage. Maintenance inspectors determined the main rotor blades, rotor head, transmission and high speed shafts required replacement. The NTSB determined the blade strike as an "Incident”, and it was further classified by the Forest Service as an “Incident with Potential”.
incidents.quote: While in the dip, the PIC heard what he suspected was a blade strike, called out the strike, jettisoned the water and immediately initiated a climb out to get clear of the area.

incidents.name: Tail Rotor Strike
incidents.summary: The pilot did not feel or hear the strike, but the helicopter manager and crew on the adjacent hill heard an abnormal “whack, whack” like a rotor blade had struck “something”.
incidents.quote: The technique to lift the snorkel off the ground, without dragging and damaging it on the rocks, involves lifting the snorkel hose off the ground while maneuvering slightly backwards.

incidents.name: Vehicle Rollover in the Dust
incidents.summary: As the vehicle’s tires run along the edge of the right shoulder, the soft material gives way. The vehicle rolls off the road, ending up on its top. Thankfully, there are no injuries.
incidents.quote: As the driver negotiates a turn, the vehicle suddenly enters a large dust cloud. The driver says that conditions quickly become similar to that of a “white out”. Almost all visibility is lost.

incidents.name: Sierra Fire Tree Strike Incident
incidents.summary: Discussion ensued about whether to complete the fireline directly under the danger tree. The CRWB was uneasy about taking this action. She had been personally connected to a previous tree-strike incident and was conflicted about whether her uncertainty concerning the wisdom of the decision to work under this tree was due to the earlier experience or discomfort with the current situation.
incidents.quote: The IC told them to take off their packs to increase their mobility since “danger trees are above you all the time.”

incidents.name: Humboldt Complex Tree Felling Accident
incidents.summary: An inmate fire crew member (SAW2), fell a tree parallel to the fireline instead of the intended lay, perpendicular to the fireline, and struck another inmate fire crew member (SAW1). The tree struck SAW1 on the head. The tree was six inches in diameter at breast height (DBH), and 18 feet tall. Examination of the stump revealed the holding wood had been cut all the way through.
incidents.quote: On August 10, 2015, at approximately 2139 hours, a CAL FIRE inmate fire crew member was struck by a felled tree while constructing fireline on the Pine Incident.
