incidents.quote: As the engine rolled to its right, windows splintered and shattered, debris ricocheted inside the cab and metal crumpled. The engine came to rest upside down against several oak trees. Everything in the cab came to a stop. A muffled and intermittently eerie buzzing came from the horn. Water hissed.

incidents.name: Eagle Creek Fire Camp Crud
incidents.summary: Due to its annual recurrence, Camp Crud tends to be seen as something wildland firefighters and support personnel endure as a normal hazard of the job. However, you should know that there are preventive measures you can use to help eliminate or reduce the incidents of Camp Crud affecting you or the fire community.
incidents.quote: Plaguing Wildland Firefighters Year After Year . . .

incidents.name: Sheep Gap Fire Heavy Equipment Burnover
incidents.summary: A Heavy Equipment Task Force consisting of two feller bunchers, a dozer, and a skidder were working on Division Zulu of the Sheep Gap Fire on the Lolo National Forest. Fire behavior prompted retreat to their designated safety zone 9 miles away. Air Attack eventually recommended they abandon slow moving equipment and evacuate personnel. All personnel were successfully evacuated. The abandoned equipment was destroyed by the fire.
incidents.quote: "When you start seeing 1,000-hour fuels burning completely, that's a good indicator it's a red flag."

incidents.name: Uno Peak Fire Boulder Near Miss
incidents.summary: On Saturday September 16, the Uno Peak Fire had begun to transition into rehab and repair operations. The three trucks and members of a 20-person crew drove a short distance down Road 8200 to load an additional stack of hose. This hose was located where the fire line crossed the road. Approximately 180 feet above this area where the hose was located, an excavator was busy rehabbing a section of fire line, which created a large amount of dust. It was at this point that the excavator dislodged a large boulder that rolled down the hill, passing between the two trucks. Fortunately, it did not strike any people or equipment.
incidents.quote: It was at this point that the excavator dislodged a large boulder that rolled down the hill, passing between the two trucks.

incidents.name: Rapid Extraction Module Support RLS
incidents.summary: The goal of this Rapid Lesson Sharing (RLS) is to provide information to Fire Managers, Incident Management Teams, and Ground and Aerial Resources about Rapid Extraction Module Support (REMS). This information, “feedback from the field,” was gathered through interviews with REMS, members of Incident Management Teams, and crews from multiple states assigned to fires in Oregon and Northern California. This RLS is intended to communicate these ongoing efforts to aid in the safe and effective use of this module.
incidents.quote: “The most important things are timing,speed, and not caring who gets the credit.” Director of Wildland Operations, Advanced Life Support – Rapid Extraction Module (ALS REM)Phoenix, Arizona

incidents.name: Kelsey/Jones Fire Faller Hit by Branch
incidents.summary: A contract faller was struck by an 8” diameter limb while felling a tree. The faller was ground transported to the IMT medical unit, then referred to a local hospital. The faller was treated and released from the local hospital on the same day. He will miss 3-5 days of work.

incidents.name: Oregon Dual Wheels Engine Incident
incidents.summary: An engine was traveling south on State Highway 78 near Princeton, Oregon. They were returning back to station at Burns Junction from a two-week fire assignment. As the Operator felt a change in driving characteristics in the engine handling, a wheel from the driver-side rear duals passed them and came to rest in an agricultural field. The second wheel came off and crossed the northbound lane into a sage flat. The Operator did not immediately apply brakes—but calmly maintained the engine in the highway lane—and was able to safely maneuver the vehicle to the right side of the highway into a driveway, out of traffic.
incidents.quote: A wheel from the driver-side rear duals passed them and came to rest in an agricultural field. The second wheel came off and crossed the northbound lane in to a sage flat.

incidents.name: AQ Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: A forecasted cold frontal passage brought high winds, which lofted an ember midway up the slope, and across the drainage to the south of AQ east (closed canopy conifer stand). This spot torched a tree, which lofted more embers to a south aspect, where it ignited flashy fuels. Crews remobilized for point protection. At this time fire was burning at a moderate rate of spread within the flashy fuels on the south slope. Additional Resources were ordered at this time. Notifications to the Duty Officer and Agency Administrator were made. Eventually the fire reached a small section of private land. Resource damage amounted to burned grass (20Acres). Notification to the land owner was made, and the Burn was declared a wildfire.
incidents.quote: It was found that the notification process for declaring a wildfire was not fully understood or followed.

incidents.name: Liberty Fire Excavator Tip Over
incidents.summary: The excavator worked the dozer line successfully. However, while making his way back down the slope, he lost traction and started to slide. The Operator attempted to stop the slide by setting his boom on the ground—but forward momentum carried him over his bucket and the thumb of his bucket got stuck under the excavator blade. This resulted in the machine tipping over on its side and trapping the operator inside the cab. The IC took a tactical pause with all operations while they developed a plan to rescue the tipped over machinery using another excavator. They successfully had the excavator upright and back on its tracks by mid-afternoon.
incidents.quote: After evaluating the line, the Operator said he could complete the line working upslope.

incidents.name: Johnson Ridge Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The Moab-Monticello Ranger District was completing a prescribed fire in the Johnson Creek–Nizhoni Prescribed Burn Project Area. Shortly after burning operations ceased, two spot fires were discovered on the adjacent slope, outside of the project area. Attempts to suppress the spot fires that night and the next day were ultimately unsuccessful. The Johnson Ridge Wildfire was declared on October 13, 2017
incidents.quote: “I was thinking, ‘Why are we burning this?’ but did not verbalize this because of the success our district prescribed burning program has had in recent years and the level of trust and comfort I have with my district fire personnel.” –District Ranger

incidents.name: Virginia Work Capacity Test Rhabdo Case
incidents.summary: A Virginia Department of Forestry (VDOF) part-time wildland firefighter reported feeling unwell after taking the ardous work capacity test. He initially attributed his symptoms to an improperly fitted vest and not proper hydration.
incidents.quote: I usually spend a couple months preparing for the test, but this year my full-time job required a lot of travel and I hadn’t been as prepared as normal.

incidents.name: Nuns Fire Water Tender Fatality
incidents.summary: On October 16, 2017, at 0650 hours, a vehicle accident occurred involving a private water tender assigned to the Southern LNU Complex fire in Napa County, California. The accident occurred on the Oakville Grade Road approximately one mile from the top of the grade.
incidents.quote: A water tender was traveling down a grade when the vehicle went off the roadway and rolled over onto its top resulting in a fatal injury to the driver.

incidents.name: Brian Head Fire BAER Fatality
incidents.summary: Bryan Burr, 58, was killed Saturday October 7 during Burned Area Emergency Response (BAER) operations on the Brian Head Fire in southwest Utah. Mr. Burr, from Alpine, Utah, was giving directions to a helicopter dropping straw mulch when he was struck on the head.
incidents.quote: Man killed during mulch operation when he was struck on the head by dropped straw mulch or debris from a nearby tree as the straw fell.

incidents.name: Nuns Fire Engine Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On the Nuns Fire, California, on the morning of October 18 at approximately 1145, during mop up operations, a large (60-inch DBH) fire-weakened, green Douglas fir tree fell from upslope, at a 90 degree angle, and landed across the hood of an engine that was parked on the road below with two people inside.
incidents.quote: “You just don't look at a green tree with smoke at the base with green stuff all around it and think to yourself that this thing’s coming down any second."

incidents.name: Mendocino Lake Complex Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: On October 19, 2017, at approximately 1800 hours, an Orange County FF/Medic was involved in a single vehicle rollover. The driver was assigned to the Mendocino Lake Complex in Mendocino County, California as a Helicopter Crew Member (HECM). The vehicle was traveling southbound on Highway 101 and began to transition onto Highway 37 when the vehicle lost traction and left the roadway. The driver was wearing his seatbelt and attempted to extricate himself but was unable due to injuries. The driver of the vehicle was transported to Navato Community Hospital for evaluation and treatment of a fractured collar bone and minor laceration. The driver was released from the hospital later that night.

incidents.name: Coyote Prescribed Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Six igniters on an Arizona prescribed fire were entrapped and forced to walk through flame and heat when firing patterns converged and cut off their escape route.
incidents.quote: As progress was made from north to south Firing group #1 held up their burn to let firing group #2 tie into their fire before moving to another section of the burn area. Additionally a fenceline slowed down some of the interior burners close to the tie in point. As the rest of the burners progressed a horseshoe occurred in the middle that cut off the interior burners separating the burn group into two groups with the horseshoe in between. As progress was made toward Group #1 fire/tie in point 6 of the burners from Group#2 were cut off from their escape route and they were forced to walk through fire/heat to get out to the road and safety. Burners along the road had brought fire too close to the tie in point and before the burners could get to the road the lines of fire had grown together and created a barrier to the road. The time of this occurrence was around 0230 on the 26th.

incidents.name: Michigan Work Capacity Test Heart Attack
incidents.summary: The patient cleared his Health Screening Questionnaire (HSQ) and had his own physical exam two weeks prior to the WCT. During lap number 9 he wasn’t looking well and seemed to be working hard. The WCT administrator and medical personnel on-scene were watching him closely. As he started the 12th and final lap he was short of breath and staggering. Medical personnel on-scene moved quickly toward him as he went down. They called 911 and had him transported to the hospital. It was determined that he had a minor heart attack. The patient was kept in the hospital for a few days and then released.
incidents.quote: The patient was an AD employee, 67 years old taking the Arduous Work Capacity Test.

incidents.name: Ponderosa Pile Escape Review
incidents.summary: On the evening of December 4th, 2017, a localized wind event known as a “Mono wind” descended upon the Sierra National Forest, Bass Lake Ranger District, in the general area of Cascadel Woods. This area is situated approximately three miles to the east of North Fork, CA. Sustained winds between 25-30 mph with gusts to 55 mph caused a prescribed fire in the Whiskey Ridge Fuel Break system to leave the unit area boundary. District personnel on scene with concurrence of the local agency administrator made the decision to declare the prescribed pile burn a wildfire.
incidents.quote: “The burn plan, overall, is acceptable in its rational and is consistent with (IFIPIPG). It is difficult to assess for all potential outcomes, however, I believe that success of burn plan implementation hinges on the execution and thoroughness to make sound judgements when implementing".

incidents.name: Creek Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: A Los Angeles Fire Department (LFD) Heavy Equipment Operator (HEO) while operating a D-8R Dozer (DZ11) was involved in a significant rollover while maneuvering on a ridgeline, adjacent to the Ebey Herreres Truck Trail. The HEO initiated a "Mayday" and self-extricated DZ11 with injuries.
incidents.quote: The operational area had varying degrees of visibility due to increased fire behavior.

incidents.name: Thomas Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: The fire made a significant run to the west. Four handcrews, 2 Type 6 engines and 2 Crew Strike Team Leaders took refuge in and around a clearing. One Emergency Crew Transport (ECT) sustained minor damage. No injuries were sustained during the event. A local government dozer and all-terrain vehicle (ATV), staged in a different but proximal Temporary Refuge Area (TRA) were impacted by the fire and sustained significant damage. The operators of the dozer and ATV were off-duty for the night. Approximately 1 hour later and 3 miles to the southwest, an excavator, staged for the night, was also destroyed by fire.
incidents.quote: A "Near Serious Accident"

incidents.name: Oklahoma VFD Vehicle Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On 12/11/17, Sunrise Volunteer Firefighter Charles Fisher was involved in a traffic accident while in route to the Sunrise Fire Station in response to a radio page out requesting mutual aid assistance to the Weleetka Fire Department. This page out was in response to a reported grass fire.
incidents.quote: Oklahoma VFD Vehicle Accident Fatality

incidents.name: Thomas Fire Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: A Fire Apparatus Engineer and 4 Fire Fighters from a Strike Team were engaged in the placement of a hoselay in support of a dozer line with fire established above the line. While attempting to suppress spot fires below the dozer line, a Fire Apparatus Engineer became entrapped and suffered fatal injuries.
incidents.quote: At 10:05 AM, the Fire Captain notified the Strike Team leader that he had located the Fire Apparatus Engineer, who was deceased, with no shelter deployment. He was found in a deep gulch, below his last seen position.

incidents.name: Thomas Fire Hazmat Mitigation
incidents.summary: An engine task force assigned to the Ojai/Oakview Division on the Thomas Fire was requested to apply large amounts of water and high concentrations of Class A foam to a known smoldering crude oil seep fire. The area of concern would have required an extensive hose lay through partially burned ground cover and a heavy over-story of green oak trees. This created difficult access and egress from noxious smoke emitting from burning oil.
incidents.quote: After a full discussion as well as consultation with subject matter experts, due to potential hazardous chemical exposure, the Task Force declines this mission and presents an alternative solution.

incidents.name: Toms Mill Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On 12/9/2017 at approximately 1030 a contract firefighter from the PatRick 20B Crew was struck by the butt of a tree he was felling.
incidents.quote: The spotter and another coworker who was posted as the road guard saw the tree falling and as it was falling it did a “Barber Chair” movement and struck the IM in his right side with the butt of the tree.

incidents.name: Work Capacity Test Cardiac Incident
incidents.summary: During an arduous level Work Capacity Test (WCT), a National Park Service Law Enforcement Ranger (LE), who is a militia firefighter, fell off pace to the point he decided to quit the test at the 1.5 mile point. He received assistance in removing his weighted vest and took a seat on the ground. The WCT Administrator and on scene EMT checked to confirm he was okay, at which point the LE said he had chest pains from breathing the cold air. The LE was transported and admitted to the hospital. It was determined that the LE had suffered some level of cardiac incident.
incidents.quote: How Do You Know if Someone is Medically Cleared to Take the Work Capacity Test?

incidents.name: Gallinas RX Review
incidents.summary: The snow across the project area melted rapidly which resulted in prescribed fire spreading away from the piles, but well within the project area. The district had a presence throughout the fall and responded appropriately to areas of concern. This strategy resulted in a long duration event. In late fall, a portion of the prescribed fire crossed into an area where fire was not desired within the unit. December 29th the decision was made to suppress this portion of the prescribed fire, and on January 18th the same portion of the prescribed fire was converted to a wildfire due to unwanted fire effects. This decision was made due to the potential for ash to enter the municipal watershed degrading water quality and community relations.
incidents.quote: In early October the Pecos/Las Vegas district, Santa Fe National Forest initiated the Gallinas prescribed fire in the municipal watershed for the city of Las Vegas, NM.

incidents.name: Kisatchie NF Prescribed Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: On January 24, 2018, the Kisatchie National Forest conducted an 883acre prescribed fire. During baseline firing operations, a snag burned through at the base. This snag fell and struck a Squad Leader on the back and left shoulder, driving the Squad Leader into the ground.
incidents.quote: “All I could do was brace for the hit. There was no time to getout of the way.”

incidents.name: Puerto Rico Pack Test Fatality
incidents.summary: On January 26, 2018 the Puerto Rico Fire Department conducted a work capacity test for those members of the interagency wildland fire program who had received the approval of the medical test that authorizes them to take the WCT. During the test, firefighter Omar Vega Rivera collapsed, hitting the ground with his face without raising his hands to break his fall. Responders immediately began to administer CPR, and subsequently transported to the hospital emergency room with a Fire Department vehicle. CPR continued at the hospital, where Rivera was eventually pronounced dead after 55 minutes of resuscitation efforts.
incidents.quote: On the sixth lap (of 12), firefighter Omar Vega Rivera passes in front of the registration table, when FF Efraín Cardona told him he was doing well, to which the firefighter Omar Vega replied "ok, in the next you give me Water".

incidents.name: Compartment 4 Escaped Prescribed Fire Review
incidents.summary: As the prescribed fire was nearing completion, the helicopter overflew the southern fireline and several aerial ignition spheres were inadvertently dropped across the unit boundary into Compartment 4. Compartment 4 adjoins Interstate 75 on its southern boundary and was outside of the planned prescribed fire project area. The fire in Compartment 4 was attacked by holding resources. The aerial ignition helicopter (Type 3) was quickly reconfigured for bucket work and began dropping water. However, attempts to contain the fire were unsuccessful.
incidents.quote: Success is not final, Failure is not fatal: It is the courage to continue that counts.

incidents.name: New London VFD Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter M.V. Hudson was injured in a fire tender (tanker) crash on the evening of February 28th. Hudson and two other firefighters were responding to a grass fire when the apparatus left the right side of the roadway and rolled over, badly damaging the cab and injuring all three occupants. The three firefighters had to be extracted from the vehicle and were rushed to the hospital. Two firefighters were subsequently released, but Firefighter Hudson died while in the hospital on March10, 2018.
incidents.quote: New London VFD Fatality

incidents.name: Engine 5670 Cab Electrical Fire
incidents.summary: Despite the engine being off and the main switch to the engine placed in the “off” position, the current to the electric cigarette lighter was still live. The flashlight apparently overheated to the point that it ejected and exploded from the cigarette lighter. Hot fragments of the flashlight caught the driver’s seat on fire.
incidents.quote: During the evening of 03/09/18, the BLM CFO fire engine 5670 caught fire. The fire was caused by a small flashlight plugged into the cigarette lighter.

incidents.name: Ellinger VFD Fatality
incidents.summary: The Caldwell County Office of Emergency Management has reported the death of Firefighter Larry Marusik. Firefighter Marusik passed away at the Brooke Army Medical Center on March 23, 2018, from injuries sustained while battling a large grass fire on March 10, 2018
incidents.quote: One fire fighter dies and one burned during firefighting operations on a grassfire when they were not wearing PPE and one fell off the T6 engine while escaping the fire.

incidents.name: Olympic NF Employee Fatality
incidents.summary: A three person crew from the Olynpic National Forest had been working to mitigate hazard trees on a local campground. The crew was in the process of packing their gear for the day when one employee complained of dizziness for the second time that afternoon. The employee collapsed, begin to convulse, and became unconscious. The two other two crew members called 911and began CPR. The employee was transported to Grays Harbor Community Hospital in Aberdeen, WA where he was pronounced deceased.
incidents.quote: A three person crew had been working to mitigate hazard trees on a local campground when an employee collapsed, begin to convulse, and became unconscious.

incidents.name: Stanislaus NF Medical Incident
incidents.summary: An Interagency Hotshot Crew crewmember (apprentice) experiencing seizures and going in/out of consciousness was transported by ground ambulance to the hospital. Diagnosed with exhaustion and dehydration, the crewmember was treated, released and ordered to take off work for a week.

incidents.name: Laguna Fire Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: A crew member fell into a hot ash pit, when the ground gave way on a berm where the employee was conducting mop up operations. The employee suffered burn injuries requiring immediate medical intervention, emergent transport to a local hospital, and subsequent aeromedical transport to a burn center. The second employee was burned while attempting to flag off the area of the the previous burn injury.
incidents.quote: On the same day, in the same location, and only 30 minutes apart, two employees were burned on the Laguna Fire.

incidents.name: Madison Township Kunkle FD Fatality
incidents.summary: After attending an earlier fire department training meeting, Assistant Chief Rodney D. Baker, Jr., responded to a grass fire at 2229hrs on March, 15, 2018. Chief Baker (Chief 51) was first on scene as the commanding officer for the incident and was back in service at 2336hrs. The following day, while attending a family event, Chief Baker became ill and collapsed at 1638hrs. Family members trained in CPR immediately came to Chief Baker’s aid while the Pioneer Fire Department and Williams County EMS were called to the scene.
incidents.quote: Assistant Chief Baker was transported to Bryan hospital where, despite all efforts, he later passed away from a reported cardiac event.

incidents.name: Initial Attack Gunshot Wound
incidents.summary: A firefighter in southwest Michigan was in the hospital Monday night after a gun that was in his pocket discharged while he was battling a brush fire. Authorities say the firefighter, who has a concealed pistol license, was doing well after the incident.

incidents.name: Mop Up Blasting Caps
incidents.summary: The fire’s forward progress was stopped and mop-up began. This area in which the fire was burning is an old mine, with several other mines also located in the general vicinity. After an hour of mop-up had passed, a firefighter noticed some “odd” items lying in the black. Thinking that these items could possibly be old blasting caps, the firefighter immediately flagged-off the area. When an Explosives Disposal Unit arrived on scene Personnel from this unit determined that the items truly were old blasting caps. It was deemed that these items were too unstable to move. The decision was therefore made to detonate the caps in place on the fire by the explosives experts.
incidents.quote: After an hour of mop-up had passed, a firefighter noticed some “odd” items lying in the black . . .

incidents.name: Santa Cruz Island Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On March 27, personnel began their normal workday with a thorough briefing. Personnel split into two groups, one to focus on cutting, the other to focus on burn piles. That morning, the piles were patrolled until about noon with no concerns indicated. All personnel were now at the cutting site. At approximately 14:20, smoke was observed at the burn pile site from the cutting site and personnel quickly responded. Upon arrival, several acres of active moving fire was observed. At approximately 14:50, a wildfire was declared with notification to dispatch and the FMO. Additional resources ordered included aviation and ground resources.
incidents.quote: “Everything went well. We could have burned every pile out there during the shift, but we were thinking ahead. We knew we’d need to chunk and patrols these and also needed to get stuff cut. We only wanted what we could reasonably deal with.”

incidents.name: Dozer Rollover In Snow
incidents.summary: The operator and his dozer were assisting an interagency partner to open a snow-covered route that provided access to sites identified in a spring burn area. The blade, the dozer tracks, and the slope of the ice aligned, creating an uncontrollable sideways slide toward the edge of the road. As a last ditch option, the operator lifted his blade, but the dozer continued to slide toward the edge. Now at the edge of the road, the dozer rolled downhill and flipped over onto its cab, but stopped before completing a full roll.
incidents.quote: The blade, the dozer tracks,and the slope of the ice aligned,creating an uncontrollable sideways slide toward the edge of the road.

incidents.name: Pine Grove Hand Piles Escaped Fire Review
incidents.summary: While snow remained on April 7 as the crew mopped up and cold trailed, it was receding, so further patrol was scheduled for April 8. The patrol crew was just arriving at the station when the fire call went out for the escaped pile burn at 1140. The fire was contained by late afternoon, but approximately 27 acres of grass and old hand piles burned on private land.
incidents.quote: Because the fire burned onto private land, the Duty Officer declared a wildfire.

incidents.name: Redondo Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The Redondo Rx was located on the Mount Taylor Ranger District, Cibola National Forest in New Mexico. Ignitions began the morning of April 9 and ceased mid-afternoon on April 10, 2018. On April 12, in the midst of an 11-hour wind event in which three separate wildfires were reported, the Redondo Rx was declared a wildfire when crews were unable to secure multiple spots across the holding line.
incidents.quote: “It blew my mind when I found out they got spots. It was clean. It looked solid. It got hit by wood haulers. The night before there wasn’t a smoke showing within a chain of the line.”

incidents.name: Shaw Fire Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: On April 12th, 2018, 61-year-old Jack Osben, a motor grader operator for Roger Mills County in Oklahoma and volunteer firefighter died as a result of thermal burns while providing initial attack to the Shaw Fire. For many readers, this analysis will serve as an introduction to a different way of fighting fire with some of these methods appearing unconventional. But, in the words of one of the grader operators, “you make do with what you have.” Even if the methods and context are different, this statement ties together the ethos of wildland firefighters everywhere.
incidents.quote: “It’s a perfect storm. I’ve seen fires move faster and have higher flame lengths, but the radiant heat coming off of this is way hotter than any other fire.”

incidents.name: Arizona Engine WCT Rhabdo Case
incidents.summary: During the final lap, the patient later stated he saw black spots and was afraid of passing out. Upon completing the WCT, the patient appeared to co-workers to be extremely pale and in need of assistance. One of the engine boss proctors thought the patient appeared ashen. His weight vest was removed and he was immediately placed into a paramedic ambulance which was on site. Treatment was initiated by fire district paramedics.
incidents.quote: The patient was quickly diagnosed with rhabdo, but ER staff did not check for compartment syndrome.

incidents.name: Rocky Mount VFD Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Wilcox responded to two fire calls on April 18, 2018, one at 1300hrs and a brush fire at 1605hrs. After returning from the brush fire, Wilcox complained of neck and back pain. He went to a local MediCenter where he was examined and then sent home. At approximately 0730hrs the next morning, Firefighter Wilcox's wife tried to wake him but found him unresponsive and immediately called 911. Emergency responders arrived on scene and began CPR, but after 30 minutes of resuscitation efforts, Firefighter Wilcox was pronounced deceased at his residence. The nature and cause of fatal injury is still to be determined.

incidents.name: Training Hike Fatality
incidents.summary: Incident Description: Inmate Firefighter Trainee Anthony Colacino was participating in a training hike when he collapsed just before 0800hrs on April 21, 2018. Fellow inmate firefighters attempted to revive Colacino before other emergency services personnel took over care. Despite all efforts, Colacino succumbed to a nature and cause of fatal injury still to be determined.
incidents.quote: Training Hike Fatality

incidents.name: Chainsaw Training Limbing Accident
incidents.summary: The Fire Captain was limbing the felled tree when the tensioned limb beneath the felled tree released and struck him in the head, knocking him off his feet downhill into tree debris and rendering him unconscious. The Fire Captain suffered significant injuries to his head, neck and chest that required hospitalization.
incidents.quote: On April 24, 2018, at approximately 1429 hours, a CAL FIRE Fire Captain who is an Advanced Faller (C-Faller) Cadre Member was struck by a grounded tree limb that was under tension from a felled tree that had landed on top of it during an Advanced Faller Training Course.

incidents.name: Sims/Grape Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: In the winter of 2017/2018, over the course of a few months, numerous prescribed fire treatments (pile burning) were conducted to meet the objectives of the Sims Fire Restoration-Roadside and Landline Reduction Fuels CE Project. In late afternoon on April 24th and approximately one week after the last ignition entry, fire behavior and intensity increased significantly within the burn unit, leading to a declared escaped prescribed fire on April 25th.
incidents.quote: “Pile burning can still be a complex burn.”

incidents.name: Veach Prescribed Fire Snake Bite
incidents.summary: The Angelina-Sabine National Forest of the National Forests and Grasslands in Texas conducted a 3,149-acre prescribed fire. During baseline firing operations, a U.S. Forest Service employee on assignment as Chief of Party (COP) with a Job Corps Module, received a snake bite to the hand.
incidents.quote: During the pre-planning phase for the burn season, the Angelina-Sabine Forest’s Prevention Technician had called each local hospital and numerous clinics to determine which locations carried antivenin

incidents.name: Monongahela NF Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: A contract firefighter on a Monongahela NF prescribed fire was field diagnosed with a HRI and transported via ground ambulance to a hospital. Treated and released same day.
incidents.quote: Monongahela NF Heat Related Injury

incidents.name: Chippewa NF Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A Job Corps student received 2nd degree burns on the leg while working a RX fire on the Chippewa NF. Patient was transported to hospital via GOV. Treated and released same day.

incidents.name: West 83 Escaped Prescribed Burn Review
incidents.summary: After the AAR, two engines, a UTV, a TFLD, and the RXB2 returned to the prescribed burn to patrol the perimeter. At about 1820 hrs, one of the engines saw what appeared to be black smoke within the drainage near DP-5, and confirmed that fire had crossed the line and the fence to the south a minute later, at 1821 hrs (Figure 7). The RXB2 radioed dispatch to request assistance from the local Volunteer Fire Department. Three of the engines that had been released, hearing about the escape on the radio, also returned to the burn area to assist with the emerging situation.
incidents.quote: It rained while ignitions were being conducted in the area of escape.

incidents.name: Cleveland NF Line Dig Rhabdo
incidents.summary: Cramping later became severe. He was evaluated by a Forest Service Paramedic and an ambulance was called. He was taken to a hospital and diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis with CK levels of 3700. The patient was hospitalized for treatment and monitoring.
incidents.quote: An AD firefighter began cramping after a line construction drill on the Cleveland National Forest.

incidents.name: Umpqua NF Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: FS employee engaged in RX burning on the Umpqua NF. Was dragging a torch and tripped and fell dripping fire/fuel on back of leg. Resulted in 2nd degree burn to calf, palm sized burn. FS EMT on-site provided initial care. Transported by agency vehicle to Mercy Hospital in Bend, OR. Treated and released the same day with follow-up instructions.
incidents.quote: Umpqua NF Prescribed Fire Burn Injury

incidents.name: Los Padres NF PT Medical Incident
incidents.summary: Transported to ER, released after testing and referred to a Cardiologist.
incidents.quote: Forest Service firefighter on the Los Padres NF complained of possible heart attack symptoms during a PT hike.

incidents.name: Idaho IHC Hit by Limb
incidents.summary: Transported to hospital via GOV, treated and released to light duty.
incidents.quote: Superior NF - Idaho IHC crewmember hit by a limb to arm while assigned to a burn on the Superior NF.

incidents.name: New Mexico IHC Rhabdo Case
incidents.summary: New Mexico IHC firefighter reported a sore arm after several days of PT. He sought care from a Doctor who diagnosed dehydration. Later the Doctor called the employee with results of blood tests and had the employee admitted to a hospital. The employee spent 5 days in a hospital diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis and was released on 5/19 to light duty.
incidents.quote: The employee had experienced Rhabdo last year and was concerned symptoms were similar.

incidents.name: Nez Perce Clearwater NF PT Medical Incident
incidents.summary: Firefighter was transported via ground and air ambulance to hospital, treated for heat exhaustion and dehydration and released the same day. Firefighter will be light duty for a couple days. AAR from District – all will review medical procedures and equipment and will become familiar with newly installed cellular service in the valley.
incidents.quote: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF firefighter became lethargic during PT.

incidents.name: Klamath NF PT Heart Attack
incidents.summary: A firefighter on a type 2 IA crew suffered possible heart attack during PT. The firefighter was transported by FS employees by ground to Happy Camp where he was life-flighted to Medford Hospital. Released after two days in hospital, directed 30 days of light duty.

incidents.name: California IHC PT Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: Transport by ground ambulance to hospital, treated overnight and released following day.
incidents.quote: California IHC firefighter suffered Heat Related Injury during PT.

incidents.name: Chippewa NF Chainsaw Accident
incidents.summary: A Chippewa NF firefighter was working on a Rx preparation project and conducting training / mentoring to another firefighter on chainsaw use.
incidents.quote: The firefighter acting as instructor was struck by the saw on the top of his hand, taken to an Emergency Room where he was treated (several stitches) and was released the same day.

incidents.name: Storrie PAC RX Engine Damage
incidents.summary: An engine sustained significant fire damage while working on a prescribed fire underburn. The engine crew was assigned to assist in a holding operation for the day. While performing a “rolling and holding” operation along a narrow National Forest System road, the engine operator parked the engine in a small turnout. She then began to grid for spot fires in the green. A spot fire ignited below the turnout on the north side of the road and ran up the slope to where the engine was parked. The driver’s side rear wheel well ignited and the fire spread to the water tank and compartments of the apparatus.
incidents.quote: “If this was the worst day of my career, that will be alright."

incidents.name: Payette NF Smokejumper Hard Landing
incidents.summary: Initial treatment by FS EMTs then transported by ground ambulance to McCall Hospital and then flown to a hospital in Boise. Patient dislocated and fractured hip. Surgery scheduled.
incidents.quote: Payette NF - One of the jumpers transitioning to a Ram-Air parachute flew into a tree during a training jump and landed hard.

incidents.name: Coldwater Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The Holding Boss evaluated the situation and decided to continue driving up FR 732 to access the main road. While driving past active fire the Holding Boss received a burn injury to the face. The burn injury consisted of a burn to the right cheek near the eye and burn to the nose most likely from an ember.
incidents.quote: While driving past active fire the Holding Boss received a burn injury to the face.

incidents.name: Kelly Creek Project Hit by Log
incidents.summary: During a conifer encroachment thinning project, a log rolled down a steep incline and impacted a member of the crew working on the thinning. The crew member was transported from the scene to an ambulance and to a nearby hospital. The crew member is recovering from injuries.
incidents.quote: “It looked like it was going to get caught in the patch of timber right below us, but as I began to run down slope yelling ‘roller,’ I saw that it was still going.”

incidents.name: Boise NF Smokejumper Hard Landing
incidents.summary: Initial treatment by FS EMTs and then he was ground ambulanced to a hospital in Boise, evaluated to temporary light duty and released with a diagnosis of severe back bruising.
incidents.quote: Boise NF - One of the jumpers in transition to Ram-Air parachutes flew into a tree, and had a hard landing.

incidents.name: Coconino NF Felling Accident
incidents.summary: The Sawyer began his back cut, but noticed it was sloped and began another back cut under the original attempt. While working the back cut, the Sawyer also attempted to bore the heart wood and unintentionally cut through all the intended holding wood. As the tree’s top brushed another tree, it made the bole rise into the air and roll off the stump onto the Sawyer’s leg before he was able to vacate the cutting area.
incidents.quote: The C Faller immediately ran to the pinned Sawyer, grabbed the chainsaw, and bucked out the section that was trapping the Sawyer.

incidents.name: Recycle Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: An AD firefighter on the Recycle Fire suffered a Heat Related Illness injury. A ground ambulance transported the firefighter to the hospital. The patient was evaluated and released same day.

incidents.name: 377 Fire Falling Accident
incidents.summary: Limb or tree top fell onto the firefighter’s shoulder. Initial treatment by FS EMTs, then transported to hospital. Evaluation indicates severe bruising and patient was released.
incidents.quote: Apache-Sitgreaves NF – An IHC sawyer was involved in a felling accident on incident # 377.

incidents.name: Prescribed Fire Smoke Exposure
incidents.summary: Willamette NF - Seven firefighters were evaluated for smoke exposure after working an Rx burn. The Forest is conducting a review.

incidents.name: Scenic Loop Complex Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: While performing wildland firefighting operations, Firefighter Richard "Andy" Loller, Jr. suffered a medical emergency. Loller was flown by helicopter to receive medical treatment and was stabilized before being placed on a medical airplane to receive further treatment at a hospital in Odessa.
incidents.quote: While in flight, Firefighter Loller passed away.

incidents.name: Boise NF Heart Attack/Stroke Scare
incidents.summary: Medical Emergency, Project Work, Hand Crews, Medical or Exertion or Heat
incidents.quote: Boise NF Heart Attack/Stroke Scare

incidents.name: Inyo Incident #903 Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: Medical Emergency, Medevac, Hand Crews, Medical or Exertion or Heat
incidents.quote: Inyo Incident #903 Heat Related Injury

incidents.name: Montana ATV Course Rollover
incidents.summary: During the field portion of the training, rider A took the lead in most of the exercises with rider B following rider A’s lead. The second to last skills station consisted of downhill and uphill riding. Rider A road downhill into a coulee bottom and proceeded up and out on a steeper slope on the other side. Rider B followed the same path down into the coulee and started up the other side. Rider B did not obtain sufficient speed when starting up the other side and powered-out half way up. The ATV began to roll backward down the hill and rider B “bailed-off”. The ATV went over backwards coming to a rest on its wheels in the bottom of the coulee.
incidents.quote: Of the two students, rider A was highly experienced, and rider B had limited experience operating an ATV.

incidents.name: Buffalo Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The crewmember did not immediately report the injury. He wrapped it with an ace bandage and continued working. As he came off the hill that night he was treated by one of the medic units from an adjacent Fire and was transported to a hospital where he was treated and released to light duty.
incidents.quote: White River NF – A Type 2 crewmember on the Buffalo fire sustained a minor burn to the right calf while performing direct attack.

incidents.name: Aragon Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: NFSR 505 contains a narrow section where the road is elevated above the natural drainage. Erosion had created a depression on the right side of the road in this narrow section. The driver steered the vehicle to the left side of the road here to miss the eroded area. The vehicle began to slide off the road and over the embankment. The vehicle rolled completely over, coming to rest upright in the bottom of the drainage.
incidents.quote: Truck #1168 in the bottom of the drainage where it came to rest after sliding off the road embankment and rolling over one time

incidents.name: Trail Mountain Fire Laceration
incidents.summary: Manti-La Sal NF – IHC crew member fell on his Pulaski. Stabilized by FS EMT. Inured was then short hauled to a LZ, then transported via ground to Price Valley Hospital in Utah. He received stitches and was released to light duty.

incidents.name: 2018 USFS Short Haul Summary Trail Mountain Fire RLS
incidents.summary: A ground-based evacuation would have been laborious and time intensive.
incidents.quote: On June 18, 2018 on the Trail Mountain Fire, a firefighter lost their footing in steep terrain, resulting in a deep pulaski wound to the thigh.

incidents.name: San Antonio Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: Joel knew that sound and he knew if he looked up he would get hit right in the face. By the look on Memo’s face (his partner), he knew he was going to be hit. A nine foot long branch-- 9 inches in diameter-- has just released from high up in the green trees’ canopy. Not knowing what direction to move, Joel shrugged his shoulders and braced for impact. Memo tried to push Joel out of the way, but there was no time. The limb struck Joel on the left side of the hard hat at an “angle smearing the hard hat off his head.” The branch also hit Memo hard on the back, knocking him to the ground.
incidents.quote: They were there for a good reason, they were cautious, they have good experience to know what to watch out for…yet they were both hurt.

incidents.name: Trail Mountain Fire Medical Incident
incidents.summary: Employee from a Type 1 interagency hotshot crew was sleeping in fire camp when he started having stomach pains. Individual was transported to Emery Medical Clinic in Castle Dale, UT and clinic could not determine what was wrong. Employee was then transported to Castleview Hospital in Price, UT for a CT scan. The CT scan shows a small bowel blockage and individual is going into surgery. Hospital Liaison and local Safety Manager accompanied employee at hospital.

incidents.name: Lion Fire Dehydration
incidents.summary: Sierra National Forest, Lion Fire. Two IHC crew members were evaluated by FS EMTs for possible dehydration. The two were flown by agency aircraft to Mammoth Airport, met by ground ambulance and transported to a local hospital. Both crew members were treated and released back to the incident that evening.
incidents.quote: Two IHC crew members were evaluated by FS EMTs for possible dehydration.

incidents.name: Lion Fire Foot Injury
incidents.summary: Crewmember was evaluated by FS EMTs and then flown by agency aircraft to Mammoth Airport, met by ground ambulance and transported to a local hospital. Patient was evaluated and released to light duty pending a specialist evaluation.
incidents.quote: Sierra National Forest, Lion Fire. An IHC crew member suffered a foot (heal) injury.

incidents.name: 416 Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: San Juan National Forest, 416 Fire. He was then transported to Durango hospital and diagnosed with 1st and 2nd degree burns to face and referred to a Burn Center in Spokane. The Vendor flew the firefighter to Spokane where upon he was evaluated at the Burn Center and determined no further treatment was necessary.
incidents.quote: A contract firefighter attempted to start a contractor supplied hydraulic pump with a missing spark plug. Firefighter was sprayed with gasoline which ignited.

incidents.name: Initial Attack Engine Burn Damage
incidents.summary: During mobile attack, the engine hit a rock, temporally high-centering the vehicle. At the same time, it was also noticed that the oil pan was damaged. As this backing fire approached the rear of the stuck engine it was noted that the engine was also out of water.
incidents.quote: As this backing fire approached the rear of the stuck engine it was noted that the engine was out of water. The VFDs therefore suppressed the fire near the engine. At the same time, more attempts were made to pull the engine to the highway.

incidents.name: 416 Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: An IHC member pushed over by hand a 4 in. diameter tree. The top 4 feet of the tree fell out striking crewmember in the back. Resulting in cut and bruises. Treated by FS EMTs on scene then transported to Durango Hospital. Patient received 7 stitches and released back to the incident to full duty.

incidents.name: East Fire Cooking Burn Injury
incidents.summary: He was treated by Forest Service EMTs and then flown out to a nearby town via a Forest Service ship where a local medical center’s Life Flight Helicopter was waiting. He was then flown to UC Davis Burn Center. He was treated and released that same day. The crew is conducting an AAR.
incidents.quote: An Elk Mountain IHC member was cooking a meal at a remote camp on the East Fire on the Mendocino National Forest and received a burn injury to the right hand.

incidents.name: Pawnee Fire Heat Related and Poison Oak Injuries
incidents.summary: An IHC crewmember suffered from a combination of poison oak, dehydration and Heat Related injuries. They were wreated by EMTs and hoist lifted by State Aircraft and flown to Red Bud Hospital.

incidents.name: Pawnee Fire Medical
incidents.summary: Treated by FS EMTs and flown by agency aircraft to Red Bud Hospital. Treated and released the same day.
incidents.quote: An IHC crewmember lacerated his hand.

incidents.name: Filmore Fire Heat Injuries and Rhabdo
incidents.summary: A firefighter complained of heat-related issues and was driven to San Gorgonio Hospital. They were admitted to hospital because blood tests indicated Rhabdo and kidney injury.

incidents.name: IHC Supt Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: Both vehicles were totaled. There were no reported Forest Service injuries as of the time of this report, however at least one civilian was transported via ambulance to a hospital.
incidents.quote: A Black Mountain IHC Superintendent’s vehicle was involved in crash with a civilian vehicle near Sierra Vista, Arizona.

incidents.name: Trail Mountain Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A contract firefighters received 2nd degree burns on his arm and calf when he stepped into a burning stump hole. He was treated on scene by FS EMTs and an air ambulanced to the University of Utah Hospital. He was treated and released the next day.

incidents.name: Hague VFD Fatality
incidents.summary: His wife, who is also a member of the department and was the driver of the brush truck, immediately drove home. He was helped inside of his house by his wife and collapsed soon after. The nature and cause of the medical emergency has yet to be determined.
incidents.quote: While riding as a passenger in a brush truck, at a parade in a nearby town, Lieutenant Cherubini became ill.

incidents.name: Dollar Ridge Fire Eye Injury
incidents.summary: He was treated on scene by a county EMT, and then flown via agency helicopter to meet incoming ambulance. He was then taken by ground ambulance to hospital. Diagnosed with a scratched cornea and ordered to light duty for two days.
incidents.quote: A firefighter received an injury to an eye.

incidents.name: Klamathon Fire Dozer Spot Close Call
incidents.summary: A dozer started a spot fire while building line in rocky terrain. The 20-30 mph winds violently blew the spot fire upslope and into the surrounding stand of decadent shrubs. The dozer operator attempted to call his scout by his call sign, "Trinity River 3" to warn him of the developing situation. On the third attempt at communication, the dozer operator called the scout by his first name. To my relief, the use of his first name on the tactical channel finally got his attention.
incidents.quote: “I'm sharing this because I don't want the naysayers to doubt that they too can start a fire. It's just a matter of time.”

incidents.name: Tanker Base Cardiac Arrest
incidents.summary: A contracted fuel service driver suffered a heart attack. Treated on scene by a FS employee that had first Aid CPR training. Initiated CPR. FS employee hooked up an AED. The AED indicated no shock was needed at that time. The contractor was then ambulanced to a hospital. Attending physician stated it was likely the FS employee saved the contractors life.

incidents.name: Weston Pass Fire Tornado Incident
incidents.summary: Firefighters on the Weston Pass Fire in Colorado, became entrapped in the path of tornado. Within seconds to no more than a minute, the tornado was fully fledged, uprooting and snapping off trees up to 27 inches in diameter. Several trees were snapped-off and broken, falling within 5-7 feet of three firefighters who were under the trees seeking refuge from the large hail.
incidents.quote: It was communicated over the radio and verbally for people to seek refuge where ever they could—in low areas, in vehicles, and under the dozer.

incidents.name: Smokejumper Proficiency Jump Hip Fracture
incidents.summary: A smoke jumper fractured his hip after hitting a tree during a proficiency jump. He was stabilized on scene by FS EMTs then Air Ambulance to St. Alphonso’s Hospital in Boise. Surgery was scheduled for 7/7/18 and a full recovering is anticipated.

incidents.name: Lake Christine Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: During extended attack on the Lake Christine Fire a D5M crawler tractor and another crawler tractor were tracking across the fire area (in the “black”). While cresting a marginal drop-off the D5M bulldozer rolled over approximately three times and came to a rest upright. The operator appeared to have lost consciousness during the rollover and the bulldozer continued to move in reverse, but was eventually stopped by the other bulldozer operator’s actions.
incidents.quote: The operator appeared to have lost consciousness during the rollover and the bulldozer continued to move in reverse.

incidents.name: North Spring Fire Rotor Strike
incidents.summary: Two of the crew’s mechanics climbed on top of the aircraft to complete their tasks. These tasks include, but are not limited to, visually checking certain fluid levels within a five minute window for the most accurate readings. As the crew members were busy at work and focused on their assigned tasks, the PIC began going through the engine start-up process to see if the error code issue was completely resolved. Two crew mechanics were on top of the aircraft, aft of the front rotor. Hearing the engines spool up, several support personnel noticed these two mechanics and began yelling: “Get down! Get down!” As the engine was spooling up and the rotors began to turn, one of the mechanic crew members was struck in the head, impacting the side of this individual’s face/head and their safety helmet.
incidents.quote: On what was described as a “normal day of flying” a flight crew on the North Spring Fire experienced an injury from a rotor strike.

incidents.name: Shasta Trinity NF Torn Esophagus
incidents.summary: Shasta Trinity NF Employee torn esophagus eating in a fire camp. Transported to Mercy Mt. Shasta Hospital where surgery was performed. A full recovery expected. Employee has been released.
incidents.quote: Shasta Trinity NF Employee Torn Esophagus

incidents.name: Fawn Fire Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: The engine came to a rest upright at the bottom of a drainage. Another fire engine crew in the convoy noticed the rollover and notified the Fawn Fire incident personnel who subsequently notified local interagency fire dispatch. The interagency fire dispatch called emergency services (911) to respond to the scene.
incidents.quote: An engine assigned to the Fawn Fire was traveling on an unpaved county road after the end of the operational shift and veered off the road and an embankment resulting in a rollover.

incidents.name: Red Canyon 2 Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter working on the Red Canyon 2 Fire on the White River National Forest, suffered a suspected heat related illness. An ambulance was called and medics administered an IV. The Firefighter was transported to a local hospital, treated and released that same day.

incidents.name: Wildhorse Fire UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: A UTV operator attempts to back up, digging in the back left tires into the ground, causing the center of gravity of the UTV to shift. The weight of the tank and pump were perceived at the time to have exasperated this weight shift. The UTV rolls one full rotation and is stopped by a ponderosa pine tree several feet downhill. During the roll, the operator tumbles in the cab, landing on his back on the interior roof half way through the roll. As the UTV continues to roll, the operator is ejected out the passenger side of the UTV.
incidents.quote: “Slow is smooth-- and smooth is fast"

incidents.name: North Spring Fire Septic Tank Incident
incidents.summary: They entered the driveway and pulled into a parking spot to turn around. A crewmember got out to assist in backing procedures. In doing so, the backer was looking at the driver and giving hand signals in the desired direction. Before the Engine Boss could understand what had happened, the crewmember reappeared just as fast as he disappeared. It immediately dawned on the Engine Boss that his crewmember had fallen knee-deep into a septic tank.
incidents.quote: It was determined by the Medic that the crewmember needed to go to the local hospital as a precaution.

incidents.name: Ferguson Fire Dozer Rollover Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter/Equipment Operator Braden Varney was assigned to the Madera-Mariposa CAL FIRE unit, which has been fighting the 130-acre Ferguson Fire in the Sierra National Forest. On 07/14/2018, Firefighter/Equipment Operator Varney was working on a ridge to create a fire break. The bulldozer Varney was operating overturned and rolled down the ridge causing Varney to suffer fatal injuries. The wreckage was spotted by airplane on 07/15/2018 and crews reached the site and removed Varney's body on 07/16/2018.
incidents.quote: Ferguson Fire Dozer Rollover Fatality

incidents.name: Martin Fire Pickup Truck Fuel Tank Incident
incidents.summary: During this incident, the dust (Moon Dust/Bug Dust) on the access roads progressively got worse and worse. The Dodge 1500s, much like other trucks, breathe through the fuel cap. On the Martin Fire, three different Dodge 1500 pickups had their gas caps plug up with dust to the point that the fuel tank couldn't breathe properly. This, in turn, caused the fuel tank to partially collapse two of the tanks and totally collapse one of the tanks.
incidents.quote: Dusty Conditions Collapse Pickups’ Fuel Tanks

incidents.name: Lodgepole Springs Prescribed Burn Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: On April 24 and 25, 2018, the Lodgepole Springs Restoration Prescribed Burn was ignited on the Emmett Ranger District of the Boise National Forest. Burn operations went as planned and subsequent ample precipitation signaled that the fire would be extinguished over time. However, intermittent smoldering and flaring resumed as warm, dry weather increased. Though the burn remained within the project area boundary, complications in managing and holding it as a prescribed burn became untenable. On July 14, 2018, it was declared a wildfire.
incidents.quote: No firelines were slated to be constructed since the snow, rock features, and riparian areas were expected to contain the burning.

incidents.name: Dog Creek Fire Burned Gear
incidents.summary: Dog Creek Fire, Twin Falls District BLM; Gooding, Idaho Eight Jumpers arrived around 1430. They stacked their gear together in the black, near the heel of the fire. A local fire department Engine radioed at approximately 1800 that the Jumpers’ gear was on fire.
incidents.quote: Dog Creek Fire Burned Gear

incidents.name: Grassy Fire Heat Exhaustion
incidents.summary: Forest Service EMTs recognized heat exhaustion. The firefighter was flown via agency helicopter to a nearby airport where an ambulance was waiting and took the patient to a hospital.
incidents.quote: While digging direct handline on the Grassy Fire on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, a firefighter became weak and dizzy.

incidents.name: Ferguson Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: He was treated and stabilized at the scene by crew EMTs and then at the Incident Medical unit. He was then flown via air ambulance to a hospital in Fresno. No further details were reported.
incidents.quote: Sierra NF, IHC crewmember received a broken leg from a falling rock.

incidents.name: Hendrix Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: It was at this moment that an awkward angle of the saw bar coming out of the kerf resulted in a violent and unanticipated kickback of the chainsaw. Simultaneously to the occurrence of the kickback, the swamper reached over the kerf where the saw struck the swamper on his left forearm. The squad leader, now standing just 10 feet away watched the incident as it happened. “I noticed a red mist and saw blood splatter on the front of the swampers yellow. I knew exactly what had just taken place”
incidents.quote: “Operational tempo was high as fire activity picked up and knowing we only had a little way to go before tying in our line” -Squad Boss

incidents.name: Hendrix Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: Hendrix Fire, Rouge-Sis NF, a Contract Firefighter suffered an apparent HRI. Patient was treated by prepositioned incident medics and then taken by ground ambulance to a hospital where s/he was treated and released.
incidents.quote: Hendrix Fire Heat Related Injury

incidents.name: Chetaslina Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: The NPS firefighter was slightly injured. The Forest Service firefighter was flown to a hospital via air ambulance. She was treated for a concussion, whiplash,and bruises and lacerations to a shoulder. She was released later that evening and flew home the following day.
incidents.quote: A firefighter from the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, along with a National Park Service firefighter, was involved in a rollover motor vehicle accident when she swerved to avoid another traffic accident that occurred directly in front of them.

incidents.name: South Umpqua Fire Complex Ankle Injury
incidents.summary: A Forest Service Transport Operator injured his ankle when he stepped off the back of transport truck. He was taken via ambulance to the hospital. Medical.

incidents.name: Taylor Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A Contract Firefighter was cutting a 6” dead Madrone and it fell back on the firefighter knocking him to the ground then he rolled down a hill. The Contract crew stabilized the firefighter using a backboard. He was taken to a hospital where he was diagnosed with a broken C6 vertebrae. Patient was hospitalized for 3 days.

incidents.name: Owyhee Fire Can Explosion
incidents.summary: A fire overhead team member parked his vehicle at the Incident Command Post. Prior to the start of his shift, this person had utilized a can of compressed air to clean equipment. The can was left for the day on the dashboard inside the vehicle. That afternoon, an IMT member discovered significant damage to the front windshield of this person’s pickup truck. The damage consisted of a 3-inch by 3-inch hole in the vehicle’s front windshield. A can of Ultra Duster (10 oz) had caused—and was partially lodged in—this hole.
incidents.quote: At an unknown time, the can of compressed air violently exploded.

incidents.name: White River Fire Springpole Strike
incidents.summary: A USFS firefighter building a fireline cut a springpole that released and hit his hardhat and scrapped off his goggles. FS EMTs treated the firefighter on scene and incident overhead drove him to an ER. Patient was diagnosed with blunt force trauma to the eye and expected to recover without surgery.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Cut to Shoulder
incidents.summary: The firefighter received stitches and was placed on light duty for 7 days. No further details reported.
incidents.quote: A firefighter suffered a chainsaw cut to left shoulder. Individual slipped and chainsaw bar touched the ground and kicked back and cut the shoulder.

incidents.name: Carr Fire Entrapment Fatalities
incidents.summary: FPI1 stated he was in the middle of the road, was getting burned over, and needed a water drop. All three dozers were violently impacted by flying debris, rocks, embers, smoke, and intense heat. The flying material shattered windows on all three dozers. SUP1’s vehicle began to shake violently, and the passenger windows shattered. SUP1 ducked down to avoid being hit by flying debris and he momentarily drove off the road. As PREV1 slowly approached the burning vehicle, he felt his pickup truck get “pushed” from the west. All the windows in his pickup truck except the windshield shattered.
incidents.quote: At approximately 1935 a fire tornado formed and impacted resources working to construct contingency line along the western edge of Redding, from the Sacramento River to the Land Park Subdivision resulting in multiple entrapments, injuries, and one fatality.

incidents.name: Carr Fire After Action Review
incidents.summary: The primary goal of this After Action Review (AAR) was, through the course of a facilitated discussion between key stakeholders, to identify significant successes or issues during the fire response and provide recommendations as appropriate.
incidents.quote: The fire burned 229,651 acres making it the 7th largest in California history, including 38,595 acres of NPS lands, before it was 100% contained on August 30, 2018. The Carr Fire destroyed at least 1,604 structures, of these at least 1,077 were homes, while damaging 277 others. It was one of the most destructive fires in California history, and caused over $1.659 billion (2018) in damages. At its height, the fire engaged as many as 4,766 personnel from multiple agencies.

incidents.name: South Umpqua Fire Complex Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: A water tender assigned to the South Umpqua Complex Fire was traveling on an unpaved road and rolled backwards off the road and resulting in the vehicle rolling on its side. The vehicle came to a rest on the driver’s side.

incidents.name: Cranston Fire Dislocated Shoulder
incidents.summary: Cranston Fire, San Bernardino NF. A USFS firefighter suffered a dislocated shoulder. No further details reported.
incidents.quote: Cranston Fire Dislocated Shoulder

incidents.name: Carr Fire Entrapment - Engine
incidents.summary: While returning to the engine 3 firefighters sustained burns to hands and faces. ENG1 made several attempts to exit the property, but ultimately had to wait for the fire front to pass.
incidents.quote: At approximately 7:05 p.m., ENG1 personnel experienced increased heat, smoke, spot fires, and area ignition of the ornamental brush near the house and driveway.

incidents.name: Carr Fire Entrapment Fatality Dozer
incidents.summary: Sometime between 5:46 p.m. and 5:50 p.m., radio traffic was heard from Dozer 1 that he was on a bench attempting to make a safety zone. Dozer 1 was also requesting water drops. After a clearing in the smoke, HLCO noticed Dozer 1 was engulfed with fire. HLCO did not observe any sign of a shelter deployment. FC1 confirmed that the dozer operator suffered fatal injuries during the burn over.
incidents.quote: Dozer 1 stated he could not get out because he was cut off by the fire, and he would push down instead.

incidents.name: Gardner Complex Broken Leg
incidents.summary: Gardner Complex near Grants Pass OR. A contract firefighter suffered a broken leg. No further details reported.
incidents.quote: Gardner Complex Broken Leg

incidents.name: Kootenai NF Smokejumper Injury
incidents.summary: A Smoke Jumper was injured jumping a fire on the Kootenai. The jumper complained of a sore neck and was helicoptered via agency aircraft. Upon consultation at the Libby Hospital it was suspected that he had cracked his T4 and 5 vertebrae.
incidents.quote: The jumper’s feet hit a downed log, upending him, causing the jumper’s shoulders and head to impact the ground.

incidents.name: Ferguson Fire Tree Strike Fatality
incidents.summary: Captain Brian Hughes and his crew were engaged in tactical fire operations on the east side of the Ferguson Fire in Mariposa County, California, when he was struck by a tree. Hughes was treated on scene, but passed away from the injuries he sustained before he could be transported to a hospital.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Killed on Ferguson Fire

incidents.name: Sugar Pine Fire Helicopter Alternate Landing Site
incidents.summary: A Type I Helicopter was tasked with a mission to provide water via a bucket to help control the fire edge on one of several fires in the area. The Type 1 Helicopter filled their bucket and waited for directions of where to drop. Within a few minutes, the fire was completely layered over in smoke. The helicopter pilots could not see the fire at all. After some coordination, the pilot was given permission to land in the open field (100 acres in size) located northwest of the ICP.
incidents.quote: Smoke Prevents Return to Helibase –What Now?

incidents.name: Taylor Creek Fire Felling Incident
incidents.summary: A contracted felling module who had just begun working that day was felling snags along the route to make conditions safe for firefighters to plumb the line and begin a potential burnout operation. At 0900 a call came across the radio announcing that there had been a tree strike and one of the fallers had been injured. DIVS working nearby rushed to the scene of the accident and took over command of the incident. One of the fallers had been struck by the butt end of a 24-inch fir he had felled.
incidents.quote: We have a 67-year-old male with a broken leg, he is conscious, alert and oriented X4 with pain that is a 7 out of 10.

incidents.name: Miner Camp Peak Fire Smokejumper Injuries
incidents.summary: Miners Camp Peak Fire, Fishlake NF, three Smoke Jumpers were injured upon landing. All three treated by FS EMTs and all three were transported by air-ambulance to a hospital in Provo, UT. 1st injury was a hand with 2 broken bones, jumper was treated and released that night. The 2nd injury was a separated shoulder treated and also released that night and additional surgery is anticipated. The 3rd jumper injury was a separated wrist with torn tendons. Surgery was scheduled for the following morning. A FLA is underway.
incidents.quote: Three Smoke Jumpers were injured upon landing.

incidents.name: Crane Prairie Guard Station Medical Incident
incidents.summary: At approximately 1830 hours, a private citizen arrived at the Crane Prairie Guard Station in a personal vehicle and shouted for help. The individual complained of sever chest pain, an inability to catch her breath, and an altered mental state. The medical helicopter landed at 2019 hours at the Crane Prairie Guard Station without incident and assisted with stabilizing the patient for transport. The patient was loaded onto the helicopter and departed the scene by 2035 hours. At this time, the patient’s condition since the incident is unknown.
incidents.quote: A private citizen arrived at the Crane Prairie Guard Station in a personal vehicle and shouted for help. The individual complained of severe chest pain, an inability to catch her breath, and an altered mental state.

incidents.name: Sugar Pine Fire Dozer Rollover and Extraction
incidents.summary: A dozer slipped off the edge of a logging road and tumbled down end-over-end, 175 feet to the bottom of a ravine.
incidents.quote: “I thought they would be doing a recovery—not a medical transport.”

incidents.name: Taylor Creek Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: The crew was constructing handline within a patch of poison oak in 2-5 inch dbh pine trees. Poison oak vines were wrapped around most of these trees. The sawyer cut a three-inch tree. The poison oak vine grabbed the chain and pulled the cut tree down into the chainsaw bar, pushing the bar into the sawyer’s leg about four inches below the left knee. The saw’s teeth grabbed the sawyer’s saw chaps and rolled them from the outside inward—exposing the sawyer’s unprotected leg. The chain bit into his leg below the knee, causing a laceration
incidents.quote: “Do they still issue two-buckle saw chaps from the cache? We must be careful with them. They bulge at the knee when working!”

incidents.name: Garner Complex Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A type 6 engine assigned to the Garner Complex working on the Graves Fire was engaged in pump operations supporting a hose lay. The pump cavitated and as the operator was shutting the pump down hot water and steam struck the crew member on the chest and abdomen. A paramedic responded and the crewmember was transported by ground ambulance to the hospital in Medford. Upon evaluation the crew member was flown to Portland Legacy Hospital Burn Unit. It has been reported that the crew member received first and second degree burns. Oregon Department of Forestry assigned a hospital liaison.
incidents.quote: The pump cavitated and as the operator was shutting the pump down hot water and steam struck the crew member on the chest and abdomen.

incidents.name: South Umpqua Fire Complex Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: A five-person squad from a contract crew was coming down Road 1610 from the north (Hamlin Prairie Helispot) into Drop Point 1. The driver noticed the resources (personnel and vehicles) scattered around the area and suddenly saw a vehicle come into his vision from the east on Road 400. At this time, the pickup engine suddenly started revving as the pickup raced across the Drop Point approximately 170 feet, slamming into the trees just south of Road 1610. The pickup just missed hitting a vehicle parked to the right, then struck and broke off an 8-inch diameter 40-foot tall tree, then traveled an additional 35 feet into the timber.
incidents.quote: “I don’t know how he missed the vehicles and people in the middle of the staging area.”

incidents.name: Edison RX Firing Device Incident
incidents.summary: The Firefighter I heard the fuse of the firing device ignite and quickly removed the web gear. The firing device fully ignited destroying the web gear and damaging the Fire Shelter. No injuries resulted from this incident.
incidents.quote: On November 1, 2018, at approximately 12:45 PM, a CAL FIRE Firefighter I was conducting firing operations as part of a firing team on the Edison VMP in Shaver Lake, CA, when a hand-throw firing device ignited in a pouch on the Firefighter I’s web gear.

incidents.name: Crescent Mountain Fire Civilian Hiker Extraction
incidents.summary: Brian determined that the best option might be to swim to an island out in the lake. After weighing the potential risks, threat of the fire to the hikers and added exposure, the group (Air Attack, Division W and Operations), decided to move forward with utilizing 1VC for the extraction—and have the Type 2 Helicopter ordered as a contingency.
incidents.quote: Although multiple plans began to emerge during this emergency, Helicopter Manager Jagger continued to pursue a plan with the least amount of exposure and risk.

incidents.name: Taylor Creek Fire Use of Drones RLS
incidents.summary: Three key missions were conducted on the Taylor Creek/Klondike Fire in Southwestern Oregon: 1) Monitoring the fire activity at night; 2) Aerial ignition; and 3) Scouting the fire’s edge and determining potential control line locations. Drones helped accomplish all three of these missions.
incidents.quote: “It was 3 a.m. I had 34 miles of rough road to look at the Division. The ScanEagle flew over. They told me that the fire’s edge was cold. It saved me two hours!”

incidents.name: Carr Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: The accident resulted in the dozer rolling downhill several times before coming to rest. The operator was transported to an area hospital and is currently being evaluated.
incidents.quote: On August 1, 2018 at approximately 12:25 am, a Call-When-Needed (CWN) bulldozer operating on Division B was involved in a rollover accident.

incidents.name: Home Creek Fire Insect Bite
incidents.summary: After being assessed by U.S. Forest Service EMTs, a medivac was ordered. An agency helicopter flew the firefighter to a helispot where a he was picked up and driven to a local hospital.
incidents.quote: While assigned to the Home Creek Fire on the Bureau of Land Management’s Burns District, a Redmond Smokejumper suffered a strong reaction to a probable insect bite or bee sting to the face.

incidents.name: Salmon Challis Smokejumper Concussion
incidents.summary: A U.S. Forest Service smokejumper jumped a fire on the Salmon-Challis. The flight resulted in the jumper going on the lee side of a ridge and a hard landing, resulting in a concussion. The jumper was assessed and then flown by agency helicopter to a local hospital. The patient was evaluated and released that evening to three days of light duty.

incidents.name: Tarina Fire Helicopter Wire Strike
incidents.summary: On August 3, 2018 at approximately 7:15 PM, a CAL FIRE helicopter was operating on the Tarina incident in Kern County, California. While operating on the incident, the helicopter, staffed with a Pilot and Fire Captain, contacted a wire. The pilot safely landed the helicopter, with no reported injuries. The helicopter sustained moderate damage.
incidents.quote: One of the helicopters currently in rotation came up on the radio and provided dip site information, including the numerous wires in the area.

incidents.name: Miriam Fire Logging Truck Accident
incidents.summary: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, A contracted logger was loading logs on to a truck using a boom type loader. A mechanical failure of boom turntable bolts resulted in dismounting of boom while in use lowering trailer section to ground. When dismount occurred, boom with operator’s seat attached pitched to the side throwing operator clear of the truck to the ground. Operator fell about 15’ resulting in head lacerations and broken ribs. Operator was transported via ground ambulance to a landing zone then picked up by an agency helicopter and transported to a hospital. Treated and released that evening.
incidents.quote: While using the Self-Loader to unload the trailer of the log truck, the bolts holding the Self-Loader platform on the truck sheared off.

incidents.name: Corta Fire Burnover and Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: Flame lengths that were initially reported at 8-10 inches increased to 4-5 feet due to increased and erratic winds. Fire impacted the engine on the front passenger side and quickly swept underneath the engine. The crewmember from E-47 escaped the heat to the northwest across the fence line, while the Captain 47 climbed to the top of the engine. The heat on top of the engine increased and the Captain 47 jumped from the engine, toward the rear. The Captain 47 ran through flames toward the direction of the escaped crewmember. E-55 witnessed the burnover of E-47. The Captain 47 sustained burn injuries during the burnover.
incidents.quote: While both engine personnel were at the rear of the engine, the fire increased in intensity.

incidents.name: Cougar Creek Fire Dozer Operator Injury
incidents.summary: Due to pre-existing hemophiliac condition, paramedic at ICP advised further evaluation and he was transported via ground ambulance to a hospital. Operator was released to home but not back to work before follow-up with physician.
incidents.quote: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF. A contract dozer operator was refueling his dozer and slipped off the dozer falling approximately 5-6 feet, then complained of back and neck pain.

incidents.name: Miriam Fire Tree in Powerline
incidents.summary: While improving a contingency line along an established road for a potential burnout operation, a standing tree made contact with a charged high voltage powerline when a logging deck of previously felled trees was bumped by a dozer. Initially, no one on the incident knew the powerline had been contacted by the standing tree. This situation was not realized until the local power company contacted the ICP to see if the incident personnel knew anything about the power outage.
incidents.quote: What would you do if you witnessed a tree or other object strike a powerline?

incidents.name: Hilltop Fire Hyponatremia Case
