incidents.summary: Manti La Sal NF. An IHC member assessed by FS EMTs was ambulanced to Provo Hospital throwing up and with low blood pressure. He was treated for acute hyponatremia (low sodium) and admitted to the hospital. IHC was released from the hospital on 8/10 and returned to the fire on 8/11.
incidents.quote: Manti La Sal NF. An IHC member assessed by FS EMTs was ambulanced to Provo Hospital throwing up and with low blood pressure.

incidents.name: 2018 USFS Short Haul Summary Cooper Mtn RLS 2018
incidents.summary: This illness was likely the result of the beginning stages of heat exhaustion due to the high outside air temperatures (95F+) and a heavy workload, coupled with a history of heart issues.
incidents.quote: On August 9, 2018 on the Cooper Mountain Fire, the patient—who had a known family history of heart related illness—was displaying cardiac symptoms.

incidents.name: Cooper Fire Chest Pain Incident
incidents.summary: The Helena Short-Haul crew was in Libby Montana and was used successfully to transport the patient approximately 4 miles to a LZ where there was Life Flight and ground transportation available. Paramedics recommended the patient be transported from there by ambulance to the Boundary County Hospital in Bonners Ferry Idaho. The patient received care and is in stable condition
incidents.quote: Idaho Panhandle NF, a firefighter from a State crew was experiencing chest pains and was unable to walk out, or get packed out in a timely manner due to the steepness of the terrain and lack of any roads nearby.

incidents.name: Ferguson Fire Tree Strikes Vehicle
incidents.summary: In the early afternoon of August 9, an incident Safety Officer on the Ferguson Fire was traveling westbound on Highway 41 when he came upon a Type 6 Engine blocking the road. Getting out of his vehicle and walking over to the engine, the Safety Officer learned that the road was closed while a crew felled a hazard tree. A few minutes later, he heard the tree fall and heard traffic on the radio stating that the tree had hit a vehicle. The uphill side of the back cut did not leave enough holding wood, causing a failure of the hinge.
incidents.quote: “The faller was on day 12 of the incident completing arduous work which could have been an influence on the decisions and ultimately the outcome.”

incidents.name: Carr Fire Driving Fatality
incidents.summary: On Aug. 9, 2018, at 12:19 a.m., Heavy Equipment Mechanic Andrew Brake was driving northbound on Highway 99 when his CAL FIRE support vehicle left the road, hit a tree and burst into flames.
incidents.quote: Carr Fire Driving Fatality

incidents.name: Ferguson Fire Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: It was early in the afternoon and I just finished filling up my Water Tender along with another Water Tender operator. We jumped into our trucks and started heading down the road to Drop Point 55. I was in the lead and driving at about 10-15 mph. Due to the dusty road conditions, the other Water Tender operator dropped back in an effort to let the dust settle. While continuing to drive to Drop Point 55, I receive a call on the radio from the other tender operator saying he went off the road and I needed to come back. It took a bit of time to make my way back to him. When I got there, I found him sitting on the bank above the rolled tender. I asked him if he was okay and he said he was. I didn’t see any evidence of injury.
incidents.quote: He couldn’t get the door open, so he had to kick the front window out to get himself out.

incidents.name: Corta Fire El Cariso IHC Member Medevac
incidents.summary: An El Cariso Interagency Hotshot Crew member began suffering chest pains. Forest Service EMTs responded with oxygen and called for a medevac.
incidents.quote: The Firefighter was medevac’d via agency helicopter (one skid helo extraction on 100% slope) and flown to the incident helibase where the Firefighter was then transferred to an air ambulance and flown to a hospital in Elko.

incidents.name: Crescent Mountain Fire Pulaski Injury
incidents.summary: He was stabilized by FS EMTs and then transported by ambulance to the hospital in Omak, WA where he received 4 stitches and was released.
incidents.quote: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, A contract firefighter was working with a hose and a Pulaski simultaneously. The hose burst under pressure and resulted in the Pulaski striking his knee.

incidents.name: Crater Lake Fire Smokejumper Injury
incidents.summary: The jumper was assessed by FS EMTs and then flown by an agency helicopter to a hospital in Hailey ID. He was released to 3 weeks of light duty.
incidents.quote: Sawtooth NF, a USFS Smoke Jumper broke his acromion bone (a bony process on the scapula) and dislocated his shoulder during a landing.

incidents.name: Miles Fire Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: The Water Tender had just completed filling porta tanks and was spraying the road while traveling out to refill. It was traveling north on Road 6640 when it left the road on the downhill side and rolled over against a tree approximatey 20 feet off the road. The vehicle rested on the driver’s side and was stopped from rolling multiple times by the downhill tree.
incidents.quote: Tree Prevents Tender from Rolling Multiple Times

incidents.name: Rattlesnake Creek Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Two crew members from the Navajo Interagency Hotshot Crew were injured by a burning snag while conducting fire suppression activities on the Rattlesnake Creek Fire, burning near Pollock, Idaho on the Clearwater National Forest. The two firefighters were moved from the fireline to awaiting ambulances that transported them to a hospital in McCall, Idaho. Both firefighters were treated and released from the hospital. One was released to go home and the other will be taken to a burn facility in Salt Lake City for additional care.
incidents.quote: “Even with a medivac situation, often times ‘slow is smooth and smooth is fast’—preparation is key.”

incidents.name: Holy Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: Around noon, I was working on a section of line that had a brush pile I was clearing out. The brush was pretty thick. I therefore didn’t realize that I was about to roll up onto a large boulder that was hidden under the brush pile. Rolling up on this boulder made the dozer tip over on its side. It all seemed to happen in slow motion. There was no violent bounce. I was wearing my seatbelt which kept me in the cab during the rollover. I was able to remove myself from the cab. I realized that I had no injuries from this incident.
incidents.quote: “The tip-over happened in slow motion.I keep replaying the slow roll-over,over and over again in my head.” -Dozer Operator

incidents.name: Ranch Fire Tree Strike Fatality
incidents.summary: On August 13, 2018 at approximately 5:25 PM, a Very Large Air Tanker (VLAT) completed a retardant drop along Division C of the Menocino Complex Fire in Mendocino County, California. Following the drop, three firefighters suffered minor injuries and one firefighter suffered fatal injuries after being struck by falling tree debris.
incidents.quote: A retardant drop from a VLAT uprooted an 87-foot tall Douglas Fir and also sheared an 89-foot tall, 18-inch DBH Douglas Fir 29 feet above the base killing 1 firefighter and injuring 3 more.

incidents.name: Donnell Fire Chest Pain
incidents.summary: He was flown off the fire to a ground ambulance and transported to a hospital. Last report was patient is in stable condition.
incidents.quote: Stanislaus NF, a firefighter complained of chest tightness and anxiety.

incidents.name: Cougar Creek Fire Snake Bite
incidents.summary: FFA had just sat down for a break and was moving around to get comfortable when he felt a sharp pain in his abdomen. He was angry as he stood up searching for the guilty bee when he noticed a snake crawling across his pack. Concerned that he’d been bitten by the snake, he checked his abdomen and discovered a small area that was pink in color and there were two small puncture wounds.
incidents.quote: The Firefighter remembered his training and focused on his breathing. He stayed calm and relaxed so the venom would not spread rapidly through his blood stream.

incidents.name: Bacon Rind Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: There the employee received 2 liters of fluid and was released from the ER and spent the day recovering in a hotel room. Back to full duty.
incidents.quote: Custer Gallatin NF: Firefighter was medevac’d around midnight due to HRI and was flown to Bozeman Deaconess Hospital in Bozeman, MT.

incidents.name: Horns Mountain Fire SEAT Emergency Landing
incidents.summary: The aircraft, working with two other Fire Bosses on the Horns Mountain Fire, went down in a group of trees next to a gravel road and came to an abrupt stop. The pilot was able to extricate himself from the aircraft and make it on his own to the gravel road. The response to this Incident Within an Incident (IWI) resulted in the pilot being airlifted to Sacred Heart Medical Center in Spokane, Washington where he was diagnosed with broken ribs and a bruised lung. He was treated and released.
incidents.quote: On August 14, Fire Boss 242 (a Single Engine Air Tanker) experienced a complete power loss and was forced to make an emergency landing.

incidents.name: Carr Fire Laceration Infection
incidents.summary: Crewmember received a laceration on the Carr Fire one and a half weeks ago and it became infected. Currently receiving intravenous antibiotics and will be released on light duty.
incidents.quote: USFS IHC crew member was admitted to Mercy hospital due to an infection.

incidents.name: Stone Fire Initial Attack Entrapment
incidents.summary: Two engine modules and a helicopter and crew were assigned. The fire almost contained at ½ acre when conditions changed and the fire behavior escalated quickly and dramatically, growing to approximately 1,500 acres that evening. Firefighters disengaged from the fire, during that disengagement their escape was compromised. A helicopter being used for bucket work, jettisoned the bucket and extracted the firefighters. No injuries were sustained.
incidents.quote: “I am not getting left here. I will hang on right here if I have to.”

incidents.name: Fire Trail Fire Unresponsive Crewmember
incidents.summary: He was packaged by two FS EMTs and flown by agency helicopter to an ambulance then driven to Star Valley medical center. Patient has been released and is on light duty until cleared by a neurologist.
incidents.quote: Bridger Teton NF: Crewmember from Idaho was found unresponsive.

incidents.name: Cougar Creek Fire Water Tender Accident
incidents.summary: Okanogan Wenatchee NF: Contractor from Twisp, WA incurred a head laceration and three broken ribs when a tender rolled off the road, down a steep slope. Incident medical personnel provided initial care and the individual was transported via incident ambulance to a drop point and then life-flighted to the hospital. The patient i believed to have been released from the hospital on 8/20/18. A RLS team is currently reviewing the incident.
incidents.quote: Once Robert emerged from the vehicle, he sat down for a few minutes and then realized that it was possible that no one knew that he had rolled over the edge. Unable to locate his radio, he grabbed his cell phone to call 9-1-1. But as Robert tried to dial out, the face of his phone kept getting covered with blood.

incidents.name: 2018 USFS Short Haul Summary Short Creek RLS
incidents.summary: When the Short Haulers arrived, Medics were on scene and conducting primary medical care, placing an IV and administering pain medication. The patient had 2nd and 3rd degree burns covering the majority of his body and multiple lacerations.
incidents.quote: On August 18, 2018 on the Short Creek Incident, there was a General Aviation Plane accident.

incidents.name: Sheep Creek Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: A helicopter crash in a remote area near Battle Mountain, Nevada ignited a wildfire, resulting in a burnover of a Type 4 engine on a Search and Rescue mission responding to the helicopter crash.
incidents.quote: Within seconds, the fire was all around Pumper-2

incidents.name: McLeod Fire Bee Sting Incident
incidents.summary: Okanogan Wenatchee NF: Crew member from a contract crew module was stung multiple times by bees while on the fire line. Employee was moved to a vehicle where he experienced hives, swelling of the nasal airway, and arms/legs. Non-Forest Service EMT provided care to patient and he was driven to an awaiting county ambulance for transport to the hospital. Employee was later released back to full duty.
incidents.quote: Crew member from a contract crew module was stung multiple times by bees.

incidents.name: Payette and Salmon Challis NFs Private Plane Crash
incidents.summary: Payette helitack responded to suppress the fire, County EMS officials launched a helicopter to handle the aviation emergency. County requested the FS helicopter (short haul qualified) to assist as one of the private aircraft passengers was determined to be in urgent need of medical attention and unable to hike to a landing zone. The FS conducted a short-haul of one of the civilians. The short haul was successful.
incidents.quote: Payette and Salmon-Challis NFs, Idaho; a private plane with two passengers crashed near the Forest’s boundary and ignited a wildland fire.

incidents.name: Short Creek Emergency Assistance to the Public Short Haul
incidents.summary: Lemhi County Dispatch received a report of a plane crash and a resulting wildland fire deep in the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness. The Salmon-Challis National Forest responded with the Challis Helitack Crew whose primary mission was to size-up the reported fire. After spotting survivors near the crash site, the crew identified and was able to land at an unimproved landing spot suitable for a Type 3 Helicopter above the crashed aircraft.
incidents.quote: Two critically injured patients with second and third degree full body burns; aggressive bees covering and stinging the patients and the rescuers; a crashed airplane that was still on fire; and all in the middle of the largest contiguous wilderness area outside of Alaska.

incidents.name: Mendocino Complex Entrapment
incidents.summary: The Mendocino Complex consisted of the Ranch and River fires that started on July 27, 2018 in Mendocino County, California. Resources from other divisions were brought over to help with the operations. These resources included federal and local fire resources and strike teams from the Los Angeles Fire Department and CAL FIRE. During the burnout operations, a sudden wind shift and explosive fire growth happened and at about 1733, personnel were cut off from their escape routes. Most of the firefighters were able to move back to their vehicles to exit the area. However, six individuals farther down the dozer line were forced to run in front of the advancing flame front, through unburned fuels to a nearby dirt road for approximately one mile before they were picked up and transported for treatment. Injuries include 1st and 2nd degree burns and a dislocated shoulder.
incidents.quote: “We felt like dogs coming out of a kennel.”

incidents.name: Corral Canyon Simulated Fire Cleveland NF Firefighter Fall
incidents.summary: The Firefighter complained of extreme hip pain to a Forest Service EMT. The EMT began immobilization and two additional cooperator Medics assisted in hiking the Firefighter via backboard to a road and waiting ALS ambulance.
incidents.quote: An Engine Crewmember working on a training fire slipped, fell and suffered a fractured hip.

incidents.name: Cougar Creek Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: Stabilized by FS EMTs and taken to Leavenworth Hospital for stitches. Released to light duty.
incidents.quote: Okanogan Wenatchee NF, A contract firefighter working as a swamper received a 3 inch laceration on one of his legs just above the boot

incidents.name: Hirz Fire Dehydration Incident
incidents.summary: Shasta-Trinity NF, crew member from IHC was transported to hospital suffering from dehydration, physical and mental exhaustion, low blood pressure and nausea. Treated and released to 24 hours of light duty.

incidents.name: Columbus Fire Bee Sting Incident
incidents.summary: Transported to Hospital in Roseburg, OR. Treated and released to full duty.
incidents.quote: Umpqua NF, A contract firefighter was stung to face with allergic reaction. Ambulance responded and medics administered an EPI, Benadryl and an IV.

incidents.name: Cabin Lake Fire Demob Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: A Public Information Officer trainee was traveling in a rental car from the Cabin Lake Fire to Denver for a demob flight the following day. While driving on I-70 near Frisco, Colorado, she became caught in a severe storm with heavy rainfall. Her vehicle began to hydroplane, went off the road, and overturned. She received a broken right arm and left shoulder, was treated at a local hospital, and kept overnight. When she returns home, she will require surgery. The State Trooper investigating this accident said that the tread levels on rental car’s rear tires were well below the allowable limits.
incidents.quote: When You Rent a Car, Do You Remember to Check the Tires’ Tread Wear?

incidents.name: McLeod Fire Hit by Branch
incidents.summary: Non-FS EMTs iced wrist and flushed eye. Contractor was taken by ambulance to hospital and was assessed by an eye specialist for scratches to eye.
incidents.quote: Okanogan Wenatchee NF, Contract firefighter was spraying water on a hot spot of a tree when a branch from above the hot spot broke off and glanced the left side of the face, right wrist and right leg.

incidents.name: Hirz Fire Hit by Rock Medevac
incidents.summary: August 22, 2018 started off like any other day. Firestorm Crew 3 began work on constructing handline in Division Tango to tie-in two stretches of dozer line. This section of line was steep and rocky, which prevented the dozers from progressing farther. Late that afternoon, a crew member began shouting “ROCK!” This boulder would end up striking two crew members assigned to Firestorm Crew 3. An Air National Guard rescue helicopter, assigned to perform medevac duties, performed the hoist mission and flew both patients to the local trauma center. Both walked out of the trauma center under their own power approximately four hours later.
incidents.quote: Two contract firefighters were hit by a bolder dislodged from a dozer operation above them. Bolder described as the size of a mini-cooper.

incidents.name: Davis Fire ICP Electrical Hazard
incidents.summary: The Base Camp Manager for the Davis Fire was plugging in power to the Information Technology trailer for the Incident Management Team when the electrical panel arced and scorched the fuse panel. This also caused a fusing of the ground on the three-pronged 120-volt adapter. After a certified electrician evaluated the fuse panel, he determined that the hot wire was grounded directly to the panel mounting screw and the neutral wire was not connected. The panel wiring allowed the metal of the trailer to be energized—causing an electrical shock hazard.After further investigation, it was determined that when this trailer was on the previous Rattlesnake Creek Fire it was directly wired to the service drop panel. When the trailer was demobed from the Rattlesnake Creek Fire, it was determined that the wiring to the service drop panel was disconnected and someone attempted to rewire the fuse panel on the trailer incorrectly.
incidents.quote: A certified electrician should handle all wiring needs.

incidents.name: Miriam Fire Shooting Incident RLS
incidents.summary: At approximately 1500, four incident personnel spot two individuals walking down the PCT approximately 200 yards below them. The incident personnel stand up and holler and wave. All four are wearing yellow Nomex fire shirts. Two had bright yellow hardhats. They therefore thought they had been seen by these two individuals. The incident personnel watched with binoculars as one of the two individuals put a scoped rifle on a bi-pod and looked up the mountain toward them. They continued to wave until a shot was fired. They then bailed off the backside of the mountain to take cover as a second shot rang out.
incidents.quote: “They have a scoped rifle and are pointing it at us!” -Lookout

incidents.name: 2018 USFS Short Haul Summary James Fire RLS
incidents.summary: On August 23, 2018 on the James Fire, the patient was indicating signs/symptoms of heat exhaustion and had been in and out of consciousness and vomiting after working a Type V fire on steep ground in extreme conditions.
incidents.quote: Short-Haul is not an air ambulance, the goal is to transfer the patient to a ground or air ambulance with advanced care as soon as possible.

incidents.name: South Sugarloaf Dozer Tip Over RLS
incidents.summary: On August 24 on Division Hotel of the South Sugarloaf Fire near Owyhee, a bulldozer experienced a tip over. In the process of offloading from the transport the dozer tipped over 90 degrees, resting on its right side.
incidents.quote: Working around heavy equipment requires increased situational awareness due to the size, weight and potential chain reactions from equipment.

incidents.name: Hirz Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: Patient was stabilized by FS EMTs and then transported via ground ambulance to hospital. Patient believed to have non-serious injuries as of the time of this report.
incidents.quote: Shasta-Trinity NF, a Sequoia NF engine crew member was hit by a rock bolder dislodged from a dozer operation above the firefighter.

incidents.name: Rabbit Foot Fire Medical Seizure
incidents.summary: A Boise National Forest employee on the Rabbit Foot Fire fireline had a seizure. He was evaluated by a municipal EMT and transported by ambulance to the Incident Command Post. In stable condition, he was transported by the crew boss from ICP to Boise to see a private specialist. He was then released to light duty on the District.

incidents.name: Rabbit Foot Fire Radio Interference
incidents.summary: On August 18, after experiencing nearly nine days of intermittent white noise—locking out the Command repeater system for 10 to 30 minutes at a time the Incident Management Team (IMT) called for an operational stand-down until radio issues could be resolved. This stand-down lasted two days until it was eventually discovered that interference from a third party was the cause of the problem and communication was restored. This third party was suspected to be a NOAA weather transmitter, however this could not be confirmed.
incidents.quote: "Some of the resources on my Division got irritated enough with the noise that they turned their radios off. I had to drive to their location to relay an important message."

incidents.name: Horns Mountain Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: Reports indicate that Aarseth developed pneumonia which became septic. Aarseth was treated at Sacred Heart Medical Center in Springfield, Oregon, but was taken off life support on Sept. 3 after suffering irreversible damage to his organs. Aarseth passed away early the following morning on Sept. 4
incidents.quote: Firefighter II Eric Aarseth worked the Horns Mountain Fire in Washington on Aug. 27 and was released at 6:00 p.m. On Aug. 28, Aarseth was found unresponsive at his home in Oregon.

incidents.name: Donnell Fire Medical Seizure
incidents.summary: A Hoist helicopter was called and flew the firefighter to hospital in Modesto. Patient was tested and released but condition not determined. Released to light duty pending further evaluation.
incidents.quote: Stanislaus NF, Forest Service engine crewmember working on this fire suffered from apparent stroke or seizure.

incidents.name: Davis Fire Explosion in ICP
incidents.summary: The Pelican Case had been placed near the heater output, which caused excessive heat within the Pelican Case. The compressed gas in the Dust-Off container expanded and caused the can to fail. The point of failure was the bottom rim of the can.
incidents.quote: In the Davis Fire’s ICP, at approximately 0230 hours in the morning, a muffled “pop” was heard in an unoccupied yurt next to an occupied yurt.

incidents.name: Cow Fire Hit by Tree Medevac
incidents.summary: The Firefighter was assisted by Forest Service EMTs and then flown via an Agency ship to a hospital in Bend, Ore. The Firefighter was evaluated and given a CT scan which revealed no significant injuries and Firefighter was then released.
incidents.quote: On the Cow Fire on the Malheur National Forest a La Grande Hotshot Crewmember was struck by an identified snag.

incidents.name: Lakeside Fire Chemical Exposure
incidents.summary: On September 1, ground and aviation resources were dispatched to a fire near an industrial plant. The initial attack response included a combination of state, county, U.S. Forest Service, and Bureau of Land Management firefighting resources, including multiple aircraft, engines, and overhead. After engaging in firefighting efforts, some aviation resources over the fire and others stationed nearly five miles from the industrial plant began reporting a taste of metal in their mouths. Concerned that they may have been exposed to hazardous emissions, they chose to disengage from the fire.
incidents.quote: “It tasted like I had pennies in my mouth.” -Air Attack

incidents.name: McLeod Fire Hit by Log
incidents.summary: Stabilized by FS EMTs and then ambulanced to a landing zone and then taken by air-ambulance to hospital in Wenatchee. Diagnosed with a collapsed lung and ? Will be hospitalized for a few days until lung re-inflates.
incidents.quote: Okanogan Wenatchee NF. A FS contract firefighter mopping up on a steep slope was hit by a rolling log, and it rolled over his chest.

incidents.name: Carr Fire Ankle Injury
incidents.summary: A Hoist helicopter was called and flew the firefighter to hospital in Modesto. Patient was tested and released but condition not determined. Released to light duty pending further evaluation.
incidents.quote: Stanislaus NF, Forest Service engine crewmember working on this fire suffered from apparent stroke or seizure.

incidents.name: Canyon 66 Rollover
incidents.summary: At about 1130 the road became invisible in extremely thick smoke. The FEMO considered stopping, but heat felt through the side window from flaming stumps along the road edge could have blistered the truck’s paint or damaged tires. While creeping at an estimated 2 mph, the FEMO thought the road had curved. While turning slightly to the right, the FEMO felt the back left tire drop a little, giving the impression that the rear driver side tire was close to the downhill edge of the road. Turning more to the right, the truck then began to slide and tip to the left.
incidents.quote: “I called out a medical emergency on the radio, thinking the truck would soon be on fire. I had responded to three vehicle fires in the previous month—all of them had caught fire and consumed in a matter of minutes.”

incidents.name: McLeod Fire Hit by Tree Top
incidents.summary: FS EMTs stabilized the patient and assisted in hiking him to a ground ambulance. The patient was admitted to a hospital in Brewster, WA and released the following day diagnosed with severe bruising to shoulder.
incidents.quote: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF. A Forest Service firefighter cutting a snag was hit by the top of the tree when it broke off.

incidents.name: McLeod Fire Slip and Fall Medivac
incidents.summary: Firefighter complained of severe pain and was unable to walk. FS EMT stabilized the patient and packaged for transport via liter to a ground ambulance. Taken to a hospital in Brewster, WA. Admitted released the following day diagnosed with muscle strain.
incidents.quote: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF. A contract Firefighter slipped and fell walking down a fire line.

incidents.name: Gold Hill Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: The vehicle came to rest at an approximate 45-degree angle. A tree prevented it from rolling over. No passengers were injured. The vehicle was recovered and returned to the road. It received a thorough inspection, including a check of all fluids, and was then returned to service.
incidents.quote: A single vehicle with three passengers was traveling with other DIV resources up a narrow, dusty mountain road when the vehicle encountered a soft, inside shoulder and was pulled off the road onto the steep fill-slope.

incidents.name: Ducor Fire Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: On September 4, 2019, at approximately 8:43 AM, a CAL FIRE engine from the San Diego Unit was driving near the community of Ducor in Tulare County, California. Four firefighters were transported to a local hospital for treatment and evaluation. The Fire Captain will remain in the hospital overnight. The three firefighters have since been released.
incidents.quote: While travelling to meet up with the rest of the strike team to be released from a cover assignment, the fire engine was involved in a rollover traffic collision.

incidents.name: Stewart Creek Fire Cardiac Medivac
incidents.summary: An Interagency Hotshot Crew firefighter on the Stewart Creek Fire showed signs of an apparent cardiac event with chest pains and shortness of breath. The patient was assessed by EMTs who called for an air ambulance. An agency helicopter picked up the patient at a helispot and was flown by the waiting air ambulance to a hospital in Boise. The patient was admitted and has since been released.

incidents.name: Tepee Fire Dozer on Fire
incidents.summary: During line construction on one of the spot fires, an ember started a small fire on the back portion of the dozer between the rear window and the mesh protective screen. An engine suppressed the fire with several gallons of water and the dozer continued direct line construction. The dozer operator noticed the smell once again, but this time much stronger. He looked out the rear window and noticed smoke coming out from between the tank guard and the fuel tank. The second attempt to suppress the fire was ineffective. Although numerous ideas to apply water or retardant were discussed, both individuals agreed that the dozer was already fully involved and was a lost cause.
incidents.quote: “By the time he could smell it, it was on fire, deep in the machine.”

incidents.name: North Fire ICP Carbon Monoxide Exposure
incidents.summary: Generators were placed within 5-10 feet of structures and window style air conditioner units were placed in the windows of the tents. AC units draw air from the outside, pass that air through a condenser, and blow into the structure to which it is attached. Thus, pollutants or gases could be passed through the unit and into workspaces. On the sixth day of the team’s assignment, Safety briefed the IC, suspecting that the generator’s exhaust was the possible cause and indicating that they should be moved.
incidents.quote: “Each day I spent the full day in camp, I got a pounding headache. In the woods, I felt great.” IMT Member

incidents.name: Pole Creek and Bald Mountain Fires
incidents.fire: Pole Creek and Bald Mountain Fires
incidents.summary: The context surrounding the Pole Creek and Bald Mountain fires was complex. An unusually wet rain storm near the end of the traditional fire season, a desire to restore beneficial fire to the landscape, and multiple lightning strikes igniting two fires in remote locations with unnaturally heavy vegetation loadings followed later by a unprecedented string of red flag warning events and an atypical pattern in the ERC index to produce a situation in which thousands of people were evacuated from their homes. This wildfire situation posed substantial danger to the lives and property of local residents. This FLA was conducted in an effort to learn from these events.
incidents.quote: Pole Creek and Bald Mountain Fires Facilitated Learning Analysis

incidents.name: Flat Fire Smoke Jumper Hard Landing
incidents.summary: Bridger-Teton NF. A Smoke Jumper had a hard landing injuring an ankle. Stabilized by FS EMTs and flown by agency helicopter to Afton Airport, then taken by ground ambulance to hospital. X-Rays indicated ankle avulsion. Patient was released to light duty with a follow-up appointment next week.
incidents.quote: Flat Fire Smoke Jumper Hard Landing

incidents.name: Defective Fusee Striker Caps
incidents.summary: During a “Firing Device Demonstration” at this S-390/190 Field Day, the instructor attempted to light a fusee to demonstrate the correct procedure for students. But the fusee would not light. It was determined that the fusees wouldlight with a striker from a different batch of fusees.Neither the original cap or other identical caps would light any of the defective fusees. However, all defective fusees that were tested successfully ignited on the first attempt with a different style of striker.
incidents.quote: Defective Fusee Striker Caps discovered during training class.

incidents.name: Howe Ridge Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: Glacier NP, A IHC crew member tripped in heavy brush and fell onto a cut stump. Patient was stabilized by FS EMTs and the taken by ground ambulance to a hospital in Whitefish and admitted. The patient has been diagnosed with a fractured rib and punctured lung. Released on 9/21/18 to light duty.
incidents.quote: Howe Ridge Fire Fall Injury

incidents.name: Delta Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: Injured individuals transported to St. Elizabeth Hospital in Red Bluff, CA. Five injuries were confirmed ranging from bruises, cuts, and scrapes. All were released from the hospital. The contract company owner tied in with folks at the hospital and later checked on the entire crew confirming their individual statuses. A thorough debriefing and pulse check with the crew was conducted and currently back on the Delta fire with replacements for the folks that were injured.
incidents.quote: California: A FS Contract Crew was en-route to the Delta Fire when they experienced a reported tire failure (between Corning, CA and Red Bluff, CA on Interstate 5) on one of the crew carrier vehicles which resulted in a vehicle accident.

incidents.name: Pole Creek Fire HRI Extraction
incidents.summary: A line paramedic responded and assessed the patient administering O2 and an IV. Due to location, a Short Haul ship was requested along with an air ambulance. Patient was short hauled successfully to a site where an air ambulance and a ground ambulance was waiting. After further assessment the air ambulance was released and the patient was transported by ground ambulance to a hospital in Payson, UT.
incidents.quote: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF. An engine crewmember suffered a Heat Related Injury.

incidents.name: Roosevelt Fire Travel Medical
incidents.summary: An Interagency Hotshot Crew crewmember, in travel status returning home from the Roosevelt Fire, had overnighted in Wendover, Nevada. A member of the crew was found unconscious the following morning. Other crew members alerted 911 and the patient was flown by air ambulance to a hospital in Salt Lake City, where he was admitted--and his condition was steadily improving.

incidents.name: Elk Creek Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: At approximately 1130 the driver of the vehicle turned a corner traveling downhill at 20 mph on forest road 622, the vehicle soon encountered a washed-out area near the embankment side of the shoulder. The driver felt the rear end of the vehicle begin to slide out, the driver attempted to apply the brakes and turn the vehicle away from the slippery shoulder embankment but with no success. The vehicle began to slide as the road conditions would not allow for effective maneuvering. As the vehicle became uncontrollable the front of the vehicle traveled off the shoulder toward the Elk Creek drainage. Next, the vehicle rolled downhill paralleling the drainage with two complete rotations then the vehicle came to a halt on all four wheels 50 – 75 feet facing downhill near the bottom of the drainage.
incidents.quote: The only way to get experience driving hazardous road conditions is to drive hazardous road conditions. Having experience is ideal, but getting experience involves risk.

incidents.name: Earling Fire and Rescue Department Fatality
incidents.summary: At approximately 2:40 p.m. on Oct. 20, 2018, Chief Tom Henrich responded with Earling Fire and Rescue Department units to a combine and field fire. While on scene, Henrich fell ill. CPR was administered and Henrich was transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced deceased.

incidents.name: Brushy Mountain RX Engine Burnover
incidents.summary: On October 22, 2018, a CAL FIRE fire engine staffed with one Fire Apparatus Engineer and two firefighters were participating in a Vegetation Management Program (VMP) hazardous fuel reduction burn near Covelo, CA. No personnel were injured during the incident.
incidents.quote: While the crew was away from the engine assisting with containment of several spot fires, the parked, unattended engine was impacted by spot fires burning outside of containment lines, and sustained major damage.

incidents.name: Cow Creek Fire Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
incidents.summary: On October 22, 2019, at approximately 0645, an employee assigned to the ICP Medical Unit was involved in a medical incident. The patient was transported to the hospital and was released the same day.
incidents.quote: Initial reports indicated the patient had been sleeping in the heated Medical Unit yurt and awoke with severe headache, nausea and vomiting.

incidents.name: CA OES Fire and Rescue Division Fatality
incidents.summary: California Office of Emergency Services Assistant Fire Chief Ken Hood suffered an acute medical emergency during a multiagency coordination meeting in Quincy, CA.
incidents.quote: Despite a valiant effort by first responders and then emergency room personnel, Hood passed away hours later at the Plumas District Hospital in Quincy, CA.

incidents.name: Drum Escaped RX Fire
incidents.summary: In this document, the team addresses the elements above as required as well as systemic opportunities for improvement in line with a forest fuels program review.
incidents.quote: The Drum Wildfire was declared on 11/1/18 from a series of pile burns that were lit beginning on 10/22/18 on the West Side of the Mount Hood National Forest.

incidents.name: Camp Fire Burn Injuries 2018
incidents.summary: Three firefighters were burned during preplanning for a firing operation on Rattlesnake Flats Road, and two engine crew members were burned in a propane BLEVE.
incidents.quote: During the first 24-hour period of the Camp Incident in Butte County, California, two accidents occurred resulting in five (5) firefighters suffering serious burns.

incidents.name: Camp Fire Propane Tank Explosion
incidents.summary: During the first 24-hour period of the Camp Incident in Butte County, California, two accidents occurred resulting in five (5) firefighters suffering serious burns. On November 8, 2018, at approximately 3:00 PM while preplanning and preparing for a firing operation, one (1) Fire Captain and two (2) inmate firefighters suffered burns and were transported to a burn center for treatment. During the same operational period, on November 9, 2018, at approximately 5:00 AM, a fire engine crew acting on a threatened residential structure were burned when a propane tank exploded. One (1) Fire Captain and one (1) Fire Fighter I suffered burns and were transported and treated at a local hospital.
incidents.quote: There was a significant north wind event affecting Northern California beginning on the night of Wednesday, November 7 and continued through Friday, November 9, 2018.

incidents.name: Woolsey Fire Hit by Vehicle
incidents.summary: On November 14, 2018 at approximately 11:45 PM, a fire department Lieutenant assigned to the Woolsey Fire was run over by a civilian vehicle while resting on the fireline. The injured firefighter was transported by a helicopter to a local trauma center. The Lieutenant was released from the hospital 37 hours later after suffering minor injuries and being held for observation.
incidents.quote: Refrain from sleeping in un-marked, non-designated sleeping areas on an incident.

incidents.name: Long Park Rx Prep Chainsaw Accident
incidents.summary: A Forest Service sawyer sustained an injury during a felling operation that resulted in a self-evacuation and trip to the hospital. During the back cut, the kickback zone came into contact with a placed wedge, resulting in a violent kickback that ultimately struck the sawyer in the abdomen, breaking skin. Fortunately the injury was superficial and did not require stitches.
incidents.quote: Chainsaw incident Laceration to abdomen resulting from kickback.

incidents.name: Cleveland NF PT Medical Incident
incidents.summary: She was diagnosed with a broken blood vessel resulting in a stroke. She is recovering and was released from the hospital a few days later.
incidents.quote: Cleveland National Forest, A IHC crew member was driven to the hospital after complaining of dizziness during PT.

incidents.name: Cleveland NF Post PT Medical Incident
incidents.summary: He was transported via ambulance and was hospitalized for two days. No further information available.
incidents.quote: Cleveland National Forest, A Helitack crewmember had an apparent seizure after PT near the helibase.

incidents.name: Tree on Powerline
incidents.summary: Mike and John further investigated. They determined that the powerline under the tree looked to be severed about 75 feet from the tree, between two power poles. The line did not appear to be active. However, this was not confirmed. Furthermore, it was not clear whether or not the line had previously been down—or if falling the tree had torn it down.
incidents.quote: “Mike picked up the powerline and rolled it up. His thought was that it was dead because of where it had broken off. But in reality, it was the common feed line and he was not grounded. By luck, he lived to tell us what he’d done.” Zone FMO

incidents.name: West Canal RX Engine Burn Damage
incidents.summary: When ignitions became established in this area with the heavier fuels, the flame lengths quickly increased from approximately 2 feet to 10 feet. This is when the Engine heat damage incident occurred.
incidents.quote: The crewmember running the hose stated that—due to the heat in both directions—they weren’t able to go forward or back up.

incidents.name: Doster Incident Hit By Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: A CAL FIRE Conservation Camp handcrew was assisting Calaveras County with vegetation removal along county maintained roads. During the project, a large log released from its position upslope of the county road. As the log rolled downhill onto the road, it struck a Calaveras County employee and CAL FIRE handcrew member. The handcrew member suffered minor injuries while the County employee suffered fatal traumatic injuries.
incidents.quote: The log gained momentum as it traveled downhill. Within seconds, it advanced into the roadway. As the log hit Cooperator 1, the butt of the tree rose up and hit a crew member (Crew Member 1) in the back who was feeding the chipper.

incidents.name: Midewin ATV Backing Incident
incidents.summary: As Pat was pushed forward into the handlebars, a sudden throttle acceleration pushed Pat off the ATV. As Pat’s right lower leg came off the ATV, it made contact with the right front tire, pulling Pat’s leg under the tire. Ultimately, the decision was made to transport via ambulance due to the serious nature of the injury and the potential for circulation and pain issues developing during transport. The ambulance arrived shortly after Pat arrived at the road. Pat’s supervisor followed the ambulance to the hospital to serve as Hospital Liaison. At the hospital it was determined that Pat had a broken fibula and was put in a cast and had surgery later to repair the break.
incidents.quote: As the Firing Boss Trainee’s right lower leg came off the ATV, it made contactwith the right front tire, sucking the leg under the tire—like a piece of paper being pulled through a printer.

incidents.name: Multiple Pile Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: On March 27, 2019, in the Amador El Dorado Unit (AEU), an inmate firefighter suffered a burn injury to the hand while adding fuel to a burn pile. Treatment continues for the burn injuries.

incidents.name: Sam Houston NF Prescribed Fire Helicopter Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On Wednesday March 27, 2019 the National Forests and Grasslands in Texas (NFGT) was conducting a series of aerial ignition prescribed burns across the Forest. At approximately 1410, the AS-350B3 (A-Star) helicopter conducting aerial ignition operations for the Compartment 9 prescribed fire on the Sam Houston National Forest (SHNF) crashed, killing U.S. Forest Service employee Daniel Laird and injuring another Forest Service employee and the contract pilot.
incidents.quote: District personnel trained and rehearsed for an “Incident Within an Incident,” which prepared them to respond to the needs of those involved in this accident, and to secure the crash site.

incidents.name: Multiple Pile Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: On March 28, 2019, in the Tulare Unit (TUU), an inmate firefighter suffered burn injuries to the torso, arm, and leg while adding fuel to burning piles. The injuries continue to be treated at the burn center.

incidents.name: Multiple Pile Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: On March 28, 2019, in the Butte Unit (BTU), a California Conservation Corp Crewmember suffered burns to due to standing too close to a burn pile.

incidents.name: Multiple Pile Burn Injuries Sonoma Lake Napa
incidents.summary: On March 31, 2019, in the Sonoma Lake Napa Unit (LNU), a CAL FIRE employee suffered burn injuries to the neck and chin.
incidents.quote: Multiple Pile Burn Injuries

incidents.name: Western Oregon Bucking Incident
incidents.summary: As it squeezed his bar out of the cut, with his chain still turning, Kip quickly pulled it out and narrowly avoided getting pinched out of the bottom compression bind. He repositioned the saw on top of the log to finish up the buck and release the final tension. As he began cutting down through the top of the of the log, he got about two inches down through the remaining top tension wood when the log violently exploded with an audible “pop” springing into the air and back toward the sawyer. This instantly moved the log approximately 6 - 8 feet both laterally and vertically breaking an internal mass of wood that was roughly the size of a 6” X 8” Douglas-fir construction beam. He found Kip in a semi-reclined sitting position on top of a smaller log that lay on the ground and was originally behind his cutting position by 4 - 6 feet.
incidents.quote: “Your focus is different when you’re sawing logs [into commercial lengths]. It’s more on your next log length and not necessarily on safety.” C-Faller and IHC Leadership on Project

incidents.name: William B Bankhead NF Felling
incidents.summary: The Sawyer became frustrated when his bar was pinched during his back cut. Unable to free his saw, he decided to call the Dozer Operator to use the dozer to push against the tree, with just enough force to release the saw. He intended to grab the saw when it was released, then use his predetermined escape route to get away from the falling tree.The Sawyer freed the saw, set it down, and as he turned away from the falling snag—attempting to clear the area—he heard the snap of the holding wood. The tree struck the dozer’s cab and pivoted off the dozer blade. The Dozer Operator looked back toward the Sawyer just in time to see that he had been launched vertically into the air.The Sawyer’s boots were literally at the Dozer Operator’s eye level. The Sawyer was catapulted by the butt of the snag and landed on a downed tree he had cut earlier.
incidents.quote: As soon as the Dozer Operator’s blade touched the snag, the holding wood snapped. The Dozer Operator watched as the tree fell toward his cab.

incidents.name: Verde Fire Medevac and COVID 19 Lessons
incidents.summary: The Verde Fire took place April 17 on the Coronado National Forest’s Santa Catalina Ranger District. It included an Incident Within an Incident, which resulted in a nighttime medical extraction. The IC worked with Dispatch to coordinate transportation of the patient via air. Because radio communications were poor in the area, most of the communication happened via cellular phone.
incidents.quote: At 2000 the IC called Dispatch with a “Yellow” medical, requesting a helicopter for extraction of a firefighter with a broken ankle injury.

incidents.name: Argyle Volunteer Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighters and EMS personnel immediately provided emergency medical aid to Hudson. He was transported to the hospital where resuscitation efforts continued but were not successful.
incidents.quote: While responding as a passenger in the department’s compressed air foam truck, Firefighter Dwain Hudson experienced a medical emergency.

incidents.name: Northeast Lakeside Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: He was immediately taken to the hospital where he passed away on April 24, 2019.
incidents.quote: On April 21, 2019, Driver/Engineer Michael Watkins was responding to a brush firewhen he suffered a heart attack.

incidents.name: Plumas Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: She was treated by Forest Service EMTs and then transported via agency vehicle to a local hospital and then transferred to the UC Davis Burn Center. She was released to two weeks of light duty and follow-up examinations.
incidents.quote: A firefighter fell into an ash pit while conducting a pile burning operation on the Plumas National Forest.

incidents.name: Tonto NF PT Rhabdo Incident
incidents.summary: After doing morning Physical Fitness training on the Tonto National Forest, the firefighter felt muscle fatigue. Three days later, the employee drove themselves to the hospital in POV and was admitted to the hospital with signs of Rhabdomyolysis. Expected to be back to normal duties in a few days.
incidents.quote: During the next two days, when the firefighter tried to do PT, became very fatigued.

incidents.name: SW Colorado Fuel Geyser
incidents.summary: When my 462C did not readily start after manual shutdown, and knowing there was still ample fuel in the tank, I suspected vapor lock. After checking the other common culprits for difficulty in starting, this seemed to be confirmed. In addition, my familiarity with Stihl chainsaws suggested that the saw may continue to not start until it had cooled.
incidents.quote: “I share this incident to remind us all that caution needs to be taken as non-COVID threats still exist in our fire world.”

incidents.name: IHC Buggy Rollover
incidents.summary: The buggies passed through the town of Burney and slowly increased to highway speeds of 55 mph. Ahead of them, a 1996 gold Lexus sedan started to drift across the yellow line; it seemed to him that the driver was looking for a pair of dropped sunglasses, maybe even had fallen asleep. . The driver of C-21A thought she was going to correct. He edged to the right.“I think we both said ‘Oh sh%it!’ together when we realized she wasn’t going to correct, I got over as far as I could, maneuvered like evasive-style - engine academy - got over as far as I thought possible, I thought she was going to scrape us, but not hit us.”
incidents.quote: “I was limp for the first roll, second roll I grabbed the box overhead and then rode it out -tried to brace, the third roll the window exploded.” - C-21B Crewmember

incidents.name: Beaver Soup RX Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On Saturday, May 11, 2019 at approximately 0625 hours, a Forest Service truck sustained significant damage to the front of the vehicle while driving to a prescribed fire (Rx) on the Helena Ranger District. The Range Specialist (RS) was traveling eastbound on Highway 200 with the sun in his eyes.
incidents.quote: “I thought I had just killed someone”

incidents.name: Tahoe NF PT Rhabdo Incident
incidents.summary: These crewmembers are on the same engine module. They were transported to hospital via a GOV vehicle for suspected dehydration/rhabdomyolysis. Both employees were held for observation, one overnight and one for two nights, and then released to light duty. Both crewmembers were confirmed to have rhabdomyolysis by the hospital. Both cases were documented on the Heat Related Illness (HRI) form on NWCG. An AAR will be conducted by the Forest.
incidents.quote: Two engine crewmembers were experiencing muscle soreness and discolored urine after physical fitness training.

incidents.name: Castolon Fire Review
incidents.summary: Residents of the town of Santa Elena, Chihuahua, Mexico made the decision to ignite a residential trash pile east of their town, along the Rio Grande. Over the next 36 hours the predominant weather flow would change and cause winds to shift and increase dramatically. This caused spotting of the trash fire across the Rio Grande and into the United States and Big Bend National Park. After crossing the river and the international border in the late afternoon of May 22, 2019, fire behavior increased dramatically due to weather and fuel conditions in the thick mesquite.
incidents.quote: “Rolling in to the fire it was apparent that the fire was more than river cane and grass…” - IC

incidents.name: Fort Jackson Prescribed Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: On 5/22/19, Fort Jackson Environmental Division personnel initiated a 424 acre prescribed fire operation for wildlife habitat improvements and fuel management. During the prescribed burn, wildlife biologist and certified wildland firefighter, Angela "Nicole" Chadwick-Hawkins was assigned a ground ignition operation, utilizing an All-Terrain-Vehicle (ATV) to conduct the task. A search of her last known location was conducted during which Ms. Hawkins' body was found.
incidents.quote: Fort Jackson Prescribed Fire Fatality

incidents.name: GB 06S Prescribed Fire and 9 Mile Ditch Wildfire
incidents.fire: GB 06S Prescribed Fire and 9 Mile Ditch Wildfire
incidents.summary: On May 22, 2019, personnel within the Gulf Coast National Wildlife Refuge Complex conducted a prescribed fire in the GB-06S unit of Grand Bay National Wildlife Refuge.The western flank of the GB-06S prescribed fire was converted to the 9-mile Ditch wildfire when the prescribed fire spotted onto private land adjacent to the SW corner of the unit and burned a total of 60 acres on one private land owner. The remainder of the prescribed fire was completed with no further issues.
incidents.quote: Be prepared for the unexpected. Ensure that the experience is commensurate with the complexity of the prescribed fire including unforeseen events.

incidents.name: Tahoe NF PT Rhabdo Incident_May 24
incidents.summary: Medical Emergency, Fitness, Rhabdomyolysis, Health and Fitness, Medical or Exertion or Heat
incidents.quote: Tahoe NF PT Rhabdo Incident_May 24

incidents.name: Payette NF Smokejumper Injury
incidents.summary: The result was a very hard impact to the ground upon landing. Forest Service EMTs responded and performed a medical assessment at the jump spot. The jumper was then transported via ambulance to a local hospital. After X-rays and a CT scan were completed, it was determined that the individual received a left groin and thigh muscle strain. He was released to light duty for one week.
incidents.quote: A McCall Smokejumper was injured during a proficiency jump. The jumper came in contact with a tree which caused his parachute to partially deflate, leading to an increase in decent rate.

incidents.name: Jordan Fire Hit By Log
incidents.summary: A Line Paramedic was present and assessed the firefighter and placed a C-collar on the patient and then assisted the patient’s hike to a helispot. The patient was then flown directly to the Fresno Regional Medical Center accompanied by the Paramedic and the IHC Captain. The patient was evaluated, received several staples, and was released to light duty for 3 days.
incidents.quote: A member of the Laguna IHC was walking on steep terrain on the Inyo National Forest when a log dislodged above the firefighter and rolled, hitting the firefighter in the head, resulting in a 3 centimeter laceration.

incidents.name: Bald Mountain Firefighter Injury
incidents.summary: While conducting mobile attack, a BLM firefighter was struck by the tire of a moving engine, impacting his foot and lower leg and pulling him to the ground, with the engine continuing to roll over his lower left leg. The resulting injury was non-life threatening, but resulted in a bone contusion and soft tissue damage, which lead to a medical recommendation of no-duty for two weeks.
incidents.quote: The Crewmember, on the hose, got a face full of smoke which caused him to react by either stopping or moving unconsciously into the path of the moving Engine (he could not recall his exact reaction).

incidents.name: Bald Mountain Fire Engine Burnover
incidents.summary: This incident occurred when an equipment malfunction related to water flow warranted the engine to stop and troubleshoot the malfunction. Both firefighters moved to the black side of the truck, during which time a spot fire ignited on the green side of the engine, rapidly spreading and impacting the engine. An attempt was made to move the engine to the black, but the crew was driven back by the fire. The two engine crewmembers utilized their escape route though the black to the Bald Mountain Road, approximately 20 yards away.
incidents.quote: The firefighter contacted a personal friend who was on the USFS Engine, via cell phone, to request assistance with suppressing the Local Engine which was now on fire because radios were in the Engine.

incidents.name: Bald Mountain Fire Engine Burnover and Firefighter Injury
incidents.summary: Two incidents occurred during the initial attack response on June 20, 2019 for the Bald Mountain Fire: an injury to a BLM firefighter (Incident 1); and the burnover of a local fire department engine (Incident 2). While both incidents occurred on this fire, they were not related and were mutually exclusive of each other.
incidents.quote: The Local Engine Captain attempted to get into the engine from the passenger side and move it, but was forced out by fire.

incidents.name: New Mexico Pack Test Rhabdo
incidents.summary: The individual does not remember starting Lap Five. The other people pacing with him say they remember him stating that he felt dizzy. The individual does not remember when or even saying this.He does remember his Supervisor telling him that he had 10 minutes to complete the final lap. And he remembers being dizzy for approximately 30 seconds (but does not remember where this occurred on the track). He remembers having tunnel vision for about 10 seconds. He does not remember collapsing.The first thing he remembers after the incident is a nurse shaking him to wake him and asking where he was.
incidents.quote: The individual was admitted to the hospitalunconscious with a body temperature of 107. The fast response and training of the fire crew probably saved this individual’s life and prevented any long-term medical effects.

incidents.name: White River NF Pack Test Medical Incident
incidents.summary: An evaluation by three Forest Service EMTs on site provided concern as she had trouble answering questions. She was taken to a local clinic. The clinic personnel then transported her via ambulance to Vail Hospital where she underwent a CT scan and was then admitted. She was released later that evening with no conclusions, but still suffering from aches. Follow-up exams requested.
incidents.quote: A firefighter taking the White River NF Pack complained of side pain.

incidents.name: Half Fire Helicopter Longline Incident
incidents.summary: As he descended above the drop area to release his load of water, the pilot inadvertently triggered the powerfill switch for the bucket instead of the release. The momentum created by the powerfill resulted in the aircraft being pulled in an unexpected direction.The bucket made contact with a 200-foot Jeffrey pine approximately 30 feet below the treetop—knocking several 3-inch limbs off the tree. This contact prompted the IHC crew members to run and seek cover behind the base of other trees
incidents.quote: “It just seemed like his [the helicopter pilot’s] reference was off. Like he was used to 100-foot line.” IHC Captain

incidents.name: West Boulder Medivac Lessons Learned
incidents.summary: At 0800 on the morning of June 25th, two Fisheries crewmembers broke camp along the West Boulder trail on the Yellowstone District of the Custer Gallatin NF. They had been working in the area the previous day and it was time to begin their 5 mile hike out to the trailhead and waiting truck. A windstorm from the previous evening had brought down several trees in the area and the ground was still wet. At approximately 9:40, while navigating a downed log across the trail, one of the crewmembers missed-stepped and rolled their ankle.
incidents.quote: Fishery Technician suffered a severely sprained ankle

incidents.name: Engine Slides Off Road
incidents.summary: On June 27th, 2019 at approximately 0900, a firefighter was transporting a type V Engine into town on a stretch of gravel road. Conditions were cloudy with a temperature of 49 degrees. Due to several thunderstorms, a 1/4 in. of rain had fallen in the last 24 hours making the road muddy and slick. The Engine went into a fence and struck a tree. No airbags deployed, and the firefighter was uninjured.
incidents.quote: On a curve in the road the Engine began to slide to the left. The firefighter braked and overcorrected sending the engine into the ditch on the right side of the road.

incidents.name: Cherokee IHC PT Rhabdo
incidents.summary: A Cherokee IHC crew member involved in physical fitness training became “over exerted”. He was evaluated by Forest Service EMTs and then taken by ambulance to a local hospital and later diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis. He is expected to make a full recovery but will remain hospitalized through the weekend.

incidents.name: Cherokee IHC PT Dehydration
incidents.summary: He was evaluated by Forest Service EMTs and then driven by an agency vehicle to a hospital where he was admitted for treatment and then released either that evening or the following day.
incidents.quote: A Cherokee IHC crew member became severely dehydrated during physical fitness training.

incidents.name: Tramway Fire Engine Crewmember Fall
incidents.summary: On the Tramway Fire—Palm Springs District (BLM)—a San Bernardino National Forest Engine Crewmember was hiking up the fireline assisting with a hose lay. Initial treatment was rendered by a U.S. Forest Service EMT. The Firefighter was unable to walk. Therefore, CALFIRE short-hauled the Firefighter to a nearby parking lot where the Firefighter was then life-flighted to a hospital.
incidents.quote: The Firefighter slipped and pulled a lower abdominal muscle.

incidents.name: Swede Mountain Chipping Incident
incidents.summary: At 1300 Crewmember A was assisting the dump truck operator in backing into place to hook up the chipper to the pintle hitch. While backing the dump truck into place, the chipper was bumped by the hitch, jarring the jack off the block of wood, resulting in the jack impacting the top of Crewmember A foot. Crewmember A ran from behind the dump truck, catching the attention of the other crewmembers on the project. The medical lead recognizing what had happened, immediately contacted the Incident Commander of the project, who initiated IWI protocols
incidents.quote: “Nothing fails harder than success” This deviation from normal operations was overlooked because they had been successful with the first 25 dump truck loads.

incidents.name: Payette NF Smokejumper Accident
incidents.summary: He was evaluated by Forest Service EMTs and then drove himself to the hospital where he was admitted, further evaluated, treated and released.
incidents.quote: A Washington Office employee conducting a proficiency jump out of the McCall Smokejumper Base experienced a hard landing resulting in a small facial laceration and broken finger.

incidents.name: Sun Country Volunteer Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: On July 1, 2019, Chief William "Casey" White responded to a grass fire mutual aid call to a neighboring county at approximately 2130 hours. After returning from the call, Chief White retired for the evening at home around 2400hrs. The next day, July 2, 2019, he returned to the station at 0930hrs to outfit a new apparatus with equipment. Chief White was found deceased at approximately 1730hrs that afternoon on the bay floor near the apparatus.
incidents.quote: Chief White was found deceased at approximately 1730hrs that afternoon on the bay floor near the apparatus.

incidents.name: South Dakota Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: Sawyer 1 went to remove his saw from the back. At that same moment, Firefighter A stepped forward to push the tree over as he believed it didn’t have enough weight to go on its own.awyer 1 felt his saw bar catch. Fearing the tree would fall on his bar, he jerked the bar out of the back cut. This caused the chainsaw tip to catch the outside of Firefighter A’s knee, causing the saw to buck against Sawyer 1.
incidents.quote: Firefighter A sustained a large laceration (approximately one to two inches deep) on the outside of his knee and multiple other gashes as the chainsaw bar skipped down his leg.

incidents.name: Mountain Fire Payson Helitack Firefighter Valley Fever
incidents.summary: A Payson Helitack Firefighter became ill on the Mountain Fire on the Tonto National Forest. The Firefighter drove to a local urgent care facility and later to a local hospital.
incidents.quote: Not getting better, he was referred to a hospital in Phoenix where the Firefighter was diagnosed with Valley Fever. The Firefighter was admitted and treated inpatient for 7 days.

incidents.name: Mulch Fire Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A mulch pile caught fire in mid-July at a local transfer station, ultimately coined the “Mulch Fire.” Every engine in the local zone and several pieces of heavy equipment took turns rotating assignments on the incident in some of the toughest environmental conditions imaginable. On the 11th day of the fire, the Incident Commander (IC) sunk into an ash pit on the Mulch Fire. A second crew member stepped into part of the hole while attempting to rescue the injured firefighter. The crewmember suffered 2nd degree burns while assisting with the rescue of the IC, who suffered 3rd degree burns across most of his legs.
incidents.quote: A Forest Service firefighter fell into a 3-foot deep ash pit during mop-up operations on the Mulch Fire on the Coconino National Forest.

incidents.name: Cellar Fire Prescott NF Valley Fever
incidents.summary: An engine crew member from the Black Hills National Forest assigned to the Cellar Fire on the Prescott National Forest was feeling ill. The incident medical personnel chose to fly her back to her home.
incidents.quote: Later that day or evening she went to the hospital and was admitted with a diagnosis of Valley Fever which is endemic to the American Southwest.

incidents.name: Limb Strike Injury
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, June 5, 2019, at 12:15 PM, a CAL FIRE employee was injured during tree limbing and removal operations east of Fort Bragg in Mendocino County, California. While tending a lowering system, the branch used for rigging failed unexpectedly and broke away from the tree, falling a distance of approximately 80’ onto the employee. The employee was transported by air ambulance to a trauma center and is being treated for serious injuries.
incidents.quote: While tending a lowering system, the branch used for rigging failed unexpectedly and broke away from the tree, falling a distance of 74 feet onto the employee.

incidents.name: Sierra IHC Crewmember Rhabdo
incidents.summary: The Captain drove him to a hospital. He was diagnosed with Rhabdo and admitted. He was treated and released that evening to light duty with a request to have a follow-up exam the next week.
incidents.quote: A Sierra IHC Crewmember had been cramping for three days after physical fitness training. EMTs on the crew suggested he might have Rhabdo.

incidents.name: Chandalar River Fire #349 Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: On July 28 and July 29, two fire fighters were hit by fire weakned trees not currently being felled on the Chandalar River Fire.
incidents.quote: He had been focused on the bigger trees out of habit. All sizes of trees are potential hazards.

incidents.name: Huron Manistee NF Dozer Operator Injury
incidents.summary: The patient was treated on scene by a U.S. Forest Service EMT and transported to a hospital via ground ambulance. The patient underwent surgery during which the thumb was reattached/repaired.
incidents.quote: While engaged in fuels reduction work, a Dozer Operator/Swamper swapping attachments nearly severed a thumb when it was pinched between the dozer and an attachment.

incidents.name: CAL FIRE Training Hike Fatality De Luz Incident
incidents.summary: On Sunday, July 28, 2019, Firefighter Katkov was on a training hike with his crew in San Diego County. During the hike, he suffered a medical emergency and was immediately flown to Temecula Valley Hospital in Riverside County where he passed away on Monday, July29,2019.
incidents.quote: CAL FIRE Training Hike Fatality

incidents.name: Milepost 97 Fire Object Strikes Crewmember
incidents.summary: Shortly after midnight on July 29th, the IHC was facilitating a burnout operation on the west side of Interstate 5. The IHC made their way down a steep slope (35-40 degrees) by mid-sloping, using a cross slope grid. As the IHC was making their way down slope, an object that was neither identified nor heard – began rolling. The object ultimately struck one of the crew members in the head, behind the left ear and below the hard hat. This impact resulted in a fall and loss of consciousness. The injured crewmember was then loaded onto a stokes litter and extracted down the steep slope by method of ‘human conveyor belt,’ both 30 feet down and upto the awaiting ambulance.
incidents.quote: Photo taken as rescuers make their way both down and up slope 30 feet to the patients location. The fire in the foreground had been previously ignited by the hand crew during burnout operations.

incidents.name: Beeskov Fire Chainsaw Cut and Medevac
incidents.summary: As the Sawyer finished his cut on a four inch Douglas fir log, it happened. The saw came off the cut and into the left outside of the Sawyer’s saw chaps. The spinning chain rolled the chaps up and then quickly sliced into his left leg above the calf before it finally stopped.
incidents.quote: It had been a long day of cutting so far and the Sawyer noted his saw wasn’t cutting all that well.

incidents.name: Angeles Engine Public Assist Medical Response Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: An Angeles National Forest engine captain and an EMT attempting to rescue an injured hiker are struck by a tree dislodged by medevac helicopter rotor wash. The two remaining uninjured firefighters on the scene provide patient care and coordinate additional rescue assistance.
incidents.quote: He hears a “WHOOOSH”, then sees a 10” diameter tree coming from the rocks above striking the EMT and CAPT on the head. The two fall back-wards face-down into the water.

incidents.name: Engine Incident Within an Incident
incidents.summary: At 10:12, the CAPT is the first to the patient. Following shortly behind is the EMT. Shortly after, the crew hears the loud pulsing sound associated with the rotors of an approaching helicopter. Expecting the helicopter to pass over, the CAPT leans over the patient in an attempt to shield her from the pending rotor wash. He remarks, to the patient “this will pass shortly.” Just as he finishes his statement, a wave of rotor wash and debris begins whirling around the canyon bottom. The EMT mirrors the CAPT body position and shields the patient from the rotor wash. FFT-2 arrives just outside of where the CAPT and EMT are conducting patient care. He turns around to set the medical bag down. As he turns back around toward the patient, he sees events unfold as though they are moving in slow-motion. He hears a “WHOOOSH”, then sees a 10” diameter tree coming from the rocks above striking the EMT and CAPT on the head.
incidents.quote: “There is no other way for Forest visitors to get help.”

incidents.name: Beeskov Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: As the mirror brushed through the alder the tip of the log slid perfectly between the side view mirror’s bracket. It was directed/pulled right into the cab as the truck moved down the road.
incidents.quote: "Before we knew it the window is exploding!”

incidents.name: Hart Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: The firefighter was approximately 25 feet from the snag as it fell. Striking him on the right side of his hardhat, the snag broke at the point of contact, with the top portion falling down the hill, the rest of the tree landing on his legs / ankles. He was knocked unconscious for nearly a minute.
incidents.quote: “THE TREE DIDN’T MAKE A SOUND, UNTIL IT HIT HIM.” -INCIDENT COMMANDER

incidents.name: Valley Fever RLS
incidents.summary: Any person who inhales the spores is at risk of infection. People who have jobs that expose them to dust are most at risk. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: “People can get Valley Fever by breathing in the microscopic fungal spores from the air, although most people who breathe in the spores don’t get sick. Usually, people who get sick with Valley Fever will get better on their own within weeks to months, but some people will need antifungal medication.”
incidents.quote: What is Valley Fever? Valley fever is a fungal infection caused by Coccidioides

incidents.name: Montana Engine Backing Incident
incidents.summary: The crew decided to back up ~50 feet to flag the intersection in case additional resources were needed. The engine crew relied on mirrors and a backup camera and did not to use a spotter for the maneuver.
incidents.quote: While backing up the driver was following the contour of road using his passenger side mirror, unaware of the sharp turn and steep slope of the road on the passenger side of the engine. This resulted with the engine backing off the road near the intersection.

incidents.name: Swan Lake Fire Bee Sting
incidents.summary: Two types of yellow jackets, aerial yellow jackets and Alaska yellow jackets—both insects in the wasp family—are more abundant than usual this year in Alaska. Alaska yellow jackets commonly build nests in the ground and tend to be more territorially aggressive than aerial yellow jackets, which usually build nests in trees and on structures.Ground nests are generally more of a threat to people because there is a higher likelihood for people to disturb them.
incidents.quote: Several yellow jacket sting incidents were reported on the Swan Lake Fire.

incidents.name: Ikes Fire Grand Canyon National Park Heat-Related Injury
incidents.summary: On the Ikes Fire in Grand Canyon National Park, a crewmember was showing signs of a heat-related injury and then deteriorated to the point of losing consciousness for a period. The firefighter was flown to the South Rim Helibase then taken by ground ambulance to a hospital in Flagstaff, Ariz. for further evaluation. The firefighter was treated for severe dehydration and released to light duty the following evening.

incidents.name: Ranch 2 Fire Second Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: An IHC Firefighter suffered a heat-related injury while working on the Ranch 2 Fire on the Angeles National Forest. The patient was assessed and treated by a U.S. Forest Service EMT and Line Medic, then transported to a hospital via a Los Angeles County Helicopter and ground ambulance. The patient was treated, transported home to recover, and assigned “light duty” for the next two days.
incidents.quote: Ranch 2 Fire Second IHC Heat-Related Injury

incidents.name: East Evans Creek Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On August 3, 2019, at approximately 0230 (PST), a snag fell and hit a member of a 20 person hand crew that was building direct handline on the East Evans Creek Fire during initial attack. The firefighter struck by the snag sustained serious injuries to the head and facial regions.
incidents.quote: “We acknowledge the possibility of getting hit by a snag, but are we acknowledging the probability of it?” LLR Team Member

incidents.name: Missoula Smokejumper Injury
incidents.summary: U.S. Forest Service EMTs evaluated and transported the patient to a hospital in a Government vehicle. The full extent of injury is still unknown due to OWCP delays in approval to see a neurologist.
incidents.quote: A Missoula Smokejumper sustained a back injury due to a hard landing on a proficiency jump near the Missoula Smokejumper Base.

incidents.name: Dollar Ridge Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: Assessed by FS EMTs, stabilized and flown by air ambulance to a local hospital. Firefighter was diagnosed with a dislocated hip and acetabular fracture. Surgery was successful and the firefighter was released on 8/7/18.
incidents.quote: Ashley NF. A Wildland Fire Module crewperson working on this fire fell while climbing a fence and complained of significant pain.

incidents.name: Pothole Fire Dozer Burnover
incidents.summary: The fire intensity, heat, and flame length increased quickly and dramatically. Without sufficient power (in limp mode), the dozer was unable to move quickly enough to escape the approaching fire, and the operator jumped out and retreated to the burned (black) safety zone.
incidents.quote: The operator escaped with only singed hair on his hands and head.

incidents.name: Williams Flat Fire Vehicle Accident Silver Creek Accident
incidents.summary: Upon completing workday on Division “I” all assigned resources drove a well maintained dirt road to the Williams Flats Incident Command Post (ICP) for the evening. This impact injured all four firefighters onboard. Three of the four occupants were wearing seatbelts.
incidents.quote: While towing a trailer loaded with a UTV, a light (4x4) truck left the roadway and traveled approximately 125 feet down a steep embankment impacting a large tree.

incidents.name: Trinity Fire Contract Firefighter Dehydration
incidents.summary: A Forest Service contracted Firefighter (GFP-contract) became dehydrated on the Trinity Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The Firefighter was assisted by EMTs from the Smokey Bear Hotshot Crew and then taken by ALS ambulance to a local hospital where the patient was treated and released.

incidents.name: Bayliss Incident Helicopter Wire Strike
incidents.summary: While performing water drops on the western portion of the fire, the helicopter contacted a fiber optic line. The pilot maintained control of the helicopter and safely landed nearby. The Forestry Fire Pilot and Fire Captain were not injured and were the only personnel aboard. The helicopter sustained no damage.
incidents.quote: As H-1 completed the water drop, the pilot banked right, resulting in the main rotor contacting and severing a ½ inch fiber optic line on the left side of aircraft.

incidents.name: Shasta Trinity NF Firefighter Ankle Break
