The patient was treated and released with a full recovery expected.
incidents.quote: A helitack crewmember accidently swallowed a large insect which became lodged in throat

incidents.name: August Complex Firefighter Fall Breaks Clavicle
incidents.summary: Assessed on scene by a U.S. Forest Service EMT, the patient was transported by an agency-owned vehicle to the hospital.The firefighter was treated and released to light duty, but will likely require surgery. A full recovery is expected.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on the August Complex on the Mendocino National Forest, fell while moving a log, landing on the shoulder, breaking the clavicle.

incidents.name: Lofer Fire Base Camp Manager Medical Incident
incidents.summary: A U.S. Forest Service AD working in ICP as Base Camp Manager on the Lofer Fire on Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Fort Apache Agency lands awoke with abdominal pain. The patient was assessed by Forest Service EMTs and was initially diagnosed with a hernia. The patient was transported via ground ambulance to a hospital where abdominal swelling (but no hernia) was diagnosed by the physician. The patient was assigned to two days of light duty.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service AD working in ICP as Base Camp Manager on the Lofer Fire on Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Fort Apache Agency lands awoke with abdominal pain.

incidents.name: August Complex Tatham Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: On August 31, 2020, a Task Force of Type 6 engines was assigned to the Tatham Fire located within the August Complex, on the Mendocino National Forest (MNF), in Tehama County, CA. During firefighting operations, one of the engines assigned to the Task Force backed up and off the road. The engine then burned over. The series of events resulted in the death of firefighter Diane Jones, while another firefighter suffered burn injuries. The firefighter that suffered burn injuries was transported by air to a burn center for treatment.
incidents.quote: When TFL1 saw E1 backing towards the road’s edge, yelled over the radio: “E1, “Stop, Stop, Stop, Stop…Stop”.

incidents.name: Colorado COVID 19 Lessons and Mitigations
incidents.fire: Williams Fork and Cameron Peak Fires
incidents.summary: The content of this Rapid Lesson Sharing (RLS) report is derived from both the Williams Fork and Cameron Peak fires. There were several COVID-19 related incidents on these two fires, which provided an opportunity to learn valuable insights. The lessons shared in this RLS were provided by members of these fire’s Incident Management Teams (IMT).
incidents.quote: COVID-19 Lessons from the Williams Fork and Cameron Peak Fires

incidents.name: Cameron Peak Fire COVID 19 Positive Incident
incidents.summary: Though this storyline ends here fire's first 21 positive COVID-19 cases, the Cameron Peak fire continued to post some impressive statistics until winter weather finally wrapped things up in December of 2020. Not only did this fire become Colorado's largest wildfire at 208,913 acres, the number of new COVID-19 positive cases continued to rise over the next three months. The final count reached 76 confirmed positive cases and 273 officially quarantined cases. Though the fire saw eight incident management team transitions, the COVID IWI provided continuity across them all.
incidents.quote: Cameron Peak Fire COVID 19 Positive Incidents

incidents.name: August Complex Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via air ambulance (level “Red”) with suspected spinal and internal injuries. This patient’s current status is unknown. Two other firefighters on the engine sustained minor injuries and planned to seek follow-up treatment on their own.
incidents.quote: On the August Complex on the Mendocino National Forest, a contract engine rolled over, injuring the driver.

incidents.name: Inchelium Complex Vehicle Burn
incidents.summary: On September 07, 2020 at approximately 1:30 p.m., during initial attack on the Inchelium Highway Fire in Inchelium, Washington, resources drove into a residential subdivision to perform structure assessment. The GSA vehicle they were driving, a 2016 Chevrolet Colorado, caught fire and was a complete loss. No injuries were reported.
incidents.quote: The GSA vehicle they were driving, a 2016 Chevrolet Colorado, caught fire and was a complete loss.

incidents.name: Dolan Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: The Dolan Fire was reported on August 18, 2020 ten miles south of Big Sur, California on the Los Padres National Forest. Beginning the evening of September 7, fire growth significantly outpaced what firefighters had experienced on this fire, with runs of over 37,000 and 34,000 acres in the days around this incident. The team had anticipated and planned for large fire growth on the night of September 7, and indeed the fire grew over 30,000 acres that night, prompting an emergency relocation of ICP. Meanwhile, the fire was moving updrainage toward the Nacimiento guard station. On the morning of September 8, fire impacted the Nacimiento guard station, where two engine crews, a dozer, and division supervisor were located. In the entrapment and fire shelter deployment, the station was destroyed along with numerous fire and personal vehicles. Three firefighters suffered burn injuries that required hospitalization.
incidents.quote: Smoke is billowing out of the barracks and hot embers are raining down all around. Engine 16 is on fire. The engine bay is on fire. Marty can’t get his pack out of the burning engine, which means he can’t get to his fire shelter. He’s just standing there, and Rene can’t get his attention. She has her shelter out, ready to go. She hits him, but he just stands there. She hits him again, but he still just stands there. Marty is not ready to commit to the shelter; he’s thinking about potential dangers from the propane tanks around them, and that more needs to or could be done. Rene hits him again and pulls down on his shirt to get him down to the ground and into the fire shelter. She takes a quick look around and then climbs in under the shelter with him. Eleven other firefighters are deployed around them in the parking lot of the Nacimiento guard station. Everyone is asking the same question: “How did we get here?”

incidents.name: North Complex West Zone Shelter Deployment
incidents.summary: A CAL FIRE Handcrew engaged in structure defense operations had their escape route cut off due to a fast-moving wildland fire. The handcrew sought refuge in an Emergency Crew Transport vehicle and then moved into a residential structure before being forced back outside to deploy their fire shelters. The deployment occurred on the North Complex West Zone Incident near Oroville, California in the CAL FIRE Butte Unit which burned over 200,000 acres in a two day period.
incidents.quote: Conditions in the vehicle were no longer tenable. Then, conditions in the house declined to the point of becoming unsurvivable as the interior became charged with smoke

incidents.name: North Complex Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The patient was attended to by Line Medics, then transported via ambulance to a hospital.
incidents.quote: While directing helicopter operations on a hot section of the North Complex Fire on the Plumas National Forest, an Interagency Hotshot Crew firefighter sustained burns to the soles of both feet.

incidents.name: Little Flats Tractor Fire
incidents.summary: At the time of the incident a small grass fire had ignited in the area. At this time, it has not yet been determined whether the equipment sustained damage as a result of the wildfire or if this is a separate incident. The tractor sustained fire damage rendering it inoperable. Other equipment was working in the area at the time of the wildfire.
incidents.quote: On September 10, 2020 at approximately 1000 hours, a tractor, pulling a mower unit caught fire and sustained damage.

incidents.name: August Complex Bee Stings Incident
incidents.summary: On the August Complex on the Mendocino National Forest, a firefighter from a U.S. Forest Service engine sustained multiple bee stings to the neck and back. The patient was transported via ambulance and agency helicopter to a hospital with suspected anaphylactic shock. Initial care was provided by a Paramedic.
incidents.quote: Firefighter sustained multiple bee stings to the neck and back

incidents.name: Grouse Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: This burn injury was located between the top of the boot and the knee. The patient was attended to on scene by a U.S. Forest Service EMT, then transported via an agency owned vehicle (AOV) to a hospital. The patient was transferred to the Boise Burn Center, then treated and released on the same night. A full recovery is expected.
incidents.quote: On the Grouse Fire on the Boise National Forest, a hand crew firefighter stepped into a hot stump hole and sustained a “fist-sized” burn to the back of one leg.

incidents.name: Beachie Creek Fire Allergic Food Reaction
incidents.summary: The patient was initially treated by a U.S. Forest Service EMT, then transported via ambulance to a hospital. The patient was treated and released back to the incident on the same day.
incidents.quote: An Engine Crew firefighter on the Beachie Creek Fire on the Willamette National Forest experienced an allergic food reaction and was administered two EpiPen injections.

incidents.name: North Complex Dislocated Kneecap
incidents.summary: The patient was stabilized by a U.S. Forest Service EMT and Line Medics, then transported via the Line Safety Officer’svehicle to a hospital.
incidents.quote: On the North Complex on the Plumas National Forest, an Interagency Hotshot Crew Firefighter sustained a dislocated kneecap after stepping into a pile of branches while hiking.

incidents.name: El Dorado Fire Fatality
incidents.summary: On Thursday, September 17, 2020, Charles ‘Charlie’ Morton was fatally burned while conducting fire suppression actions on the El Dorado Fire on the San Bernardino National Forest. We continue to ask our wildland fire responders to save communities that are becoming increasingly unsavable. At what point do we declare communities without any semblance of defensible space not worth the risk of trying to save under extreme fire behavior conditions?
incidents.quote: “It was good until it wasn’t.” “Wind shift, wind shift, wind shift. Everyone starts looking for spots, we’re gonna get spots!” “We’ve got ember wash on the corner!” -Division O Holding Resources

incidents.name: Inchelium Complex Herniated Disc
incidents.summary: The patient was administered a shot of Toradol (a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug) by the Medical Unit. The crew demobed the following day and brought the patient to a hospital where a herniated disc was diagnosed. Light duty for the next eight days was prescribed. A full recovery is expected.
incidents.quote: On the Inchelium Complex on the Colville Reservation, a U.S. Forest Service Firefighter from a Type 2 Initial Attack Crew experienced back pain while brushing fireline.

incidents.name: Archie Creek Firefighter Death
incidents.summary: The Southern Area Red Team, who has been managing the Archie Creek Fire on behalf of the Bureau of Land Management, Douglas Forest Protective Association and Umpqua National Forest, regrets to report the death of Walter (Wally) Samuel Elsbury, Jr., a firefighter assigned to the Archie Creek Fire. Fire personnel found Mr. Elsbury unresponsive in his vehicle at a fire staging area Friday morning, September 18, 2020, before he began his shift as a heavy equipment operator. The Douglas County Sheriff’s Office responded and notified Mr. Elsbury’s family. No foul play is suspected. Mr. Elsbury, of Elsbury Logging Company in Burns/Hines, Oregon, had been working on the Archie Creek Fire for about a week as skidgeon operator. He was helping to protect structures along Little River Road south of Glide on the west flank of the fire.
incidents.quote: Fire personnel found Mr. Elsbury unresponsive in his vehicle at a fire staging area Friday morning.

incidents.name: Riverside Fire Rhabdo
incidents.summary: The patient was transported to a medical center via incident ambulance and was tested for COVID-19 and Rhabdomyolysis. The patient’s test results were negative for COVID-19 and positive for Rhabdo. The patient’s current status unknown
incidents.quote: On the Riverside Fire on the Mount Hood National Forest, a contract firefighter experienced nausea, diarrhea, vomiting and dehydration.

incidents.name: Schill Fire SEAT Fatality
incidents.summary: The airplane descend over an intermediate ridgeline and into a valley. About 3 seconds later, the airplane momentarily returned to level flight before it pitched to a nose-high attitude. The airplane subsequently impacted rising terrain approximately 80 feet below the ridgeline.
incidents.quote: On September 22, 2020, Firefighter/Pilot Ricky Fulton died after his single-engine air tanker crashed while he was fighting the Schill Fire near Emmett, Idaho.

incidents.name: North Complex Burn Injury 9/23
incidents.summary: Medevac, Medical Emergency, Fall, Burn Injury
incidents.quote: North Complex Burn Injury

incidents.name: Mendocino Complex Tree Felling Incident
incidents.summary: U.S. Forest Service EMTs provided initial care. The patient was transported via air ambulance to the hospital. The patient was casted and released with follow-up consultation and potential surgery being required.
incidents.quote: On the Mendocino Complex on the Mendocino National Forest, a contract faller was injured while felling a tree, sustaining multiple fractures to the lower leg and foot.

incidents.name: August Complex Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: A U.S. Forest Service contract Water Tender driver was involved in a vehicle accident on the August Complex (South) on the Mendocino National Forest. The patient was treated on scene by Forest Service EMTs and transported via Agency helicopter to a hospital. The extent of injuries are unknown. The patient was released from the hospital two days after being admitted.
incidents.quote: “He was crawling out from under the front of the truck when I pulled up.”

incidents.name: August Complex South Broken Ankle
incidents.summary: A contract hand crew member was injured with a broken ankle on the August Complex (South) on the Mendocino National Forest. The patient was assessed and transported via a Rapid Extraction Module Support (REMS) Team and handed-off to an ambulance which transported the patient to a hospital.
incidents.quote: A contract hand crew member was injured with a broken ankle

incidents.name: Dolan Fire Dislocated Shoulder
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via ground ambulance to a hospital for treatment. The patient’s current status is unknown.
incidents.quote: A firefighter sustained a dislocated right shoulder on the Dolan Fire on the Los Padres National Forest.

incidents.name: August Complex Hit By Tree Medevac
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the August Complex (Northeast Zone) on the Mendocino National Forest. The patient was initially unresponsive and was treated on scene by a Rapid Extraction Module Support (REMS) Team. The patient, transferred via ground and air ambulances to a trauma center, was assessed to have multiple compressed cervical vertebrae and multiple crushed thoracic vertebrae.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service Strike Team Leader was in a truck when a tree fell on the truck, injuring the firefighter.

incidents.name: Creek Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the Creek Fire on the Sierra National Forest. The patient, who was ambulatory and able to walk off the fireline, was transported to the Incident Command Post. The patient was then transported via ground ambulance to a hospital and was subsequently treated and released to full duty.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service firefighter was operating a chainsaw when they were struck on the head and shoulder by an adjacent snag that was 20-feet-tall and from 6 to 8-inches in diameter.

incidents.name: Creek Fire South Zone Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The patient was initially treated by a Line Medic, then transported via horseback and helicopter to a hospital. The patient’s current status has not been provided.
incidents.quote: While working in an ash pit on the Creek Fire’s South Zone on the Sierra National Forest, an Interagency Hotshot Crew member experienced partial thickness burns to both feet.

incidents.name: Creek Fire South Zone Bee Sting
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the Creek Fire’s South Zone on the Sierra National Forest. On that day, the patient was initially treated by a Line Medic and transported via helicopter to a regional medical center. The patient’s current status has not been provided.
incidents.quote: A firefighter, stung by a bee October 13, started experiencing an allergic reaction—swelling to the face—the following day.

incidents.name: Area Command COVID 19 FLA
incidents.summary: This FLA examines the unintended outcomes associated with Area Command Team members contracting COVID-19 during an assignment. The ability to safely perform wildland fire responsibilities during a pandemic is critically important and must be continuously evaluated and enhanced as the best available information continues to improve. Monitoring activities and identifying limitations in practices to offer a foundation to build ways to sustain safety and success in operations is the focus of this report.
incidents.quote: “We had a COVID plan at work but what happened off time was unknown and not standardized”.

incidents.name: East Troublesome Creek Fire Fractured Femur
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the East Troublesome Creek Fire on the Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forests. The patient was treated on scene by a Forest Service EMT and diagnosed with a fractured femur with no vascular compromise. The patient was transported via ground ambulance to a hospital, underwent surgery the next day, and is currently recovering. The surgeon reported the fracture as critical because it extended to the knee joint and included a broken patella. The surgery was successful. A full recovery is expected after rehabilitation.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service crewmember working a spot fire lost footing while moving downhill and fell onto a large rock.

incidents.name: Cell Phone Boost Lesson
incidents.summary: A lesson about getting phone calls and texts out when you’re in an area of poor service. In a location where you have one bar but cannot get a call out or a text. Almost without fail, if you put your phone on speaker and place it on the dash with it leaning against the windshield you will be able to get a call or at least a text out.
incidents.quote: Poor Cell Service? Try This Method for Getting a Call or Text Out

incidents.name: Silverado Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Fire suppression resources (Local, State, and Federal) were assigned to a vegetation fire in the area of Santiago Canyon Road west of Silverado Canyon Road, near the community of Silverado, CA. At approximately 12:00 PM, during suppression activities, two Hand Crew Firefighters were overrun by fire and subsequently transported to the hospital with critical injuries. Two other Firefighters also suffered heat injuries.
incidents.quote: Crew members attempted to initiate the firing operation with drip torches; however, the wind was too strong and the drip torches would not stay lit.

incidents.name: August Complex Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: The patient self-extracted and was transported via ground ambulance to a local hospital, remaining there overnight for observation. A full recovery is expected.
incidents.quote: On the August Complex on the Mendocino National Forest, a U.S. Forest Service Felling Boss involved in a single-vehicle rollover (single occupant) sustained bruises, abrasions, and a possible concussion.

incidents.name: Creek Fire Hit By Log
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via ground ambulance to a local hospital and was subsequently treated and released to light duty.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service contract firefighter rehabbing dozer line on the Creek Fire on the Sierra National Forest sustained a crush injury to a finger when a log was inadvertently tossed onto the victim’s hand.

incidents.name: Unit 217 Prescribed Fire UTV Fire
incidents.summary: While operating a 2018 Polaris 900 UTV on the Unit 217 prescribed fire, Apalachicola National Forest, Florida, the operator noticed the brakes were not working. After a second attempt of mashing the pedal to the floor, the operator looked down—and realized that the floorboard under his feet was on fire.
incidents.quote: “I looked downand the floorboard was on fire. We bailed!” UTV Operator

incidents.name: August Complex North Zone Dislocated Shoulder
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via ground ambulance to a local hospital, then subsequently treated and released.
incidents.quote: On the August Complex North Zone on the Mendocino National Forest, a firefighter experienced a fall ile ascending a hill carrying a line pack and saw, sustaining a dislocated shoulder.

incidents.name: Cranston Piles Escaped Prescribed Burn
incidents.summary: Beginning in January 2021, San Bernardino National Forest (California) firefighters began burning piles of cut and stacked fuels in the Cranston Fire scar. The total acreage of all pile burn units within this project is 110 acres. Over three days of ignitions (January 6th, 7th, and 12th), fire personnel successfully burned 49 acres of this 110. In the very early morning of January 15th, a fire was reported adjacent to the burn unit from January 12.
incidents.quote: Total burned area from the wildfire was 715 acres. Ultimately the the fire was determined to be a prescribed fire escape.

incidents.name: Tractor Fire Heavy Equipment Swamper Injury
incidents.summary: On Sunday, January 17, 2021, Texas A&M Forest Service (TFS) resources responded to the Tractor Fire in Burnet County, Texas. During initial attack operations, a dozer swamper (ground man) suffered a broken leg after being entangled in brush being pushed by the dozer. The patient was extricated from the tree in which he was entangled and immediately transported to the hospital.
incidents.quote: “I just killed somebody. I killed my ground man.”

incidents.name: Punkin Fire Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The firefighter was transported to the hospital by an agency vehicle, was treated and released back to full duty.
incidents.quote: During mop-up operations on the Punkin Fire on Arizona State Division of Forestry lands, a U.S. Forest Service Firefighter stepped into hot ash, resulting in a 2-inch by 2-inch burn to the lower leg.

incidents.name: Shooting Range Prescribed Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: The dozer operator, operating a 2016 John Deere 550K XL Dozer, was asked to assist with snag removal on a dozer line across three steep drainages on the Shooting Range Prescribed Fire. The burn unit is located on the Talladega Ranger District, National Forests in Alabama. The plan was to walk the dozer down an existing dozer line on a ridge to where the snags were located. The operator was unharmed and the machine was undamaged.
incidents.quote: While traversing the unit, a large branch supporting the dozer broke, causing the machine to roll onto its side.

incidents.name: Hoosier NF Rx Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: An Rx Module was prepping the 147-acre Harding Flats Prescribed Fire unit, Hoosier National Forest, Indiana. At approximately 1330 hours, one of the FAL2 qualified personnel was attempting to fall a hung up, split-top ash snag within falling distance of the holding line. The sawyer sustained a leg fracture.
incidents.quote: During felling operations, the split-top broke and fell toward the sawyer, hitting them while they attempted escape.

incidents.name: Schroeder Fire Smoke Exposure
incidents.summary: The firefighter lost consciousness. Once revived, the individual had difficulty breathing. The firefighter was transported via Rapid City Ambulance to a medical facility. The individual was treated and released the same day. X-rays were taken and indicated that the lungs were clear and functioning well.
incidents.quote: A wildland firefighter engaged in fire suppression actions on the Schroeder Fire, located near Rapid City, South Dakota, was overcome with smoke inhalation and had an asthma attack.

incidents.name: Gross Dam Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On April 1, 2021 the Arapaho Roosevelt NFs and Pawnee National Grassland in Colorado responded to a smoke report with cooperators near Gross Reservoir Dam. The District had initiated a 79-acre pile burn project in the same area on March 21. When personnel arrived, the fire was spreading to the northeast, fanned by breezy and dry conditions. Fire managers recognized at that point that the fire had originated from a pile that had been ignited 11 days earlier. The Fire was contained at 2000hrs at 8.65 acres of non-Forest Service land. No improvements were damaged or threatened.
incidents.quote: The Forsythe II Unit 51 pile project was declared the Gross Dam Wildfire.

incidents.name: Lennox Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: Lennox RX is a large (6,566 acres) unit of mixed pine/hardwood forest over rocky mountainous ridges in the Ouachita National Forest in Eastern Oklahoma. Most of the day, the holding groups reported spots but could be handled by resources on scene but inevitably stretched resources thin. One of the spots was below a resident and wasn’t realized until it was well established. Resources responded and extinguished the spot at 8 acres. There was minimal timber damage to the private property but a small utility trailer was damaged. Two engines responded and were able to extinguish the spot before it reached the home.
incidents.quote: One of the spots was below a resident and wasn’t realized until it was well established.

incidents.name: Mark Twain NF Rx Public Incursion
incidents.fire: Mark Twain NF Rx Public Incursion
incidents.summary: The Council Bluff Telleck Branch Prescribed Fire unit consisted of a 2,907-acre block located inside the Council Bluff Recreation Area, Mark Twain National Forest, Missouri.
incidents.quote: During ignitions, two incursions by recreationists occurred into the prescribed fire unit. There were no injuries.

incidents.name: Albright Volunteer Fire Department Vehicle Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On Sunday, April 4, 2021, Captain Charles Wesley “Chuck” Miller, Jr. was responding to a brush fire in his personal automobile. He was killed when his vehicle went off the road and into a ditch on North Preston Highway, West Virginia. The investigation into the incident is ongoing.

incidents.name: Weber E Escaped Prescribed Fire Review
incidents.summary: Litchfield Wetland Management District implemented a prescribed fire on the east unit of the Weber Waterfowl Production Area (Minnesota) on April 5th at 1230. The wildfire burned 96 acres, 38 acres of private and 58 acres of US Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) lands.
incidents.quote: Around 1545 the fire spotted outside the planned perimeter and was declared a wildfire at 1555 hours.

incidents.name: Laurel Creek Rx Drip Torch Leg Burn
incidents.summary: During ignition operations on the Laurel Creek Prescribed Fire, Daniel Boone National Forest, Kentucky, a firefighter was carrying a drip torch during lighting and spilled drip torch fuel on the left leg (back of calf area) which resulted in burning the employee. The employee walked out under their own power and was transported to and received initial treatment at the hospital in Somerset, Kentucky. The employee was then referred to the Burn Center at the University of Louisville Hospital, where they underwent successful skin graft surgery on their calf. The employee is recovering and doing well.
incidents.quote: “In my mind, it was happening quickly and slowly—at the same time.” Lighter, after realizing she couldn’t pat out the flames.

incidents.name: Clear Creek Rx Drip Torch Leg Burn
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest on the Madison Ranger District in Montana. The resulting fire involved potential 2nd and 3rd degree burns to the employee’s lower legs. Prompt action by surrounding individuals, including pouring water on and smothering the flames, suppressed the fire. The employee was treated on-scene by a qualified EMT. Both air and ground ambulances were ordered. The employee was transported via air ambulance to a burn center.
incidents.quote: During ignition operations on the Clear Creek Rx, a drip torch collar “popped” off after pressurization, spilling drip torch fuel down an employee’s lower legs as the individual was crossing over a small 3-inch line of active fire—which caused the fuel to ignite.

incidents.name: St Joe Divide Rx Helitorch Gel Burn Injury
incidents.summary: During suppression actions to extinguish the burning gel, a wildland firefighter received minor 2nd degree burns to the hand. The individual, treated by county medical personnel and a U.S. Forest Service EMT, remained on scene until operations were complete. The employee was later evaluated and treated at a local hospital then returned to work.
incidents.quote: During helitorch operations on the St. Joe Divide Prescribed Fire on the Idaho Panhandle National Forests, discarded helitorch gel ignited.

incidents.name: Coronado NF Physical Training Incident
incidents.summary: After completing physical training, a wildland firefighter, who is also an EMT, self-assessed rhabdomyolysis symptoms, drove self to hospital after work, was evaluated and released, and placed on light duty for a week.

incidents.name: School House C Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The National Forests in Alabama, Talladega National Forest, Talladega Ranger District conducted the School House C&D prescribed burns 3.5 miles northeast of Hollins, AL on April 19th, 2021. On April 21, 2021 the School House C prescribed burn escaped and was converted to a wildfire by the local unit. The fire was contained at 14 acres on private land and 1 abandoned structure was destroyed. No injuries resulted from the escape.
incidents.quote: There's just a lot of red line on that unit.

incidents.name: Buck/Trout Creek Prescribed Fire UTV Fire
incidents.summary: The Angelina-Sabine National Forest in Texas were conducting the 3300-acre Buck Creek-Trout Creek Prescribed Fire on April 22, 2021. While aerial ignitions were ongoing, a firefighter noticed that a UTV in use was burning underneath. The UTV was offloaded of gear and supplies, but the vehicle itself was destroyed by fire. No one was injured.
incidents.quote: A UTV one the Buck/Trout Creek Prescribed Fire was destroyed by fire.

incidents.name: Brittle Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On April 23, 2021, staff from the East Zone of the Huron-Manistee National Forest in Michigan gathered to conduct the Brittle Prescribed Fire. Spot fires were observed during firing operations. These spots were easy to suppress at first, but more were detected and ignition operations ceased at 1252. Spots continue to grow and at 1424 the Rx is declared a wildfire.
incidents.quote: After blacklining the unit, aerial ignition was conducted by a helicopter with a plastic sphere dispenser.

incidents.name: Switching Transport Trailer Hitches Driving Incident
incidents.summary: The trailer began to fishtail and tip from side to side. Its right front corner dug into the pavement. This caused the safety chain bolt to sheer off, the tie-down straps to break, and the Marsh Master® to roll over onto the highway.
incidents.quote: While hauling a Marsh Master amphibious vehicle from a prescribed fire, the trailer became unhooked and rolled the heavy equipment on the highway. The trailer hitch and trailer ball were different sizes. There were no injuries.

incidents.name: Becker FFR Escaped Prescribed Pile Burn
incidents.fire: Becker FFR Escaped Prescribed Pile Burn
incidents.summary: On April 27, 2021, the Bureau of Land Management’s (BLM) Vale District Fire and Fuels Management Unit (Oregon) conducted a prescribed pile burn on public land in the Malheur Field Office that resulted in an escape, which was subsequently declared a wildfire per direction of the agency administrator and the FMO. The wildfire was contained at 5.75 acres that burned outside of the burn unit onto adjacent private land.
incidents.quote: Resources that were planned to check the prescribed burn discovered the escaped wildfire the morning of April 28, 2021 and the spread had mostly been stopped on its own overnight.

incidents.name: Johnson Gulch Rx Fire Incidents
incidents.summary: On Saturday, May 1, 2021, during implementation of a prescribed burn, it was discovered that ignitions had occurred in an unharvested timber harvest unit, killing a few trees and scorching others. Roughly a week later it was also discovered that a pile burn had crept into another unharvested unit scorching trees identified for harvest under the same timber sale contract.
incidents.quote: “Fuels was really working hard on trust and relationships with the CO. We got some space from the CO. The thing that bothers me the most is that we lost that trust.”

incidents.name: Unit 38 South Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On May 4, 2021 the Great Plains Fire Management Zone conducted a prescribed burn on Unit 38 South at Ft. Niobrara National Wildlife Refuge, Nebraska. Unit 38 South is 337 acres.
incidents.quote: There was a large fire whirl that traveled from the middle of the unit across the Southern holding line, resulting in a 12-acre slopover on private land, causing the prescribed burn to be declared a wildfire.

incidents.name: Natwick Rx Unit Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.fire: Natwick Rx Unit Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On May 5, 2021, J Clark Salyer National Wildlife Refuge (NWR) conducted prescribed fire operations on the Natwick Prescribed Fire Unit. The 310-acre treatment unit is located in the southwest corner of the Refuge in McHenry County, North Dakota. At 1730 strong gusty winds from the North pushed smoke across Natwick Rd. (southern prescribed fire unit boundary). A spot fire ignited on Refuge property south of the prescribed fire unit. Initial attack efforts on the spot fire were unsuccessful. 130 acres of private property and 413 acres of additional refuge land was burned before the prescribed fire crew and contingency resources contained the escape fire later that evening.
incidents.quote: The RXB2 converted the prescribed fire to a declared wildfire at 1800 hours.

incidents.name: Missoula Smokejumper Physical Training Incident
incidents.summary: The individual was assessed by EMTs and transported to the hospital. The individual was reassessed at the hospital, treated, and released to light duty. A follow-up appointment was scheduled.
incidents.quote: On the Lolo National Forest in Montana, a smokejumper experienced difficulty breathing following routine physical training.

incidents.name: North II Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: The Fremont-Winema National Forest, Chiloquin Ranger District, in Klamath County, Oregon planned on burning 3,278 acres in the North II project area over 2 days. On the afternoon of May 4, several spot fires were detected and worked by holding forces. On the morning of May 5, two holding groups were identified, one to work on the large slopover, and another to monitor the blacklining operation from the previous day. By noon it was determined that the objectives of the burn were not being met, and that more resources would be needed to contain the slopover before a predicted frontal passage on the evening of May 6.
incidents.quote: At 1223 the North II Prescribed Burn was declared a wildfire, became the Meadow Fire, and was contained at 832 acres on May 12, with no fire growth mapped after May 5.

incidents.name: Tussock Fire Medical Norovirus Outbreak
incidents.summary: An IWI team was assembled to manage support and follow-up with the ill individuals.
incidents.quote: Over the course of several days in May 2021, 49 individuals on the Tussock Fire in Arizona were diagnosed with norovirus.

incidents.name: Brundage Rx Drip Torch Equipment Issue
incidents.summary: Over the course lighting on the Brundage Rx on the Payette National Forest, Idaho, the collar ring came off the drip torch on two occasions. No injuries were reported. The torch was taken out of the service; it was determined the collar ring and torch body had mismatched threads.
incidents.quote: Brundage Rx Drip Torch Equipment Issue

incidents.name: Four Mile Unit J Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.fire: Four Mile Unit J Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On May 6, 2021, the Krassel Ranger District concluded their spring prescribed burning with a one-day aerial burn in the Four Mile project area. The fuels and fire behavior in Unit J did not react as expected for spring burning conditions. A common tactic to let fire back into a riparian zone on the southern project boundary would be tested. Eleven days later a recon flight confirmed that fire had crept across the southern boundary.
incidents.quote: The early conversations are why everyone is comfortable about what we did and why.

incidents.name: Eicks Fire Smokejumping Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On Monday, May 24, 2021, resources responded to a fire on private land seven miles north of the United States-Mexico border in Hidalgo County, New Mexico. During a late afternoon fire jump, Smokejumper Tim Hart landed on a rocky slope at the base of a ravine. Tim’s injuries were severe, and despite immediate care from emergency medical technicians (EMTs) and a well-coordinated air ambulance response, he passed away on June 2, 2021.
incidents.quote: "In large organizations and amidst bureaucratic complexity, “there can be the institutional deception to believe that risks are being mitigated, when in fact they are just being traded for other types of unseen risks." – Preston Cline Academic Reviewer

incidents.name: Thunderbolt Escaped Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: A forest burned machine slash piles in two timber sales from April 16-22, 2021. On May 20, 2021, after the snow had melted, smoke was reported in the vicinity. Although there had been lightning that week, an investigation determined the source was one of the Thunderbolt piles. As a result, the prescribed fire was declared a wildfire on May 27, 2021.
incidents.quote: When you don’t see smoke for a day or two, everyone goes back to their day jobs; the piles were forgotten.”

incidents.name: Sycan River Fire Firefighter Stroke Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: On the Sycan River Fire on the Fremont-Winema National Forest, a firefighter was injured when they exited a vehicle and felt fuzzy, then passed out and sustained a head injury. The individual was taken via Life Flight to Sky Lakes Medical Center in Klamath Falls, Oregon, where it was determined that the patient had suffered a stroke. Five days later, at the time of this report, the patient remains in the hospital.
incidents.quote: A Sycan River Fire Firefighter suffered a Stroke while exiting a vehicle.

incidents.name: Los Angeles County Fire Department Shooting Fatality
incidents.summary: On Tuesday, June 1, 2021, Firefighter Specialist Tory Carlon was shot and killed and a captain was injured at the Agua Dulce Fire Station, Agua Dulce, California. The assailant, an off duty firefighter also with the Los Angeles County Fire Department, then set fire to his house. He was later found deceased in a small pool outside the home from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The captain was transported to the hospital in critical but stable condition. Investigation into the incident continues.

incidents.name: Gila NF Firefighter Seizure Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: During an AAR on the Reserve Ranger District, Gila National Forest, a firefighter made an unusual noise and then fell to the ground—experiencing a seizure for approximately 45 seconds. Once oxygen was administered, the seizure subsided. The patient was transported to the hospital, treated, and released.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on the Gila NF suffered a seizure

incidents.name: Chugach National Forest ATV Training Accident
incidents.summary: The class was comprised of seven total ATVs, one for each student and one for the instructor. They ascended the trail without issue, turned around at the top and started descending the trail back to the Work Center. Based on this increased pain/tenderness and a pre-existing medical condition, Student 1 and 2 drove to Providence Alaska Medical Center in Anchorage to receive more advanced medical care.
incidents.quote: Student 1 was in the middle of the pack as they approached a right-hand turn into the first switchback and lost control, rolling the ATV to the right—pinning Student 1 underneath.

incidents.name: Pack Creek Fire IA Engine Burn Damage
incidents.summary: On June 9th at 1550 hours, Helitack reports a smoke in the Pack Creek area near a subdivision near Moab, Utah. One helicopter, two BLM engines (Eng1 and Eng2) are immediately dispatched and local VFD resources and a an ICT3 are ordered. During initial attack, spots are detected and fought, and strong winds cause a pulse of heat that leads to the IC withdrawing resources to structure protection. After several hours, Engines 1 and 2 are released. The following day, heat damage is discovered on Eng1.
incidents.quote: "I didn't expect this fire behavior in Pack Creek drainage" - Duty Officer.

incidents.name: Twin Peaks IA Crew Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On June 11, Twin Peaks Initial Attack, a Utah Division of Forestry, Fire and State Lands (FFSL) Type 2 IA crew, had a vehicle that was impacted by a soft shoulder that resulted in the vehicle being pulled from the road grade and rolling over the embankment. No injuries to crewmembers were reported. The vehicle sustained substantial damage and had to be removed and transported via wrecker.
incidents.quote: The vehicle—carrying four crewmembers—rolled twice, landing on its wheels in an upright position.

incidents.name: Deep Creek Fire Helicopter Incident
incidents.summary: While responding to the Deep Creek Fire near Townsend, Montana, a Montana Department of Natural Resources and Conservation (DNRC) helicopter experienced a hard landing that resulted in a fire. As the pilot maneuvered the helicopter to land, it began to descend from 500 feet in a phenomenon known as "settling with power." The pilot committed to landing, and upon touching the round, the helicopter spun and rolled over. The helicopter was destroyed in a post-accident fire. All personnel on board were able to safely exit the aircraft.
incidents.quote: Helicopter destroyed in a post-accident fire.

incidents.name: Pinnacle Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: The individual was ground transported by ambulance to Mt. Graham Regional Medical Center in Safford, AZ. and was diagnosed with heat exhaustion. The individual was treated and released to light-duty.
incidents.quote: An individual working on the Pinnacle Fire on the Coronado National Forest, Arizona, experienced a “Yellow” heat-related injury (HRI).

incidents.name: East Troublesome Fire Excavator Tip Over
incidents.summary: On June 15, a John Deere 160G Excavator tipped over onto its side while navigating a steep section of dozer line on the East Troublesome Fire, Kremmlig Field Office, BLM, Colorado. The operator was unharmed and was able to safely exit the excavator after the tip-over. Damage to the excavator was minor and the equipment was fully operational once recovered from the site.
incidents.quote: “I wish I would have had the time to say: ‘No, don’t go’.”

incidents.name: Soda Bear Rx ATV Rollover
incidents.summary: During prescribed fire operations on the Soda Bear Rx in Oregon, an ATV parked on a slope rolled over when a rock it was parked on shifted. Proper Department of Transportation (DOT) helmet was worn with chinstrap fastened. This significantly reduced injuries to Holder 1.
incidents.quote: The rider was thrown from the ATV and landed 17 feet down slope.

incidents.name: Pinnacle Fire Fall Short Haul Extraction
incidents.summary: In a remote Division on the Pinnacle Fire, Coronado National Forest, Arizona, a crew was tasked with securing the fire’s edge. A saw team was traversing a steep canyon. This began a “Red Medical” at approximately 0900 in remote country on a day with temperatures predicted to reach 112 degrees (the Type 3 helicopter’s temperature limitation). Within one hour and 52 minutes, the sawyer was in an Air Ambulance headed to a Level 1 Trauma Center. By the end of that day, the sawyer was released from the hospital with a hairline fracture to the lower leg and serious bruising. Later, it was discovered that the sawyer’s injuries were more extensive with fractures to the foot and ankle, as well as muscle damage.
incidents.quote: As the sawyer worked around a boulder the size of a small car, he brushed the boulder, setting it loose, and plummeting both the sawyer and the boulder down the canyon toward his swamper. During his fall, the sawyer and boulder collided—smashing the sawyer’s leg.

incidents.name: Bear Fire Initial Attack Burn Injury
incidents.summary: While engaged in initial attack operations on the Bear Fire on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests, Arizona, a crewmember on a 10-person initial-attack hand-crew sustained a small 1st degree burn to the tip of nose. The patient was initially treated by EMTs, then hiked to a remote helispot and was transported by an agency Type 3 helicopter to a hospital in Safford, Arizona. The individual’s burn was treated, airway and lungs checked, and was then released and is in good condition.
incidents.quote: A wind shift had resulted in the flaming front pushing flames, heat, and gas toward this individual and crew.

incidents.name: Deep Creek Canyon Fire Hit by Log
incidents.summary: A short module of four firefighters were spread out along a hillside performing assigned work on the Deep Creek Canyon Fire, Montana. A downed log covered a hot spot. The sawyer’s plan was to make two angled chainsaw cuts to the log and deliberately roll the middle chunk away. Near the end of the first cut, the log snapped free, rolling over the small diameter sapling that was holding it. Not anticipating the log to roll, the firefighter located directly downhill from the log back-peddled to avoid it, but instantly found himself on the ground— with the log rolling over him. The firefighter was able to walk to a vehicle without assistance and was transported to medical care.
incidents.quote: The log jammed his face and head into the ground. He could feel the sides of his helmet squeezing his head.

incidents.name: Backbone Fire Fall Laceration to Hand
incidents.summary: An Interagency Hotshot Crew member on the Backbone Fire on the Coconino National Forest, Arizona, tripped and fell, causing a laceration to the hand by the tool being carried. An ambulance transported the patient to Life Flight. The patient was treated and released back to work.

incidents.name: Backbone Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: While preparing contingency line, an engine crew member on the Backbone Fire on the Coconino National Forest, Arizona, suffered a heat-related illness. The patient was treated with IV fluids by EMS personnel and released back to work.
incidents.quote: Backbone Fire Heat Related Illness

incidents.name: Koffman Road Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The Koffman Road Fire was reported east of Kittitas, Washington on June 27th around 1306 Hrs. At approximately 1330 hours, a Washington Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Type II IA hand crew arrived on scene and the Crew Superintendent (SUP1) and Foreman (FOR1) were scouting Division A of the fire near the south flank looking for a safe location to engage the fire with the crew. At approximately 13:45 hours, SUP1 and FOR1 determined the civilian bulldozer and operator were in a safe location and were planning on burning out fuel between the road and south flank of the fire. During this time a wind shift proceeded to intensify fire behavior and threaten their position. Upon recognition of the injuries, on-scene personnel provided immediate medical care and transport for evaluation and treatment.
incidents.quote: In the process of egressing the area , SUP1 only had time to jump on to the rear of a vehicle, and was exposed to flame and heat while the foreman drove their escape route to the west.

incidents.name: Central Mat-Su Fire Department Medical Emergency Fatality 2021
incidents.summary: Engineer Justin Hansen worked a 24-hour shift, ending the morning of Sunday, June 27, 2021. While on-duty Engineer Hansen responded to both fire and EMS calls. A few hours after returning home, Engineer Hansen was found deceased. The cause of his death was cardiac related.

incidents.name: Muddy Slide Fire Headache/Gastrointestinal Issues
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Muddy Slide Fire on the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests, Colorado, who experienced headache and gastrointestinal issues—and whose status was reported as “Green”—was transported by incident ambulance to a local medical center.

incidents.name: Muddy Slide Fire High Blood Pressure/Heart Rate
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Muddy Slide Fire on the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests, Colorado, who experienced high blood pressure and heart rate—and whose status was reported as “Green”—was transported by incident ambulance to a local medical center.

incidents.name: Juniper Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: The patient, categorized as a “Yellow Medevac,” was stable at the time of transport via air ambulance then by ground ambulance. The patient was treated and released on the same day.
incidents.quote: An engine crewmember suffered a heat-related injury on the Juniper Fire on Modoc National Forest, California.

incidents.name: Hatch Mountain Fire Fuel Geysering
incidents.summary: The Hatch Mountain Fire was reported on July 7 at approximately 1300 hours, located approximately six miles west of Hatch, Utah. The fire was responded to by multiple resources including a Type 6 engine and five-person squad. The team had an Intermediate Faller (FAL2)—using a Stihl 461 that had been in service for approximately one year—with an Advanced Faller (FAL1) providing mentorship. They had been having a difficult time keeping the saw running correctly all day. While troubleshooting the saw, the FAL1 carefully opened the gas fill cap.
incidents.quote: The saw fuel geysered and covered the firefighter's pants and shirt.

incidents.name: Lava Fire Helicopter Accident
incidents.summary: A Bell 212 Helicopter working under contract with the US Forest Service experienced an accident while supporting the Lava Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The pilot was the sole occupant of the aircraft and was utilizing Lake Shastina as a dip site when the event occurred. The pilot was able to secure the aircraft fuel and electrical before exiting the aircraft and then was assisted by another incident helicopter to get to shore. The aircraft tipped on its side and became fully submerged. The pilot was not injured.
incidents.quote: The pilot was descending to the dip when the aircraft experienced an unknown issue that caused it to settle into the Lake.

incidents.name: Happy Gulch Fire Smokejumper Injuries
incidents.summary: On the Happy Gulch Fire on the Kootenai National Forest, a smokejumper suffered a knee injury on landing. Medical size-up indicated a “Green” medical. The patient was successfully packaged and delivered to a ground ambulance for transport to a medical facility. Once assessed at the medical clinic, it was determined that the smokejumper could have a possible skull fracture (due to the MVA) and was transported to Kalispell Regional Medical Center in Kalispell, Montana. where it was determined that the smokejumper had a fractured skull (from the MVA) and a broken patella (from the jump injury)
incidents.quote: During patient transport, the ambulance was involved in a motor vehicle accident (MVA), resulting in additional injuries to the smokejumper.

incidents.name: Pine Fire Broken Ankle
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via agency vehicle to Mammoth Hospital in Mammoth, California.
incidents.quote: A crew member on the Pine Fire on the Inyo National Forest suffered a potential broken ankle.

incidents.name: Mud Lick Fire Burned Gear
incidents.summary: Rappelers were deployed to initial attack the Mud Lick Fire on the Salmon-Challis National Forest in Idaho. Fire behavior increased rapidly necessitating fire crew evacuations. All personnel were able to evacuate but some gear was not able to be backhauled and was destroyed by fire the day after initial attack began.
incidents.quote: "You’re never going to prioritize gear over people.”

incidents.name: Lava Fire Short Haul Incident
incidents.summary: Initial medical size-up categorized the patient as “Yellow” (“Serious Injury or Illness”) on the Medical Incident Report (MIR). Based on the size-up and location, the patient was short hauled to a ground ambulance and transported to the hospital.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on the Lava Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest in California fell and presented with wrist, hip, and rib pain.

incidents.name: Elbow Creek Fire Smokejumping Accident Short Haul
incidents.summary: Smokejumpers were ordered to staff the Elbow Creek Fire on the Custer Gallatin National Forest in Montana. After jumping from the aircraft, turbulent air was felt by the jumpers at approximately 100 feet above ground level. Jumper 1 attempted to “land” in a tree. The tree top broke out, causing Jumper 1 to fall to ground, sustaining significant injuries. A National Park Service helicopter, also dispatched to the fire, arrived shortly after this injury incident and configured for short-haul. The patient was then transferred to an air ambulance helicopter and transported to the hospital in Bozeman, MT, where they were diagnosed with a broken pelvis, fractured tibia, broken heel, and a mild concussion.
incidents.quote: While “treeing-up” is thought to be a safer option for smokejumpers in turbulent wind conditions, the drought conditions and low fuel moistures may now make this a less desirable option.

incidents.name: Cedar Basin Fire Aircraft Accident
incidents.summary: Subsequently, the airplane impacted side of a ridgeline in mountainous desert terrain about 15 miles northeast of Wikieup. The wreckage was consumed by a post-crash fire. Debris was scattered over an area of several acres. The left wing was located about 0.79 miles northeast of the main wreckage and did not sustain thermal damage. No distress call from the airplane was overheard on the radio
incidents.quote: According to a witness, the airplane was observed in a steep dive towards the ground.

incidents.name: Burnt Peak Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: At the time of this report, all were in stable condition. EMTs provided first aid and evaluated the patients. For precautionary reasons due to their mechanism of injury, two patients were transported via ground ambulance to the Cabinet Peaks Medical Center in Libby, MT.
incidents.quote: Five U.S. Forest Service employees were involved in a rollover at a slow rate-of-speed on the Burnt Peak Fire on the Kootenai National Forest in Montana.

incidents.name: Green Ridge Fire Short Haul
incidents.summary: There was no clear mechanism of injury or obvious trauma, but the firefighter had 90 minutes of lost memory. Due to the location and potential mechanism of injury, the patient was transported via short haul helicopter. During this medevac, another firefighter fell and struck their head, doubling the number of injured. Both patients were transported, Hospital Liaisons were utilized, and both patients were released.
incidents.quote: On the Green Ridge Fire on the Umatilla National Forest in Oregon, a firefighter was found on the fireline semiconscious.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Imperiled Crew
incidents.summary: A Forest Service recreation crew on the Payette National Forest in Idaho were working in the backcountry in the general area of the Dixie Fire, which was across the Salmon River from their location. Remote sensing indicated the fire may have spotted onto the same side of the river as the crew, endangering them. The decision was made to have them hike out, though the exact location or existence of the spot fire could not be immediately verified.
incidents.quote: One crew member wondered if he was in for an “early and tragic death."

incidents.name: Glacier Fire Cut Hand
incidents.summary: The wound required stitches. The patient was transported via helicopter to Bishop Helibase and then ground transported to the Northern Inyo Hospital for treatment. The firefighter has returned to their duty station.
incidents.quote: A firefighter cut their hand while hiking into the Glacier Fire on the Inyo National Forest, California.

incidents.name: Log Fire Engine Burn Damage
incidents.summary: While attempting to suppress spot fires on the green side of a road on the Log Fire, Oregon, a BLM engine was impacted by a sudden flareup from the opposite side of the road. Other firefighters working in the green escaped to their engine and were not impacted by the flareup. The BLM engine suffered burn damage during the 60 to 90-second increase in fire behavior. No one was injured.
incidents.quote: The winds changed 180 degrees and 30- to 40-foot flames advanced toward the engine.

incidents.name: Burnt Peak Fire Medevac
incidents.summary: On the Burnt Peak Fire on the Kootenai National Forest in Montana, an employee experienced chest pain, dizziness, and numbness. EMTs provided first aid and evaluated the patient. The patient was transferred to the ambulance and then to Life Flight which flew to the Kootenai Medical Center in Coeur d’ Alene, Idaho.
incidents.quote: This medical incident was categorized as “Red”. Both an ambulance and Life Flight were ordered.

incidents.name: Red Apple Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: On July 13, 2021, a fire of unknown cause was reported in the Monitor area, northwest of Wenatchee, Washington. On July 15, an engine crew is assigned to an active flank of the fire, given a scouting mission to evaluate containment opportunities.
incidents.quote: While scouting, the engine boss stepped out of the black to get fresh air when the fire switched directions quickly overtook his position, resulting in burn injuries.

incidents.name: Active Shooter on a Helibase RLS
incidents.summary: On July 17, 2021, a motorist entered the active helibase area of Shoshone County Airport in Smelterville, Idaho. The man acted erratically, threatening helibase personnel with a firearm, then shot several bullets into the air and ground. No one was injured and the man was apprehended by law enforcement officers.
incidents.quote: "I was Sure Josh was Dead."

incidents.name: Mt Jefferson Public Search and Rescue
incidents.summary: During a wildland firefighting Initial attack pre-position assignment in Sunriver, Oregon, the Siskiyou Rappel Crew responded to a request for search and rescue mutual aid from the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office Search and Rescue (SAR) Team. The subject was a lost and distressed hiker located in the Sisters Ranger District, Deschutes National Forest, in the Mount Jefferson Wilderness outside of Sisters, Oregon. Rappelers were delivered to the hiker's location to begin delivering care. The hiker was successfully hoisted and transported to the hospital by a National Guard helicopter.
incidents.quote: The subject was a lost and distressed hiker located in the Sisters Ranger District, Deschutes National Forest, in the Mount Jefferson Wilderness outside of Sisters, Oregon.

incidents.name: Anderson Hill Fire Medevac
incidents.summary: An employee experienced multiple seizures on the Anderson Hill Fire on Montana Department of Natural Resources and Conservation (DNRC) land. The patient was flown via Life Flight helicopter to a hospital in Missoula, Montana. At the time of this report, the patient had been treated and was stable.
incidents.quote: An employee experienced multiple seizures on the Anderson Hill Fire

incidents.name: Chuweah Creek Fire Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: The patient was transported by ambulance to a local hospital. The patient was diagnosed with mild anemia and angina and released from the hospital. The firefighter returned to work the next day.
incidents.quote: A firefighter was experiencing chest pain on the Chuweah Creek Fire in Washington.

incidents.name: Peak Fire Heat Related Incident
incidents.summary: The patient was transported off the fire via helicopter to an air ambulance that flew the patient to the hospital. The firefighter was treated and released and returned to light duty for a few days.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on the Peak Fire on the Sequoia National Forest, California, exhibited symptoms of Heat-Related Illness (HRI).

incidents.name: Bear Creek Fire Chain Catch Failure
incidents.summary: The saw’s chain catch, designed to help reduce the risk of operator contact by a chain when it breaks or comes off of the bar, failed—resulting in the chain missing the chaps and striking the sawyer’s inner right thigh. The sawyer was treated by an onscene EMT and was able to return to work.
incidents.quote: While clearing a helispot on the Bear Creek Fire, Minnesota, a sawyer was bucking/limbing a spruce tree when they threw the saw’s chain.

incidents.name: Tamarack Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: While preparing to assist with a firing operation on the Tamarack Fire, which had crossed from California into Western Nevada, resources noticed a spot fire on the green side of the road. Though a dozer attempted to line the spot, it was soon evident that the spot would not be controlled, and resources decided to leave the area. During their escape to the safety zone, a Type 6 engine became stuck trying to turn around. It was later determined that the engine was stuck because it was connected to a hoselay. Firefighters went to assist the Type 6 engine, and in the process one firefighter received burns to the elbow, face and neck. Eventually all resources escaped without further injury.
incidents.quote: We’ll get you checked out when we get out of here.

incidents.name: Devils Creek Fire Entrapment 2021
incidents.summary: On July 22nd, 2021, at approximately 1755 hours (Mountain Time), resources were engaged in suppression actions on the Devils Creek Fire. A thunderstorm several miles west of the fire area caused a wind shift and strong outflow winds. The increased rapid spread of the fire front trapped multiple resources in the path of the Fire. There were no shelter deployments.
incidents.quote: While both the ICT3(t) and Type 2 IA handcrew superintendent called resources off the line, the situation changed faster than anyone expected. Firefighters started rolling-up hoses and moving toward safe zones, but “there wasn’t even enough time for people to take two or three steps” before an intense gust of wind hit. Some called it 60 mph; others described ponderosas bent over like “whip antennas.” Personnel in vehicles reported that their vehicles shook. Everyone noted how the sky transitioned from black to orange. In the blink of an eye, total chaos ensued as overwhelming convective heat blasted through a 70 yard-wide area where the engines and Type 2 IA handcrew were working. Firefighters were thrown to the ground and attempted to curl up to protect themselves. Another firefighter frantically crawled into the back seat of an engine, but he didn’t want to shut the door because his pack was on fire.

incidents.name: Bootleg Fire Medical
incidents.summary: A firefighter assigned to the Bootleg Fire, Fremont-Winema National Forest, Oregon, was transported to the hospital for a seizure.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Fire Train Entrapment
incidents.summary: The Dixie Fire started on July 13th on the Plumas National Forest (California) in the Feather River Canyon and quickly spread. The private railroad companies were utilizing “fire trains” to protect their assets. A new fire, the Fly Fire, located to the east of the Dixie Fire, was also pushing more heat into the area around Keddie, California. The rail companies were going to work where the fires threatened their structures the most, which took them into this area. As the fire train was traveling north out of Keddie, those on board could see the fire activity greatly increase and cross Highway 89. When the fire train entered the tunnel, the engineer quickly brought the train to a stop because of increased fire behavior. In the ensuing entrapment, two firefighters became separated and took refuge in the tunnel. One of these injured his arm during the escape.
incidents.quote: “Knowing that they were there and coming to get us was a good feeling. They weren’t going to give up. I thought they all perished. And they thought we all perished."

incidents.name: Alder Creek Fire ICP Smoke Exposure and Air Quality
incidents.summary: Fire camp was located in an area where smoke from multiple fires was collecting. A Regional Smoke Specialist was ordered and they collected samples in camp. Readings were "Unhealthy", "Very Unhealthy", and "Hazardous". Camp was moved 10 miles down the road where the PM 2.5 readings were in the acceptable range.
incidents.quote: That night, the monitor collected five readings. All of them were in the “Unhealthy” range before the monitor lost power.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Dark Ravine Engine Crew Near Miss
incidents.summary: The Dixie Fire started on July 13, 2021 on the Plumas National Forest. On July 29, Strike Team 49C was assigned to their second operational shift to mop-up on Division November on the Dixie Fire’s East Zone. Multiple members of Strike Team 49C had to drop packs and tools and run with fire shelters in hand to escape increased fire behavior due to a passing front.
incidents.quote: “Drop your packs and tools, grab your fire shelters and run up here! There’s clean air up here!"

incidents.name: Molybdenite Fire Falling Incident
incidents.summary: While assigned to the Molybdenite Fire on the Colville National Forest, Washington, a sawyer on a 10-person fire module was hit by a helicopter water drop while falling a tree. The sawyer was uninjured and able to safely fall the tree.
incidents.quote: Shocked, drenched and furious.

incidents.name: Dixie Jumbo Fires Exertional Heatstroke
incidents.summary: A Bureau of Land Management engine crewmember was constructing indirect fireline during a high heat watch day. The firefighter displayed symptoms of heat illness and crewmembers requested a Line Medic. Responders initiated a “RED” medevac.The firefighter was transported via agency helicopter from the incident to a hospital in Missoula, Montana. The firefighter was diagnosed with exertional heatstroke. The firefighter was released from the hospital three days later.
incidents.quote: This heat illness progressed quickly and the firefighter became unresponsive to verbal stimuli.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Nez Perce National Forest Medical
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember was constructing indirect fireline during a high heat watch day on the Dixie Fire, Nez Perce National Forest, Idaho. Responders initiated RED medivac and the firefighter was transported via agency helicopter from incident to hospital in Missoula, MT and diagnosed with exertional heatstroke. The firefighter was released August 3, traveled home and continues to rest/recover per medical instruction.
incidents.quote: The firefighter displayed symptoms of heat illness and crewmembers requested a line medic. Heat illness progressed quickly and they became unresponsive to verbal stimuli.

incidents.name: Johnny Canyon Fire Lightning Strike
incidents.summary: A three-person initial attack crew were suppressing the Johnny Canyon Fire, Colorado, when they were informed by other fire personnel of active thunderstorms in their area. The crew decided to hike out of the fire and were impacted by a severe thunderstorm. While crossing a fence a lighting strike nearby was felt by two firefighters in their limbs. On the drive out in a UTV though rain and hail, the firefighters experienced early stages of hypothermia. After heating up in their truck they drove to their station without further incident.
incidents.quote: Lightning does not have to directly strike you to cause injury or worse.

incidents.name: River Complex Loss of Consciousness Due to Heat
incidents.summary: The patient was transported to the hospital and diagnosed with dehydration/exertion/heat-related illness. The patient was treated and released the same day. After resting in a hotel, the firefighter rejoined their crew.
incidents.quote: A U.S. Forest Service Rappel Crew member lost consciousness due to heat exhaustion on the River Complex on the Klamath National Forest.

incidents.name: Cub Creek 2 Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: Firefighter sustained a chainsaw injury while assigned to the Cub Creek 2 Fire, Washington. Sawyer transported to the hospital, received treatment then released and demobilized.

incidents.name: Morgan Creek Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A wildfire module crewmember on the Morgan Creek Fire, Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest, Colorado, sustained a chainsaw injury to the middle and ring finger. The firefighter was medevacked to a medical center, treated and released to the care of a hand specialist. The firefighter, currently on light duty, is expected to fully recover.
incidents.quote: A wildfire module crewmember on the Morgan Creek Fire, Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest, Colorado, sustained a chainsaw injury to the middle and ring finger.

incidents.name: Elbow Creek Fire Feller Buncher Rollover
incidents.summary: On the Elbow Creek Fire on August 5 at approximately 4:20 pm, a contract logger (part of the Contingency Group on the fire) operating a tracked Timberpro Feller/Buncher was involved in a rollover accident. The operator was engaged in hazard tree removal on Forest Road 6212 of the Walla Walla Ranger District, Umatilla National Forest, Oregon. The operator was uninjured.
incidents.quote: Standing at the top of the hill from where the Feller/Buncher rolled down the steep hillside, it is amazing that the operator was not seriously injured or worse.

incidents.name: McFarland Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On August 6, 2021, a 20-person hand crew was entrapped while suppressing a spot fire on an active flank of the McFarland Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California. Though they had multiple lookouts in place and an accessible safety zone, factors aligned to create a sudden, exponential increase in fire behavior right along their escape route. Crewmembers escaped into the black, ran through the flames, and/or took shelter behind a dozer on the road at their location. In all, 10 people (8 crewmembers, a dozer operator, and dozer swamper) were involved in the entrapment incident. Five crewmembers received first- and second-degree burns to small portions of their bodies, and one crewmember suffered smoke inhalation. All injured firefighters have recovered.
incidents.quote: It sounded like 10 freight trains going over the top of us and all you could see was a wall of flame 150 feet high.

incidents.name: Driving Home from Washington Fire Incident Vehicle Crash
incidents.summary: Driving home from an assignment on a fire incident in Washington, a firefighter crashed a non-agency vehicle and sustained injuries. The patient was transported to a hospital and received surgery for various fractures.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On Saturday, August 7, 2021, at approximately 1:00 AM, one CAL FIRE Fire Captain and three CAL FIRE Firefighters were injured by a falling tree during handline construction on the Dixie Fire, north of Chester, California. Two Firefighters were transported to Banner Lassen Medical Center in Susanville with minor injuries and were evaluated and released. The third Firefighter and Fire Captain were transported to Enloe Medical Center in Chico. The Firefighter was evaluated and released with minor injuries. The Fire Captain suffered lacerations, broken bones, and musculoskeletal injuries.
incidents.quote: Four Firefighters injured by a falling tree during handline construction on the Dixie Fire.

incidents.name: Monument Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: Initial report: two lacerations, approximately 1.5-2 inches. The patient was transported by ambulance to a hospital in Weaverville.
incidents.quote: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, a firefighter sustained a chainsaw cut to the foot.

incidents.name: South Yak Fire Masticator Operator Fall
incidents.summary: The patient was transported by ambulance to a local community hospital, where the patient’s status was elevated due to a punctured lung and four broken ribs. The patient was then Life Flighted to the Kootenai Health Medical Hospital in Coeur d’Alene, Idaho.
incidents.quote: On the South Yak Fire on the Kootenai National Forest, Montana, a contractor masticator operator fell approximately 15 feet off the masticator’s boom onto the machine’s tracks, injuring the operator’s side/ribs.

incidents.name: River Complex Medical Extraction
incidents.summary: On August 11, 2021, a member of a hand crew assigned to the River Complex on Northern California’s Klamath National Forest suffered a knee injury that required transportation to medical care.
incidents.quote: Due to the notoriously poor air quality and low visibility in the Klamath Mountains, it ultimately took the efforts of 40 people and two pack stock to coordinate and carry out a patient extraction by trail.

incidents.name: Character Complex Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: A contract ambulance transported the patient to the hospital for additional screening. The firefighter was released after screening determined that no broken bones or additional injuries were present.
incidents.quote: On the Character Complex on the Idaho Panhandle National Forest, a contract firefighter was struck by a 10-inch DBH tree while working in a burn area.

incidents.name: Monument Fire Cardiac Issues
incidents.summary: Later that evening, the firefighter was released fromhospital.
incidents.quote: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta Trinity National Forest, a firefighter was transported to the hospital in an ambulance for cardiac issues.

incidents.name: Rough Patch Complex Heavy Equipment Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Tree strike on Skidgine assigned to Rough Patch Complex, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon. The operator was transported to hospital with a shoulder injury.

incidents.name: Summit Trail Masticator Burn Damage
incidents.summary: On Sunday, August 15, 2021, forecasted and expected weather on the Summit Trail Fire, Washington, led to increased fire behavior. A masticator was assigned to work in an area of dozer improved roads on the north end of the incident. At approximately 13:15 hours that day, winds increased, and the decision was made to park the piece of equipment and for personnel to relocate to a specific drop point further down the hill and away from current fire activity. All personnel were accounted for at drop points away from fire activity and at approximately 18:00 hours, all personnel assigned to the division left the area enroute to ICP. Two days later, resources gained access to the site and determined the equipment had been burned over.
incidents.quote: Early the next morning, IMT members were awoken to address an unprecedented fire run that would total approximately 10,000 acres.

incidents.name: McFarland Fire ICP Relocation
incidents.summary: McFarland Fire Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California August 2021 Around 0900 the decision is made to evacuate the Incident Command Post (ICP). This decision is communicated via a preidentified text string. The movement of pre-identified personnel and their essential equipment (computers, etc.) is orderly and methodical. Engines and other operational resources begin arriving in the ICP area to begin structure protection prep work. The IC accepts that there may be a loss of some contractor property
incidents.quote: Around 0900 the decision is made to evacuate the Incident Command Post (ICP).

incidents.name: Monument Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: A ground ambulance provided transport to the hospital. The firefighter was treated and released back to full duty.
incidents.quote: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, an Interagency Hotshot Crew crewmember was struck in the arm and groin by a three-inch diameter snag.

incidents.name: Devil's Knob Complex Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A tree fell and it's branches struck two firefighters assigned to the Devil's Knob Complex, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon. One was transported to ER.

incidents.name: Antelope Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: On the Antelope Fire on the Klamath National Forest, California, an Interagency Hotshot Crew crewmember sustained a chainsaw cut to the elbow and thigh. Initial care was provided by the crew EMT, with further evaluation by a Medic (Green injury). Initially, the patient was not transported to a medical care facility. The IHC transported the firefighter to medical care the following day without IMT involvement
incidents.quote: Interagency Hotshot Crew crewmember sustained a chainsaw cut.

incidents.name: Trapper Creek Job Corps Multiple Incidents
incidents.summary: This FLA examines the two air ambulance rides and the stress-, heat-, and nutrition-related illness events to see what lessons might be shared with others.
incidents.quote: Over the course of five weeks, five separate medical incidents occurred involving the Trapper Creek Job Corps fire crew.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter sustained superficial burns to hand moving a hot rock while assigned to the Dixie Fire, California. Transported to medical facility for evaluation and treatment. Released to light duty for three days then returned to full duty.

incidents.name: West Lolo Complex Medical Incident
incidents.summary: The firefighter was released the same day.
incidents.quote: On the West Lolo Complex on the Lolo National Forest, a firefighter from an Initial Attack Crew was transported to a local hospital via ambulance due to chest pains, shortness of breath, and dizziness.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Firefighter Fall
incidents.summary: The initial report was back and abdomen pain. The firefighter was transported to the hospital, where the X-rays were negative.
incidents.quote: On the Dixie Fire in California, an Interagency Hotshot Crew crewmember fell 30 feet during night operations.

incidents.name: Character Complex Concussion
incidents.summary: Assessed on site by an EMT, it was determined that the firefighter had sustained a concussion. The patient was transported by ambulance to a hospital for further evaluation and was released the same day.
incidents.quote: On the Character Complex on the Idaho Panhandle National Forest, a firefighter was found unconscious with a knot on the side of the firefighter’s head.

incidents.name: Antelope Fire Hard Landing
