incidents.summary: On August 22, 2021 on the Antelope Fire on the Klamath National Forest in California, a Eurocopter AS-350 B3 experienced a hard landing. The pilot reported light winds on final approach after completing a high reconnaissance of the landing zone. At approximately 1 to 2 feet from the ground, a brownout condition developed, completely obscuring the ground from view of the pilot. The pilot continued to the ground and felt a slight bump as the aircraft touched down just a few seconds later. As visibility returned, the pilot shut the aircraft down and the aircrew exited the aircraft. At this time the Pilot noted the left skid was slightly bent and the bracket attaching the skid to the cross tube was cracked.
incidents.quote: A Eurocopter AS-350 B3 experienced a hard landing.

incidents.name: Monument Fire Hit by Tree Arm Injury
incidents.summary: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, an engine crewmember received a tree strike to the arm. The firefighter was taken by ground ambulance to Mad River Community Hospital in Arcata, California.
incidents.quote: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, an engine crewmember received a tree strike to the arm.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: When asked about the condition of his boot on that foot, the firefighter indicated that the boot was in poor condition (prior to this incident) and that its stitching threads between the leather seams was split and open—contributing to the burn on his foot.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on an Initial Attack Engine Crew was mopping-up along a handline on the Dixie Fire in California when, at 1240 hours, the firefighter stepped into a hot ash pit, receiving second-degree burns to the instep on the right foot.

incidents.name: Caldor Fire Burn Injury to Hand
incidents.summary: The firefighter was transported to hospital, treated, and then released back to the incident.
incidents.quote: On the Caldor Fire on the Eldorado National Forest, California, an interagency hotshot crew member received second degree burns to the hand.

incidents.name: Caldor Fire Pulaski Cut
incidents.summary: Initial care was provided by an EMT. The patient was provided ground transport by the Medical Unit to a local hospital.
incidents.quote: On the Caldor Fire on the Eldorado National Forest, California, an interagency hotshot crew firefighter sustained a pulaski laceration to the toe.

incidents.name: Spokane County Fire District #9 Fall Fatality
incidents.summary: Lieutenant/Paramedic Traber was on-duty at Fire Station 92. At approximately 9:43 p.m., Lieutenant/Paramedic Traber responded on E92 to a report of a brush fire near State Route 395 and Wandermere Road. E92 arrived on scene at approximately 9:49 p.m. and parked on the State Route 395 overpass above the entrance to the Little Spokane Valley. Lieutenant/Paramedic Traber exited E92 to begin searching for signs of the reported brush fire. Shortly thereafter, he fell from the overpass.
incidents.quote: Lieutenant/Paramedic Traber was confirmed deceased having fallen 210 feet from the overpass.

incidents.name: Monument Fire Fall from Tree
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via helicopter to a hospital, underwent surgery, and was scheduled for release to light duty.
incidents.quote: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, a Line Medic fell from a tree and broke their leg.

incidents.name: South Fire Severe Dehydration
incidents.summary: The patient was treated and released to light duty and was expected to return to full duty in two days.
incidents.quote: On the South Fire on the San Bernardino National Forest, California, a firefighter with severe dehydration was transported via ground ambulance to a hospital.

incidents.name: Monument Fire Hit By Branch
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California. A firefighter from a felling module was struck in the head by a tree branch, resulting in the loss of consciousness. The patient passed all neurological tests and was then transported to another medical facility for further evaluation.
incidents.quote: The patient was taken by ground transport to a local medical facility, where the injury was determined to be a skull fracture.

incidents.name: South Fire Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: On the South Fire on the San Bernardino National Forest, California, a firefighter was transported to the hospital for a confirmed case of Rhabdomyolysis (Rhabdo).

incidents.name: Colfax Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: On Saturday, Aug. 28, 2021, Chief Emeritus James Krouse responded to a wildland fire. While stretching hose lines, he experienced a medical emergency and collapsed. He was immediately taken to the local hospital where he passed away from an apparent heart attack.

incidents.name: Caldor Fire Ash Pit Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: On Saturday August 28, 2021, at approximately 1:55 PM, during mop up operations, a Local Government firefighter suffered 2nd & 3rd degree burns. The injuries occurred on Division Juliet of the Caldor Incident in El Dorado County just west of Strawberry. The firefighter was treated by incident personnel and ground transported to the UC Davis burn center. Due to smoke conditions on the incident, transport by air ambulance was not possible.
incidents.quote: The firefighter fell into an area of white ash, resulting in burns to both hands, forearms, and abdomen.

incidents.name: Roadside Fire Chest Pains
incidents.summary: On the Roadside Fire on the San Bernardino National Forest, California, an engine crewmember was transported to the hospital due to chest pains.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire COVID-19 Fatality
incidents.summary: While assigned to the Dixie Fire, Aug. 10-29, 2021, Assistant Fire Engine Operator Marcus Pacheco had close contact with a COVID-19 positive individual. He became ill and tested positive for the virus on Aug. 29, 2021. Assistant Fire Engine Operator Pacheco passed away due to complications from the virus on Sept. 2, 2021.

incidents.name: Middle Fork Complex Diabetic Incident
incidents.summary: On the Middle Fork Complex on the Willamette National Forest, Oregon, a firefighter was transported to the hospital due to a diabetic issue. The patient was then transported to the hospital, treated, released and de-mobbed.
incidents.quote: The firefighter had failed to eat dinner. Their diabetic monitoring device therefore sent a message to the firefighter’s significant other, who called the fire camp. Next, the IMT went to check on the firefighter.

incidents.name: Rough Patch Complex Tree Strikes Vehicle
incidents.summary: A Division Supervisor (DIVS) on the Rough Patch Complex, Oregon, attempted a face-to-face meeting to improve communications with a Falling Module who were working alone along a Forest Service road. The DIVS narrowly escaped injury when his truck was struck by a tree during felling operations.
incidents.quote: “Shock ran through me as I turned my head to see a large tree falling straight at me. I thought it was going to T-bone the cab of my truck.”

incidents.name: Monument Fire Hit By Limb
incidents.summary: On the Monument Fire on the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, a firefighter sustained injuries to the head and back via a fallen tree limb strike. A National Guard helicopter was activated to transport the firefighter to the hospital.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Fall From Trailer
incidents.summary: On the Dixie Fire in Northern California, a firefighter sustained an injury to the arm from falling off a trailer. The patient was transported to a hospital and required surgery.

incidents.name: Summit Trail Fire Drip Torch Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter was using a drip torch during a firing operation on Division G on the Summit Trail Fire in Washington. The firefighter believes that the drip torch’s vent must have been leaking fuel onto his pants as he was walking and, eventually, this fuel on his pants combusted.
incidents.quote: While burning with the drip torch in his right hand, his Nomex pants caught fire.

incidents.name: Middle Fork Complex Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On the Middle Fork Complex on the Willamette National Forest, a contracted logging truck went off the road and into a creek. The driver was transported to the hospital, treated, and released same day.

incidents.name: Middle Fork Complex Swamper Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: On the Middle Fork Complex on the Willamette National Forest, Oregon, a firefighter sustained a chainsaw cut to the arm while swamping. The patient was transported to the hospital for stitches and was then released back to fire camp on light duty.

incidents.name: Rough Patch Complex Log Roll Injures Leg
incidents.summary: The patient was transported to a local medical facility, treated, and released that evening.
incidents.quote: On the Rough Patch Complex on the Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, an Interagency Hotshot Crew member injured their leg when a log rolled over it.

incidents.name: Texas Tree Felling Near Miss
incidents.summary: On September 4, 2021, Texas A&M Forest Service employees were involved in the second day of clearing tree blowdown from a severe storm. Two fallers (a FAL3 and FAL2) assessed a snag next to a power pole. After using a pole saw to remove a limb from the snag that blocked felling it in the intended lay, the FAL2 was nearly struck when the snag fell unexpectedly.
incidents.quote: Texas Tree Felling Near Miss

incidents.name: Tumbledown Fire Sawyer Burn Injury
incidents.summary: On the Tumbledown Fire on the Panhandle National Forest, Idaho, a firefighter from a Wildland Fire Module sustained two minor burns to the lower part of the arm while cutting a hazard tree during line construction activities. The patient was transported to the hospital, treated, and released—with the potential for a referral to a local regional hospital.
incidents.quote: Due to the angle of the saw during the back cut, chips and burning debris flew up the firefighter’s shirt sleeve.

incidents.name: Devil's Knob Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: One or more members of a hand crew was hit by rocks on the Devil's Knob fire

incidents.name: Antelope Fire Lava Beds Water Tender Entrapment
incidents.summary: On 9/9/21 the Antelope Fire made a significant run into the monument ultimately crossing the main park road (10 Road) and burning into the 2020 Caldwell Fire scar. During this event a Lava Beds National Monument (California) water tender conducting preventative maintenance tasks was impacted by the fire front, became stuck and suffered burn damage to the vehicle but no injuries to firefighters.
incidents.quote: The operator had already emptied the tank and attempted to drive the vehicle back onto the roadway but was unable to get back up the embankment in the loose soil.

incidents.name: Rough Patch Complex Stump Hole Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The patient was treated and returned to the fire on light duty.
incidents.quote: On the Rough Patch Complex on the Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, a firefighter sustained a minor burn to the foot by stepping into a stump hole.

incidents.name: Schneider Springs Fire Twisted Knee
incidents.summary: On the Schneider Springs Fire on the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest in Washington, a firefighter was transported to the hospital due to a twisted knee.

incidents.name: Devil's Knob Complex Potential Broken Leg
incidents.summary: A firefighter assigned to the Devil's Knob Complex, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, was transported to hospital with potential broken leg.

incidents.name: Antelope Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: This incident occurred on the Antelope Fire on the Klamath National Forest, California. A firefighter received minor burns to the hands and ear when their Water Tender took direct flame impingement during retreat from the fire. These burn injuries were received when the firefighter partially deployed their shelter when exiting the immobilized vehicle to join with another vehicle. The patient was transported to a medical center, treated, and released the same evening.
incidents.quote: The noise of the fire was so loud that Engine-4 couldn’t hear anything except the fire beating against their engine.

incidents.name: Angeles NF Initial Attack Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: Firefighters sustained minor burn injuries during initial attack of a fire in Los Angeles County, California, when a firewhirl ran through the flank as the initial attack engine was establishing an anchor. The firefighters were treated and released. A joint review of this incident is being coordinated with the Los Angeles County Fire Department and the Angeles National Forest.
incidents.quote: Firefighters sustained minor burn injuries during initial attack.

incidents.name: Muckamuck Fire Hose Rolling Injury
incidents.summary: While working at a Spike Camp on the Muckamuck Fire, Washington, a crewmember on a Camp Crew was seriously injured while rolling hose on a machine. Pulled unexpectedly through the machine, both bones in her arm were broken.
incidents.quote: Her radius and ulna bones were shattered by the force of the machine and the steel of the rods

incidents.name: Route Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Firefighters from Los Angeles County (LAC) and the U.S. Forest Service (Angeles National Forest - ANF) were dispatched to a fire on ANF land near Castaic, California. Just after initial attack resources arrived on the scene, the fire spotted across Highway 99 and quickly established on the slope. Crews initially used a direct attack strategy to flank the fire, but after these spots established, the flank quickly became the head. In the resulting confusion, the fire behavior forced a LAC hand crew into two FS engines during escape efforts.
incidents.quote: These events happened within the first half-hour of initial attack.

incidents.name: Copter 205 Power Loss
incidents.summary: While conducting hoist rescue training just east of Vina Helitack Base, California, S-70i C-205 experienced a loss of power in one of two engines. The aircraft began to descend with a rescuer attached to the hoist hook causing the rescuer to contact the ground. The aircraft began to gain elevation bringing the rescuer to approximately 15 feet above ground level. Due to the power loss, the aircraft began to settle again. The rescuer received minor cuts and bruises and was transported to the hospital for medical evaluation.
incidents.quote: For the safety of the rescuer, the cable cut switch was engaged shearing the cable and rescuer from the hoist.

incidents.name: Dixie Fire Dehydration 1
incidents.summary: Heat Injury, Medevac, Extended Attack, Medical or Exertion or Heat
incidents.quote: A firefighter on a CAL FIRE division of the Dixie Fire, California, was transported to hospital for dehydration.

incidents.name: KNP Complex Firefighter Fall
incidents.summary: The patient was transported to the hospital and released home the same day.
incidents.quote: On the KNP Complex at Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, a firefighter fell approximately 10 to 15 feet and sustained a knee injury. Due to the pain in the knee, the patient lost consciousness.

incidents.name: Windy Fire Hit By Tree
incidents.summary: The tree had burned through its base. The firefighter, who received fractures to the spine (L-1 and L-2), had no loss of consciousness or loss of motor functions. The patient was transported via ambulance to the Drop Point, then via helicopter to a Level 2 Trauma Center, where the patient underwent surgery.
incidents.quote: While digging handline on the Windy Fire on the Sequoia National Forest, a firefighter was struck across the back by a 10-inch-diameter live oak tree.

incidents.name: McCash Fire COVID 19 Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter/Paramedic Brookfield was exposed to COVID-19 during on-duty activities. He became ill and his health worsened. He died on Sept. 29, 2021, as a result of COVID-19 complications.

incidents.name: Windy Fire Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The patient was transported via ground ambulance to a Drop Point, then via helicopter to Helibase where Life Flight provided transport to a Level 1 Trauma Center with an accredited Burn Center.
incidents.quote: While swamping for a falling module on the Windy Fire on the Sequoia National Forest, a firefighter fell hands-first into an ash pit, receiving second degree burns from the elbow to wrist on both arms—with an estimated 16 percent of burn coverage.

incidents.name: KNP Complex Tree Strike
incidents.summary: Firefighters working on the KNP Complex in Sequoia Kings Canyon National Park were hauling hose and appliances up a fireline to support a hoselay and direct line construction when a snag fell and hit another tree causing it to fall. Four firefighters were struck by the trees and injured. Firefighters on the hill performed triage on the injured personnel and were able to transport them off of the hill to a higher level of care within a relatively short timeframe using soft stretchers, a Stokes litter basket, and backboard.
incidents.quote: So what does this mean for wildland firefighters working under timber? This question was posed during interviews. Across the board the answer was consistent. This is the job; these are the conditions we face as wildland firefighters and we have to do the best we can to recognize and mitigate snag hazards.

incidents.name: Turkey Tracks Prescribed Fire Drip Torch Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Burn Injury, Firing Operation
incidents.quote: Turkey Tracks Rx Drip Torch Burn Injury

incidents.name: KNP Complex Calf Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Hand Crews, Extended Attack, Medevac, Burn Injury
incidents.quote: KNP Complex Calf Burn Injury

incidents.name: KNP Complex Rock Strike 1
incidents.summary: Medical Emergency, Hand Crews, Hit by Rock
incidents.quote: KNP Complex Rock Strike 1

incidents.name: KNP Complex Rock Strike 2
incidents.summary: Hand Crews, Medical Emergency, Hit by Rock
incidents.quote: KNP Complex Rock Strike 2

incidents.name: Alisal Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Alisal Fire, R5 Los Padres NF - 2nd degree burn to Federal Engine Crewmember. Ground transport to Goleta Valley ER for evaluation. Treated and released back to duty.
incidents.quote: Alisal Fire Burn Injury

incidents.name: Harrison County Snag Near Miss
incidents.summary: The Harrison County Sheriff’s Office requested Texas A&M Forest Service assistance on a wildfire with structures threatened on the afternoon of October 20, 2021. Upon arrival, multiple local fire departments were already on scene and taking action. While the ICT4 was talking with one of the engine operators, they were both unaware they were standing approximately 30’ away from a fire-weakened snag. The ICT4 heard a loud “pop," recognizing that sound to be a tree breaking, but he did not know where to go since he could not see the tree.
incidents.quote: “That’s what kills firefighters. Driving and snags.” – Agency Administrator The ICT4 and engine operator ran as fast as they could to safety, the snag fell in the exact location they had been standing.

incidents.name: Joes Volunteer Fire Department Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Wyant was out of the truck attempting to get a hose line stretched when the fire overtook him. He passed away at the scene.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Wyant and the members of his department faced 30 mph winds, with gusts up to 60 mph, with the wind direction changing as they worked to stop the fire.

incidents.name: Kruger Rock Fire Seat Accident
incidents.summary: On Tuesday, Nov. 16, 2021, Pilot Marc Olson was the sole occupant of a Single Engine Air Tanker (SEAT) that had been ordered by Laminer County to help fight the Kruger Rock Fire. During the mission, the plane crashed, killing Pilot Olson.
incidents.quote: Night-flying Single Engine Air Tanker crashes during the first tactical use of a SEAT at night.

incidents.name: Marshall Fire Initial Attack Mass Evacuations
incidents.summary: Firefighters, law enforcement officers, utility crews and volunteers worked inside the smoky fire perimeter, sometimes in piecemeal safety gear. Helmets and eye protection were stripped off by the wind, doors were bent back, and rocks, wood and sheet metal shattered the glass in emergency vehicles. Responding emergency personnel worked to battle the flames and evacuate about 35,000 people from the area, including hospitals and care facilities.
incidents.quote: The Marshall Fire began as a wildland fire, but it quickly moved into structures. Driven by wind gusts of up to 115 miles per hour, it swept through subdivisions and commercial buildings in the communities of Louisville and Superior, Colorado, and over a six-lane highway. Firebrands and flaming debris were carried ½ mile in front of the main fire.

incidents.name: Cherokee NF Tree Felling Injury
incidents.summary: After a recent winter storm caused road damage on the district, employees of the Cherokee National Forest, Tennessee attempted to clear trees on the 477 Road on January 12, 2022.
incidents.quote: A cherry tree being felled by a sawyer working alongside a backhoe broke and struck the sawyer in the face, breaking his nose.

incidents.name: Texas Interagency Coordination Center Continuity of Operations
incidents.summary: In mid-January 2022, an employee at TICC was symptomatic and tested positive for COVID-19. The other TICC employees had been exposed. The U.S. Forest Service employees began following reporting responsibilities to the National Forests and Grasslands in Texas (NFGT) Leadership at the Supervisors Office (SO). Due to the January 2022 agency quarantine requirements, the Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) was placed in motion by putting thebackup dispatch area into operation.
incidents.quote: “We thought we were prepared, but we hit a lot of stumbling blocks. We made it happen, but preplanning is a must.”

incidents.name: Compartment 68 Prescribed Fire Heavy Equipment Incident
incidents.summary: On the morning of February 5, 2022, the Oakmulgee Ranger District, National Forests in Alabama, was preparing multiple compartments for prescribed fire by using several dozers at different compartments. During the morning operational briefing, two firefighters were assigned to work Compartment 68 on a John Deere 450J. After about two and half hours of line prep, they had made significant process, until the dozer became stuck in some soft dirt. During an attempt to winch the dozer out, the dozer swamper was attempting to free the winch cable which would not freespool. The winch became activated and crushed the swamper's middle and index fingers.
incidents.quote: The operator unintentionally engaged the winch in gear, immediately crushing the swamper’s hand in between the roller ball and the winch cable. He was able to quickly pull his hand away, but not before his left index and middle finger were crushed.

incidents.name: Red Rio Prescribed Fire UTV Fire
incidents.summary: On February 9, 2022, on the Red Rio Prescribed Fire unit on the Las Cruces District, Bureau of Land Management, New Mexico, a group of three patrolled the unit on a UTV. The firefighters were not aware that vegetation had become wedged between the UTV’s bed and cab. As they continued driving and patrolling the fire’s edge, this wedged vegetation caught fire and melted a corner of the UTV’s bed. The operator smelled the melting plastic and quickly stopped the UTV. The fire was quickly extinguished with no injuries, and the UTV was still functional.
incidents.quote: I smelled the melting plastic and quickly stopped the UTV.

incidents.name: Compartment 15 Prescribed Fire UTV Fire 2022
incidents.summary: On February 10, 2022, the Davy Crockett National Forest of the National Forests and Grasslands in Texas conducted prescribed fire operations on two separate burn units. Toward the end of the day, two fire personnel, a firefighter and a UTV Operator, were assigned firing operations of the control line between two drop points. Suspecting a fuel leak on the UTV, the UTV Operator stops to investigate. As the UTV Operator begins to dismount the UTV, they are immediately surrounded by black smoke and flames coming from under the UTV between the driver’s seat and the cargo bed. There are no injuries but the UTV is destroyed.

incidents.name: LaGrange Fire Department Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On Sunday, Feb. 20, 2022, Captain David Holmes responded to the scene of a brush fire. While at the incident, he experienced breathing problems. Captain Holmes was immediately transported to the hospital where he was placed on life support. He was then moved to the Cape Fear Hospital where he was removed from life support on Monday, Feb. 28, 2022. The nature of his death was a massive heart attack.
incidents.quote: When his son joined the department, David came out of retirement so he could help train his son and serve alongside him.

incidents.name: Jim Fire Blasting Incident
incidents.summary: On March 2, 2022, a 553-acre wildfire was ignited by super-heated rocks landing in dense brush from fish barrier removal blasting efforts on the Cleveland National Forest in Southern California.

incidents.name: Ward Volunteer Fire Department Burn Injury Fatality
incidents.summary: On Thursday, March 3, 2022, Acting Chief Freddy C. Reeves was attempting to put out a grass fire when his pants caught fire and he was injured. When an ambulance arrived, Acting Chief Reeves was transported to a local hospital and then to the burn center at the University of Mississippi Medical Center in Jackson, MS. Reeves subsequently became increasingly ill after responding to treatment and passed away from his injuries on Friday, March 25, 2022.

incidents.name: Lynn Fire and Rescue Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: Lynn Fire and Rescue was dispatched to assist Haleyville Fire with a wildland fire. During containment operations, Engineer/Operator Larry Harbin experienced a sudden medical emergency which led to cardiac arrest. Harbin was treated by paramedics from Lynn Fire and Rescue and Regional Paramedic Services and immediately transported to Lakeland Community Hospital where he was pronounced deceased.

incidents.name: Angelina Sabine Tree Felling Incident
incidents.summary: On March 6th, a Type 6 USFS engine module with 3 personnel, was assigned to complete prescribed fire (RX) prep on the Angelina/Sabine National Forests of The National Forests and Grasslands in Texas. Using road guards on the still-open public road, the engine captain felled a tree that brushed three trees as it fell. Two green pines broke and fell into the road, impacting the very rear of a boat being hauled by a pickup truck.
incidents.quote: The Engine Captain saw green needles from the broken pines appear to come very close to an unexpected red pickup pulling a boat traveling in the far lane at a high speed eastbound.

incidents.name: Monongahela NF RX Prep Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A firefighter was struck by a piece of a tree while felling a hazard tree during line preparation for an upcoming prescribed fire on the Monongahela National Forest, West Virginia. The top 3-4’ of a 3-4” diameter tree broke off and fell, striking the firefighter on their left arm. EMTs on scene rendered immediate aid stabilizing the injuries. The decision was made to transport the injured party via agency vehicle to the nearest emergency department for further evaluation. They were assessed and diagnosed with a break in the ulna and fracture of the radius.
incidents.quote: A firefighter was struck by a piece of a tree while felling a hazard tree.

incidents.name: King Road Fire Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: At 1224 the Edgewater Volunteer Fire Department was paged out to a fire near King Road. Two volunteer firefighters responded to the scene with a Type 6 Engine and began suppression operations. During suppression actions one firefighter became separated from the apparatus and was subsequently entrapped and burned over.
incidents.quote: On Sunday, March 20, 2022 April Lynn Partridge,a member of the Edgewater Park Volunteer Fire Department, was entrapped and burned over during firefighting operations on the King Road Fire.

incidents.name: Ouachita National Forest Heavy Equipment Incidents
incidents.summary: Between August 2021 and March 2022, the Ouachita National Forest in Arkansas had three separate bulldozer fire incidents involving three different operators. Two of these incidents occurred during prescribed burns and one happened during road maintenance.
incidents.quote: I wanted to save the machine, so I radioed for the UTV pumper. I threw out my shelter and iPad and grabbed the fire extinguisher!”

incidents.name: Antihorse Prescribed Fire Drip Torch Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The Antihorse Prescribed Fire, ignited on March 20 and March 27, covered approximately 2,700 acres of Black Hills National Forest lands in South Dakota. Just prior to ignitions completing at around 1650, an Engine Boss was utilizing a drip torch to burn out remaining islands of grass along the highway but believed the torch contained bad fuel. He removed the torch’s cap and attempted to pour out its remaining fuel. When doing so, flames from a nearby fuel source ignited the drip torch fuel. A crewmember, standing by the engine, grabbed the charged hardline and extinguished the fire on the pant leg. An EMT responded to the scene and noticed a small burn to the crux of the knee and a half-dollar-sized blister below the knee on the inside of the calf.
incidents.quote: He removed the torch’s cap and attempted to pour out its remaining fuel. When doing so, flames from a nearby fuel source ignited the drip torch fuel.

incidents.name: Beaver River Fire Engine Rollover and Entrapment
incidents.summary: On April 5, 2022 during initial attack efforts on the Beaver River Fire, a Balko Volunteer Fire Department engine (Balko 5) was responding to the Beaver River Fire on County Road 22, Beaver County, Oklahoma. Poor visibility conditions existed due to smoke and dust. Balko Engine 5, with two occupants, veered slightly off the road onto a gravel shoulder that collapsed. As a result, the engine slid off an embankment approximately six feet in depth and rolled over on its top into the side ditch. Subsequently, an active area of the fire switched directions as it was impacted by strong winds that had shifted from west to northwest. Prior to the fire arriving at the accident scene both occupants were able to self-evacuate. However, both firefighters sustained 1st and 2nd degree burns to their arms and hands as the fire burned past. In addition, one victim possibly suffered a concussion during the vehicle rollover.
incidents.quote: Initially both victims were listed in critical condition.

incidents.name: Gallinas Las Dispensas Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire Review
incidents.summary: The Gallinas Watershed Prescribed Fire, Las Dispensas Unit, is located on the Santa Fe National Forest, Pecos-Las Vegas Ranger District in New Mexico. Test fire ignitions began the morning of April 6, 2022. The test fire was determined successful at 1234, and ignitions continued. The prescribed fire was declared a wildfire (Hermit’s Peak Fire) about four hours later. On May 10, 2022, USDA Forest Service Chief Randy Moore launched a review team to conduct a Declared Wildfire Review of the incident.
incidents.quote: Gallinas Las Dispensas Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire after 4 hours.

incidents.name: Sand Creek Fire Dozer Water Crossing
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, April 6, 2022, the State of Texas deployed multiple fire resources from across the state to engage in initial attack and wildland fire responses in the Amarillo, Texas area. While working to contain the Sand Creek Fire, a bulldozer was attempting to ford a seemingly safe, low-water “rip-rap” structure crossing when it became unstable and the dozer was quickly submerged. The Dozer Operator, with help from the Task Force Leader, narrowly escaped drowning in the dozer.
incidents.quote: “I hollered on the radio. Get out! Get out! Get out!” - Task Force Leader Trainee

incidents.name: South Overflow Wetlands Rx Review
incidents.summary: On April 7, 2022, at 1130 the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Pecos District, Fire Management Program initiated a planned 330-acre prescribed broadcast burn on a portion of the South Overflow Wetland unit (type 2) on BLM public lands in the Roswell Field Office, New Mexico. During the prescribed fire, a dust devil carried embers across the north control line that onsite resources were unable to contain. After determining the initial suppression actions were not going to be successful in containing the slop over and nearby structures were threatened, the decision was made to declare the South Overflow Wetland prescribed burn a wildfire.
incidents.quote: This fire whirl caused mass ignition of fuels on the other side of the control line, which in turn, created unpredicted fire behavior due to strong gusty winds and multiple spot fires.

incidents.name: Road 739 Fire Driving Fatality
incidents.summary: While driving on a highway to navigate through the fire scene, a Fire Chief and a County Emergency Manager were involved in a head-on collision with a water tender. The crash resulted in the death of the Fire Chief and life-threatening injuries to the Emergency Manager, who was driving the vehicle.
incidents.quote: Visibility due to blowing smoke and dust was less than 10 feet.

incidents.name: Montana Engine Operation Lessons
incidents.summary: The wildland engine was on an established road traversing the middle of the fire heading towards a private structure that was near the head of the fire when it struck the rear of the private vehicle. Just before being struck by the wildland fire engine, the private vehicle struck another private vehicle ahead of it on the same road while trying to return to the private residence.
incidents.quote: Several recent incidents involving other fire departments from across the nation have once again highlighted a recurring theme that often the most dangerous thing we do is driving to, at, and from emergency scenes.

incidents.name: Augusta IHC Rhabdomyolysis Medical Incident
incidents.summary: A crewmember on the Augusta Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC), Skylar, was diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis (Rhabdo) after four days into their “80 critical hours” of mandatory training for IHCs at their home base. Because the EMT and crew superintendent had a general working knowledge of Rhabdo and its impacts on wildland firefighters—and because they took decisive action—they were able to get Skylar immediate medical care. He was admitted to the hospital with extreme levels of creatine phosphokinase (CK) in his urine.
incidents.quote: "We have a process. Let’s trust the process and take him to the hospital.”

incidents.name: Hermits Peak Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter assigned to the Hermits Peak Fire, Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico was mopping up with a backpack pump. While hiking uphill a gust of wind unbalanced him and he fell backwards, landing on a tool that was slung on his back. The firfighter sustained a lower spine compression fracture. He was transported to hospital via incident ambulance; treated and released and expected to make a full recovery after a few weeks and physical therapy.
incidents.quote: A firefighter sustained a lower spine compression fracture while working on the Hermits Peak Fire.

incidents.name: Hoosier NF Rx Fire CPR & AED Use
incidents.summary: A firefighter assigned to a prescribed fire was found unresponsive at the conclusion of the prescribed burn. EMTs on site started CPR and utilized an AED and were able to reestablish breathing and a heartbeat. The individual was life flighted to a hospital in Louisville, KY, where a stint was put in place.
incidents.quote: The evaluator found the AD firefighter on the ground halfway under his private vehicle in a prone position

incidents.name: Engine Bay Backing Incident
incidents.summary: As the engine was backing, the driver heard a coworker yell out, but the driver did not stop in time. Compartment 9 was open and contacted the edge of the engine bay. The door was crumpled and a hinge was bent.
incidents.quote: As an engine was backing into the Engine Bay a compartment door was open which caused it to be damaged.

incidents.name: Road 702 Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: John P. Trumble, 66 of Arapahoe Nebraska died Friday evening, April 22, 2022 at approximately 7:00 p.m. as a result of the Road 702 Fire in Red Willow County. Mr. Trumble was retired as the Cambridge Fire Chief, but was assisting with firefighting efforts by acting as a spotter. Mr. Trumble’s vehicle was north bound on road 407 approximately seven miles southeast of Bartley, Nebraska when it left the roadway due to poor visibility from smoke and dust, where he was overcome by smoke and fire.

incidents.name: Jackson IHC Close Call Motor Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: The crew was traveling in a convoy consisting of the superintendent truck, two crew carriers (buggies), and a GSA short-term rental with trailer (this vehicle has no warning lights or striping). While going over a blind hill, a major accident occurred in the middle of the convoy. A car pulled out in front of a pickup traveling the opposite direction of the crew. The accident resulted in the pickup being sent airborne and rolling several times in the oncoming lane. Our second buggy had a following distance of 8 to 10 seconds. The driver of that buggy needed every second of that distance to stop
incidents.quote: “In all my years in the hotshot world, this is the closest I have come to having our crew vehicles involved in a major accident.”

incidents.name: Crooks Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: A firefighter sustained a foot injury from a falling rock while cutting hand line. Another crewmember was standing on a rock uphill, which broke off and fell approximately 3 feet and struck the patient in the shin and knee, then landed on the foot. FS EMTs on scene did an initial assessment, and the patient was transported via incident ambulance then 911 ambulance to a local hospital. Patient diagnosed with a fractured foot (metatarsals) and is currently recovering at home.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on the Crooks Fire was hit by a rock dislodged from uphill.

incidents.name: Central Conejos Fire Protection District Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.fire: Central Conejos Fire Protection Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: Cordova responded to a grassland fire near Manassa, to help with protecting structures. Shortly after arriving at the scene, he told colleagues that he wasn’t feeling well and went home. A short time later, his family called 9-1-1 and he was rushed to the Conejos County Hospital where he passed away from an apparent heart attack.
incidents.quote: He was the longest-serving member of the Central Conejos Fire Protection District, Manassa Fire Department, where he had served with dedication for 66 years.

incidents.name: Federal Firefighter Presumptive Illness
incidents.summary: In May 2022 a federal firefighter undergoing brain cancer treatment filed a claim to the Office of Workers’ Compensation Programs (OWCP) for medical expenses under presumptive illness direction covering certain illnesses in federal firefighters. His cancer treatment was covered by OWCP.
incidents.quote: As the result of the specific exposures that routinely occur in the course of their employment, Federal firefighters are at increased risk of certain types of cancers, heart disease and lung disease.”

incidents.name: Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: While preparing for a firing operation on the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon Fires, Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico, crews identified a burning snag that needed to be addressed. A sawyer attempted to fall the snag but it became hung up in a live tree. The sawyer used a notch and hinge cut to attempt to bring the snag to the ground safely. On the final cut the snag dislodged. The base hit the ground and pivoted. The snag fell and struck the sawyer in the back.
incidents.quote: Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Hit by Tree

incidents.name: Calaveras Big Trees State Park Rx Hit By Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: On Friday, May 6, 2022, Wildland Firefighter Darin Banks was assigned to a Type II Initial Attack Hand Crew working to prepare an area for a prescribed burning in Tuolumne County. While working the area, he was hit by a dead tree that fell. He was transported down the hill to the medics where CPR was performed. All life-saving measures were unsuccessful and he was pronounced deceased.

incidents.name: Left Fork Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: On April 7, 2022, with snow on the ground, resources lit 25 acres of slash piles in a recent timber sale on the Dixie National Forest, Utah. On May 9, high winds pushed embers from the still smoldering piles across the unit boundary and the Left Fork Prescribed Fire was soon declared a wildfire. It was determined that the pile burn had crept around within the burn unit until igniting heavy fuels, lofting embers into the now snow-free receptive fuels, adjacent to the burn unit.

incidents.name: Smokejumper Training Rhabdo
incidents.summary: A Forest Service Region 1 smokejumper trainee was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis (rhabdo) on the second day of initial smokejumper training in Idaho. Because the program and parties involved were familiar with rhabdo and took timely action, the firefighter received appropriate medical care in time to prevent the case from becoming a more serious medical emergency with the potential for long-term effects.
incidents.quote: At this point, the firefighter realized, obviously, something wasn’t right and that it wasn’t just fatigue.

incidents.name: Fresno-Kings Unit Initial Attack Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: The firefighter was assisting another crewmember with a hose pack when the rock struck. Patient fell down hill with the rock approximately 10 feet and the rock continued downslope. Patent received treatment on scene immediately, then was hoisted via CHP helicopter and transported to the hospital. All tests came back negative (e.g. no broken bones, strained muscles, torn tendons, etc.); patient was released and will be on light duty for a couple days then released back to full duty.
incidents.quote: A Forest Service firefighter was hit by a large rock while performing initial attack on a Cal Fire jurisdiction incident on the Fresno-Kings Unit in California.

incidents.name: Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire Dozer Operations Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: During night shift on the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire, Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico, an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) module was assisting with dozer line construction. A squadleader was acting as a dozer swamper by helping direct the dozer operator as a line locator. While approaching a fence at 0100, the dozer knocked over a tree which struck the squadleader. The injured firefighter was treated onscene and packaged for trasnport. He was taken to the hospital by ground ambulance as conditions were not conducive to air medevac.
incidents.quote: I’d like to make the point that Night Group 4 ensured that all resources knew what medical resources we had on the Division and where they were located every operational shift. This greatly assisted during this medical incident.

incidents.name: Bear Trap Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: An EMT assessed the patient, who was transported to a medical care facility via agency vehicle. The patient was assessed, treated and released that same day, and received a referral to a hand specialist.
incidents.quote: A hand crew member assigned to the Bear Trap Fire, Cibola National Forest, New Mexico, suffered a ground fall on an outstretched arm/hand, resulting in a finger fracture.

incidents.name: Redding Smokejumper Training Broken Femur
incidents.summary: On May 16, 2022 six rookie smokejumpers in California boarded the plane for their final rookie training jump. The second person on the third stick (Rookie #6 - jumpers often jump in pairs called a “stick”) brushed a tree on final approach to the jump spot. He was swept off course and he impacted the ground with enough force to break his femur.
incidents.quote: A trainee in the Redding Smokejumper school was swept off course and impacted the ground with enough force to break his femur.

incidents.name: Plumtaw Fire Potential Operational Delineations Use
incidents.summary: The Plumtaw Fire was ignited May 17, 2022 on the San Juan National Forest, Pagosa Ranger District, Colorado, by suspected human activities. The fire ignited within a pre-identified Potential Operational Delineation (POD) developed by staff and cooperators on and adjacent to the San Juan National Forest in 2019. PODs are fire management and planning units whose boundaries are defined by potential control features—such as roads and natural barriers— within which fire risk to values can be quantified and summarized.
incidents.quote: The Risk Management Assistance (RMA) Dashboard was used early in the incident to evaluate POD lines against Potential Control Location Likelihood.

incidents.name: Helicopter Manager Fatality
incidents.summary: With the assistance of Arizona Department of Public Safety Air Rescue, the body of 38-year-old Patrick Gladics was located shortly before 12:30 p.m. on May 17, 2022. He had been in the area on a fire assignment as a helicopter manager. Gladics was found deceased in a desert area in Sierra Vista.
incidents.quote: Video surveillance showed Gladics running northbound from the parking lot toward the desert at 5 a.m. on Saturday

incidents.name: Cerro Pelado Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A handcrew member assigned to the Cerro Pelado Fire, Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico, was struck by a small tree/limb and sustained swelling and bruising to the lower back. The patient was transported to a medical care facility via incident ambulance and is stable. A short rehabilitation time is expected before a return to full duty.
incidents.quote: A handcrew member assigned to the Cerro Pelado Fire was struck by a small tree/limb.

incidents.name: Simms Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire Review
incidents.summary: On May 16, 2022, firefighters ignited a 188-acre prescribed fire on the Ouray Ranger District of the Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre, Gunnison National Forest near Montrose, Colorado. The burn unit was within the wildland-urban interface (WUI) and directly adjacent to private land. Mop up and patrol continued for the next three days, with smoldering and smoke production decreasing over time. On May 19, a forecasted cold front arrived. That afternoon, a wildfire became established adjacent to the burn unit on private land. Ultimately, one primary residence and two other structures were destroyed, and 313 acres of private and Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land outside of the unit were burned.
incidents.quote: A Simms Prescribed Fire ignited after 3 days with high winds and became a wildfire.

incidents.name: Black Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: EMTs were involved in transporting the patient via agency helicopter to a local hospital. The patient sustained a fractured elbow, orbital fracture and a laceration that did not require stitches. The patient was still in the ER at the time of the report, but due to be released that evening.
incidents.quote: A base camp manager on the Black Fire, Gila National Forest, New Mexico, experienced a fall onto concrete stepping onto a cooler from the tailgate of a truck.

incidents.name: Lost Lake Fire Bee Sting Infection
incidents.summary: On May 27, 2022 the morning briefing on the Lost Lake Fire, Arizona, began at 0600 in the shade of flowering eucalyptus trees. This particular morning thousands of bees were very active and a water tender crew member (FF1) was stung on the right middle finger. Although allergic to bees, FF1 had been stung on the hand years ago and experienced only localized tenderness with minimal swelling. The following day, an increasing reaction to the sting caused FF1 to go to a medical facility where the severity of his injury was diagnosed and treated.
incidents.quote: Stressing that the finger might not be saved convinced FF1 to immediately drive to a medical facility

incidents.name: Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire Hit by Water Drop Injury
incidents.summary: Three hotshot crews were assigned to secure a portion of the edge of the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon Fire in New Mexico. Crews put in line and used a helicopter for water drops. Three members of one of the crews sustained injuries after being struck by a water drop. One suffered "red" injuries, two were classified as "green". Patients were transported to a higher level of care via UTV, ambulance, and helicopter.
incidents.quote: “I saw the ship drop on Vale, but I assumed they got out of the way. I should have checked on them, but there was no yelling like we yelled on the first drop. So I assumed they were OK. I felt bad. We could have helped carry people.”

incidents.name: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fall off Heavy Equipment
incidents.fire: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fall off Heavy Equipment
incidents.summary: An excavator operator assigned to the Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fire on Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico, fell off the equipment while checking the oil and sustained injuries. The patient was transported to a local hospital via national guard Blackhawk and stayed overnight. Patient’s injuries included a broken arm (radius and ulna), dislocated elbow and contusions and lacerations on the head/face. Surgery was planned for the broken arm.
incidents.quote: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fall off Heavy Equipment

incidents.name: Black Fire Pulaski Cut
incidents.summary: A hand crew member was moving through thick brush on the fire line while responding to a new start (crew was on loan from Black Fire - Gila National Forest, New Mexico - for IA response), using a pulaski to help stabilize while moving and inadvertently swung the tool into the lower leg, resulting in a laceration to the right shin (approx. 1” in length and ¾” in depth). Initial first aid provided by EMT-B-certified crew member, then patient transported to a regional medical center. Patient restricted to light duty and transport home planned for the following day.
incidents.quote: A hand crew member on the Black Fire was using a pulaski to help stabilize while moving and inadvertently swung the tool into the lower leg, resulting in a laceration to the right shin.

incidents.name: White Mountain NF ATV Training Rollover
incidents.summary: On June 15, an ATV certification and refresher course was held on the Androscoggin Ranger District of the White Mountain National Forest, New Hampshire. During the training, students were instructed to practice loading and unloading ATVs on a trailer. One student lost control of the ATV while ascending the ramps and the machine nearly rolled over on top of them. No serious injury occurred.
incidents.quote: "The ATV was uncontrollable, and I bailed off. I thought the ATV was going to flip backwards on top of me."

incidents.name: Sheep Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A crewmember presented with nausea and vomiting on the Sheep Fire, San Bernardino NF, and was transported to a hospital via agency vehicle, where they were treated for heat stress and dehydration.

incidents.name: Aggey Creek Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: The individual was transported via air to a hospital and admitted for the night. An orthopedic doctor examined the injury and provided further care, and the individual was released to be non-weight bearing for at least a few weeks.
incidents.quote: A hand crew member assigned to the Aggey Creek Fire, Alaska, was injured while swamping for a sawyer when the saw made contact with the front of the shin.

incidents.name: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fire Fall
incidents.summary: A crewmember assigned to the Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fire on Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico, fell down while walking in the performance of suppression rehabilitation work and broke a finger. Patient transported to hospital via crew vehicle, where the finger was splinted and the patient was released to spend a couple days in a hotel then return to the crew.
incidents.quote: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fire Fall

incidents.name: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Twisted Ankle
incidents.summary: A crewmember assigned to the Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Fire, Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico, twisted an ankle while walking, requiring helicopter transport off the mountain and crew transport to the hospital, where the individual received treatment.
incidents.quote: Hermits Peak-Calf Canyon Twisted Ankle

incidents.name: Maxwell Community Volunteer Fire Department Vehicle Accident Fatalities
incidents.summary: Two brothers, Assistant Chief Jonathon Coco and Firefighter Hunter Coco, were returning from the scene of a wildland fire on Texas Highway 20 in a brush truck when the driver of a privately owned vehicle failed to yield and was struck by the truck. The brush truck rolled over killing both Assistant Chief Jonathon Coco and Firefighter Hunter Coco.

incidents.name: Backbone Fire Seizure
incidents.summary: An ambulance transported the patient to medical care. The patient was then released back to their home unit. It was determined that this event was non-incident related.
incidents.quote: A firefighter on the Backbone Fire on the Coconino National Forest suffered a seizure while walking.

incidents.name: Clear Fire Helicopter Crash Fatality
incidents.summary: On Sunday, June 26, 2022, Pilot Douglas "Doug" Ritchie, the sole occupant of a Bell UH-1B helicopter, was supporting firefighting efforts at the Clear Fire, Alaska. While hovering with a longline, Ritchie maneuvered the helicopter to position the remote hook for external load hook up. A loud mechanical noise was heard and the helicopter rolled right and fell to the ground in a nose-low attitude from a height of about 150 feet.
incidents.quote: A loud “snap” or “bang” was heard, and the helicopter “bucked”.

incidents.name: Angelina/Sabine National Forests UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: Two personnel from the Angelina/Sabine National Forest in Texas were assigned to check dozer lines for erosion in the Red Hill Burn Unit. The UTV they were driving began to fishtail as they descended a steep slope and rolled over an estimated two and a quarter times. Both the driver and passenger were wearing their seatbelts, securing them in the UTV.
incidents.quote: Steep terrain was identified as a potential Watch Out situation during the morning briefing.

incidents.name: Northern Rockies Firefighter Smoke Exposure
incidents.summary: A USFS engine in Montana responds to initial attack a fire burning in a Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) setting. While engaging in suppression activity, a wind shift causes exposure of the engine crew to toxic smoke from burning structures. The crew seeks medical attention after they exhibit symptoms including irritated eyes, prolonged coughing and vomiting.
incidents.quote: “There was a sudden wind reversal, and it blew hot air and smoke directly into my face, and I felt the effects of it immediately."

incidents.name: Max Fire Short Haul Initial Attack
incidents.summary: Because of the amount of time it would have taken to hike two personnel in, contain the fire, and hike back out— and with the potential for adverse weather moving in—everyone on board agreed that a short-haul fire insertion would be the safest and most efficient way to contain the fire. The Duty Officer was contacted on the radio and the crew relayed that a short-haul operation would be the best, safest option for getting fire personnel into the fire quickly. The Duty Officer agreed and gave the approval to proceed.
incidents.quote: Max Fire Short Haul Initial Attack

incidents.name: Minto Lakes Fire Lightning Strike Near Miss
incidents.summary: An incident ambulance crew of two people was staged at their posting position at a Drop Point (DP) on the Minto Lakes Fire, Alaska. The DP was at a high point of terrain relative to the surrounding terrain and was also the site of a utility tower. At approximately 1845, while the ambulance crew was sitting in their tent structure taking shelter from rain, a lightning strike occurred on—or very near—their tent. They evacuated the tent and climbed into a van with other personnel to wait out the weather.
incidents.quote: The crew observed sparks and the smell of burning plastic.

incidents.name: Goose Fire Pulaski Cut
incidents.summary: A hand crew member struck the lower leg with a pulaski during suppression activities on the Goose Fire, Alaska. The individual was transported to a medical facility via Guardian air, and initial reports were of a 2” laceration to the medial side of the right foot.
incidents.quote: Goose Fire Pulaski Cut

incidents.name: Fire 525 Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A group of smokejumpers were suppressing fire with water in a patch of birch trees near a deep, identified ash pit on Fire 525 in Alaska. One individual stumbled when moving positions and fell head first into the ash pit, disappearing completely under the ash surface. He emerged from the pit and was helped to solid ground where he was initially evaluated and his burned hands cooled with water. At the medevac site he was treated by smokejumper EMTs, and was flown of the fire approximately one hour after the injury occurred.
incidents.quote: He disappeared completely beneath the surface of the boiling ash and dust. I looked at the spot where he had disappeared and was momentarily stunned—not believing what I had seen

incidents.name: Clear Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A handcrew member received an approximately 8” long x 2” deep cut to the calf from a chainsaw while assigned to the Clear Fire, Alaska. Initial reports are that the crewmember ran into a saw team. Crewmember was transported to a hospital for care.
incidents.quote: A crewmember ran into a saw team and suffered a deep cut on the Clear Fire.

incidents.name: East Mesa Fire Helicopter Accident
incidents.summary: On Saturday, July 16, 2022, Lieutenant Matthew King from the Bernalillo County Fire Department, and three members of the Bernalillo County Sheriff’s Office, were aboard a helicopter returning to Albuquerque after performing aerial wildland fire suppression at the East Mesa Fire. The helicopter crashed killing all four occupants.
incidents.quote: Two witnesses on a ridge about 0.5 mile east of the accident site were observing the sunset and reported the helicopter flew past their location westbound, then rapidly descended without making any turns.

incidents.name: Dalton Highway Complex Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: The swamper and sawyer were facing away from each other and turned in the same direction, causing a strike to the back of the swamper’s hand. The crewmember was transported to a hospital and received stitches for an approximately 1.5” laceration.
incidents.quote: A handcrew member sustained a cut to the hand from a chainsaw on 7/16 while swamping for the sawyer while constructing line on the Dalton Highway Complex, BLM, Alaska.

incidents.name: Red River County Downed Electrical Line
incidents.summary: On July 27, 2022, Texas A&M Forest Service resources were requested on a small wildfire in Red River County with multiple structures threatened. While establishing dozer line through thick vegetation to stop fire progression toward a barn, a hidden, live electrical line was broken and fell between the blade and the front of the dozer. The operator was able to safely stay in the dozer while the electricity could be turned off and the electrical line removed without incident.
incidents.quote: A dozer came in contact with a downed hidden power line and had to wait for the line to be turned off.

incidents.name: Weasel Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: The employee suffered bumps, bruises, abrasions and a possible concussion. EMTs transported the patient via sked off the fireline to an ambulance, which transported the patient to a rendezvous site with Alert Aire ambulance to transport to the hospital. Employee was released on 7/31 for one week of no active duty, after which the employee will be reevaluated by medical staff.
incidents.quote: An engine crewmember was struck by the top of a snag while scouting a potential sawline on the Weasel Fire, Kootenai National Forest, Montana

incidents.name: Calf Canyon Fire Air Curtain Burner Lessons
incidents.summary: More than 30 miles of contingency line were installed on the north end of the Calf Canyon Fire (Santa Fe National Forest, New Mexico) during suppression operations. This involved logging equipment used in the cutting, skidding, processing and decking of material that generated large amounts of activity fuel (slash) piled at multiple points along the contingency line.
incidents.quote: Calf Canyon Fire employed two Air Curtain Burners (ACB) on Division Sierra as a trial to test the effectiveness and efficiency of slash disposal with this relatively new tool for repair work.

incidents.name: Williams Lake Fire Engine Burnover
incidents.summary: A brush fire was reported in Spokane County, Washington. Units from several surrounding Fire Districts including the Cheney Fire Department’s Brush Truck CB1, were dispatched to the Williams Lake Fire for a “two-acre brush fire.” While trying to access the heel of the fire, CB1 realized they actually were on a road nearer to the head of the fire. While trying to return to the road junction behind them, the vehicle entered timbered area where smoke heavily impacted the road. CB1 became stuck when it left the road surface and struck a tree. The occupants of CB1 abandoned the stuck vehicle and safely retreated to a safety zone. The vehicle was destroyed but none of the firefighters were injured.
incidents.quote: "There was a challenge getting good info out and there was a lack of radio etiquette. You want to be respectful, but it is frustrating when the radio is bogged down. The first thing that fails on fire is communication.”

incidents.name: Vantage Highway Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Initial and extended attack was rapidly engaged, however the terrain, wind, and difficult access made for limited success. A sudden wind change rapidly increased the fire behavior and direction of spread. During the crew’s suppression actions, a firefighter sustained knee/ankle injuries, 2nd degree burns, and multiple small lacerations.
incidents.quote: New relationships take time to gel and work out efficient communication patterns.

incidents.name: Moose Fire Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: On August 4 at 7:23 a.m., a water tender rollover was reported on the Moose Fire, Salmon-Challis National Forest, Idaho. The reporting party provided the rollover site’s coordinates and requested medical response. An ambulance was dispatched to the scene.
incidents.quote: A water tender driver on the Moose Fire was driving slowly uphill when he was “blinded” by the sun—and drove off the road’s right side.

incidents.name: Windigo Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Windigo Fire, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon received treatment and was released the following morning. Patient received initial treatment by IHC medical personnel, then transported via agency vehicle to ALS ambulance, then to the hospital.
incidents.quote: A firefighter sustained a chainsaw cut to the shin/calf while swamping.

incidents.name: Yeti Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: An hand crew member assigned to the Yeti Fire, Klamath National Forest, California, was struck by the top of a tree while assisting a faller. The individual was serving as the swamper, and the top of the tree broke off and impacted the individual’s hip. The crewmember was evaluated by line medics and cleared; however the patient later sought medical attention for secondary infection associated by the splinters. The patient was referred to a medical center for a tertiary evaluation, and was released to full duty.
incidents.quote: A hand crew member was struck by the top of a tree while assisting a faller.

incidents.name: Beech Creek Fire Hit by Log
incidents.summary: A firefighter was struck by a log/stump and sustained a hip injury while assigned to the Beech Creek Fire, Oregon. Patient was transported to the hospital for further evaluation/care.
incidents.quote: Beech Creek Fire Hit by Log

incidents.name: Calf Canyon Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: The driver was transported to the hospital via ambulance and remained overnight for observation (released the following morning). Reported injuries include clavicle fracture, bruising of the arm, chest and shoulder, and bruising to the left side of head.
incidents.quote: A cache driver crashed a delivery truck after driving into a rainstorm returning from delivering and picking up supplie on the Calf Canyon Fire.

incidents.name: Six Rivers Lightning Complex Crew Transport Burn Damage
incidents.summary: At approximately 1800 on August 6, resources engaged on the Waterman Fire, Six Rivers National Forest, California, reported a high intensity uphill run that resulted in the total destruction of 2 crew carriers parked on a road. Resources were not with the crew carriers at the time and there were no injuries.
incidents.quote: I heard a radio transmission where someone said, "there’s fire in the buggies".

incidents.name: Windigo Fire Medical
incidents.summary: An individual assigned to the Windigo Fire, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, reported difficulty breathing and was transported via ground ambulance initially, then transferred to air transport due to long transport times. Patient was diagnosed with rhabdo and COVID, treated then released.
incidents.quote: An individual assigned to the Windigo Fire was diagnosed with rhabdo and COVID.

incidents.name: Big Swamp Fire Hit by Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: On August 10, 2022, Craig Interagency Hotshot crew was involved in suppression operations on the Big Swamp Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon, when a crewmember, Collin Hagen, was struck by a tree. Fellow crewmembers provided immediate medical care on scene until additional resources arrived to assist with medical efforts and patient extrication. Concurrent to providing medical attention, a helicopter was dispatched to begin short haul operations. Upon helicopter arrival, Hagen was short hauled from the area. He was pronounced deceased while enroute to the hospital in an air ambulance.
incidents.quote: The whooshing sounds of falling trees and cracking branches filled the air. The ground shook. As the dust settled, IHC crewmembers immediately began shouting to one another to account for everyone's safety.

incidents.name: Murphy Peak Fire Smokejumping Accident
incidents.summary: The patient was transported to a hospital using a BIA exclusive-use Type 3 helicopter. Surgery was performed on 8/14/22, with anticipated release from the hospital on 8/15/22.
incidents.quote: A smokejumper sustained a break to the end of the ulna bone in the arm during a jump operation on the Murphy Peak Fire, Flathead Indian Reservation, Montana, when the individual’s arm impacted with a tree.

incidents.name: Cedar Creek Fire Impalement Injury
incidents.summary: An engine was driving on a road on the Cedar Creek Fire in Oregon. The passenger side window was rolled down and the passenger had their arm resting on the door frame. Suddenly the passenger's arm was impaled by a tree limb.
incidents.quote: He did his best to communicate their medical situation while, internally, he was struggling.

incidents.name: Bull Complex Leg Fracture
incidents.summary: The patient was transported to a hospital for treatment and released back to their home unit.
incidents.quote: On the Bull Complex on the Mount Hood National Forest, Oregon, a firefighter sustained a leg fracture during firefighting operations.

incidents.name: Lassen National Forest Hazard Tree Removal Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A sawyer sustained a cut to the left arm via chainsaw during tree felling operations on the Lassen National Forest, California. Patient was transported to a local hospital via agency vehicle for treatment of the laceration.
incidents.quote: A Lassen National Forest firefighter received a laceration from a chainsaw while felling a Hazard Tree.

incidents.name: Angeles National Forest Engine Bay Departure Incident
incidents.summary: During morning maintenance checks, an engine on the Angeles National Forest, California, the engine was driven out of the engine bay with a compartment door open. The compartment door and engine bay door rail were damaged.
incidents.quote: I immediately stopped the engine, looked in both mirrors, and saw that one of the passenger compartment doors was on the ground

incidents.name: Post Office Fire Smokejumping Accident
incidents.summary: The jumper was extracted from the incident and evaluated at the local hospital, where the injury was diagnosed as bruising and a small fracture to the wrist.
incidents.quote: A smokejumper sustained an injury during a hard landing responding to initial attack the Post Office Fire, Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest, Idaho.

incidents.name: Four Corners Driver Fatality
incidents.summary: At approximately 1820 on August 24, an excavator with a masticator head assigned to the Four Corners Fire, Payette National Forest, Idaho, experienced the collapse of the roadway’s downhill shoulder and rotated halfway over onto the steep downhill slope.
incidents.quote: A masticator head on the Four Corners Fire rolled over after collapsing a soft road shoulder.

incidents.name: Hog Trough Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A hand crew member sustained a leg injury while performing hazard tree mitigation in front of the crew. A snag was felled and hung up in another tree; in the process of removing the hung-up tree, a piece of the trunk unexpectedly came loose and struck the sawyer in the lower leg.

incidents.name: Wallow Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A handcrew member assigned to the Wallow Fire, Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest, Idaho, was injured while operating a chainsaw during indirect line construction. The crewmember slipped on a cut bank and fell on the chainsaw, cutting an approximately 3” gash on the upper wrist. A crew EMTB provided initial treatment, then escorted the injured crew member to the hospital via agency helicopter. The crewmember had surgery to repair the damaged tendons then was released, expected to have a full recovery.
incidents.quote: "For something so wrong to happen, everything went so right. Right next to the helispot. Right next to the trucks."

incidents.name: Lightning Complex Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A crewmember assigned to the Lightning Complex, Six Rivers National Forest, California, sustained a head injury and was transported to a local hospital via agency vehicle. Initial reports was that the crewmember was struck by a tree limb. The crewmember was diagnosed with a minor concussion and was released from the hospital with doctor instructions to have a rest day before rejoining the crew.

incidents.name: Lightning Complex Fall/Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Crewmember was transported to UC Davis Burn Center, later released with family. Unsure final diagnosis/release conditions.
incidents.quote: A crewmember assigned to the Lightning Complex, Six Rivers National Forest, California, sustained burns to the right hand after the crewmember slipped and fell while hiking into the fire.

incidents.name: Four Corners Fire Driver Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter suffered a medical emergency driving from the Four Corners Incident, Idaho, and died.

incidents.name: Lightning Complex Fall
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember slid 20 feet into a tree and sustained injury to the back and leg while on assignment to the Lightning Complex, Six Rivers National Forest, California. The crewmember was able to walk back to the engine, was driven to ICP then transported to the hospital via ambulance for further care/evaluation. The crewmember was released later that evening.
incidents.quote: An engine crewmember slid 20 feet into a tree and sustained injury to the back and leg while on assignment to the Lightning Complex.

incidents.name: Double Creek Fire Civilian Extraction
incidents.summary: One person was flown out, one party was guided out a trail, one party conducted a burnout operation based on instruction by IMT members, and one party hiked to their rafts and rafted out of the fire area.
incidents.quote: Multiple groups of recreationists and hunters had to be evacuated from the Double Creek and Sturgil Fires (Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, Oregon) when fire behavior and fire size significantly increased.

incidents.name: Copper Point Fire Smokejumping Accident
incidents.summary: Initial reports indicated the jumper was experiencing severe back pain and hoist capable extraction was requested. An agency short haul ship was immediately dispatched to the incident. The patient was short hauled to FS guard station location, then transferred to a LifeFlight helicopter, which delivered them to the hospital. The jumper was diagnosed with mild T4 and T5 compression fractures and is expected to be released from the hospital with a brace on 9/5/22.
incidents.quote: A smokejumper was injured upon landing at the jump spot for the Copper Point Fire, Idaho Panhandle National Forest.

incidents.name: Wildhorse Fire Puncture Wound
incidents.summary: Due to the amount of bleeding, the employee was transported to a hospital via life flight. At last report, the employee was expected to be stabilized.
incidents.quote: A firefighter sustained a stab wound to the arm, near the wrist, via a sharpie-sized stick.

incidents.name: Hog Trough Fire Parking Break Failure
incidents.summary: While enroute to the Hog Trough Fire, Montana, an engine stopped at a gas station to fuel and clean the windows. The parking brake failed, which caused the engine to roll back into a curb and mailbox located approximately 35 feet behind the gas pump.
incidents.quote: An engine mobilizing to the Hog Trough Fire had the parking brake fail while stopped at a gas station.

incidents.name: Kalama Fire Helicopter Accident
incidents.summary: At approximately 1600 hours, an Exclusive-use Bell 205A1++ was filling its bucket at Merrill Lake for its fifth drop on the fuel cycle on the Kalama Fire, Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Washington. While the bucket filled, the helicopter lost power and began to descend. The pilot maneuvered the falling helicopter towards the shore of the lake, where it impacted the water surface and rolled onto its right side. The pilot was able to evacuate the aircraft.
incidents.quote: He performed four uneventful water dip and drop runs.

incidents.name: Williams Creek Fire ATV Burnover
incidents.summary: A point protection strategy has been implemented on the Williams Creek Fire to protect the community of Orogrande and other values at risk. As the fire nears Orogrande, a firefighter is assisting the division supervisor by assessing helicopter bucket drops and tracking fire progression towards a trigger point. Once the trigger point is reached, the firefighter assists evacuations and prepares to depart when their ATV becomes trapped by falling trees. The firefighter escapes on foot to a pickup truck of another firefighter. The ATV is destroyed.
incidents.quote: “I heard ‘TREES!’, then radio silence… I feared the worst”

incidents.name: Kootenai River Complex Yurt Fire
incidents.summary: At approximately 0330 local time, one of nine yurts being used on the Kootenai River Complex, Idaho Panhandle National Forest, was set on fire by a suspected arsonist. Two individuals were asleep in the opposite end of the yurt. One woke up and was able to get the other out of the yurt.
incidents.quote: IMT Members Wake Up in a Burning Yurt

incidents.name: Moose Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: While traveling through the Moose Fire area from a different local fire, a Forest Service employee pulled over to the side of the road to use his mobile phone. Before coming to a complete stop, the driver reached for the phone, and the vehicle tires contacted the soft shoulder, making it collapse and cause the vehicle to roll off the road and down the hillside. The driver was not seriously injured.
incidents.quote: "I looked down to check the map on my phone to make sure I was traveling the right direction. I slowed and pulled to the right and the embankment gave out."

incidents.name: Kalama Fire Firefighter Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A firefighter was struck on the head and shoulders from a green tree falling while assigned to the Kalama Fire, Gifford-Pinchot National Forest, Washington. The firefighter maintained consciousness and was alert and verbal on scene. Transported to medical facility for evaluation, treated and released.

incidents.name: Cedar Creek Fire East Zone Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A member of a hand crew falling team was struck on the head and shoulders by a falling tree during falling operations on the Cedar Creek Fire, Oregon. The firefighter was extracted from the injury site by a Rapid Extraction Module Support unit (REMS), then transported by ambulance to the hospital.
incidents.quote: A hung-up tree is most often a sign of a high complexity cutting operation.

incidents.name: Moose Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: On September 16 at 1015 on the Moose Fire, Salmon-Challis National Forest, Idaho, an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) crewmember sustained a chainsaw cut to the left leg. The swamper sustained a four-inch laceration which took 10 staples to close. The firefighter was released later that evening to light duty.
incidents.quote: While swamping for their sawyer, the chainsaw kicked back, striking and cutting into the swamper’s chaps.

incidents.name: Cedar Creek Fire East Zone Div J Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Two brothers on the same crew were engaged in a falling operation on the Cedar Creek Fire, Oregon. The younger brother walked up and placed an undercut in an 8-inch diameter lodgepole pine that was 25 feet in height. Just as he finished his back cut, he was surprised as the tree began to sit back and fall 180 degrees in the opposite direction from where he had intended it to go. His older brother was bucking a log a short distance away—in the direct path of the falling tree that was now heading directly for him. The tree struck the sawyer's brother, who was taken to medical care with a concussion.
incidents.quote: "I didn’t really think there was much to be concerned about as we were only falling smaller sized trees.”

incidents.name: Moose Fire Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: During the early morning hours of Tuesday, Sept. 20, 2022, while assigned to the Moose Fire on the Salmon-Challis National Forest, Idaho, Crew Boss Gerardo Rincon suffered a medical emergency and passed away.
incidents.quote: Moose Fire Medical Emergency Fatality

incidents.name: Mosquito Fire Chainsaw Dogs Injury
incidents.summary: A hand crew member sustained a stab/cut injury to the forearm from a chainsaw while assigned to the Mosquito Fire, Tahoe National Forest, California.
