While carrying a chainsaw on the shoulder while walking down a steep drainage, the crew member lost footing and fell. The chainsaw’s dogs cut into the individual’s forearm. The crew member was able to hike to a drop point to be assessed by line medics, then transported via agency vehicle to a hospital. The patient received stitches at the hospital and was released to light duty for three days.

incidents.name: Anderson Butte Fire Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: Attempting to locate the reported Anderson Butte Fire, three Type 6 engines were traveling along a well-maintained gravel road, into the sun. An engine in the convoy temporarily lost sight of the road by hanging dust and severe sunlight glare, and drove off the outside shoulder of the road on a curve. The engine tipped and rolled more two complete times. The driver suffered minor injuries and was treated and released by an ambulance that arrived on site.
incidents.quote: He said the visibility had become greatly reduced to the point where seeing the road was difficult. He was relying on the emergency lightbar of the engines ahead of him to find his way.

incidents.name: Bovee Fire Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On Sunday, Oct. 2, 2022, while fighting the Bovee Wildfire near Halsey, Nebraska, Assistant Chief Michael Moody suffered an apparent heart attack and passed away.

incidents.name: Mosquito Fire Stump Hole Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Line medics provided initial care and determined the injury was a 1-2% second degree burn below the area behind the right knee. The crew member was transported via ambulance to a hospital for further evaluation and treatment and was released later that day.
incidents.quote: On the Mosquito Fire on the Tahoe National Forest, California, a firefighter sustained a burn injury to the leg after stepping into a stump hole while performing mop-up operations.

incidents.name: Placerville Incident Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: On Sunday, October 9, 2022, at approximately 6:30 PM, in Placerville, California, a Fire Captain and Firefighter I were performing minor repairs to an Emergency Crew Transport (ECT) when a fire started in one of the compartments on the vehicle. While attempting to extinguish the fire with portable fire extinguishers, the fire grew rapidly causing 2nd and 3rd degree burns to the upper body of the Fire Captain and Firefighter I. Both were transported to UC Davis Burn Center and remain hospitalized.
incidents.quote: A Fire Captain and Firefighter I were performing minor repairs to an Emergency Crew Transport (ECT) when a fire started in one of the compartments on the vehicle.

incidents.name: Uncle Morris Prescribed Fire Fall/Burn Injury
incidents.summary: The crew member was hiking through the black at the end of the shift when the individual slipped and fell. The right hand/arm above the glove contacted a small ash pit, causing burns to the wrist/forearm.
incidents.quote: A hand crew member sustained a second-degree burn injury to the arm while on the Uncle Morris Prescribed Fire, Clearwater National Forest, Idaho.

incidents.name: Timber Mountain Rx Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: On the Timber Mountain Prescribed Fire on the Colville National Forest in Washington, a firefighter stepped into a stump hole ash pit and received 1st and 2nd degree burns to the calf area. The individual was transported to a nearby medical center and received treatment. A burn center was not determined to be necessary. An updated report two days later, stated: “superficial burns, salve and dressing change daily.”
incidents.quote: A firefighter stepped into a stump hole ash pit and received 1st and 2nd degree burns to the calf area.

incidents.name: Goat Rocks Fire Firefighter Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: . The individual remained alert and verbal, and was able to walk out without assistance. The individual was transported to a medical facility, where an evaluation indicated no broken bones or serious injury. The individual was treated and released.
incidents.quote: A crewmember was struck by a limb while assigned to the Goat Rocks Fire, Gifford-Pinchot National Forest, Washington

incidents.name: Idaho Falls District Fuels Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter was conducting fuels project work and returning to the office when he felt symptoms of a heart attack, called 911, and was transported via ambulance to the hospital where he later succumbed to his condition.
incidents.quote: Idaho Falls District Fuels Fatality

incidents.name: Mosquito Fire Feller Buncher Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A feller buncher operator burned two knuckles when trying to bead a tire: first degree burn to one knuckle and potentially second degree burn to another. The individual was transported via ground ambulance to a burn center for evaluation and treatment.
incidents.quote: A feller buncher operator burned two knuckles when trying to bead a tire.

incidents.name: Mark Twain National Forest Low Clearance Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On October 24 at 1535, a U.S. Forest Service dozer/roll back transport package was responding to a resource order request for fire suppression assistance on private land in Missouri. While driving on a state highway the operator approached a railroad trestle underpass. The driver slowed the speed of the transport due to concerns that the clearance appeared low. As the driver approached at a low speed to test the clearance height, the Roll Over Protection System (ROPS) of the dozer came into contact with trestle. No significant damage was detected.
incidents.quote: Always be aware of low clearance passage on transportation routes.

incidents.name: Mosquito Fire Spike Camp Finger DeGloving
incidents.summary: While breaking down a spike camp at the Mosquito Fire, Tahoe National Forest, California, a contractor was securing a supply load in a truck, lost balance, and fell. In the process of going to the ground, the ring got caught on a piece of metal tubing, which cause the finger to be degloved. Medics and an incident ambulance provided initial care and transported to the local hospital.
incidents.quote: Mosquito Fire Spike Camp Finger DeGloving

incidents.name: Flat Creek Fire Heavy Equipment
incidents.summary: This Safenet describes three separate incidents involving the same John Deer K550 dozer during the same initial attack efforts: a hydraulic line broke, low coolant alarms went off, then in the third incident, the alarms went off indicating low fuel pressure and the machine went into “limp mode.” All three incidents occurred while the dozer was actively engaged in initial attack suppression activities on the Flat Creek Fire, Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, Georgia. The first two incidents were able to be handled via in the field replacements/corrective actions; the third required a repair technician to be able to track the machine out and load onto the transport.
incidents.quote: A Flat Creek Fire dozer broke down 3 separate times durung initial attack.

incidents.name: Cherokee NF Prescribed Fire Insect Sting
incidents.summary: The crew EMTs began treatment, including administration of the individual’s epi-pen and oxygen while requesting both ground and air transport to a higher level of medical care. The air transport was not filled, as the ceiling was too low, so the crew packed the crew member out to an agency vehicle and met an ambulance on the highway. The ambulance transported to a hospital, where the crew member was treated and released within about 2 hours. The crew superintendent worked with the local unit for any CISM needs and the crew member returned to work the same day.
incidents.quote: A hand crew member working on containment line preparation for a prescribed burn on the Cherokee National Forest in Tennessee was stung in the face resulting anaphylactic shock and loss of consciousness.

incidents.name: Hoosier National Forest Prescribed Fire UTV Accident
incidents.summary: The UTV was going thru a tight spot between some trees and the individual’s boot was just off the edge of the UTV floor. During the maneuvering, the boot caught; twisting the leg backwards and pinching it between the UTV seat and the tree.

incidents.name: Shanty Pond Prescribed Fire Vehicle Accidents
incidents.summary: Private vehicles were involved in accidents on Florida's Highway 314 due to limited visibility in the morning following prescribed fire operations in the vicinity the preceding two days. Although there were several accidents and there was damage to vehicles, no airbags deployed and there were no reported injuries. Due to visibility concerns, Highway 314 was closed that morning. In addition, a public-facing news flash was sent out by the media for Marion County residents.
incidents.quote: Due to limited visibility, at approximately 0744 that day, four vehicles (one towing a boat), were involved in a “pile-up” collision.

incidents.name: Dudda Shop Prescribed Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: However, the machine would not start. Realizing they needed to abandon the machine, both individuals jumped out the passenger’s side because fire was encroaching on the driver’s side. The UTV operator grabbed a handheld radio and the fire extinguisher that was mounted above the passenger side seat. The fire extinguisher let off “one quick burst” directed under the UTV but it did not fully discharge its contents. The firefighters abandoned the vehicle and ran to safety.
incidents.quote: When the UTV operator tried to back up, the vehicle stalled. Knowing there was active fire located directly behind them, he tried to restart the UTV to get away from the growing flames.

incidents.name: National Forests of Mississippi Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.fire: National Forests of Mississippi Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: A crewmember received a minor burn to the lower leg while performing prescribed burning ignition operations on a unit on the National Forests of Mississippi. The firefighter was able to free themselves, and began “patting” out the fire, without success. There was a standing pool of water next to them, and they were able to submerge their leg and douse the flames.
incidents.quote: While firefighter was working their way out of the bush their drip torch fuel landed on the outside of their leg

incidents.name: Wolf Creek Rx Burn Injury
incidents.summary: As a firefighter was working uphill on a prescribed fire, two lines of fire came together. The change in slope and terrain and increased fire behavior all aligned quickly where the firefighter was standing adjacent to the fireline. The light flashy fuels ignited quickly and the firefighter inhaled hot gasses. The firefighter instantly had a sore throat but did not realize they had a burn injury until two days later.
incidents.quote: "It felt like breathing heat"

incidents.name: Apalachicola National Forest Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember was burning out around an aviary when the employee became entangled in a briar bush long enough to receive a burn to the leg from the drip torch spilling onto their pants.

incidents.name: Oconee Ranger District UTV Tree Strike
incidents.summary: A FFT2 had been sitting in the driver side rear UTV seat with his seat belt on. Two firefighters shouted at him to “Run!” He was able to quickly unbuckle and exit the vehicle just before the tree trunk struck the UTV’s roof. Because the tree was laying on the powerlines, personnel maintained their distance from the UTV until utility workers arrived on scene.
incidents.quote: While attempting to flag a cat-faced hazard tree during prescribed fire operations, the tree came down and struck a UTV and nearby powerline.

incidents.name: Compartment 68 Rx UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: The passenger grabbed the rollover protection system (ROPS) above his head with his right hand and the driver’s arm with his left hand. The driver grabbed the steering wheel with his left hand and the passenger’s shirt with his right hand. The UTV came to a rest on its right side. Both the driver and the passenger had their seatbelts and their Department of Transportation (DOT) helmets on keeping them in their seats and heads protected as the machine tipped over and came to a stop.
incidents.quote: The back right passenger tire sunk into a rut and the front of the machine raised up. When the machine leaned back, the straps holding the water tank into the bed of the UTV broke. The UTV tipped over to the right.

incidents.name: Pebble Volunteer Fire Department Vehicle Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On Sunday, Feb. 19, 2023, Chief Steven Michael Smith was killed in a single vehicle accident while responding to an incident on his personal motorcycle to a woods fire with a potential residential structure involved.

incidents.name: Paw Paw VFD Powerline Incident Fatality
incidents.summary: While operating with crews at the scene of trees on fire and wires down due to an ice storm, a tree broke in the vicinity of the incident and caused a power line to collapse and strike Lieutenant Quillen.

incidents.name: RED HOUSE RX ATV BURN DAMAGE
incidents.summary: A lead igniter on a Honda ATV with a rear-mounted electronic torch, stalled out on rocks in tall grass leaving little time for the ATV operator to move the vehicle before it was impacted by the strip fire they had just lit.

incidents.name: BIA Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: Two firefighters departed their home unit enroute to Engine Operator training. While driving the Type 6 wildland fire engine was hit by high winds and veered into the oncoming lane of traffic. The driver was able to quickly return the engine to the correct lane of the highway, though the momentum of the engine caused the vehicle to “fish tail” and again entered the oncoming lane. The engine struck the guard rail on the opposite side of travel, spun counterclockwise and exited the highway, landing in a sandy area adjacent to a cement culvert.
incidents.quote: High winds impacted the Type 6 engine causing it to veer into the oncoming lane of traffic.

incidents.name: Blaylock Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: While walking through thick vegetation on a prescribed fire, the crewmember became stuck, and dripped drip torch fuel to the back of the lower leg.

incidents.name: Virginia Department of Forestry ATV Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: Forest Technician Rocky S. Wood was scouting a 15-acre wildfire in Buchanan County to determine where to create a containment line around the perimeter of the fire when the ATV he was driving overturned and he was killed.

incidents.name: Tonto NF Vehicle Collision with Elk
incidents.summary: A single driver was traveling at 55 mph on Arizona Highway 60, a two-way, single-lane county highway when an elk suddenly charged toward the vehicle from the trees. The driver pressed the brakes to minimize the impact, avoid any other collisions with oncoming traffic, and maintain control enough to stay on the highway. The elk crashed into the vehicle’s passenger side.

incidents.name: Harvey Prescribed Fire/ Rx Drip Torch Burn Injury
incidents.summary: During prescribed fire operations an out of region firefighter from California received a burn injury while using a drip torch in heavy “briar.” The torch was not lit but fuel spilled on the firefighter's pants as he fought to get out of a briar patch. The fuel then ignited, and the firefighter sustained a burn injury.
incidents.quote: The firefighter did a drop and roll, but when he hit the ground, the leaf litter ignited from the fire on his pants—adding significant heat to his burning pants and leg.

incidents.name: Texas AM Forest Service Prescribed Fire Pipeline Rupture
incidents.summary: On March 20, 2023, personnel from the Livingston office with the Texas A&M Forest Service were preparing to conduct a prescribed burn. While refreshing fire breaks along the edge of a pipeline right-of-way, a dozer operator noticed a hole in the ground. After brief observation, it was determined the hole was caused by a ruptured underground pipeline. The personnel cleared the scene and contacted pipeline officials. The issue was resolved without incident.
incidents.quote: “It wouldn’t be a bad idea to come check pipelines before burns or even prep work. Take a lap with the UTV.”

incidents.name: Moody Forest Natural Area Prescribed Fire/Rx Unexplode Ordinance/UXO
incidents.fire: Moody Forest Natural Area Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: Around a deer stand, I used my Rhino tool to pull some fuel away from the legs of the ladder. As I did so, a bullet “cooked off”—exploded.
incidents.quote: Close Call with an Exploding Bullet on a Prescribed Fire

incidents.name: Waynoka Fire Department Entrapment
incidents.summary: During initial attack a Waynoka Fire Department engine became stuck. Two firefighters were forced to use an escape route. The fire burned intensely causing burns to one firefighter and smoke inhalation to the other.

incidents.name: West Virginia Division of Forestry Hit by Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: On Thursday, April 13, 2023, Service Forester Cody J. Mullens was fighting a fire in Fayette County. While at the scene, a tree fell on him, killing him instantly.

incidents.name: Frederick County Fire and Rescue Department Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: Multiple fire and rescue stations from Frederick County, VA and Hampshire County, WV responded to a wildland fire in Frederick County. The wildland fire burned several acres of brush and woods with total incident duration lasting approximately seven hours. Deputy Chief Chester Taylor Lauck was the operator of the UTV and performed firefighting operations, to include extinguishment with a hose line and applying a fire line.
incidents.quote: Approximately two hours after arriving home, Deputy Chief Lauck began to feel ill and 9-1-1 was immediately called.

incidents.name: Siskiyou Rappeler Physical Fitness Medical
incidents.summary: The employee felt poorly with leg cramps during the work shift but not severely unwell. During the evening, the employee’s partner provided transportation to Providence Medical Center in Medford, OR, where the employee was admitted. The employee was released 4 days later.
incidents.quote: An employee of the Siskiyou Rappel Crew was diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis following routine physical fitness.

incidents.name: Nigh Creek Prescribed Fire UAS Flyaway
incidents.summary: When the flyaway occurred on this prescribed fire, an Incident Within an Incident (IWI) was declared. Ignition operations were ceased and transitioned to holding operations as a plan was formulated to try to recover the UAS.
incidents.quote: While igniting the Nigh Creek burn unit on the Superior National Forest (Minnesota), the unmanned aircraft system (UAS) (drone) that was being used as the primary ignition tool lost contact between the GPS and flight controller and a UAS “flyaway” occurred.

incidents.name: Las Tusas Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: During initial attack of the Las Tusas fire in New Mexico in May 2023, a Forest Service engine crewmember received second degree radiant heat burns to the hand and ear. The engine also sustained exterior damage.
incidents.quote: The DIVS asked FFT2 about what happened the day before and learned that her ear “got hot”. The DIVS looked at her ear and saw a blister approximately 1.5 inches long.

incidents.name: San Bernardino National Forest Physical Training Medical
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember participating in a physical training/hose-lay exercise passed out. The firefighter was treated on scene, and transport via ambulance was recommended. The employee was later transported to the hospital by supervisor, where the individual was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis and admitted to the hospital for several days.

incidents.name: Weber Basin Job Corps Center Shelter in Place Event
incidents.summary: During a shelter in place incident at a Job Corps center in Utah, an armed assailant standoff near the center prompted key staff members to successfully implement emergency response measures. However, differing interpretations of the threat led to friction among employees, particularly regarding the directive for a “soft lockdown.” Some employees felt their workday was disrupted, while others adapted by leaving the center, emphasizing the need for clear communication and a defined chain of command in such crises.
incidents.quote: Are we adequately equipped to handle an extended shelter in place scenario at our center?

incidents.name: Magnetic Safety Light
incidents.summary: A hand crew on assignment to the Cibola National Forest, New Mexico, in May 2023, shares the utility of magnetic light that can be used detached in the hand or attached to vehicles such as a UTV for visibility and signaling.
incidents.quote: A light or strobe to serve as a constant identifier 360 degrees, or at least front and back, would be ideal during nighttime operations.

incidents.name: Stanislaus National Forest Large-Scale Prescribed Fire Case Study
incidents.summary: This document highlights the challenges that the Stanislaus NF faced in trying to mobilize for prescribed fire in a way that is commensurate with wildfire.
incidents.quote: "You’ve got to break the system to make the system."

incidents.name: Red Mountain Fire Medical
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember suffered a heat related injury (dehydration and extreme cramping) while assigned to the Red Mountain Fire in Arizona. Local law enforcement (Maricopa County Sheriff’s Department) provided on-scene medical support. The firefighter was transported via ambulance to the hospital. The firefighter was treated and released on the same day.

incidents.name: Georgia Forestry Commission Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On Monday, June 5, 2023, Wildland Firefighter Shaun Luke Daniel, while on-duty at a contained wildfire in Washington County, Georgia, was walking a firebreak and suddenly collapsed. Fellow emergency responders provided CPR on-scene and he was immediately transported to a local hospital where he was pronounced deceased from an apparent heart attack

incidents.name: Lolo National Forest Proficiency Jump Smokejumping Accident
incidents.summary: On a training jump, a jumper’s parachute landed in a tree, breaking the top of the tree and the jumper fell approximately 15-20 feet to the ground.
incidents.quote: Jumper was diagnosed with several pelvic injuries after hitting and falling from tree.

incidents.name: Ottawa National Forest Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: A Bureau of Land Management (BLM) engine crew in a chase truck was involved in a roll-over while on the Ottawa National Forest in Michigan. An on-scene EMT assessed both occupants, and both were transported to the hospital. One firefighter was treated and released with minor scratches and bruises, and the other was admitted with a broken rib, and a slight punctured lung.

incidents.name: Wallowa-Whitman National Forest Dual Wheels Engine Incident
incidents.summary: A Type 6 engine was driving outside of Stanfield, Oregon, on the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, when they “felt a shimmy” in the engine. Suddenly, the rear driver-side wheels (“dualies”) were rolling down the highway next to the engine. No injuries reported. Additional analysis of this incident is ongoing.

incidents.name: Wilbur Fire Firefighter Fall
incidents.summary: Firefighter was patrolling the fireline on the Wilbur Fire (Arizona) when they stepped up on an unstable rock, and lost footing. Patient described rolling the right ankle and hearing a "pop".

incidents.name: Southfork Prescribed Fire Medical
incidents.summary: While supporting holding operations on the Southfork Rx, Stanislaus National Forest in California, two 50’ x 50’ and multiple smaller spot fires ignited. An on-scene/assigned ambulance provided initial response and transport to the hospital. The firefighter remained in the hospital and was released 3 days later.
incidents.quote: Firefighters responded in heavy smoke with line construction and hose lays, and one firefighter suffered from smoke inhalation/carbon monoxide poisoning.

incidents.name: Thomas Mountain Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember was on the southern edge of the prescribed fire unit during the firing phase when a flare up occurred. As the crewmember was moving out of the flare up area, he raised his arm to block the heat and his elbow sustained a burn injury. The crewmember was initially treated by a local ambulance. The recommendation was made for the crewmember to go to a burn center due to location of burn on the elbow. The crewmember was transported to Arrowhead Regional Hospital in San Bernardino, California with an Agency vehicle.

incidents.name: Wildcat Fire Medical
incidents.summary: A crewmember experienced a heat exhaustion/dehydration. The firefighter was ground-transported with an assigned ambulance. The firefighter received treatment for dehydration and was released on 6/17. Several days of light duty were expected before return to normal duties.

incidents.name: Bitterroot National Forest Firefighter Medical
incidents.summary: A firefighter in the backcountry of the Bitterroot National Forest, Montana, was showing signs of dehydration and hyperthermia. The firefighter was evacuated via life flight helicopter and treated in Missoula.

incidents.name: Superior National Forest Prescribed Fire Fall 2023
incidents.summary: An employee who was out looking at a prescribed fire on the Superior National Forest, Minnesota, slipped and fell and dislocated their elbow

incidents.name: Unit S04 Prescribed Fire Medical
incidents.summary: A firefighter was treated for smoke inhalation and carbon monoxide poisoning while on a prescribed fire on the Stanislaus National Forest, California. Initially, based on the difficulty the firefighter was having breathing, the incident was classified as a “red” incident. Once the firefighter received oxygen, symptoms improved quickly. The on-scene/assigned ambulance transported the firefighter to the hospital where the firefighter was treated and released.

incidents.name: Hamilton Airport Helitack Rescue Medical
incidents.summary: Forest Service Helitack witnessed a fatal plane carsh and pulled the pilot out of the wrecked aircraft. This resulted in inhalation of smoke from the burning aircraft.

incidents.name: Rolling Pin Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Rolling Pin Fire, Nolan County Texas — The Roscoe Volunteer Fire Department's heavy brush truck was severely damaged by fire. The heavy brush truck got stuck in sand with 2 firefighters on it. The fire burned over the truck. The two firefighters abandoned the truck and declared a mayday requesting help. They made it safely back to a road.

incidents.name: Pole Mountain Prescribed Fire UXO Incident
incidents.summary: The Pole Mountain Prescribed Fire on the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest in Wyoming was conducted on land that had been a US Army mortar range, and unexploded ordinance (UXO) was a known hazard. Three individuals from an engine module were assigned to holding on the unit when one firefighter discovered as unexploded mortar shell in the black. The explosive was replaced as it was found and authorities were contacted.
incidents.quote: After lifting the object about six inches off the ground, the fins of the UXO pulled out of the ground. At that time, we both realized what this object actually was.

incidents.name: Marble Fire Heat Related Injury Medevac
incidents.summary: A USFS smokejumper suffered extreme dehydration and heat exhaustion while hiking out of a remote wildfire. A challenging overnight search and rescue operation culminated in a successful hoist medevac by the California Highway Patrol.
incidents.quote: “My mouth was so dry, I couldn’t swallow without dry heaving and my legs were cramping up. When I saw that snowbank, I clawed at it for a minute with my fingers before finally scraping some ice off with my teeth. I kept thinking I would be okay if I could just make it to the creek…”

incidents.name: Savage Mountain Fire Fall
incidents.summary: A member of an initial attack module was building direct fireline when the firefighter’s leg got stuck between two logs. The firefighter fell with full body weight on the stuck leg, and this fall forced the knee to bend awkwardly. An EMT assisted in treating, evaluating, and transporting the patient to the medivac site, and accompanied the injured firefighter to the hospital.

incidents.name: Fort Huachuca Air Tanker Base Insect Sting
incidents.summary: An employee was stung by a bee and based on vitals and patient history, the decision was made to transport the employee to the local hospital.

incidents.name: Russell Gulch Fire Medical
incidents.summary: A crewmember on a Type 4 Engine was building handline on the Russell Gulch Fire, Tonto National Forest, Arizona, when HRI was detected. After 10-15 minutes of IV treatment, the crewmember’s condition improved. The crewmember was transported to the local hospital in Globe, AZ, where bloodwork was completed and reviewed. Crewmember was released within an hour and cleared for fully duty.
incidents.quote: The injury was described as a “green” medical, the patient was conscious and alert and the local FD administered an IV quickly.

incidents.name: Three Lakes Fire Blister Infection
incidents.summary: The origin of the infection was an initial small blister in the ankle area on his left foot. The receiving Doctor states: "It's infected, close to being serious, almost septic." The firefighter spent one week in the hospital.
incidents.quote: A wildland firefighter assigned to the Three Lakes Fire on the Kaibab National Forest, Arizona, was admitted to the hospital with a foot infection.

incidents.name: Devil's Butte Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: During initial attack at approximately 1200, fire pushed toward a heavy brush engine that was stuck in powdery soils forcing the operator and crew member to retreat uphill, through unburned fuels. Approximately two hours later the fire burned toward a grader and two engines constructing line in a wheat field. Once the grader encountered direct fire against the blade, the grader operator and both engine operators began to retreat to the north, away from the fire. The engine became inoperable, and the engine operator and crew member retreated to a nearby burned area on foot.
incidents.quote: Higher than normal fire intensity necessitates the need for firefighters to be very close to the black and maintain effective escape routes and safety zones.

incidents.name: Tonto National Forest Initial Attack Medical
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember was engaged in the second initial attack of the day on the Tonto National Forest, Arizona, when dehydration/heat injury was detected. Temperatures were at near-record highs during this fire activity. Firefighters provided on-scene first aid, and the injured firefighter was transported to the hospital, where IV therapy was administered, and a prescription for potassium was given. The firefighter was cleared to return to work.

incidents.name: Weigle Fire Chainsaw Puncture Injury
incidents.summary: While walking off the line down a steep ridge on the Weigle Fire, Coronado National Forest, Arizona, a sawyer on a hand crew was injured when they lost footing, and had their chainsaw come down on their forearm.

incidents.name: Haight Creek Fire Water Tender Accident
incidents.summary: When the water tender driver departed for ICP she noted the tender was full of water. The highway became winding and narrow the closer she got to the ICP. As she rounded a curve, there was an oncoming log truck that was partially over the centerline. She gently nudged the steering wheel to move the tender as close to the edge of the road as possible, but its dual back wheels caught soft dirt along the ditch line.
incidents.quote: The watertender fishtailed uncontrollably and then rolled one and a half times, coming to rest on the passenger side.

incidents.name: Chimney Fire Medical
incidents.summary: While engaged in direct attack, a crewmember displayed symptoms consistent with Heat Related Illness. The injured crewmember was placed in the shade, and given fluids that wouldn’t stay down. The crewmember was flown off the fire, transferred to an ambulance, and taken to the hospital.

incidents.name: Lolo National Forest Project Work Medical
incidents.summary: A crewmember displayed signs/symptoms (nausea, dizziness, vomiting) of heat-related injury (HRI) after a day operating a saw in hot temperatures on the Lolo National Forest, Montana. After evaluation by an EMT, the decision to transport the crewmember to the hospital was made. Crewmember was admitted to the hospital, released 7/22/23, and returned to full duty on 7/25/23.

incidents.name: Flat Fire Medical
incidents.summary: A short haul rescue was utilized on the Flat Fire due to the terrain. The injured individual was transferred to an ambulance.

incidents.name: Nez Perce-Clearwater Proficiency Jump Smokejumping Accident
incidents.summary: After evaluation by several agency medical personnel, the smokejumper was flown via agency-contracted helicopter to Idaho County Airport, and transferred to a commercial air ambulance for flight to Lewiston, Idaho. The smokejumper was treated at hospital ER and released. A full recovery is expected.
incidents.quote: The jumper landed in a tree at the edge of the jump spot on the Nez Perce National Forest. While performing let-down (rappel) procedures, the parachute slipped and the jumper fell to the ground.

incidents.name: Racetrack/Grapevine Fires IHC Medicals
incidents.summary: Three IHC crewmembers were taken to the hospital. Two were eventually diagnosed with Rhabdomyolysis and one with a fungal and staph infection.
incidents.quote: Some crewmembers admitted to not taking (powdered mix) packets from the crew supply because they didn’t want to be “that person” who takes too many or takes the last one.

incidents.name: Newell Rd Fire Medical
incidents.summary: The crewmember was evaluated by an assigned structure engine paramedic, and the decision to transport to ICP and then the local clinic was made. The firefighter was given fluids enroute to the clinic, and treated and released shortly after arrival.
incidents.quote: Handcrew member was showing symptoms of dehydration.

incidents.name: Blum Fire Transport Vehicle Burn Damage
incidents.summary: A transport unit caught fire while parked in the 'black' on the Blum Fire. The fire likely started in the engine compartment because the front passenger tire was parked on a small tree limb buried in a shallow mound of juniper needle duff.
incidents.quote: "I heard a pop and a hiss, and went over to check the transport."

incidents.name: Noonan Fire Power Line Incident
incidents.summary: A wildfire kicked off the evening of July 26, 2023, in Campbell County, Wyoming, near Williams Road and Story Ave, and a Forest Service Type 4 engine with two crew members headed out from the station within minutes. Their plan was to hit the most active edge first, working west to east along the south flank to tie the fire back into the road. While working the line in heavy smoke, the crew didn’t see some low‑hanging power lines, and the engine made contact—leading to an arc flash, a loud pop, and even a wire scraping across the top of the truck. Once they realized what happened, they drove forward to get the engine clear of the hazard before continuing suppression efforts.
incidents.quote: A�er the arc was no�ced and a loud pop was heard, the engine crew drove forward clearing the scene from wires, while doing so they heard a power line scraping the top of the engine.

incidents.name: York Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: One of the five passengers sustained a recordable injury. All were wearing seatbelts.
incidents.quote: While assigned to the York Fire in the Mojave National Preserve, California, a crew vehicle traveling on a dirt road struck a pile of gravel causing the vehicle to roll over. There were 5 people in the crew cab pickup truck. There was one worker who sustained a recordable injury. All passengers were wearing seatbelts.

incidents.name: Elkhorn Fire Large Fire Point Protection
incidents.summary: The Elkhorn Fire was detected on the evening of July 24, 2023 on the Payette National Forest, within the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness, in Idaho. On the afternoon of July 30, the Elkhorn Fire made a 20,000-acre, 9-mile run up the Salmon River Canyon, destroy 7 structures, and required firefighters to make quick decisions and take independent action to ensure not only their own safety but that of the public as well.

incidents.name: Little Mesa Fire UTV Fire
incidents.summary: During initial attack operations on the Little Mesa Fire in southwestern Colorado, a Type 4 engine crew experienced a mechanical issue on their 2017 Honda Pioneer 1000 – 5-Seater UTV which caused the UTV to catch fire. There were no injuries associated with this incident.
incidents.quote: The crew discovered that a 2.5-pound ABC fire extinguisher... was not enough to extinguish the fire, even though the UL rating exceeded the minimum requirements.

incidents.name: Tecuya Fire Hit by Water Helicopter Incident
incidents.summary: On August 2, 2023, crews and aviation resources responded with an aggressive initial response effort to the Tecuya Fire near Frazier Park, California. Several fixed-wing and rotor-wing resources were assigned, with an equally aggressive response from the ground. During this initial attack, a Type 1 helicopter water-dropped on eight hotshot crewmembers. Two crewmembers sustained injuries that required medical transport to a local hospital. Both were released with minor injuries—both were also diagnosed with having a concussion.
incidents.quote: As one injured crewmember stated, when this happened, he felt his knees buckle and fell to the ground. He remembers his helmet impacting the ground.

incidents.name: Texas Engine Rear Stabilizer Link
incidents.summary: Two Type 6 engines on a prescribed fire lost a critical nut connecting the rear stabilizer link. The issue was caught during post-shift checks, preventing a failure.
incidents.quote: Thorough preventative maintenance checks by the most junior member of the engine crew resulted in an immediate recognition that something looked wrong with the undercarriage.

incidents.name: Snow Hill Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Two swampers received burn injuries when fire behavior rapidly increased during an operator swap. They escaped down the plow line through 10-15 foot flame lengths.
incidents.quote: As the growing fire quickly moved toward the crew, they were forced to make hasty decisions in order to find safety. "We were looking at the fire behavior we had instead of what we could have had."

incidents.name: Initial Attack UTV Accident
incidents.summary: A BLM initial attack squad in the Southwest Colorado District was utilizing a 2015 Polaris Ranger 800 UTV to scout a reported smoke when the UTV tipped onto its side after making a sharp turn in the mud. While the operator was not injured, the two passengers sustained minor injuries and soreness.
incidents.quote: Upon reaching this flat ground, the operator made a quick left turn into a muddy area and the UTV tipped onto the passenger’s side.

incidents.name: Modoc National Forest Crew Carrier Rollover
incidents.summary: A veteran crew experienced a crew carrier rollover on the Modoc NF during a preposition assignment. One individual treated and released from the hospital for neck pain.

incidents.name: Rogue River - Siskiyou Vehicle Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: At approximately 1330 hours on August 4th, a Forest Service vehicle carrying three firefighters went off the road while driving to the Powers Ranger District with a destination of the Gold Beach Ranger District, both on the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, Oregon. Tragically, one of the occupants suffered fatal injuries during the incident. The other two firefighters were taken to the hospital; one received treatment for minor injuries, the other was evaluated out of an abundance of caution and both were released later that evening. Another firefighter, who arrived at the scene in a separate vehicle, was also taken to the hospital as a precautionary measure but was subsequently discharged.
incidents.quote: When a paramedic arrived on scene, he “saw what we all didn’t; Ben was already gone.” What had seemed like minutes to some, actually turned out to be closer to two hours.

incidents.name: Corduroy Fire Helicopter Accident
incidents.summary: An agency-contracted Type 1 Helicopter (CH-46E) experienced a mechanical failure and loss of power while performing bucket operations in support of the Corduroy Fire located on the Alpine Ranger District, Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, Arizona. The flight crew reacted by releasing the load of water, jettisoning the bucket, and performing a hard landing in a field. The helicopter rolled onto its side and subsequently was destroyed in a post-crash fire. The three crewmembers on board were able to walk away with minor bumps and bruises. All three were transported via ground to the hospital in Show Low, AZ. CT scans were performed on each crewmember, and all were cleared.
incidents.quote: After they had filled the bucket with water and began to climb, the crew heard an extremely loud horn in their helmets; loud enough that it was difficult to understand what was being said.

incidents.name: Broadway Fire Helicopter Accident
incidents.summary: On Sunday, August 6, 2023, two firefighting helicopters, a Sikorsky S-64E and a Bell 407, collided in Cabazon, California, while battling the Broadway Wildland Fire, a vegetation fire sparked by a nearby structure fire. While the Sikorsky S-64E helicopter was able to land safely, the Bell 407 crashed. All three occupants of this helicopter, Assistant Chief Josh Bischof, Captain Timothy “Tim” Rodriguez, and Contract Pilot Tony Sousa were killed. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash.
incidents.quote: After HLCO1 completed the left 360 degree turn, HLCO1 and HT1’s courses began to converge due to the terrain, hazards, and the location of a dip site HT1 was enroute to. These trajectories led to a mid-air collision.

incidents.name: Lost Horse Creek Fire Pump Accident Burn Injury
incidents.summary: On August 7, 2023 on the Lost Horse Creek Fire in Alaska, a wildland firefighter sustained a serious burn injury caused by overheated water erupting from a Mark-3 pump he was operating. The injured firefighter was transported by ambulance off the line to the local hospital’s Emergency Department for evaluation and treatment of his partial thickness burn and referred to another medical center for a follow up evaluation the following day.
incidents.quote: After opening the valve, the suction hose violently slipped out of the coupling, spraying scalding water and leaving the operator and another nearby firefighter scrambling to flee the immediate vicinity for safety.

incidents.name: Umpqua National Forest Project Work Fall
incidents.summary: While engaged in work at the Ranger Station compound on the Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, a firefighter fell off a ladder resulting in serious injuries. The firefighter was flown to the hospital, has been through surgeries, and is currently in ICU. A regional response team and a CARE team have been assembled to assist with the response to the incident.

incidents.name: Hayden Fire Vehicle Incident
incidents.summary: A 25-person hand crew assigned to the Hayden Fire, Salmon-Challis National Forest, Idaho, was traveling in a six-vehicle convoy. One fatigued driver veered his pickup to the right, driving partially off the embankment until the vehicle was stopped by a tree. Neither the driver nor passengers were injured.
incidents.quote: Then the driver started to nod off—and veered off the right shoulder of the road.

incidents.name: East Fork Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: An IHC support vehicle experienced a rollover on the East Fork Fire, Kootenai National Forest, Trego, Montana. No injuries were reported.

incidents.name: Six Rivers Lightning Complex and Happy Camp Complex Large Fire Strategy
incidents.summary: Over weeks and months, IMTs managed the Six Rivers Lightning Complex and Happy Camp Complex by implementing strategies determined by agency leadership, fire management staff, IMT staff, and local partners
incidents.quote: Begin with Trust: The First Step to Becoming a Genuinely Empowering Leader

incidents.name: Bedrock Fire UTV Accident
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew assigned to the Bedrock Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon, was driving a UTV and swerved to avoid a collision with wildlife. The UTV rolled, but the crewmember was seat-belted in the UTV and was wearing a UTV helmet. The crewmember was transported to the hospital, diagnosed with bruised ribs, and released on the same day (8/14/2023).

incidents.name: SKU August Lightning Complex Dozer Entrapment
incidents.summary: On August 15, 2023, a CAL FIRE bulldozer was entrapped while constructing direct fire line during initial attack on the Ranch Fire in Siskiyou County, California. At 2341 hours, outflow winds from a passing thunderstorm increased fire behavior, forcing the dozer to abandon line construction and retreat. The dozer was impacted by direct flames and extreme radiant heat while traveling down the line before becoming inoperable. The dozer operator deployed the fire curtains (protective barriers for heavy equipment similar to a fire shelter) within the cab and dressed them to the window frames during the entrapment. The operator was not injured.
incidents.quote: HFEO1 tried “at least a dozen” times to restart the bulldozer in an attempt to continue moving to the meadow, located 315 feet away. These attempts were unsuccessful due to the damage D1 sustained from direct flame impingement and extreme radiant heat.

incidents.name: Holiday Fire Burned Gear
incidents.summary: On August 15, 2023, a load of 10 smokejumpers were dispatched to the Holiday Fire on the Six Rivers National Forest in Northern California. After the jumpers were on the ground the fire activity significantly increased due to thunderstorms in the area. Based on current and expected fire activity, the jumpers made the decision to leave the jump spot and their gear and utilize their planned escape route. The end result was the loss of eight sets of jump gear and additional cargo.
incidents.quote: The decision was made and—without their gear—they proceeded down and out their escape route.

incidents.name: Lone Pine Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: During initial attack, two members of an engine crew were installing a hose lay when fire behavior rapidly increased. Their planned escape route into the cold black was less viable as the flank of the fire picked up—and escaping uphill would prove difficult. They were forced to move laterally, away from the left flank of the fire and into the green.
incidents.quote: FF-1 recalled, “We had two choices, drop packs and run for it—or deploy here.”

incidents.name: Ridge Fire Stick in Eye Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) took a stick to an eye. The crewmember was evaluated by a USFS EMT and taken by ambulance to the hospital. The crewmember was evaluated, treated, and released that night (8/16/2023) to several days of light duty.

incidents.name: Slide Fire Medical
incidents.summary: A member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) assigned to the Slide Fire, Mendocino National Forest, California, was hoisted from the fireline by a CAL FIRE hoist-capable helicopter and transported to the hospital in Chico, CA. The crewmember was diagnosed with heat exhaustion and released to three days of light duty on 8/16/2023.

incidents.name: Lone Pine Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Toward the end of the operational period, a crewmember from an Interagency Hotshot Crew was struck by a tree while working to suppress a spot fire on the Six Rivers Complex, on the Six Rivers National Forest in California. The firefighter was transported by a non-USFS helicopter to a hospital in Redding, CA. The firefighter suffered serious spinal injuries.
incidents.quote: He needed to begin moving toward definitive care due to the possibility of internal bleeding and a potential traumatic head injury. With the help of arriving crew members, they moved him away from the heat, using their hands to stabilize his cervical spine.

incidents.name: Lookout Fire Insect Sting
incidents.summary: A member of a hand crew was stung by a bee and experienced an allergic reaction while assigned to the Lookout Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon. USFS EMTs provided medical attention. The firefighter was transported to the hospital via ambulance, treated and released that night (8/17/2023) and returned to work the following day.

incidents.name: Bedrock Fire Thumb Crushed by Logs
incidents.summary: A member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) had a thumb crushed between two logs while assigned to the Bedrock Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon. USFS EMTs, along with a Rapid Extraction Module (REM) provided medical aid. The crewmember was taken to the hospital, evaluated (lacerations and a fracture) and released with a follow-up appointment scheduled.

incidents.name: Kanaka Fire Fall
incidents.summary: A firefighter experienced heart palpitations and lost consciousness while assigned to the Kanaka Fire, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, Oregon. A “red” medical emergency was declared and several aviation resources were ordered while a ground-based carry-out proceeded. The firefighter was eventually transported to the hospital via ground ambulance. After transport to the hospital, it was reported that the firefighter had fallen on 8/22/23.

incidents.name: Little Mesa Fire Broken Kneecap
incidents.summary: A Forest Service firefighter suffered a broken kneecap while assigned to the Little Mesa Fire, Uncompahgre Field Office BLM, Colorado. The firefighter was transported to the hospital with an agency-owned vehicle. The firefighter was treated and released. Arrangements for travel home were underway as of 8/23/22.

incidents.name: Shearwood Creek Fire UTV Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On August 24, 2023, during initial attack operations on the Shearwood Creek Fire in Jasper County, Texas there was an incident involving a tree strike to a UTV. While tracking down pre-existing fireline, the UTV was hit by a tree that was unknowingly cut and pushed by a Caterpillar D6T with a shear blade. There was substantial damage to the UTV, however, the operators of the dozer and the UTV did not sustain any injuries during the incident.
incidents.quote: I heard a crack and then I was on my side.

incidents.name: Ridge Creek Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On August 25, a falling team was engaged in hazard tree falling in Division Echo of the Ridge Creek Fire on the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The top of a hung-up tree broke off and struck the faller. The faller was hit on his helmet, neck, shoulder, and back. The faller received immediate medical care from resources on the fire and was transported via helicopter to a hospital where he spent two days before being released.
incidents.quote: While working to safely remove a hazard tree to the ground that had been caught-up in some limbs of nearby green trees, the top of the tree being fallen broke off and struck the faller

incidents.name: Central Washington Interagency Communication Center Power Outage
incidents.summary: On Friday, August 25, 2023, at 1300 hours, the Central Washington Interagency Communication Center lost phones, internet, and radios due to a power outage. Late August in the northwest is a period of high fire danger, and lightning was expected through that Saturday. At that time, the dispatch center had an emerging Type 3 wildland fire incident and another new smoke had just been reported. Over the next several days, the dispatch worked through a variety of fixes, coordinated with an adjacent dispatch center, the Forest Service Regional Office, the internet service provider, and others, to maintain communication and accountability across a huge portion of Washington.

incidents.name: Camp Creek Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: A member of a hand crew suffered a suspected broken arm after being struck by a falling rock on the Camp Creek Fire, Mt. Hood National Forest, Oregon. Initially reported as a Red Medical and downgraded to a Yellow after EMT size-up. The crewmember was transported to the hospital and diagnosed with a “badly bruised” arm. The firefighter was released after diagnosis.

incidents.name: Whiskey Creek Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A complex accident on a 75% slope involved a falling tree, fuel container failure, and subsequent pack fire. One firefighter suffered second-degree burns and another a knee injury.
incidents.quote: "A flaming firefighter was tumbling downslope like a rag doll." - Engine Crew Member

incidents.name: Smith River Complex North Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter suffered burn injuries to the hand and forearm (estimated at 9%) after falling down a slope during burnout operations on the Smith River Complex, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, Oregon. No further information at time of posting.

incidents.name: Montana Dillon Engine Accident
incidents.summary: On August 27th, 2023, fire personnel were performing routine cleaning on the exterior of E-7225. As the driver was pulling out of engine bay, the passenger side cargo bin door of Engine 7225 was left open and came into contact with the building and garage door frame. This caused damage to both the cargo door bin, garage door frame, and a load bearing wall.

incidents.name: Tyee Ridge Complex Medical
incidents.summary: While performing handline construction on the Tyee Ridge Complex, Central Unit, Oregon Department of Forestry, a member of a hand crew experienced infected blisters on both hands. The crewmember was evaluated by crew EMTs, who provided minor remedies. The crewmember was transported to the hospital, evaluated, and admitted to the hospital for two days with an infection on both hands. The crewmember was released and flew home on 09/01/2023.

incidents.name: Anvil Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: A firefighter was struck by a rolling rock and suffered a suspected broken ankle while assigned to the Anvil Fire, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, Oregon. A U.S. Coast Guard hoist-capable helicopter was requested and used due to the location of the injury: a very remote, deep canyon bottom and in heavy smoke. The firefighter was transported to the hospital and diagnosed with a broken fibula.

incidents.name: Tamarack Springs Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: During initial attack operations on the Tamarack Springs Fire, Umatilla National Forest, Washington, a hand crew member was struck when the top of a snag fell. The injured firefighter was transported by agency vehicle to an ambulance, and then to the hospital in Lewiston, Idaho. At the hospital, a third degree burn on the upper back was identified and the firefighter was further transported to the burn center at Harborview Medical Center in Seattle. Treatment and recovery is ongoing.
incidents.quote: The top glanced the side of their hardhat and impacted their shoulder. The IC heard the top break out and witnessed this impact to the crew member

incidents.name: Smith River Complex South Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A crew member on a hand crew assigned to the Smith River Complex, Six Rivers National Forest, California, suffered burn injuries on the hand (middle finger), wrist and forearm. The firefighter was transported to the hospital, treated, and released.

incidents.name: Track Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Track Fire, San Bernardino National Forest, California, slid down a steep hill into some hot material and suffered a burn to his forearm. The firefighter was transported to the hospital, treated, and released.

incidents.name: Camp Creek Fire Fall
incidents.summary: While conducting fireline operations on the Camp Creek Fire, Mt. Hood National Forest, Oregon, a firefighter stepped in a rut and fell onto their left leg/knee. The kneecap/patella was dislocated upon hitting the surface of the ground. Patient was able to reduce the dislocation on her own before medical resources arrived on scene. A fireline paramedic (EMPF) was on scene wrapped and iced the knee. Crew Leader advised they would transport patient to Meadow Base Camp via POV. Patient has been released from urgent care and was advised to place zero weight on injured knee. Will be demobed to return home for care.

incidents.name: Tyee Ridge Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Flat Fire, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, Oregon, suffered a fist-sized, second degree burn injury to the leg, just above the boot line. No further information at time of posting.

incidents.name: Chilcoot Fire Insect Sting
incidents.summary: A firefighter was stung by a bee and experienced an anaphylactic reaction while assigned to the Chilcoot Fire, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon. The reaction was treated with two rounds of epinephrine and Benadryl, along with O2. The firefighter was transported to the hospital. No further information at time of posting.

incidents.name: Flat Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter assigned to the Flat Fire, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, received burns and debris to face and eyes when a can of soup exploded. Patient was transported to hospital in Gold Beach, Oregon for evaluation and treatment. No further information at time of posting.

incidents.name: Chilcoot Fire Chipper Operator Insect Stings
incidents.summary: A chipper operator/crewmember received multiple bee stings on the Chilcoot Fire, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon. The firefighter was transported via assigned ambulance and local ambulance service to the hospital in Eugene, OR where the firefighter was evaluated, treated and released.

incidents.name: Chilcoot Fire Engine Crewmember Insect Strings
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember on the Chilcoot Fire, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, received several bee stings that resulted in fireline medical emergency. Several aviation assets were ordered initially, but the medevac and transport to the hospital eventually was accomplished by assigned ambulance. The crewmember was transported to the hospital, evaluated, treated and released with a prescription for an epi-pen (epinephrin).

incidents.name: Anvil Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: On September 10, an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) assigned to the Anvil Fire on the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest near Sixes, Oregon experienced an Incident Within an Incident (IWI) when a sawyer’s hand came into contact with the running chainsaw they were operating. At the time of the incident, the IHC was engaged in indirect line construction on a steep slope with thick, tall brush and difficult footing. The sawyer received onsite care before being transported by cooperator ambulance to a local hospital. Due to the severity of the injuries, emergency surgery was required the following day.
incidents.quote: Knowing they were also falling dangerously close to the saw, Sawyer 1 reached out to push the saw farther away and into the dirt, so they wouldn’t fall directly onto it—severely impacting three fingers on their left hand.

incidents.name: Lookout Fire Swamper Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A Type 2 Initial Attack (IA) crew was working on the Lookout Fire on the Willamette National Forest, Oregon, the afternoon of September 12. They were constructing indirect handline to cut off a road switchback. During snag felling, a swamper assisting the faller during the saw operation was struck by the hazard tree being felled. The swamper was struck across the back, dislocating their hip.
incidents.quote: A hazard tree fell 120 degrees off its intended lay, striking a swamper as they fled the stump.

incidents.name: Anvil Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: While cutting a tree during line construction efforts on the Anvil Fire, Rogue-River Siskiyou National Forest (Oregon), a sawyer was struck by a chunk of bark that sluffed off from high in the tree. The sawyer was struck in the head/helmet by the sluffed off bark. Short haul was initially requested and then canceled. The crewmember was able to walk off the fireline. Assigned and local ambulances worked to transport the crewmember to the hospital, where the examination revealed a concussion. The crewmember was released after the examination.

incidents.name: Bolt Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: After a shift of direct attack on the Bolt Fire, Coronado National Forest in Arizona, a crewmember experienced muscle cramping and exhibited early signs of heat stress and dehydration during the hike off the line. The crewmember was able to hike out to a UTV, which was used to transport to an incoming ALS ambulance, and then on to the hospital. The crewmember was treated and released the same day.

incidents.name: Lookout Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) working on the Lookout Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon, became overheated, began to cramp, and feel generally ill then sat down around 1330. His fellow crewmembers helped him up leading to him losing consciousness and demonstrating seizure type activity. He regained consciousness but remained disoriented. A nearby paramedic responded and performed a field assessment resulting in transport to the hospital in an incident ambulance.

incidents.name: Ida Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: While mopping up, the firefighter was using a backpack blower to improve some fireline when the backpack blower caught on fire, and burned the firefighter. The firefighter was able to ditch the backpack blower, however not before receiving several burns. Firefighter was treated at the hospital for several minor burns, and a moderate burn under one arm. The firefighter was released with a referral to a burn center when they arrive home.
incidents.quote: As he was ditching the backpack blower, he noticed that his pack was also on fire. He began yelling vigorously to his crew for help as he quickly shed more of his gear.

incidents.name: Lookout Fire Dehydration Medical Incident
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) assigned to the Lookout Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon, experienced altered level of consciousness due to dehydration. Enroute to the hospital, the crewmember responded well to dehydration interventions and was given further interventions at the hospital, where the crewmember was treated and released.

incidents.name: Anvil Fire Extraction
incidents.summary: Anvil Fire, October 2, 2023. At 1700 hours a medical emergency Incident Within an Incident (IWI) came over the command repeater. The initial Medical Incident Report (MIR) was for “heat exhaustion, patient unable to walk and patient condition: Yellow”. A Rapid Extraction Module Support (REMS) Team Leader reached the patient at 1704. A short-haul helicopter was available at the Helibase, a 5-minute flight away. However, the decision was made to carry the patient up the steep slope to a Drop Point 1 mile away. Once atop the steep section, it was determined the patient still could not walk and would have to be carried the remaining distance. Therefore, the total carry time was 3 hours and 18 minutes.
incidents.quote: An additional 20-person crew joined the carry up the final ridge, bringing the total to 54 people extracting the patient by ground.

incidents.name: SRF Lightning Complex Bee Sting Reaction
incidents.summary: Six Rivers National Forest: A contracted crewmember was stung in/around the mouth while constructing a fuel break and was assessed by a line medic who observed signs of worsening allergic reaction. Patient was treated on scene by line EMPF, transferred to a local ambulance and transported to the hospital. Crewmember remained stable throughout transport.

incidents.name: Highway Tanks Rx Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Tonto National Forest: An FS employee on an R5 IHC was struck on top of the helmet with an approximately 8” diameter branch while swamping during chainsaw operations. FS EMTs assessed the crewmember and they were transported to the hospital by agency vehicle. X-Rays were taken and the crewmember was released with no restrictions.

incidents.name: Quarry Fire Aerial Ignition Devices
incidents.summary: While performing Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) aerial ignition operations on the Quarry Fire, Stanislaus National Forest, California, firefighters encountered plastic aerial ignition spheres commercially known as “Dragon Eggs” that were incredibly volatile. After bench testing with different batches of plastic spheres and different mixes of chemicals, they concluded that a batch of Dragon Eggs manufactured in 2023 were overly volatile.
incidents.quote: The sound was similar to a small caliber bullet.

incidents.name: Williams Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On Friday, October 6, 2023, at approximately 1520 hours the Williams Incident occurred in the San Benito – Monterey Unit. A CAL FIRE engine was attempting to gain access to the vegetation fire when it became inoperable. As the fire progressed, it became established in a drainage below the engine’s location. The crew deployed two engine protection lines to defend their position while the fire burned through and past their location, causing them to seek refuge on the passenger side of the apparatus. A Fire Captain and two Firefighters suffered minor burn injuries. All three were transported via air ambulance to Fresno Regional Medical Center and were released.
incidents.quote: All three were forced lower and lower to the ground until they were forced to seek refuge under the engine.

incidents.name: Bedrock Fire Hit by Log
incidents.summary: An employee on the Bedrock Fire, Willamette National Forest, Oregon, was struck by a bucked log in the leg and sustained a broken tibia and fibula. The patient was transported to the hospital and underwent surgery to repair the broken bones.

incidents.name: Nelder Grove Hazard Tree Falling Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A faller working on the Nelder Grove project, Sierra National Forest, California, was struck on the left shoulder by a treetop during tree felling operations. The faller was carried out and transported via ground ambulance to Community Regional Medical Center in Fresno, with what was believed to be a broken clavicle.

incidents.name: Green Mountain Rx UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: A crew assigned to the Green Mountain Rx, Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, was in the process of shuttling crewmembers with a UTV. While on a steep slope, with 5 crewmembers on board, the UTV flipped over backwards, and rolled down the slope. Some brush caught the UTV and prevented the UTV and crewmembers from rolling much further down the slope. Several crewmembers had injuries described as “green” injuries, and several crewmembers were transported by ambulance to the hospital. As of this posting, a Facilitated Learning Analysis is planned to capture lessons associated with this rollover.

incidents.name: Highland Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: At approximately 2245 on October 30, a firefighter from the Cleveland National Forest, California, received burns to the face (cheek) and both knees while suppressing the Highland Fire. As the firefighter was crossing a fence, the firefighter was caught in the fence before falling into open flame. The firefighter was transported by ground ambulance to Temecula Valley Hospital. Upon arrival, he was immediately flown to the University of California-San Diego burn center.

incidents.name: Oregon Tree Felling Chainsaw Cut
incidents.fire: McCoy Road Hazard Tree Abatement Project
incidents.summary: A USFS smokejumper felling a 36-inch Douglas fir using a plunge-cut technique sustained a six-inch laceration when the saw kicked back. Effective use of a CAT tourniquet and prompt medical evacuation facilitated a successful recovery.
incidents.quote: The sawyer accidentally caused the chainsaw guide bar to make contact with the strap wood, resulting in a kickback that was forceful enough to cause the guide bar to exit the back cut kerf and strike the sawyer on their upper right arm.

incidents.name: Osceola National Forest Prescribed Fire Prep Medical Dehydration
incidents.summary: While clearing red cockaded woodpecker trees for prescribed fire on the Osceola National Forest, Florida, a crewmember from a prescribed fire module passed out from what appeared to be dehydration. The crew returned the crewmember to the hotel where the crewmember passed out again. The crewmember was then transported to the hospital, diagnosed with dehydration, treated, and released.

incidents.name: East Eagle-Mud Springs Prescribed Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.fire: East Eagle / Mud Springs Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: As part of burn unit preparation (snag mitigation) on the East Eagle-Mud Springs Prescribed Fire, Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest, Arizona, a sawyer was struck by a portion of a dead aspen tree with two tops. As the faller completed the cut, the tree fell to the desired lay, but when it hit the ground, one of the tops came back and struck the sawyer. On the ground, the sawyer was in pain (leg and back) and was tended to by a qualified EMT. The sawyer was transported via agency vehicle to the hospital (Springerville, AZ) where diagnosis of broken fibula and 3 broke ribs was provided.
incidents.quote: The sawyer had all the required PPE. However, the tree strike knocked off his helmet.

incidents.name: Stringtown Gulch Prescribed Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: As part of burn unit preparation on the Stringtown Gulch Prescribed Fire, Arapahoe-Roosevelt National Forest, Colorado, a sawyer received a chainsaw cut to the left forearm after experiencing saw kickback during tree felling operations. The sawyer was transported via ground ambulance to the hospital in Loveland, CO.

incidents.name: Troublesome Hollow Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) fell during fireline operations on the Troublesome Hollow Fire, Tennessee. The crewmember was transported to the hospital and diagnosed with a concussion after CT scan and MRI.

incidents.name: Horseshoe-Wild Bill Prescribed Fire Burned Line Gear
incidents.summary: The complexity of the trees indicated the necessity for removing line gear for firefighter safety—to quickly move along escape routes. Crewmembers removed their line gear and set them near the cleanup work on the felled hazard trees. Earlier, a drip torch that had an incorrect collar leaked because it could not properly seal. We believe this drip torch fuel absorbed into the crewmembers’ line gear. Aided by wind, the fire crept through the pine needle cast under the line gear. The fuel that had been absorbed into the material caused the line gear packs to be more flammable. The line gear was discovered to be on fire when fusee firing devices ignited in the pack’s side pouches. Crewmembers applied their drinking water to the packs to extinguish the flames.
incidents.quote: Aided by wind, the fire crept through the pine needle cast under the line gear. The fuel that had been absorbed into the material caused the line gear packs to be more flammable.

incidents.name: Juniper Lake Piles Burn Injury
incidents.summary: An experienced three-person crew were burning machine piles in the remote Juniper Lake area of Lassen National Park. They were burning to further the park’s prescribed fire accomplishments and eliminate the accumulated piles created by the ongoing recovery from the Dixie Fire. The crew was successfully burning several piles that day, all within the LAVO Pile RX Plan. The Burn Boss/FMO sustained burn injuries to their hands and face when fuel fumes ignited unexpectedly, when adding fuel to a large machine pile.
incidents.quote: Moments later while the Burn Boss was pouring fuel from the 5-gallon can onto the pile, fire erupted from below the Burn Boss and the fuel container, engulfing him in flames.

incidents.name: Buchanan Ridge Fire UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: A UTV operator began to transport firefighters and equipment to strategic locations along the fireline’s perimeter. Part of this route was downhill where a root ball was located in a portion of the installed line. As the operator drove the UTV around the root ball, the front tire gained traction on the cut bank and quickly climbed up the bank, putting the center of gravity too high, causing a slow rollover.

incidents.name: Clinton-Warren Joint Fire and Rescue District Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On Sunday, Dec. 24, 2023, Chief Robert Wysong responded to a brush fire. After the call, he returned home. Later in the evening, his wife found him unresponsive. He was immediately transported to the Clinton Memorial Hospital where he was evaluated and then subsequently transferred via Miami Valley Care Flight to the Miami Valley Hospital where he passed away on Tuesday, Dec. 26, 2023, from a heart attack.

incidents.name: Dogwood Trail Project Work Tree Strike
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, January 10, 2024, a group of Texas A&M Forest Service firefighters were working on a trail improvement project on Dogwood Trail in Tyler County. The task for the day was hazard tree removal in order to improve safety for the public that utilize the walking trail. While felling a sizeable southern magnolia (Magnolia grandiflora), a sawyer was struck in the face by a falling limb, resulting in multiple injuries.
incidents.quote: It happened very quickly and someone yelled out a warning. Just as the trainee was tilting his head up to look for overhead hazards, the limb struck him vertically across the forehead/nose area.

incidents.name: Savannah River Site Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: While conducting ignitions on a prescribed fire on the Department of Energy's Savannah River Site, a firefighter suffered burn injuries to the back of one leg. While moving through thick fuels—which included vines—the firefighter became entangled/caught up and drip torch fuel burned the back of one leg. The firefighter was transported by agency-owned vehicle to Augusta Burn Center, where a 1/2-dollar size 1st and 2nd degree burn was assessed. He was treated and released with no need for follow up.

incidents.name: Glendale Fire Department Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Robert Earl Brown, Sr. was at the scene of a brush fire pulling hose when he suffered a medical emergency. He was immediately taken to the Spartanburg Regional Medical Center where he passed away a short time later from an apparent heart attack. Firefighter Robert Earl Brown, Sr., was the past chief of the Glendale Fire Department from 1976 to 2017.

incidents.name: Florida Hose Reel Wiring Issue RLS
incidents.summary: A BFX 643P Type 6 Engine assigned to the Apalachicola National Forest discovered melted hose reel wiring during routine Preventative Maintenance Checks and Service (PMCS). It was determined that the back of the hose reel control switch was open to the elements. Moisture between the exposed contacts created a low amperage pull that gradually melted the wiring on the hose reel. A fuse holder and 15-amp fuse were installed to prevent any further damage to the hose reel or other wiring.

incidents.name: Buffalo Pasture Prescribed Fire ATV Fire
incidents.summary: On the Buffalo Pasture Prescribed Fire in South Dakota, two ATVs with mounted torches were used to ignite the prescribed fire. During operations, one of the ATVs tried to traverse a sleep slope and began to roll over. The operator jumped off and rolled clear as the ATV landed backwards on its seat. The ATV then rolled downhill and was consumed by fire as the operator had to leave the area due to fire behavior. The ATV was destroyed by fire but the operator was not seriously injured.
incidents.quote: As they were attempting to turn uphill the ATV struck an unknown object throwing it off balance and the ATV started tipping over and they had an “oh no” moment.

incidents.name: Mark Twain NF Prescribed Fire Prep UTV Bed Fire
incidents.summary: While engaged in prescribed fire preparation utilizing a bed-mounted turbine debris blower in the back of a UTV, it is assumed that the heat from the blower exhaust ignited a nylon covered elastic bungee cord that was securing a 5-gallon “safety can” of gasoline. The burning cord ignited the fuel can while in the bed of the UTV.

incidents.name: Kentucky Engine Broken Wheel Studs
incidents.summary: While traveling on a paved highway the engine driver noticed a small vibration in the vehicle. Seconds later, he felt major shaking and then felt the back-end drop. As the rotor hit the ground, the driver saw the outside dually release and cross to the opposite side of the road. As the driver brought the vehicle to a stop, the inside dually came off and rolled past the vehicle a short distance, stopping in a drainage on the same side of the road.
incidents.quote: Seconds later, he felt some major shaking from the vehicle and then felt the back end drop. As the rotor hit the ground, the FEO saw the outside dually release and cross to the opposite side of the road.

incidents.name: Poteau/Cold Springs Ranger District Prescribed Fire Fall Broken Leg
incidents.fire: Poteau/Cold Springs Ranger District prescribed fire
incidents.summary: An EMT-qualified firefighter was walking through the prescribed fire unit on the Ouchita National Forest when they “took a bad step” and injured their leg. The firefighter called in a “green” medical and treated themselves. Transported to hospital via an agency-owned vehicle with a broken leg. Treated and released with follow up treatment planned.

incidents.name: Holly Springs National Forest Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Shortly after burning a section of line on a prescribed fire on the Holly Springs National Forest, Mississippi, a firefighter stepped into a hot stump hole and sustained a burn the size of two palms on the back of leg. They were treated and released from ER.

incidents.name: Hotshot Crew Physical Training Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an interagency hotshot crew experienced an episode of rhabdomyolysis. The crewmember experienced leg cramps at the very beginning of physical training (PT). Crew overhead noticed the symptoms and took individual to hospital, where diagnosis of rhabdomyolysis was confirmed. The firefighter spent 2 nights in the hospital and was released on 2/22/2024.

incidents.name: Compartment 154 Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: On February 22, 2024, firefighter received burns on the back of the leg during firing operations on the Compartment 154 prescribed burn on the Oconee Ranger District, Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, Georgia. While walking/moving through some vines, drip torch fuel was spilled on pants, which ignited and caused burn injuries. The firefighter was transported by agency-owned vehicle to the local hospital with a larger than palm-sized burn, initially believed to be 2nd degree burns.
