The following day, the firefighter was treated in the Augusta, Georgia burn center for 2nd and 3rd degree burns. Treatment included skin grafts.
incidents.quote: A few minutes after he began lighting again, he found himself in thick vines and vegetation. As he worked to get free, the vines quickly stopped him and he lost situational awareness of where the fire was at the end of his torch.

incidents.name: Roland Prescribed Fire UTV Electrical Fire
incidents.summary: On February 26, at approximately 1445 hours, while performing mop-up operations on the Roland prescribed fire, Hoosier National Forest, Indiana, a U.S. Forest Service 2020 Can-Am 6X6 Defender HD Series UTV had an electrical issue that resulted in a vehicle fire. There were no injuries to the UTV occupants, who were able to access a fire extinguisher and quickly suppress the fire.
incidents.quote: While performing mop-up operations on a prescribed burn, a U.S. Forest Service 2020 Can-Am 6X6 Defender HD Series UTV had an electrical issue that resulted in a vehicle fire.

incidents.name: Dobson Knob Prescribed Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: During ignition operations on the Dobson Knob Prescribed Fire, Pisgah National Forest, North Carolina, a firefighter became entangled in vegetation (described as “briars”) and was burned on the thigh with drip torch fuel. The injury was not initially reported, and unit was made aware on March 4th of the injury, as the employee went to a walk in clinic on March 3rd and was treated and released.

incidents.name: Catesby Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On Wednesday, February 28, 2024 a member of the Alva Fire Department was pinned between the cab of the truck and water tank as a result of a two vehicle collision on the Catesby Fire, Ellis County, Oklahoma. The firefighter was extricated and airlifted to OU Trauma Center with trunk and leg injuries, having suffered a broken pelvis.

incidents.name: Davy Crockett 4 Prescribed Fire Heat Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Davy Crockett 4 Prescribed Fire on the National Forests and Grasslands of Texas experienced a heat related injury. The firefighter was evaluated by onsite medical personnel and transported to the hospital, treated and released with no restrictions.

incidents.name: Cibola National Forest Work Capacity Test Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: An employee sponsored by the Cibola National Forest collapsed while performing the Work Capacity Test (WCT) or "Pack Test." A Forest Service EMT and a local fire department ambulance were on site and responded immediately. Patient was transported by ambulance to the hospital in Albuquerque, New Mexico, where the employee was admitted on 3/08/2024 and remained overnight. As of 3/09/2024, the employee was scheduled to have a heart stent procedure.

incidents.name: San Bernardino National Forest Motor Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: An Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) carrier was involved in a head-on collision with a civilian vehicle. The driver of the civilian vehicle died of their injuries. Nine IHC crewmembers were transported to the hospital with a range of injuries. All crewmembers were treated and released.

incidents.name: Colorado Fire Camp Training Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Colorado Fire Camp (CFC) is a privately run training center in central Colorado that has been training wildland firefighters for almost 20 years. CFC students run through the S-212 or, as of May of 2023, the Developing Thinking Sawyers (DTS) curriculum. The emphasis focuses on: Objective, Hazards, Leans, Escape route, Cut plan (OHLEC). During field day operation on a complex felling operation that included multiple binds and a stuck saw, a student following their planned escape route was struck on the head and shoulders by a 20-foot-long limb was around 5 inches in diameter at the point that it struck.
incidents.quote: The binds in the tree released all at once. This wasn’t a slow release. In a few microseconds, all the kinetic energy stored in the hidden binds of the tree explosively broke free. It was only when everything began to settle that it became evident that Ryan had only made it a couple steps down the escape route toward safety when a large limb hit him from behind and crumpled him to the ground.

incidents.name: Dobson Knob Prescribed Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Dobson Knob Prescribed Fire, Pisgah National Forest, North Carolina, was carrying a chainsaw when a container of bar oil rolled down hill and tripped them. The sawyer fell on the saw and received about a 2" laceration. The sawyer was transported to a local emergency room, treated and released with no restrictions.

incidents.name: Compartment 22 Prescribed Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: A firefighter was mitigating a snag inside the prescribed fire unit on the Savannah River Site, South Carolina, when fire behavior increased. As the firefighter quickly moved back towards the line, they became caught up in vegetation and had fire and heat impact their location. Burn injuries were assessed by on-scene EMT, who called for an ambulance. Firefighter was transported to Augusta, GA to an emergency room at a Level II trauma center and was subsequently transferred to the hospital’s burn center. The firefighter received skin grafts on 3/21/24 to both knees, both elbows and an inner thigh.
incidents.quote: Deciding to withdraw and try a new approach, the ENGB turned around, immediately noting that fire behavior had increased. His council rake was entangled in the brush. He therefore dropped it and continued toward the fence. After another step or two, he became completely entangled in the vines. At that point, the fuels around him “self-ignited.”

incidents.name: Tonto National Forest Training Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: During an afternoon First Aid/CPR Training on the Tonto National Forest, Arizona, a firefighter noticed his leg muscles were really stiff and sore from the morning PT run. After driving home from work (~1 hour drive) his legs muscles were so stiff he could barely walk. He decided to go to the local ER. Patient was immediately administered an IV and the doctor ordered a blood test because of suspected rhabdomyolysis, which was later confirmed. Patient was released at 0030 on the morning of 3/28/2024, with instructions to rest and hydrate for 4 days and will need a follow-up visit with a doctor before returning to work.

incidents.name: Prescott National Forest Crew Physical Training Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: After hiking for ~30 minutes en route to a training location on the Prescott National Forest, Arizona, a member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) verbalized not feeling well to a Captain. When the Captain turned to respond, the crewmember was observed falling to the ground, without trying to break his fall. It appeared to be a complete black-out that lasted for less than one minute. Upon regaining consciousness, patient was alert and oriented, and aware that he had blacked out. The crewmember was transported to a waiting ambulance and taken to hospital where a CT scan was performed. CT scan results were not conclusive, and the crewmember was referred to primary care.

incidents.name: Virginia Department of Forestry Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On Saturday, March 30, 2024, Firefighter James Ward, Jr. was at the scene of a three-acre wildfire in Virginia when he collapsed while working with a hand crew. CPR was initiated and Firefighter Ward was then transported to the Holston Valley Medical Center in Kingsport, Tennessee, where he was pronounced deceased. The cause of death has yet to be determined. The fire was contained by Saturday evening.

incidents.name: Inyo Felling Incident Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On April 3, 2024, a sawyer from an Interagency Hotshot Crew sustained serious face and head injuries and was knocked unconscious by a large branch during a tree felling operation on the Inyo National Forest near Mammoth Lakes, California. The sawyer and other crew members were falling select trees to prepare for being advanced faller candidates in an upcoming evaluation session. The supervisor and crewmember on scene initiated a coordinated medical response using available first aid resources and immediate notification requesting an ambulance and hospital transport for evaluation and treatment.
incidents.quote: “I immediately thought he was dead.” -IHC Captain

incidents.name: Mamre Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: Litchfield Wetland Management District in Minnesota implemented a pile prescribed fire on the Mamre Waterfowl Production Area (WPA) on March 27, 2024. This operation was to ignite 11 individual tree piles that were a byproduct of a tree removal project on the WPA completed in the fall of 2022. On April 6, 2024, the fire escaped under red flag conditions and burned a portion of the WPA and then burning onto private land.

incidents.name: Huron-Manistee NF Drip Torch Injury
incidents.summary: On a prescribed fire on the Huron-Manistee NF, a firefighter topped off their drip torch using a jerry can that was missing a nozzle. While refueling the drip torch, a “copious” amount of torch mix spilled on the ground as well as on their lower right pant leg and boot. The crewmember used the torch for ignitions on the burn, and noticed that their right leg was on fire. They extinguished the fire using their gloved hands. The hospital determined the firefighter had sustained 2nd degree burns.
incidents.quote: The crewmember remembers thinking “this is really hot.” Looking down, the crewmember noticed that their right leg was on fire.

incidents.name: Cave Springs Fire Vehicle Fire
incidents.summary: On April 6, the human-caused Cave Springs Fire was reported at approximately 1200 hours. This fire was located on private lands nine miles southwest of Stilwell, Oklahoma. The fire was contained at approximately 2100 hours; all resources were released. The next day, the Task Force Leader (TFLD), a Type 6 Engine, and a squad returned to the Cave Springs Fire, which had escaped containment. As suppression efforts were underway, an explosion was heard from the direction of the parked vehicles. It was discovered that TFLD's vehicle had caught fire. It was a total loss, but no injuries occurred.
incidents.quote: After driving approximately 50 yards, the driver had to abandon the TFLD’s vehicle as the tire fire worked its way up onto the vehicle’s fiberglass canopy shell.

incidents.name: Arizona Physical Training Hike Pulaski Cut
incidents.summary: During a PT hike, a firefighter, who was carrying a pulaski, tripped over a rock and fell. His initial attack gear went up over his head as he fell, making the fall awkward. As he got up, he covered his right wrist as blood spurted out—from a pulaski laceration. He called out for an EMT. The first EMT to reach him instantly noticed bright red blood dripping from his right wrist from under his hand. The cut required surgery to repair tendons, arteries, and nerves that had been severed.
incidents.quote: One of the firefighters, who was carrying a pulaski, tripped over a rock and fell. His initial atack gear went up over his head as he fell, making the fall awkward. As he got up, he covered his right wrist as blood spurted out—from a pulaski laceration.

incidents.name: Hoy Prescribed Fire Slopover Response
incidents.summary: On April 11, 2024, fire personnel from the US Fish and Wildlife Service conducted a prescribed burn on the Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge in northwestern Colorado. Shortly after ignitions began, several small slopovers necessitated altering firing patterns. At 1140 the fire crossed the eastern fireline and ultimately burned an area of 16 acres on federal lands. Contingency resources were called and successfully contained the slopover as firing continued on the prescribed fire unit. Ignitions on the unit were completed at 1654. Due to the effective response by holding and contingency resources, the prescribed fire was not declared a wildfire.
incidents.quote: During their firing operations, variable winds and fuel-driven fire made it difficult for the Alpha side to “stay ahead” of the main fire. Eventually, at 1140 hours, the fire crossed the eastern line—hereafter referred to as the “Slopover”—outside the burn unit in the drainage located in the burn’s northeast corner.

incidents.name: Hoy Prescribed Fire UTV Accident
incidents.summary: On April 11, 2024, fire personnel from the US Fish and Wildlife Service conducted a prescribed bun on the Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge in northwestern Colorado. While prescribed fire operations were ongoing, a UTV carrying the Prescribed Fire Burn Boss Type 2 (trainee) and the Agency Administrator impacted a culvert pipe and ditch and rolled over. The Agency Administrator was injured and transported to the hospital.
incidents.quote: At that moment, the Agency Administrator exclaimed: “Watch out!” The driver turned their head, saw the culvert and ditch directly ahead, applied the brakes, and turned back toward the impoundment. Before the UTV could stop, it hit the culvert, the passenger tires and UTV entered the ditch—landing on the driver’s side.

incidents.name: Yauney Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire Review
incidents.summary: The Yauney prescribed fire was implemented on 4/14/2024. It was 160 acres. On the afternoon of 4/15/2024 it was reported to the local Fire Department. US Fish and Wildlife employees arrived, and two "fingers" were declared a wildfire resulting in 148 acres of private land being burned.

incidents.name: Montana State DNRC Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On Tuesday, April 16, 2024, Firefighter John Norris Raisler suffered a medical emergency during a practice for a pack test. CPR was immediately performed and he was then transported to the local hospital where he was pronounced deceased from an apparent heart attack.

incidents.name: Funston Road Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On the Funston Road Fire in North Carolina, two different tractor-plows were burned over. The first tractor-plow operator was able to use their escape route to a preidentified safety zone. The second tractor plow operator was entrapped and burned over but sustained no injuries. The fire investigation team has determined these events meet the criteria of near miss, entrapment and burnover as defined by the NWCG. A final report with findings and recommendations will be released and distributed at a later date.
incidents.quote: The fire investigation team has determined these events meet the criteria of near miss, entrapment and burnover as defined by the NWCG.

incidents.name: Blue Panther Prescribed Fire Broken Wheel Studs
incidents.summary: On April 19, 2024, at approximately 1800 hours, a Type 6 Engine with the crew was enroute to the Blue Panther Rx near Warm Springs, Virginia, for night operations. The vehicle had a minor shake that was noticed about five minutes away from the destination. Soon after this shaking began, driving speeds were reduced to 35-40 mph, and an audible “clank” type noise was heard. This was believed to be a possible rock dislodged from the dualies. Within another minute or so, the vehicle lost both passenger-side rear wheels. The engine operator safely guided the apparatus off the road and onto the shoulder. Studs on the wheel had sheared completely off.
incidents.quote: Within another minute or so, the vehicle lost both passenger-side rear wheels.

incidents.name: Tri-County Prescribed Fire Limb Strike
incidents.summary: While working on the Tri-County RX in Virginia, a sawyer was struck on his hardhat by a 6 inch diameter branch that fell from a green, live oak tree.
incidents.quote: While standing on the cutbank assessing his work, Bravo Sawyer felt and heard a large thud on the top of his head.

incidents.name: Bowers Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember stepped into a hot stump hole during mop-up operations. The firefighter received initial treatment from a local fire department assigned to the fire, and was transported to the hospital in an agency vehicle. The firefighter was referred to a burn center for follow-up by initial attending physician.

incidents.name: Sinking Creek Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: The Eastern Divide Ranger District (EDRD) of the George Washington & Jefferson National Forests (GWJ) initiated a prescribed burn (Rx) on Unit Two of the Sinking Creek RX Project. As ignitions began that morning, fire effects were consistent with the plan’s objectives. Relative humidity on the fire decreased rapidly, however, and by afternoon the fire began to spot outside of its containment lines.
incidents.quote: An outlier weather event occurred, causing the RH to drop significantly below what was forecast for the day.

incidents.name: Huff Hollow Prescribed Fire Dozer Transport Rollover
incidents.summary: A 15-year employee of the U.S. Forest Service (FS) experienced a complete rollover while traveling for assignment as an equipment operator on Prescribed Fire (Rx) Support for the George Washington and Jefferson National Forest’s (GWJ) South Zone. The employee had previously worked on the GWJ in various capacities and was familiar with the mountainous terrain and the area’s steep winding roads. They had recently obtained their commercial driver’s license and had been assigned to a transport and dozer that they were not familiar with during this assignment.
incidents.quote: When they attempted to apply the airbrakes again, they felt no resistance and recognized that the brakes had failed. Panic set in. In a desperate attempt to stop the truck, the operator pulled the parking brake. However, that also failed because the parking brake requires the same compressed air as the standard airbrakes.

incidents.name: Blankenship Hollow Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: At 1755 hours on April 25, 2024, a significant fire broke out from a structure fire in Blankenship Hollow at Stopover, KY (Pike County). During the intense initial attack firefighting operations, a Kentucky Division of Forestry firefighter was tragically entrapped. The Incident Commander Type 5 and the fire crew, demonstrating exceptional teamwork, were able to assist the injured firefighter from the scene of the burnover to the waiting ambulance in Blankenship Hollow. After a thorough assessment by the EMTs, it was deemed necessary to request the life-flight helicopter for the firefighter's urgent transport to the burn unit at Cabell Huntington Hospital in Huntington, WV, to treat the severe burns covering their hands, knees, and face.
incidents.quote: After tripping and rolling down the hill, the firefighter got up and knew they were in a bad situation. The f irefighter could hear the crew leader shouting at them to deploy their shelter and the voice in the back of the firefighter’s mind was saying “deploy your shelter”.

incidents.name: Utah Fuels Work Woodchipper Malfunction
incidents.summary: An agency woodchipper experienced a malfunction while being used by an eight-person crew comprised of seasonal fuels crew and Conservation Corps members. On the morning of the incident, a crew member was feeding a branch into the chipper when a loud crashing noise was heard. Metal material was seen shooting out of the chute and bolts sheared from both blades, causing them to fall out of the rear feed tray. The operator quickly shut down the machine immediately following the noise and this metal discharge. No injuries occurred.
incidents.quote: On the morning of the incident, a crew member was feeding a branch into the chipper when a loud crashing noise was heard. Metal material was seen shooting out of the chute and bolts sheared from both blades.

incidents.name: Cherokee National Forest Insect Sting Allergic Reaction
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Cherokee National Forest experienced anaphylactic shock from a bee sting. The firefighter was flown by agency helicopter to an awaiting ground ambulance and was then transported to local hospital for treatment. The firefighter was released the same day.

incidents.name: Pittman Fire Pulaski Cut
incidents.summary: While engaged in mop-up activities on the Pittman Fire, Ocala National Forest, Florida, a firefighter received a laceration just below the left ankle. The injured firefighter was cutting out a small root wad when the firefighter’s pulaski happened to ricochet and struck the left ankle. The firefighter was taken via ambulance to ER, stitched up and released same day with a recommendation for a follow-up at a surgery center in Orlando, FL as the local center does not accept OWCP.

incidents.name: Chainsaw Evaluation Vehicle Tree Strike
incidents.summary: On May 8, 2024, 2 USFS personnel were being evaluated as chainsaw operators. During the evaluation one of the operators cut through the hinge wood on a tree, causing it to fall in an unintended direction and damage the evaluator's truck. No one was injured but the vehicle sustained damage to utility boxes, and a chainsaw in the truck was also damaged.
incidents.quote: Just before the cuts were made to fall the tree, the Crew Boss/Chainsaw Evaluator told the sawyer: “Don’t hit my truck.” The fir fell across the campground road and struck the parked fire vehicle that belonged to the evaluator administering the evaluations.

incidents.name: Kisatchie National Forest Heat Illness
incidents.fire: state of LA firefighter funeral service
incidents.summary: A group of USFS firefighters were representing the USFS Fire Program, in full uniform, at a funeral for a State of Louisiana firefighter. During the outdoor phase of the ceremony, one of the USFS firefighter collapsed. An ambulance was called, and the employee was transported to the hospital. Employee was treated with IV fluids, testing was completed, and the employee was released at 19:00 on May 9, 2024, directed to rest, hydrate and return to work on Monday.

incidents.name: Fry Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire Review
incidents.summary: On May 15, 2024, the Tofte Ranger District in the Superior National Forest implemented the Fry Prescribed Fire with good fire effects. Shortly after beginning the prescribed firing operations, spot fires were detected outside the unit boundaries. An escaped wildfire was declared, and local resources and air attack responded. Resources reported 100 percent containment by the evening of May 18. Approximately 137 acres outside the Rx unit were burned, and about 49 acres within the Rx fire unit.
incidents.quote: While Paul was observing the fire behavior in the unit, Steve was looking across the river and saw smoke. Several other people saw the spot fire at the same time, and it immediately began to grow.

incidents.name: Illinois Track Loader-Drum Mulcher Equipment Fire
incidents.summary: While engaged in mulching vegetation with a track loader with a mulching head (also called a masticator), a Forest Service employee in Illinois noticed smoke coming from the machine. The source of smoke was revealed to be in the area of the rear engine compartment. Three fire extinguishers were unable to put out the fire. The fire was eventually extinguished by the local fire department.
incidents.quote: This exposed sparks and a small fire where the smoke was emitting. At this time, the reverse fan engaged and fed the fire air—which increased the fire activity.

incidents.name: Idaho Longline Training Helicopter Autorotation
incidents.summary: On May 17, 2024, while supporting RT-219 (Helicopter Transport of External Cargo Refresher Training), a Bell 205 A1++ helicopter was forced to perform an autorotation due to low rotor RPM. While an autorotation is a maneuver every helicopter pilot must practice and be able to perform, it is rare that they are forced to do this in the operational environment.
incidents.quote: “It’s crazy how quick things can go wrong.”

incidents.name: Blue 2 Fire IHC Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: An IHC crew member was exhibiting signs of heat exhaustion on the Blue 2 Fire. Patient was evaluated by incident medical personnel, and was transported via incident ambulance to the local hospital, treated and released back to crew with no further treatment required.

incidents.name: Blue 2 Fire Rappelling Back Injury
incidents.summary: A heli-rappeller experienced a rapid descent and hard landing during rappel operations on the Blue 2 Fire. A crew EMT evaluated the injury on-scene, and an agency T3 helicopter transported the injured FF as a “Green” medical. The injured rappeller was then transported by ground ambulance to the hospital, diagnosed and released with a follow-up appointment needed.

incidents.name: Rum Creek Fire Tree Strike Fatality
incidents.summary: Logan Taylor was an Oregon Department of Forestry contractor who died as a result of critical injuries sustained during firefighting operations on the Rum Creek Fire on August 18, 2022. He was struck by a tree while engaged in fire suppression activities on BLM-managed public lands within the Medford District. Taylor was extracted from the location and transported via helicopter to Asante Regional Hospital in Medford, Oregon. He was pronounced dead at the hospital.
incidents.quote: Rum Creek Fire Tree Strike Fatality

incidents.name: Wyoming Work Capacity Test Hit by Vehicle
incidents.summary: On May 31, 2024, during a Work Capacity Test (WCT), or "pack test," located in Pinedale, Wyoming, three participants were struck by a car. After reaching the turnaround point, three employees were crossing the same two-lane road, approximately 100 yards from the finish line, when they were struck by a private vehicle turning right. With EMTs onsite during the WCT, the medical response was outstanding. Two of the firefighters struck were treated and released on site. The third firefighter was injured and transported via ambulance to the local hospital. The injured firefighter is expected to make a full recovery.
incidents.quote: “I looked up and said to myself: ‘I sure hope (the driver) sees us’.”

incidents.name: Bandit RX Smoke Inhalation
incidents.summary: After working on the Bandit RX, a fire fighter was driven back to his duty station feeling unwell. On the drive from the RX back to the duty station, the firefighter was disoriented and threw up multiple times. Once the driver got into cell phone range, he made the decision to call an ambulance and have the firefighter taken to the hospital. The firefighter was taken to the hospital ER by ambulance, treated and released with no specific restrictions.

incidents.name: BDF Crew Training Heat Injury
incidents.summary: As an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) was engaged in crew PT and line construction training, a crewmember began experiencing dehydration/heat illness symptoms. After initial treatment on-scene by crew EMTs, the decision was made to place the crewmember onto a collapsable litter to be carried out to the nearest road, where an ambulance was available to take the crewmember to the hospital where the crewmember was evaluated, treated, and released.

incidents.name: LaCrosse Volunteer Fire Department Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On the morning of Thursday, June 6, 2024, Firefighter Caldwell responded to a f ield fire. During the response, Firefighter Caldwell used rescue equipment to cut through a fence so other firefighters could get equipment to the area of the fire. After the fire, he returned to the station and cleaned up the equipment. He mentioned to others that he was going to stop and get his mail on the way home. That evening, he missed a work detail at the firehouse. On Friday, June 7, 2024, he failed to respond to a call. By Sunday morning, June 9, 2024, Firefighter Caldwell had not been seen or heard from since Thursday. Members of his department went to his residence to check on him. They found him deceased inside the home. He had collapsed and died while opening his mail, just a few hours after his emergency response to the fire incident.
incidents.quote: He had collapsed and died while opening his mail, just a few hours after his emergency response to the fire incident.

incidents.name: Toyo Fire Valley Fever
incidents.summary: On 6/9/2024, a crewmember from an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) was admitted to the hospital with suspected pneumonia. Eventually, the firefighter was diagnosed with the fungal infection known as Valley Fever (Coccidioidomycosis), and the firefighter underwent surgery to remove fluid in the chest (pleural effusion) on 6/9/24. The crewmember was likely exposed to the fungus (Coccidioides sp.) sometime between May 11 and May 15, 2024, when the IHC was assigned to the Toyo Fire (San Carlos BIA, AZ). One other firefighter assigned to the Toyo Fire has been diagnosed with Valley Fever (received medication and but not hospitalized). A third firefighter assigned to the Toyo Fire is suspected of Valley Fever (also not hospitalized), but conclusive tests are still pending as of 6/17/24.

incidents.name: South Beaver Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: South Beaver is a landscape-scale prescribed fire project designed to improve forest health and vegetation diversity, reduce fuel buildup, and enhance wildlife habitat. Several units were ignited in May 2024 utilizing snow lines. Over the ensuing weeks, as expected, fire continued to spread within those units as the snow melted. Eventually management and resource needs were greater than could be handled by the prescribed fire organization
incidents.quote: Even though it remained entirely within the project boundary, 42 days after initial ignitions, the South Beaver prescribed fire was declared a wildfire.

incidents.name: Thomas Prescribed Fire Heat Illness/Dehydration
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew experienced serious dehydration/heat illness as the crew was engaged in cutting handline up a steep slope. The crewmember never lost consciousness but did experience some muscle cramping in both arms, chest and abdomen. Employee was assessed by the paramedic on scene initially resulting in a "Yellow" status. After receiving a bag of fluids via IV the employee was reassessed as a "Green,” and was ground transported to the hospital. The crewmember was assessed, treated and released by 1900, with direction to avoid arduous duties for three days then return to full duty.

incidents.name: South Beaver Prescribed Fire Scouting Close Call
incidents.summary: During their scouting mission a large flame front developed moved up canyon toward them. The lookout notified them of the increased fire behavior. The AFEO knew of a nearby rock scree that was approximately 100 yards by 100 yards in size and could serve as a safety zone and they moved to it. They made the decision to stay in the rock scree and let the fire pass through. Due to heavy smoke, this took approximately four hours. To be prepared, the two scouters pulled their fire shelters from their line gear.
incidents.quote: Know the size and limitations of your safety zones. While this “safe area” was appropriate for two firefighters, it may have been too small for a handcrew.

incidents.name: Kootenai National Forest Work Capacity Test
incidents.summary: A non-fire employee was taking the work capacity test and began to feel dizzy and fell, injuring their knee and ankle. Test administrators took the employee inside hoping some cooler air and hydration may help. However, conditions worsened with employee experiencing shortness of breath with an elevated heart rate. An ambulance was called, and the employee was transported to the hospital and kept overnight. Eventually, rhabdomyolysis was the diagnosis.

incidents.name: Smokejumper Operations Jet Incursion
incidents.summary: On June 7, 2021 and again on June 14, 2024, smokejumpers were conducting live training when a military fighter jet narrowly missed the jump plane and aerial firefighters.
incidents.quote: “I saw it [the F-18] three miles out and we tried to make real-time radio contact… but the jet flew between the plane and the jumpers and we were never able to contact them.”

incidents.name: North Cascades Practice Jump
incidents.summary: A smokejumper from the North Cascades Smokejumping base suffered an injury during a practice jump. Based on the initial assessment of a broken femur, a USFS Short-Haul helicopter was requested to provide medevac support. The helicopter was able to land near the injury scene, and the injured smokejumper loaded into the helicopter and flown to the hospital in Wenatchee, WA. After diagnostics at the hospital, the injury was determined to be a “deep bruise” and the smokejumper was released.

incidents.name: Salt Fire Heat Illness
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember experienced nausea and vomiting while in camp. The firefighter was assessed by the incident medical unit and was eventually transported by incident ambulance to the emergency room in Ruidoso, NM. The firefighter was treated and released on 6/21/24, with instructions to take 1 day off work.

incidents.name: Capitan SEAT Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On June 21, 2024, about 1045 mountain daylight time, an Air Tractor Inc AT-802A airplane, N331BS, was destroyed when it was involved in an accident near Capitan, New Mexico. The pilot, Ronald Patton, was fatally injured. The airplane was in the number two position in a flight of three airplanes that had completed their firefighting duties in Texas and were repositioning the airplanes to Oregon. They planned a refueling stop in Gallup, New Mexico. Before the flight reached Gallup, they encountered weather near the Capitan mountains. The lead airplane and number 3 airplane climbed and turned towards the east to avoid the weather. The lead and number 3 airplanes landed at GUP and realized that the accident airplane did not arrive and was missing. The Federal Aviation Administration was notified and shortly thereafter issued an Alert Notice for the missing airplane. Later that afternoon, an airplane located the wreckage about 9 miles east northeast of Capitan.
incidents.quote: They realized that the accident airplane did not arrive and was missing.

incidents.name: Little Twist Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: On June 23, 2024, a Bonneville Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) crewmember, while assigned to the Little Twist Fire, was struck by a falling snag. The crew was actively working on a spot fire in conjunction with a type one helicopter. The forest conditions, combined with the intense rotor wash, caused what appeared to be a sound standing snag to fall over and strike the Bonneville IHC crewmember across the back of the head and shoulder, pinning them to the ground, resulting in serious injuries. The Bonneville IHC provided immediate medical care until additional medical providers could arrive to extract the crewmember by foot and agency helicopter directly to the hospital.
incidents.quote: “When I got hit, blood was coming off of me, I was starting to get spinny and I couldn’t hear anything. Then someone grabbed my hand, and I knew I was still alive.”

incidents.name: Cribby Creek Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A crewmember (swamper) on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) was hit by a tree while constructing indirect fire line around a native allotment. The swamper was moving cut material when their saw partner cut a dead standing spruce (approximately 6 inches in diameter and 15 feet tall) in the direction of the swamper, who was struck on the back part of the top of his head resulting in minor neck pain. The swamper was taken by helicopter to the Mat Su Regional Hospital and was treated and released.

incidents.name: Monument Ridge Prescribed Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: While working on the Monument Ridge Prescribed Fire, a crewmember on a Wildland Fire Module (WFM1) experienced a tree strike to the head and shoulders as the crewmember was working in the black. The crewmember was evaluated on-scene, and it was determined that no loss of consciousness was sustained. The crewmember was subsequently flown to Hoback Junction Guard Station where ground transportation took them to St. John’s hospital in Jackson Hole, WY. The crewmember was diagnosed with a stable fracture to the C1 vertebrae and released on 7/3/24 with a c-spine collar and instructions for use.
incidents.quote: A fire-weakened green lodgepole pine tree was about 50 feet tall and 8 inches in diameter when it fell. The tree’s crown struck the crew boss's hard hat, back, and shoulder.

incidents.name: Thompson Fire Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: A CAL FIRE Fire Engine (E1) was involved in a single vehicle rollover while responding to the Thompson Incident. The rollover occurred at 0727 hours on Wednesday, July 3, 2024. The engine was staffed with three CAL FIRE employees consisting of one Fire Apparatus Engineer and two Firefighters. E1 was traveling north on a narrow, two-lane paved county road approximately 19 feet in width. E1 left the east side of the roadway, rolled over, and came to rest upside down facing south. All three occupants suffered injuries: moderate injuries to one Firefighter and minor injuries to the Fire Apparatus Engineer and other Firefighter.
incidents.quote: The fire engine then crossed over the southbound lane, rolled over, and came to rest on its roof in the southbound shoulder facing south.

incidents.name: California Crew Physical Training Suspected Heat Illness
incidents.summary: During a crew physical training (PT) hike on the Sequoia National Forest, a firefighter displayed heat-related illness symptoms. An agency helicopter was utilized to move the firefighter from a ridge top to a ground ambulance which transported the firefighter to the hospital Kern Valley Medical Center. The firefighter was later transported to Bakersfield hospital for further evaluation and was released on 7/5/24 with instructions to follow-up with a cardiac specialist.

incidents.name: Balsam Root Fire Narrow Escape
incidents.summary: Early on the morning of July 5, 2024, a task force of fire resources from western Washington prepositioned for initial attack in the Wenatchee area responded to a grass fire near Confluence Park. A plan was devised for the engine crews to construct indirect handline uphill over a distance of 550 ft, then install a hoselay back down as they fired the line. During line construction, a crewmember acting as a lookout noticed the fire had reached the bottom of the hill and soon after that fire behavior was increasing. The crew escaped uphill towards a fenced area with an irrigated lawn that was accessed by a gate. The lookout was the last through the gate, 25 ft ahead of the flaming front. There were no injuries.
incidents.quote: After a few minutes, this firefighter, acting as the lookout, turned and started walking back toward the crew. The fire was rapidly approaching—it was time to escape.

incidents.name: Basin Fire Heat-Related Illness
incidents.summary: A public information officer (PIO) on the Basin Fire, Sierra National Forest, California, displayed symptoms consistent with HRI. The PIO was transported to the hospital and admitted for treatment, with an unclear diagnosis. The PIO was released on 7/14/2024 (7 Days hospitalized).

incidents.name: Salt Creek Fire Dozer Narrow Escape
incidents.summary: On July 7, 2024 contracted dozer was working on a fire near Butte Falls, OR. After leaving the dozer in a safety zone to bed down, the operator returned for the night shift, to find active fire behavior next to the dozer. The operator pushed out a larger safety zone and worked with the air attack and a lead plane to cool down the area with water and retardant, allowing the dozer to egress.
incidents.quote: One of the calls that heightened their concern was when the dozer operator stated: “We are trapped in an area I have pushed down to dirt.”

incidents.name: Lake Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember on a hand crew suffered burn injuries while shielding their face from the heat of a hotspot/flare up on the Lake Fire, Los Padres National Forest, California. The crewmember was transported initially by ground ambulance to Cottage Hospital-Santa Barbara and then transported via ground ambulance to Grossman Burn Center-West Hills LA County. Burn injuries were estimated at 7% total body surface area (TBSA), and the crewmember was treated and released to rest in a hotel for several days. Follow-up with burn center was recommended.
incidents.quote: A single firefighter simply held his hand up to shield his face and sustained a noticeable two-inch burn injury to his hand. Once at the Drop Point, the T2IA Superintendent noticed additional redness on the patient’s neck. A second patient assessment was performed that revealed burns to the shoulder and arm with skin starting to slough off.

incidents.name: Lake Fire Fall Injuries
incidents.summary: A member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) slipped and fell a very long distance down a slope, perhaps in the range of 200 feet, while assigned to the Lake Fire, Los Padres National Forest, California. The firefighter was flown via helicopter medevac to the hospital. Diagnostics, including CAT scans didn’t reveal any significant injuries. That said, the firefighter did receive numerous bumps and bruises including a possible knee injury. The crewmember was released the same day.

incidents.name: Upper Pine F Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: Upper Pine F, a 1,064 acre landscape underburn, was awarded to a local contractor for implementation. The contractors and Contracting Officer Representatives (COR) worked closely to monitor spring burn conditions and began ignitions May 20 and 21, 2024 on the Emigrant Creek Ranger District. The conditions on the burn were considered acceptable per the contract and the District obtained full responsibility for patrol and monitoring on June 13. By July 4, personnel recognized that fire season had arrived and conditions were not going to improve. On July 8, the Forest determined the burn would imminently escape and made the decision to declare a wildfire.
incidents.quote: Fifty days after ignition, Upper Pine F prescribed burn was declared a wildfire. It had yet to escape containment lines. It was not outside the project boundary. What happened?

incidents.name: Fremont-Winema NF Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: After the completion of a District Work Capacity Test (pack test), a firefighter assigned to the Bly Ranger District collapsed. An involved medical response occurred, immediately after the firefighter collapsed. Tragically, the firefighter was pronounced deceased at Sky Lakes Medical Center, in Klamath Falls, Oregon, shortly after 1200.

incidents.name: Pioneer Fire Cardiac Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: A faller experienced chest pains on the Pioneer Fire, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Washington, and a “red” medical emergency was declared. A life flight helicopter was launched as was an Agency Short-haul helicopter. The life flight was able to land and subsequently transported the patient to hospital. The faller was admitted to the hospital and released on 7/11/2024.

incidents.name: Horse Gulch Fire Fixed Wing Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: During its first scoop sequence, witnesses on the lake and the pilots of the 2 SEATs flying behind the accident airplane saw the airplane make a left turn to the southwest. Subsequently the airplane impacted a vertical rockface bordering the southern shoreline of the lake, fell into the lake, and sank.
incidents.quote: Wildland firefighting pilot Juliana Turchetti was killed in a single engine water scooper crash while assigned to the Horse Gulch Fire on the Helena Lewis and Clark National Forest.

incidents.name: Shelly Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A firefighter was working on the fireline on the Shelly Fire, Klamath National Forest, California, and became dehydrated, stopped sweating, and had cramping in the legs and back. Ground ambulance to hospital. Employee was treated with IV fluids and released with medical clearance to return to work on July 12.

incidents.name: Lake Fire Saw Mix and Poison Oak Exposure Injury
incidents.summary: A hand crewmember on the Lake Fire, Los Padres National Forest, California, received a chemical burn from gas that poured out of a faulty Dolmar, which was missing an O-ring on the fuel lid. The burn injury was reported as a 2nd degree burn. The injury was magnified by poison oak on same part of body gasoline contacted. The firefighter was flown to Grossman Burn Center in Bakersfield, CA. Treated and released back to full duty.

incidents.name: Bench Lake Fire Helicopter Mishap
incidents.summary: At approximately 17:10, on July 11, 2024, a helicopter conducting bucket operations on the Bench Lake Fire on the Sawtooth National Forest experienced a mishap. The helicopter experienced an unknown issue and went into Bench Lake while collecting water. The pilot was able to exit the aircraft and swim to shore, where he was met by on scene firefighters, who then hiked with the pilot to a nearby trailhead. The pilot was evaluated and released by the EMS on scene.

incidents.name: Shelly Fire Chainsaw Cut to Hand
incidents.summary: A hand crewmember on the Shelly Fire, Klamath National Forest, California, suffered a chain saw laceration to the hand. The firefighter was transported to Fairchild Medical Center in Yreka, CA. The firefighter received stitches and was released the same day, 7/11/24.

incidents.name: Pony Lake Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On February 29, 2024, the Pony Lake Wildfire started in the right of way of Hwy 83 South of Valentine Nebraska at roughly 1330 hours. During initial attack, a Type 6 engine stopped on a flank of the fire to cut a fence to gain access and continue flanking the fire. While stopped, a wind shift occurred that resulted in the engine being overtaken by a flaming front. One firefighter sustained injuries and the Type 6 engine was damaged.

incidents.name: Lake Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On the Lake Fire on the Los Padres National Forest, California, a member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) was hit on head by a 4-6” diameter tree branch. The crewmember experienced a loss of consciousness, had no event recall and demonstrated an altered level of consciousness. Incident medical personnel on the Division (a Medic and EMT) assisted, and the Crewmember was flown off the Division to Santa Barbara, CA Airport, and then taken by ground ambulance to Cottage Hospital. The crewmember was treated and released with orders to take a day off to rest before returning to work in light-duty status.

incidents.name: Shelly Fire Chainsaw Cut to Face
incidents.summary: A swamper on an Interagency Hotshot Crewmember on the Shelly Fire, Klamath National Forest, California, received a laceration on the chin and mouth when he was struck by his saw partner (sawyer). The injured swamper was taken by ambulance. The sawyer did not see the swamper and impacted him in the face with the chainsaw, resulting in lacerations the chin and mouth. Employee was transported via government vehicle to medical facility and treated with 15 stitches, and released.

incidents.name: Horse Gulch Fire Allergic Reaction
incidents.summary: On the Horse Gulch Fire, Helena/Lewis and Clark National Forest, Montana, a crewmember on a T2 Crew engaged in mop-up had a medical emergency when the crewmember ate nuts contained in a nutrition bar. An incident-assigned paramedic was on-scene within minutes and recommended a ground ambulance to a local hospital after the patient aspirated after taking Benadryl. No epinephrine was administered by the paramedic. The crewmember was treated, released from the hospital, and was back with his crew at the end of shift.

incidents.name: Vista Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Vista Fire, San Bernardino National Forest, California, experienced heat related illness and a “yellow” medevac occurred. The firefighter was taken to the hospital and spent three days hospitalized. It was reported that kidney issues related to dehydration existed. The firefighter was released from the hospital on 7/15/2024.

incidents.name: Trout Fire Emergency Smokejumper Extraction
incidents.summary: On July 13, 2024, the lightning-caused Trout Fire on the Sequoia National Forest, California, was staffed by a load of smokejumpers who intended to establish an anchor point, develop incident objectives, and perform overhead functions. As the day progressed, fire behavior became more active, instigating the smokejumpers to burn the existing fuels in their jump spot/safety zone. Ultimately the decision was made by fire management and the smokejumpers to extract the personnel from the site by helicopter. The extraction was performed without incident and there were no injuries.
incidents.quote: “Oh, they’re in trouble. They’re about to get burned up.”

incidents.name: Shelly Fire Unknown Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: A member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) experienced an unknown medical emergency on the Shelly Fire, Klamath National Forest, California. The individual was unresponsive but breathing, with no visible trauma. A helicopter medevac was conducted. Upon arrival at the hospital, the crewmember was feeling much better, but was admitted in-patient overnight for observation. While the precise diagnosis was unclear, the crewmember was released on 7/14/24, but not allowed to return to full duty, pending additional diagnosis.

incidents.name: Black Fire Fall Head Injury
incidents.summary: While working a piece of line on the Black Fire, Tonto National Forest, Arizona, a crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) fell off a ledge and hit his head. The crewmember was evaluated by U.S.F.S. EMTs who determined that the head injury should be seen by a doctor. The crewmember was transported via medivac helicopter from the fire to the hospital in Phoenix, AZ for further evaluation. The crewmember was in the hospital overnight and was released on the morning of 7/14/24 with instructions to rest for 1 day before returning to the Crew.

incidents.name: Falls Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A firefighter experienced a heat related injury while assigned to the Falls Fire, Malheur National Forest, Oregon. Incident medical personnel responded and the firefighter was transported to the hospital, treated and released on 7/16/24.

incidents.name: Horse Gulch Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A hand crewmember engaged in mop-up on the Horse Gulch Fire, Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest, Montana, experienced heat related illness. The crew member was wearing multiple wool & cotton layers on top and bottom to avoid insect bites/stings. Additional layers were worn on day shift in high-90s weather conditions. Assigned EMTs assisted, and the crewmember was transported to the hospital with an incident-assigned ambulance. The crewmember was treated and released on 7/16/24.

incidents.name: Horse Gulch Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: While engaged in line construction on the Horse Gulch Fire, Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest, Montana, a sawyer on a handcrew lost control of their chainsaw/saw powerhead and the chain encountered his gloved hand as it came to a stop, resulting in cuts on thumb and finger. The sawyer was supported by EMTs as well as the incident Medical Unit Leader (MEDL) who asked sawyer to go to the hospital due to the loose skin that needed to be excised. The sawyer was driven to the hospital and was treated and released.

incidents.name: Buckhorn Fire Dehydration Illness
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an engine module was working on indirect fireline construction on the Buckhorn Fire, San Carlos Agency, Arizona, when the crewmember became nauseous and experienced vomiting and diarrhea. Line medics assessed patient and called in a "yellow" medical. The crewmember was transported via incident ground ambulance to the hospital and were treated and released the same day (7/17/24). The following day was a normal day off, the crewmember was back to work on 7/19/24.

incidents.name: Shelly Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: A crewmember from an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) assigned to the Shelly Fire, Klamath National Forest, California, was hit by rock and received lacerations to their face. The crewmember was taken by ground ambulance to the hospital, given stitches, and released.

incidents.name: Moose Fire Helicopter Accident
incidents.summary: On July 21, 2022, a Boeing CH-47D helicopter assigned to the Moose Fire crashed into the Salmon River near the Indianola Work Center in Idaho. Numerous firefighters swam across the Salmon River to extract the pilots and provide first aid care; sadly, both pilots, Jared Bird and Thomas Hayes, succumbed to their injuries.
incidents.quote: Moose Fire Helicopter Accident

incidents.name: Pioneer Fire UTV Accident
incidents.summary: On July 21, 2024, three members of a camp crew on the Pioneer Fire on the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest were involved in a UTV accident when the driver lost control and crashed into the side railing of a wooden bridge. One patient had altered mental status, one had a hematoma on the forehead and one had a possibly fractured forearm. Due to the remoteness of the accident, the patients were flown by helicopter to local medical facilities.
incidents.quote: “I was going too fast and couldn’t make the turn.”

incidents.name: Apache Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A crewmember from an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) on the Apache Fire, Los Padres National Forest, California, experienced heat-related illness (HRI). The crewmember was taken by ground ambulance to the hospital, treated and released.

incidents.name: Apache Fire Saw Gas Exposure Chemical Burns
incidents.summary: A crewmember from an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) on the Apache Fir, Los Padres National Forest, California, experienced a chemical burn from saw gas. The crewmember was taken to the hospital, treated, released and advised to follow up with burn center.

incidents.name: Falls Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: An engine assigned to night shift on the Falls Fire, Malheur National Forest, Oregon, was directed to assess and prep a historic structure. A firefighter used a chainsaw to open the road for the engine, deciding to do this brief task without wearing chainsaw chaps. Once at the structure, saw operations continued still without protective chaps. The chainsaw experienced kickback, striking the firefighter on the leg immediately above the knee. The firefighter was taken to the hospital where the wound received 78 stitches.
incidents.quote: “At first, I thought it just cut my pants,” the firefighter said. “Until I looked down and saw blood.”

incidents.name: Clearwater Fire Fall and Seizure
incidents.summary: A firefighter/paramedic assigned to a Wildland Fire Module (WFM) experienced a seizure after a fall in Riverton, Wyoming. Module was en route the Clearwater Fire on the Shoshone National Forest. The firefighter was flown to the ICU in Casper, WY and was stable and intubated upon admission. As of 7/28/24, the firefighter had been moved from the ICU to the neurology ward. A lengthy recovery is expected.

incidents.name: Bridge Creek Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: On July 22, 2024, a bulldozer was assigned to build indirect line. The Heavy Equipment Boss and Dozer Operator walked around the area on foot to establish a plan. After talking it over they decided where to start and began work. As the line was being pushed the Dozer Operator felt his blade hit a rock and he lifted the blade to pass over the rock. Once he believed he was past the rock and his tracks were stable, the Dozer Operator put his blade back down and began to push again. He was not aware that the entire dozer was on a large rock face. As the Dozer Operator began to push, he lost all control of his machine. The dozer began an uncontrolled slide down the rock face eventually rolling over and coming to rest on its cab.
incidents.quote: He was not aware that the entire dozer was on a large rock face. As the Dozer Operator began to push again, he lost all control of his machine. The dozer began an uncontrolled slide down the rock face.

incidents.name: Gold Fire Heat Related Illness
incidents.summary: A crewmember from an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) experienced heat-related illness (HRI) on the Gold Complex, Plumas National Forest, California. The crewmember was taken by ground ambulance to the hospital, treated and released.

incidents.name: Miller Peak Fire Heat Related Injury
incidents.summary: A member of the catering staff on the Miller Peak Fire, Lolo National Forest, Montana, went to the incident medical unit complaining of dehydration and muscle cramps. Patient was extremely sweaty, with a rapid heart rate. Patient vitals included extremely high blood pressure, and the individual has a family history of high blood pressure and heart issues. The patient was transported by incident ambulance to the hospital, treated and released the same day.

incidents.name: Microwave Tower Fire Fall Injuries
incidents.summary: A crewmember from an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) on the Microwave Tower Fire, Oregon, fell and was suspected to have broken ribs. The firefighter was taken to the hospital and no fractured ribs/bones were diagnosed. The crewmember was released to several days of light duty.

incidents.name: Cougar Fire Communication Issues
incidents.summary: A recurring radio anomaly occurred on the Cougar Fire in Washington, causing repeaters to be "locked" open, prohibiting individuals from transmitting for extended periods of time. After troubleshooting a number of possibilities, the issue was isolated to a base station radio unit that was placed in a staging area under a covered porch near a structure. Lawn sprinklers in the area which were believed to have been turned off, were spraying in the area of the radio, just enough to dampen the base station and cause an open mic. Once this radio was removed from the network, the anomaly issue was resolved.

incidents.name: Apache Fire Ash Pit Burn Injury
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember experienced an ash pit burn to their legs on the Apache Fire, Los Padres National Forest, California. The burns were initially thought to be first degree/superficial burns. The following day, the firefighter was sent to a level 1 trauma center and then a burn center. Eventually, the diagnosis was some second degree/partial thickness burns, with third degree/full thickness burns on back of calves. A follow-up appointment at a burn center is set for 8/8/2024.

incidents.name: Bench Lake Fire Medical Emergency Extraction
incidents.summary: On July 25, a medical incident occurred involving a patient experiencing shortness of breath and chest tightness near the remote Fishhook Trail while working on the Bench Lake Fire, Sawtooth National Forest, Idaho. The emergency response involved a coordinated effort between a Type 1 hotshot crew EMT, firefighters on-the-ground, and air ambulances. The use of a wheeled litter for patient extraction was critical in ensuring timely and efficient transport to definitive care.
incidents.quote: A “Yellow” Incident Within an Incident (IWI) was called into Great Basin Complex Incident Management Team 4 Communications, reporting a patient experiencing shortness of breath and chest tightness.

incidents.name: Falls Fire SEAT Crash Fatality
incidents.summary: A single engine airtanker went missing on July 25th, 2024 while working in the vicinity of the Falls Fire, on the Malheur National Forest. The aircraft struck terrain approximately 30 nautical miles from the Burns Municipal Airport while setting up for a third drop. Following the conclusion of search efforts, the US Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management issued a joint news release to report the death of the pilot, James Bailey Maxwell.
incidents.quote: The trailing pilot turned to the west and saw the accident pilot maneuver his airplane to a trailing position behind him. A few seconds later, the pilot lost sight of the accident airplane.

incidents.name: Cherry Creek Fire Insect Sting
incidents.summary: A crewmember of a Type 2 crew stepped on a wasp nest and received multiple stings on the Cherry Creek Fire, Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The crew was engaged in night-time initial attack cutting fire line and clearing brush. The crewmember started to experience allergic reaction and had difficulty breathing. A Forest Service EMT provided epinephrine. Firefighter was transported from fire to hospital by ground ambulance, dispatched through Grangeville Interagency Dispatch and Idaho County. The firefighter was released from hospital/ER later that night.

incidents.name: Frazier Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On 7/25/24 a member of a contract engine crew was hit by a tree on the Malheur National Forest. The patient remained alert and conscious with tingling and pain. An Oregon National Guard Blackhawk was utilized to medevac the firefighter to Boise, Idaho. Once at the hospital, initial diagnosis included a burst-fractured vertebrae and a broken ankle (requiring surgery). Diagnosis was updated later to include damage to several vertebrae and a broken scapula. As of 7/29/24, the firefighter was still in the hospital.

incidents.name: Big Horn Fire Vehicle and Equipment Issues
incidents.summary: It's the end of July in Eastern Washington. An engine boss arrives on the Big Horn Fire and experiences a series of vehicle and equipment issues. Things can fail when you need them most. Know your equipment. Know how it operates. Know how to fix it.
incidents.quote: While assigned as the Engine Boss on the Big Horn Fire in Kittitas County, they encountered multiple mechanical and safety issues with the brush truck, including an inaccurate fuel gauge, missing gear, a venting chainsaw, and a pump that became hydro‑locked due to a faulty fuel shut‑off. After temporary fixes and a long trip to replace a broken spark plug, additional failures led them to recommend the truck be taken out of service. A disagreement with the Strike Team Leader followed, they were reassigned, and the truck was ultimately retired.

incidents.name: Battle Mountain Complex Narrow Escape
incidents.summary: On July 27, 2024, Crew 8, a Type 2 hand crew, is assigned with two other hand crews to line a slopover on the Battle Mountain Complex in northeastern Oregon. Crew 8 begins working in an area downhill from their identified safety zone, when fire behavior increases at 1300. With rollout and snags falling into the green, the crew begins to fire around their position and consider shelter deployment. Shortly after, helicopters cool down their location and a READ in the area scouts an escape route for the crew back to their vehicles. There were no injuries.
incidents.quote: The crew is experiencing snags falling around them. One tree trunk rolls into the green, throwing sparks and starting spot fires around them.

incidents.name: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF Crush Injury
incidents.summary: A fire lookout was as assisting other firefighters in clearing trees that had fallen during the severe thunderstorm/wind event that impacted Region 1 on 7/24/24. As firefighters worked to open a trail, the lookout was helping roll a cut round, when the cut tree slid and pinched her hand between the round and the cut end. Trained Forest Service personnel provided medical support, and mobilized a USFS-contracted helicopter for the medevac. Once at the hospital, the firefighter was admitted for continued monitoring due to concerns of potential development of Compartment Syndrome / Crush Injury Rhabdomyolysis from significant swelling, and elevated Creatine Kinase (CK). The firefighter was still hospitalized as of 7/29/2024. A Rapid Lesson Sharing (RLS) may be conducted on this incident.
incidents.quote: The lookout was helping roll a cut round, when the cut tree slid and pinched her hand between the round and the cut end.

incidents.name: Devils Gulch Fire IWI
incidents.summary: A medical emergency on the Devil's Gulch Fire necessitated the use of the local rappel helicopter and an air ambulance to get the patient to a nearby medical clinic. Due to prior training for these types of Incident within Incidents, those involved including the Dispatch Center, the helicopter manager, the pilot, the Unit Aviation Officer and the Forest Duty officer communicated quickly and efficiently to complete the medevac.
incidents.quote: Within minutes, the medical was elevated to a “Red” or critical.

incidents.name: Italian Fire Firefighters Struck by Water Drop
incidents.summary: Two engine crewmembers were struck by a Type 1 Helicopter water drop while performing fire suppression duties on the Italian Fire on the Sierra National Forest. Initially, no injuries were reported. However, over the next few days, the two engine crewmembers had complaints of sore necks and one had numbness and tingling in their arm.
incidents.quote: On this drop, the water forcefully impacted two unsuspecting ENG3 crewmembers located on the road conducting mop-up operations.

incidents.name: Willamette NF Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A firefighter was hit by a limb or debris during tree felling operations. The strike resulted in a loss of consciousness and lacerations. The firefighter regained consciousness and walked to a waiting ambulance, and was transported to the hospital, where the firefighter was treated and released.

incidents.name: Bluff Creek Complex Fall Injuries
incidents.summary: A firefighter was performing mop-up in steep terrain and fell on the Bluff Creek Complex, Idaho Panhandle National Forest. Forest Service EMTs including a paramedic from an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) performed initial medical treatment and a short-haul helicopter and an air ambulance were used to get the firefighter to the hospital. The firefighter was treated and released with follow-up required.

incidents.name: Cherry Creek Fire Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: On the Cherry Creek Fire, a crewmember on a Type 2 crew experienced severe stomach and abdominal pain. The individual was transported from the fire to emergency room via agency vehicle, accompanied by a fellow crew member. At the hospital the firefighter was diagnosed with appendicitis after diagnostic testing. The firefighter was admitted to the hospital 7/30 and had surgery (appendectomy) the following morning. The firefighter was released later that day 7/31 and cleared by doctor to travel home.

incidents.name: Borel Fire Dozer Rollover RLS
incidents.summary: On July 30, 2024 the Borel Fire had slopped over and was burning uphill toward a mid-slope road on Division H. Strike Team members were not comfortable sending people down into the drainage to go direct in order to anchor into the fire and instead decided to build dozer line along a ridgetop that ran perpendicular to the road. Crew called for dozer E-47 to report to the area to begin work. As E-47 proceeded downhill off the ridge, the dozer started to slide a bit. As the operator attempted to maneuver back where he came from, the dozer began to roll down the hill - rolling six or seven times until it stopped. The medics and Strike Team members packaged the patient and initiated transport via helicopter hoist.
incidents.quote: As the operator attempted to maneuver back where he came from, the dozer began to roll down the hill - rolling six or seven times until it stopped.

incidents.name: Swawilla Fire Wing Strike
incidents.summary: On July 31, 2024, two Washington DNR 802 Fire Boss Water Scoopers were assisting with the suppression of the Swawilla Fire in northeastern Washington state, near the town of Keller, WA. One of the Fire Bosses descended to the Columbia River and filled its tank. As it began to ascend, the aircraft struck a utility line that was stretched across the river. After the impact, the pilot continued his ascent and alerted Air Attack of the wire strike. All three aircraft (the two Fire Bosses and the Air Attack platform) decided to fly to Grand Coulee Airport, where the aircraft safely landed.
incidents.quote: As it began to ascend, the aircraft struck a utility line that was stretched across the river.

incidents.name: Pyramid Fire Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: A firefighter experienced an allergic reaction after a bee sting. A line paramedic was present and administered epinephrine. After the treatment on the line, the firefighter was able to walk out to the ambulance for transport to the hospital. The firefighter was treated and released.

incidents.name: Crazy Creek Fire Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: On the Crazy Creek Fire, Ochoco National Forest, a contracted firefighter experienced a suspected heart attack and was flown by air ambulance to the hospital. Once at the hospital, the firefighter was diagnosed with a heat related illness and released.

incidents.name: Durkee Fire Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) assigned to the Durkee Fire, Oregon, was transported to the hospital in Ontario, OR, for a suspected internal infection, and was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis. The crew member was hospitalized for 4 days. He was admitted to the hospital on 8/3/24 at 0500. He was discharged on 8/6/24 at 1230.

incidents.name: Nez Perce-Clearwater NF Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: On the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest, a firefighter was refurbishing equipment from a recent fire assignment as part of post-incident rehab work. The firefighter was stung by wasps and experienced a severe allergic reaction, with symptoms including hives and difficulty breathing. Both an air ambulance and USFS helicopter with EMT were ordered due to the remote location. An Air ambulance flight nurse administered epinephrine, and the firefighter was flown to hospital in Lewiston, ID. The firefighter was treated in the ER and released later the evening of 8/2.

incidents.name: Stockade Canyon Fire Helicopter Incident
incidents.summary: Aircraft and crew were returning from the Stockade Canyon fire when they experienced an emergency that necessitated an autorotation into a field. All were transported to local hospital for evaluation and released.

incidents.name: Limepoint Fire Burned Vehicle
incidents.summary: On August 2, 2024 at approximately 1600, fire behavior on the Limepoint Fire started picking up in Division Papa. Division Papa’s and Branch’s vehicles were both parked in a small bare dirt clearing outside the fireline near a pile of hose and pumps. As the trees around the area torched out, an ember landed in and ignited that pile of hose. Division Papa’s vehicle was parked within 10 feet of these supplies. Division Papa’s vehicle received fire/heat damage to: the passenger side front quarter panel; both the front and rear door passenger’s-side; the left front side of the grill; and front passenger-side tire.
incidents.quote: Attempts were made by a UTV with a water tank to hose down the burning supplies and the vehicle—but the area became too hot and the UTV had to retreat from that area.

incidents.name: Chicopee Memorial State Park Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On August 2, 2024 three firefighters from a Massachusetts state district were removing smaller trees with chainsaws to make room to park their trailer and store other items at Chicopee Memorial State Park. As they were clearing the slash, a dead limb from a green tree broke off and struck one of firefighters in the helmet/shoulder, knocking him to the ground. As the firefighter was wearing proper PPE, he only received minor injuries.
incidents.quote: As they were clearing the slash, a dead limb from a green tree broke off and struck one of firefighters in the helmet/shoulder, knocking him to the ground.

incidents.name: Wolf Creek Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) was felling a tree in hot ash and sustained burn injuries to feet while assigned to the Wolf Creek Fire, Payette National Forest, Idaho. The injury, which took some time to emerge, was initially assessed by crew EMT and then line medic as a green medical (blistering) and treated on site. The following day (8/4) it was re-assessed as a yellow burn injury and patient was transported to a local hospital in Cascade, ID. The local hospital conducted a virtual consultation with the University of Utah Burn Center. He was diagnosed with second degree/partial thickness burns to both feet. The crewmember rested for several days before travelling home on 8/7/24 with instructions to rest and follow-up with the University of Utah Burn Center.

incidents.name: Crazy Creek Fire Spike Camp Incidents Within an Incident (IWI) RLS
incidents.summary: While sleeping in the designated sleeping area on the Crazy Creek Fire, Ochoco National Forest, Oregon, a crewmember from an interagency hotshot crew (IHC) was run over by a vehicle. Initially suspected to have significant leg injuries, the firefighter was taken by ground ambulance to the hospital. The crewmember was treated and released with a week to 10 days of light duty.
incidents.quote: Trying not to wake anyone at such an early hour, he turns off his headlights and proceeds to slowly drive through the camp on the peripheral gravel road...shortly after leaving the gravel road to park his pickup and set up his camp, the driver hears a scream.

incidents.name: Crazy Creek Fire Suspected Heart Attack Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: A firefighter experienced a suspected heart attack while assigned to the Crazy Creek Fire, Ochoco National Forest, Oregon. The firefighter was flown to Bend, OR and admitted to the hospital overnight for observation. A cardiac issue requiring surgery was detected and a procedure was conducted.

incidents.name: Kootenai National Forest Physical Training Injury
incidents.summary: An engine crewmember was performing physical training (PT) earlier in the week and believed they pulled or strained a muscle. As the crewmember’s pain increased later in the week, they opted to go get checked out on 8/6/24. The crewmember was transported by agency vehicle to the hospital, was diagnosed with a sprain/strain, and released with no follow-up.

incidents.name: Bucktail Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A swamper from an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) assigned to the Bucktail Fire, Grand Mesa Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forest, was swamping brush and contacted the moving saw chain with a gloved hand. USFS EMTs provided initial medical support. Based on several factors (distance to hospital, limited ambulances on the incident) the swamper was transported in a Colorado State/Division of Fire Protection and Control (DFPC) helicopter to the airport in Montrose, CO. A ground ambulance from airport to hospital completed the medical transport. The firefighter was treated for lacerations to palm of hand, which required stiches. The firefighter was released after this treatment.

incidents.name: Whisky Creek Fire Insect Sting
incidents.summary: A crewmember on a hand crew was stung by a bee during mop-up operations on the Whisky Creek Fire, Mt. Hood National Forest, Oregon. Benadryl was administered twice, but swelling continued. Incident EMT provided treatment on scene, and an assigned ambulance transported the crewmember to the hospital. The crewmember was treated and released; no follow-up needed.

incidents.name: Coffee Can Saddle Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: Wildland fire fighter was struck by a snag and sustained severe injuries, resulting in permanent disability. Crew members worked tirelessly without adequate trauma response equipment (which was present but could not be located in the rig) and successfully transported the patient by foot, then truck, to ambulance and air support. Patient underwent 6 surgeries over 16 months and returned home to Idaho in December 2026.
incidents.quote: “When the tree struck him, it hit his head and shoulder, causing him to get folded over, and then shoved him headfirst into another tree.”

incidents.name: Warner Peak Fire Trailer Hitch Crushed Finger
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Warner Peak Fire, Hart Mountain National Antelope Refuge, was hooking up a trailer as a piece of the hitch got stuck. While working to unstick the hitch, the trailer dropped onto the hitch, crushing the top of his middle finger (including nail and tip of bone.) The firefighter was transported to Lakeview, Oregon and received stiches and was released on the same day.

incidents.name: Schenk Prescribed Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On August 13, 2024, a skid steer operator with nearly 30 years of experience was working pushing dead and down debris away from a road on the Schenk Prescribed Fire. At one point, the operator selected a tree, grabbed the end of the tree with the grapple, and began pushing the tree into the burn unit’s interior. The tree, met with resistance from the windrow, slipped off his grapple and impacted the lower portion of the skid steer door, breaking through the one-half inch polycarbonate glass, and struck the operator on the right thigh about three inches above the knee. Within minutes, an engine captain arrived on scene to assess the incident. Upon examination, they discovered a five-inch laceration to the operator’s upper right thigh.
incidents.quote: The tree impacted the lower portion of the skid steer door, broke through the one-half inch polycarbonate glass and struck the operator on the right thigh, about three inches above the knee.

incidents.name: Crest Trail Fire Hit by Log
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an engine assigned to the Crest Trail Fire, Coronado National Forest, had bucked up a large (30 inch) tree into 2-foot sections and placed those to the side. Work on the fire was continuing when the crewmember heard a noise and looked up to see one of the rounds rolling down the hill approximately 30 feet above him. The crewmember attempted to avoid the rolling round but lost his footing, fell into a prone position facing uphill, and was struck on top of the hard hat by the round. The crewmember experienced neck pain, bi-lateral shoulder/arm numbness, disorientation, and later developed nausea as the disorientation improved. A paramedic met the patient as an agency vehicle moved the crewmember 8 miles to the helispot. The crewmember was flown by helicopter from Portal, Arizona to Saint Joseph’s Hospital in Tucson, AZ. The crewmember was evaluated and released at ~2400hrs on 08/15/24 with a referral to a neurosurgeon for evaluation and completion of an MRI.
incidents.quote: The crewmember attempted to avoid the rolling round but lost his footing, fell into a prone position facing uphill, and was struck on top of the hard hat by the round.

incidents.name: Limepoint Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: After explaining my cut plan to my saw partner, I bored into the tree, and it started off as planned. Watching my kerf, it remained open until I was 90-95 percent of the way through the tree. At that point, the stump roots gave way—causing the tree to release from the stump. It swung on the downhill side of the stump not the uphill as anticipated. The tree swung toward the trunk of the tree it was hung up in, while the top held in place. The top then released directly back toward the stump and me.
incidents.quote: " I lost my footing and the second top fell into my secondary escape route and caught the left heel of my foot— scissoring my ankle on another downed log"

incidents.name: Cypress Fire Dozer Rollover
