incidents.summary: On August 17, 2024, at approximately 1820 hours, a CAL FIRE Bulldozer was assigned to a vegetation fire east of Cambria in San Luis Obispo County, California. While working in Division Whiskey, the bulldozer was involved in a rollover and sustained major damage. The Heavy Fire Equipment Operator (HFEO) self-extricated and was transported to Twin Cities Community Hospital with minor injuries. The HFEO was released to full duty after an evaluation.
incidents.quote: When high blading, the blade should be kept low to help lower the center of gravity and detect objects that are not visible.

incidents.name: Willamette Complex South Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: A faller on the Willamette Complex South, Willamette National Forest, experienced a chainsaw laceration to several fingers. Initial treatment was provided by the IMT medical unit, and the faller was transported via ground ambulance to Sacred Heart Medical Center in Springfield, Oregon. Upon arrival, the faller was evaluated (X-rays), treated (stiches) and released back to full duty (on 8/17/24) with instructions to follow-up with a hand surgeon in a several weeks.

incidents.name: Diamond Complex Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Diamond Complex, Umpqua National Forest, Oregon, was felling a 6" diameter tree and when it landed it sprang back and struck him in the face. The injured firefighter was assessed on the line, and the firefighter was transported to ICP. Initial diagnosis included cuts, bruises and some broken teeth. The firefighter was transported by ground ambulance and diagnosed with a broken upper palate and released.

incidents.name: Diamond Complex Long Line Incident
incidents.summary: A helicopter carrying a blivit sling load misjudged wind and tree height conditions resulting in the load striking the trees below. Radio traffic was very congested with the complexity of several fires in the complex. The sling load was released into the trees below and was damaged.
incidents.quote: Because the radio was so busy, he was unsure if he heard his traffic. The helicopter proceeded toward the sling site but was much too low for the height of the trees.

incidents.name: Warner Peak Fire Rollover
incidents.summary: At approximately 1450 hours on Tuesday, August 19th, 2024, a septage vacuum truck rolled over while traveling south on Lake County Rd. 3-13, west of the Warren Peak Fire. The operator lost control of the vehicle when entering a downhill, slight right-hand turn. An immediate incident within an incident response was initiated and the operator was transported via ambulance to Lakeview Hospital. The operator sustained broken bones and the vehicle was destroyed.
incidents.quote: The operator lost control of the vehicle when entering a downhill, slight right-hand turn.

incidents.name: Illinois Bee Sting Fatality
incidents.summary: A Shawnee National Forest employee, Austin Davidson, died after being stung by bees. Working in a lowland management area, Austin and a coworker were clearing brush utilizing weed trimmers. Austin came upon a concealed ground nest, the bees were disturbed, and an attack response was provoked. The bees stung multiple times delivering a large amount of bee venom that led to an unrecognized medical emergency that resulted in death roughly five hours after the incident.
incidents.quote: This accident could have occurred on any forest, to any field-going employee.

incidents.name: Hobson Fire Fall Head Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Hobson Fire, Nevada BLM, slipped and fell, resulting in combative, atypical behavior. The firefighter was taken to the hospital in Ely, NV. Diagnosis included a concussion, dehydration and a twisted knee. The firefighter was released on 8/20/24 after diagnosis and treatment.

incidents.name: Coffee Pot Fire Concussion
incidents.summary: While working on the Coffee Pot Fire, Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Park, a crewmember on a Type II Crew lost consciousness briefly after being hit in the head by a branch thrown by a crew swamper. The crewmember was transported to the hospital and treated and released.

incidents.name: Wapiti Fire Camp Evacuation
incidents.summary: Fire spread modeling predicted that the Wapiti Fire would impact the Warm Springs forward operating base (FOB). In the midst of team transitions, the decision was made to relocate the FOB outside the probable fire growth area, to Valley Creek. Some fire personnel remained at the Warm Springs site on August 23 to implement some defensive firing to protect the equipment left on site, after which they evacuated the site as well. After the flaming front had passed, IMT members returned to the site to find that one yurt had burned, and with no other significant damage to incident supplies or equipment.
incidents.quote: The incident at Valley Creek highlights the critical importance of collaborative decision-making and sharing assumptions, especially when relying on models. How do you use modeling to make decisions?

incidents.name: Oregon Initial Attack Pinned Firefighter
incidents.summary: An Initial Attack crew was constructing line and needed to remove an approximate 36-inch DBH buckskin Douglas fir tree with its root wad attached to continue line construction. The sawyer voiced his plan to buck the tree and instructed everyone to clear the area in case the tree rolled. Unknown to the sawyer, the swamper was below the root wad portion. The tree rolled and pinned the swamper.
incidents.quote: When the tree rolled, the root wad folded the swamper awkwardly in half—pinning him to the ground under the root wad with his head against his left boot

incidents.name: Sharrott Creek Fire Hit by Rock
incidents.summary: While engaged in fireline construction on the Sharrott Creek Fire, Bitterroot National Forest, Montana, a crewmember on a hand crew was on a road when a rock came down the hill striking him near his armpit sending him roughly 50ft down the hill below the road where he came in contact with a tree.

incidents.name: Wapiti Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: During burnout operations on the Wapiti Fire, Boise National Forest, a member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) suffered a dislocated elbow. The crewmember fell and tried to catch themselves with an outstretched arm.

incidents.name: Park Fire ICP Carbon Monoxide Exposure
incidents.summary: At a brand new ICP on the Park Fire in Northern California, generators were placed close to the main concentration of ICP trailers, known as "Main Street." Safety Officers expressed concern at the close proximity and smell of exhaust. On September 1, an occupant of a trailer closest to the generators showed symptoms of possible carbon monoxide exposure. After evaluation, they were deemed to have had a medical issue that lead to the high blood level of CO. The generators were moved as far from the trailers as power cables would allow.
incidents.quote: An occupant of a trailer closest to the generators showed symptoms of possible carbon monoxide exposure, including a very high reading of CO in the blood.

incidents.name: Sharrott Creek Fire Crushed Finger
incidents.summary: While building a pump site for portable pump operations in a creek on the Sharrott Creek Fire, Bitterroot National Forest, a firefighter suffered a crushed finger injury. One firefighter passed a rock to another firefighter, and as they were receiving the rock, the second firefighter lost his balance and crushed his finger between the rock he was being passed and another rock on the ground. After receiving initial care at an emergency room, the firefighter had a follow-up consultation with an orthopedic surgeon on 9/8. Due to the condition of the finger, the surgeon recommended amputation of the fingertip (above the distal joint).

incidents.name: Daly Fire Vehicle Tree Strike
incidents.summary: They drove west looking for the felling module’s truck to indicate the area in which the fallers were working. During their drive, a tree fell onto their truck. The tree struck the hood of the truck and went over the truck’s cab and box.

incidents.name: Sheep Fire Hit by Log
incidents.summary: An Assistant Fire Engine Operator (AFEO) was mopping-up on the middle to upper third of the slope, moving hose around and spraying water, when a huge log rolled onto her foot, spun her around, knocked her over, and rolled right over the back of her head. Those on scene packaged her in a position of comfort in a “MegaMover” and lined out down the slope. The T2IA, IHC, and Engine Crew personnel utilized the “conveyor” patient transport method to carry her down the slope, across the river, and up to a pickup truck on the road. They carefully drove a bumpy forest road to an awaiting agency helicopter. The AFEO’s injuries included a skull fracture and concussion, soft tissue injuries to ribs and her left hand, and a sprained knee.
incidents.quote: An Assistant Fire Engine Operator (AFEO) was mopping-up on the middle to upper third of the slope, moving hose around and spraying water, when a huge log rolled onto her foot, spun her around, knocked her over, and rolled right over the back of her head

incidents.name: Boulder Fire Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: A member of the incident management team (IMT) on the Boulder Fire, Boise National Forest, began having chest pains while at ICP. The IMT member was transported to Cascade, Idaho by ground ambulance for further evaluation. No additional information.

incidents.name: Black Eagle Fire Tripping Injury
incidents.summary: A Medical Unit Leader (MEDL) on the Black Eagle Fire, Salmon-Challis National Forest, Idaho, tripped over a railroad tie bridge and suffered a broken leg (broke the top of the tibia). After diagnosis, the MEDL was released and transported home.

incidents.name: Snag Fire Sawyer Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A sawyer suffered burns when the chainsaw he was operating ignited. He had just refueled. It appears the quarter-turn “toolless” fuel cap was not fully aligned, seated, and sealed when he flipped the saw to carry it over his shoulder. Fuel poured out of the tank and was ignited by open flame.

incidents.name: Coffee Pot Fire Fall Injury
incidents.summary: A crewmember from a Wildland Fire Module (WFM) assigned to the Coffee Pot Fire, Sequoia-Kings Canyon National Park, slipped and fell and injured lower back and right leg. The crewmember was medevacked via helicopter to Visalia, California. The crewmember was treated and released with several medications and light duty restrictions.

incidents.name: Fosset Gulch Prescribed Fire Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: During routine operations of the Fosset Gulch Prescribed Fire, a .05-acre spot fire occurred on adjacent private lands. The spot was contained and extinguished quickly with resources on-scene and caused no concerns from the landowner or the Archuleta County Sheriff’s Office.

incidents.name: Watch Valley Fire Valley Fever
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an R1 engine crew was digging fireline on the Watch Valley Fire, San Carlos BIA, while working in close proximity to Type 1 helicopters. The area consisted of high traffic and dust. Crewmember inhaled fungal spores found in the ground and released into the air when disturbed. Employee visited the emergency room initially followed by doctor and lung specialist visits. The employee did receive a positive test result for Valley Fever.

incidents.name: Bachelor Complex Unresponsive Crewmember
incidents.summary: On the morning of Thursday, September 12, 2024, a Bureau of Land Management crewmember, was found unresponsive and is believed to have suffered from carbon monoxide poisoning from a heating device in an unventilated tent. Prior to the incident, the crew member had been mobilized on the Bachelor Complex Wildfire for three shifts. The crew member was transported to a hospital in Bend, Oregon.

incidents.name: Lane 1 Fire Heavy Equipment Rollover
incidents.summary: An equipment operator running a road vibrating compactor roller, ventured too close to a soft shoulder while doing repair work on Bureau of Land Management (BLM) ground on the Lane 1 Fire located southeast of Cottage Grove, Oregon. As the roller started to tip over, the operator was able to jump free and the equipment rolled end-over-end approximately 150 feet down an 85 percent slope, hitting numerous trees and receiving massive damage. The operator was unhurt.
incidents.quote: The machine rolled multiple times, hitting several large trees before coming to a stop in several large pieces.

incidents.name: Airport Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: Eight members were injured, six were critically injured and transported to area hospitals.
incidents.quote: Eight OCFA Handcrew members were returning from battling the Airport Fire when they were involved in a rollover crash on a freeway.

incidents.name: Rail Ridge Fire Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: A member of the incident camp crew on the Rail Ridge Fire, Ochoco National Forest experienced a medical emergency influenced by new medication and heat illness/injury. The crewmember was taken by ambulance to John Day, Oregon and admitted until 9/20/2024.

incidents.name: Willamette Complex South Medical Emergency
incidents.summary: While at a drop point on the Willamette South Fire, Willamette National Forest, a member of a hand crew was experiencing chest pains and asked the staged ambulance for some aspirin. The paramedic conducted further assessment and in short order, the firefighter was connected to the EKG on the ambulance. The EKG revealed the firefighter was experiencing or had experienced a heart attack. A medevac response ensued, where the firefighter was taken to Crescent, Oregon by ambulance, and then by helicopter to Bend, Oregon for surgery. The firefighter was released from the hospital on 9/25/2024.

incidents.name: Lava Fire Sawyer Hit by Log
incidents.summary: A member of an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) on the Lava Fire, Boise National Forest, was bucking a log from the downhill side when the log rolled over and pinched his lower left leg. The crewmember was stabilized on the scene and flown by agency helicopter to Saint Alphonsus Hospital in Boise, Idaho. The crewmember’s left leg was suspected to be broken, but upon examination, no broken bones were found. Tissue damage was diagnosed. The crewmember was released with light duty restrictions.

incidents.name: Airtanker Retardant Loading Carbon Monoxide Emissions
incidents.summary: On June 24, 2024, a carbon monoxide (CO) sensor installed on a BAe-146 Airtanker at the Colorado Springs Airtanker Base indicated concentrations at—or above—the Occupational Safety and Health Administration’s (OSHA) threshold for CO. Five days later, high CO readings were once again identified inside a BAe-146 Airtanker at the Colorado Springs Airtanker Base. These high concentration readings were taken from inside the cockpits during retardant loading operations. The pilots properly vented the aircraft to allow the contaminate to escape and the airtanker personnel completed both missions without incident.
incidents.quote: [A] carbon monoxide (CO) sensor installed on a BAe-146 Airtanker at the Colorado Springs Airtanker Base indicated concentrations at—or above—the Occupational Safety and Health Administration’s (OSHA) threshold for CO.

incidents.name: Coffee Pot Fire Laceration
incidents.summary: A crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) suffered a laceration to the face on the Coffee Pot Fire, Sequoia & Kings Canyon National Park. A “yellow” incident-within-an incident (IWC) was called in, and an air ambulance requested. Eventually, the crewmember was transported by ground to local medical facility where they were treated and released.

incidents.name: Winnemucca Staging Heart Attack
incidents.summary: A firefighter staging for initial attack in Winnemucca, NV experienced a heart attack and was transported by ground ambulance to local hospital, and then to Reno, NV. The firefighter was diagnosed with a minor heart attack, and two blocked arteries, both of which required surgery for placement of stints. The firefighter was released from the hospital 8/28 and flew back home on 8/29/24.

incidents.name: Goosmus Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: On the evening of September 28, 2024, at approximately 2005 hours, a vehicle from a Washington Department of Natural Resources (DNR) handcrew experienced a vehicle rollover incident while returning from fire operations on Upper Danville Road, near the Goosmus Fire in Danville, Washington. The vehicle was a Ford F-350 crew cab, with an enclosed utility bed, and four occupants. Due to the nighttime driving conditions combined with heavy dust kicked up by the convoy vehicles up ahead, visibility was significantly impaired. The driver misjudged a curve on the road, causing the front left tire to slip off the soft shoulder. All crew members exited the vehicle safely through the rear driver’s side window. Minor abrasions from their seat belts were reported by two individuals.
incidents.quote: After attempting to correct the vehicle’s course, both left tires went off the road, resulting in a rollover down a 25foot embankment.

incidents.name: Willamette Complex After Hours ICP Medical Incident
incidents.fire: Willamette Fire Complex South (formerly Oakridge Lightning Fires)
incidents.summary: On September 29, at the Incident Command Post (ICP) for the Willamette Complex, Oregon, a 70-year-old member of the Incident Management Team (IMT) awoke at 0239 feeling dizzy with pressure in their chest. Calling the Incident-Within-an-Incident (IWI) Emergency Phone Number printed on the cover of the Incident Action Plan, the IMT member activated a medical response that promptly handled the situation and got the IMT member to definitive care. The IMT member was back at work later that day.
incidents.quote: The team member knew that if consciousness was lost, they may not be found for several hours.

incidents.name: Hurricane Helene Response Hit by Tree Limb
incidents.summary: While clearing road access on the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, Georgia, during Hurricane Helene response, a firefighter was cutting out a hazard tree and a limb struck him in the head hard enough to break his hard hat. A USFS EMT was in the immediate area and provided initial medical support. The injured firefighter was transported via USFS vehicle to Chattanooga, TN. After diagnosis of fractured skull (no surgery needed) and a concussion, the firefighter was released on the evening of 9/30/24. As the firefighter was driving home, they felt ill and returned to the hospital and spent the night for observation.
incidents.quote: [A] limb struck him in the head hard enough to break his hard hat.

incidents.name: Jack Wells Fire Engine Burnover
incidents.summary: Around 3:00 p.m., a sudden wind shift caused the fire’s behavior to change rapidly—with flame lengths increasing to 8-10 feet. The initial attack plan was to suppress the fire as it approached the road. But with this sudden wind shift, the radiant heat from the fire intensified—causing flame lengths to surge to 15-20 feet. As the fire’s intensity grew, both engines were engulfed by flames, and the crews sought cover behind their engines for protection. The firefighters were not injured, and the engines were able to continue fire operations, though they sustained heat damage to plastic parts such as mirrors and lightbars.
incidents.quote: As the fire’s intensity grew, both engines were engulfed by flames, and the crews sought cover behind their engines for protection.

incidents.name: Tiger Creek Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: The Tiger Creek prescribed fire on the Walla Walla Ranger District of the Umatilla National Forest was declared a wildfire. Ignition actions for the 355 acres planned under the original project began on September 30, 2024, on National Forest lands located in the vicinity of the Mill Creek Watershed, a remote and rugged area south and east of the city of Walla Walla, WA. The Tiger Creek prescribed fire was intended to manage fuel loadings and wildfire risk to the Mill Creek Municipal Watershed that provides nearly 90% of the water needs to the city.
incidents.quote: The wildfire was contained at 534 acres with a total cost of about 10 million dollars.

incidents.name: Upper Finney Chute Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: In consideration of the fact that fire had been established on private land by actions of the Forest Service and that WADNR resources would be needed to suppress the resulting fire spread, the Upper Finney Chute Prescribed Fire was declared the Gee Lake Wildfire on the afternoon of October 4th.
incidents.quote: Piles from a timber harvest on private lands had been inadvertently lit by Forest Service resources earlier that week.

incidents.name: Shoe Fire Heat Illness and Laceration
incidents.summary: Late in the evening (2330) of 10/09/2024, a crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew (IHC) assigned to the Shoe Fire, Shasta-Trinity National Forest, California, experienced a possible heat injury with a secondary injury of a 1-inch laceration to the wrist. The initial treatment was provided by an agency EMT, and the injured crewmember was transferred to the ground ambulance at 0045 on 10/10/24. The crewmember and a squad boss arrived at Mercy Medical Center in Redding at 0300. The employee was treated and released back to full duty as of 0530 on 10/10/24.
incidents.quote: [A] crewmember on an Interagency Hotshot Crew...experienced a possible heat injury with a secondary injury of a 1-inch laceration to the wrist.

incidents.name: Yellow Lake Fire Vehicle Burnover
incidents.summary: Around 1345, after safely arriving at a lookout point west of the vehicle, the Superintendent briefs both Branch and Division on the situation and the vehicle’s location. It was decided to assess the vehicle after the fire moderates later that evening. By 1830, the fire behavior moderates and the vehicle is reached and assessed. The truck has burned and is considered a total loss.
incidents.quote: The truck has burned and is considered a total loss.

incidents.name: Tiger Creek Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A firefighter assigned to the Tiger Fire, Umatilla National Forest, Oregon, was struck by a tree and suffered an injury to an ankle. Short haul extraction was used to extract the injured firefighter. Once at the hospital, no broken bones were diagnosed. The firefighter was given crutches and told to ice and use crutches. No additional information.

incidents.name: Wapiti Fire Unknown Illness Medevac
incidents.summary: A crewmember from a Wildland Fire Module (WFM) assigned to the Wapiti Fire, Boise National Forest, was flown by helicopter to the hospital in Boise, Idaho after complaining of significant abdominal pain. A CT scan did not reveal any information on the abdominal pain, and the crewmember was released with 1 day of light duty.

incidents.name: Hurricane Helene Response South Carolina Hit by Tree Limb
incidents.summary: While bucking a storm damaged tree from Hurricane Helene on the Francis Marion and Sumter National Forests, South Carolina, a sawyer was struck on the helmet by a limb. The impact forced his head into the top handle of the chainsaw and broke a tooth. A Yellow medical response was initiated, and the injured sawyer was transported by government vehicle to the local ER. The injured sawyer was treated and released.
incidents.quote: The impact forced his head into the top handle of the chainsaw and broke a tooth.

incidents.name: Sontano Prescribed Fire Engine Fire
incidents.summary: A U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Type 6 Engine caught fire on the afternoon of October 11, 2024, while assisting the Carson National Forest on the Sontano Prescribed Fire. The engine was parked on the "burn" side of the road, in a pocket of green, while the unit was in the patrol/securing phase. Once the fire was discovered, the vehicle could not be extinguished with resources on scene. The vehicle was a total loss, but no injuries occurred.
incidents.quote: The vehicle was a total loss, but no injuries occurred.

incidents.name: Top of the World Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: The Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area (CRGNSA) began implementation of the Top of the World Prescribed Fire. The initial results of the test fire were favorable and burning continued into the early afternoon. Around 1600 a sudden increase in winds led to an increase in fire behavior which resulted in multiple spot fires. The rates of spread in the new spot fires quickly outpaced the on-site resources’ ability to contain them and the prescribed fire was declared a wildfire at 1625. The fire was kept exclusively on NFS lands and impacts to the public were limited to smoke created by the fire.
incidents.quote: The fire was contained at 171 acres with 45 of the burned acres being within the prescribed burn unit and 126 acres outside of the unit boundary.

incidents.name: Hawthorne Fire UTV Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: On Tuesday, October 22, 2024, Engineer Robert “Sharky” Sharkevich, Sr., was battling a brush fire on Lamentation Mountain in Berlin, CT, when the Utility Terrain Vehicle (UTV) he was operating rolled over a steep, rocky incline. He was pronounced deceased at the scene. Three other firefighters were taken to local hospitals with non life-threatening injuries.

incidents.name: Rush Fire Masticator Ignition RLS
incidents.summary: The Rush Fire started on Oct 24, 2024, in the Wichita Mountains National Wildlife Refuge. A skid steer masticator was conducting a hazardous fuels reduction treatment along a paved road when it sparked the fire—most likely by hitting a rock that was located underneath the vegetation...conditions that day were hot, dry and windy[.]
incidents.quote: As he turned farther, he could see that a fire had ignited a few hundred feet behind him. It was already the size of a pickup truck.

incidents.name: Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest Project Work Cardiac Issue
incidents.summary: A firefighter lost consciousness upon return from project work to the district office on the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest in Wisconsin. Forest Service EMT and fire crew member called local ambulance. Initial evaluation didn’t reveal any obvious diagnosis. The firefighter was eventually taken to a local hospital and underwent testing which indicated cardiac concerns. Firefighter was held at the hospital overnight for observations. Firefighter was released back to regular work and has a heart monitor to wear for several days.
incidents.quote: The firefighter was eventually taken to a local hospital and underwent testing which indicated cardiac concerns.

incidents.name: Huron-Manistee National Forest Work Capacity Test Multiple Injuries
incidents.summary: During an arduous work capacity test (WCT or “pack test”) a wildland firefighter experienced back pain, lower extremity cramps, and elevated heart rate. An on-site ambulance was called over and EMS provided patient care and transport to the local hospital. The firefighter was eventually diagnosed a fractured T12 vertebra. In addition, rhabdomyolysis and a minor heart attack were both suspected. As of 11/5/24, the firefighter remains hospitalized, and the rhabdomyolysis and cardiac concerns have been ruled out.
incidents.quote: The firefighter was eventually diagnosed a fractured T12 vertebra. In addition, rhabdomyolysis and a minor heart attack were both suspected.

incidents.name: Mansfield Fire Department Hit by Tree Branch
incidents.summary: On November 8, 2024, at approximately 1401, the Mansfield Fire Department responded to a brush fire on Cabot Blvd. Upon arrival, crews discovered that the entire wooded area between the street and the building was on fire. While working to contain the fire and prevent it from spreading to the structure, two firefighters sustained injuries when a large dead branch unexpectedly fell from approximately 35 feet up.
incidents.quote: Based on the trauma physician's assessment, he was transferred to Boston Medical Center for further evaluation.

incidents.name: Sterling Forest State Park Hit by Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: At approximately 3:30 p.m. Saturday, an 18-year-old Wildland Fire Crew Member, Dariel Vasquez, was fatally injured while working the fire line of a brush fire in Sterling Forest State Park near Greenwood Lake. The injury was the result of a fallen tree in the vicinity of the fire.

incidents.name: Oregon Prescribed Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: On November 15, 2024, on a prescribed fire in Oregon, the burn boss and fire resources were driving to the burn unit in UTVs when one of the UTVs broke down. While attempting to pick up the broken UTV with a truck and trailer, the burn boss noticed that the previously frozen gravel road began to thaw and offer less traction. The trailer was disconnected, and the burn boss backed the pickup truck down the road. The pickup began to slide to the downhill, outer edge of the road as it backed down the road. Ultimately, despite attempts to correct the slide and maneuver the vehicle back towards the center of the road, the truck rolled off the road when the shoulder gave way. The burn boss was not seriously injured in the accident
incidents.quote: Despite attempts to correct the slide and maneuver the vehicle back towards the center of the road, the truck rolled off the road when the shoulder gave way.

incidents.name: US Fish and Wildlife Service Medical Line of Duty Death
incidents.summary: At approximately 2250 hours on Thursday, November 28, 2024, U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (FWS) Fire Planner Brian Wolgamott died following a two-year battle with cancer. The U.S. Department of Labor Office of Workers’ Compensation Program deemed Mr. Wolgamott’s cancer to be proximately caused by employment in federal fire protection activities under the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act. As such, the FWS has determined Mr. Wolgamott’s death qualifies as a line of duty death.

incidents.name: Mirror Lake Snowmobile Search and Rescue
incidents.summary: Three Forest Service employees departed a trailhead on snowmobiles. Their mission for the day was to check snow conditions, educate the public in avalanche safety, monitor snow-loading on the roof of a backcountry station, and prepare for an upcoming snowmobile training. Due to snow depth and conditions, they became stuck numerous times throughout the day as they traveled the 30 miles to the backcountry station. As the day went on, they realized their communication devices were not functional. Exhausted and with stuck machines, they traveled on foot to reach the backcountry station, which would provide shelter for the night.
incidents.quote: “When it was light outside it did not seem like it was that big of a deal, but when it got dark…it was like, whoa. This is real.”

incidents.name: Bureau of Land Management Utah Medical Line of Duty Death
incidents.summary: Firefighter fatality from Malignant Neuroblastoma of the brain from a rare form of cancer after extensive treatment.
incidents.quote: Firefighter succumbs to Malignant Neuroblastoma of the brain after prolonged treatment.

incidents.name: Nacimiento Road Unit 3 Pile Burning Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A large pile of debris created by the Dolan Fire (2020) was ignited. While ignitions were ongoing, a cloud of flammable vapor and/or fuel ignited and burned a firefighter. They were treated onscene by fellow crewmembers, and taken medevac air ambulance to a trauma center, and then to a burn center. They are expected to fully recover.
incidents.quote: Don’t add straight gas/diesel mix to the pile after it has been lit. Fumes can—and will—ignite before the liquid mix gets to a flame source. This is especially important when working with log deck type piles that can be strung out for 50 to 60 feet.

incidents.name: Turkey Neck RX Smoke Impact
incidents.summary: During a morning recon day after successful ignitions on Turkey Neck Rx, the helicopter reported that the area around Route 15 looked “soupy", however the fire was still within the unit and no other concerns were noted. Shortly after this helicopter recon, the unit received a call from the local county emergency management officer who had called into the District Office to report a minor vehicle accident on Route 15.
incidents.quote: As they left the Rx for the evening, neither of them had concerns.

incidents.name: Mechaw Fire Shed Compartment 171 Declared Wildfire
incidents.fire: Mechaw Fire Shed Compartment 171 Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: On February 26, 2025, the Francis Marion Ranger District’s Agency Administrator (AA) authorized the Mechaw Fire Shed Compartment 171 Prescribed Fire (C-171 RX). Weather parameters were within prescription, although the KBDI required a Forest Level Variance. Following a 1000 onsite briefing and test fire, resources began ignitions to include hand and aerial firing. By 1500, numerous spots had lofted across holding lines, and the Prescribed Fire Burn Boss Type 2 (RXB2) contacted the AA saying, “we lost it.” The AA interpreted that phone call as a declaration and proceeded to inform the Forest Supervisor and others that the C-171 RX was declared a wildfire, becoming the Lincoln Wildfire.
incidents.quote: "Stopping firing in the bay earlier probably would have been best. You can always turn the machine back on."

incidents.name: Johnson County Fire Protection District Medical Fatality
incidents.summary: At 1345 the District was dispatched to a reported fast-moving half-acre field fire in rural Johnson County. Captain Collett arrived and began extinguishing the fire when he collapsed. Other District personnel located Captain Collett and began administering care, including CPR and multiple shocks with an AED. Ambulance and air ambulance services arrived on scene and continued care for nearly an hour but were ultimately unable to revive Captain Collett.
incidents.quote: Captain Vernon Collett died in the line of duty while battling a natural cover initial attack fire.

incidents.name: Pilot Grove Fire Protection District Medical Fatality
incidents.summary: Assistant Chief Donald Kammerich responded to a grass fire where he strenuously fought the fire for approximately 2 hours. After the emergency response, Assistant Chief Kammerich returned home. Only a few hours later at 9:00 p.m., the Pilot Grove Fire Protection District received an emergency call to Assistant Chief Kammerich’s home address. Upon their arrival, firefighters found Assistant Chief Kammerich in distress and began CPR. Despite the lifesaving efforts, Assistant Chief Kammerich was pronounced deceased at the scene.

incidents.name: West Beach Prescribed Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: On March 18, 2025, a burn injury to a firefighter occurred along with UTV damage while trying to suppress a spot fire on the West Beach Rx Unit. Medical treatment was conducted on scene. Due to the location of burns on the body, the firefighter was transported by ambulance to a local hospital, then later was transferred to a burn center that specializes in facial burns and plastic surgery. It was determined that the firefighter had received first and second degree burns to their face and was subsequently treated and released from the burn center that evening.
incidents.quote: Deceptively light flashy fuels burn hot and move quickly. Frontal assault on a fire is a “Watch Out” and is a tactic to be utilized in limited situations.

incidents.name: Middle Mountain UTV Rollover
incidents.summary: On a prescribed fire in West Virginia, a UTV operator was approaching a log that was encroaching the dozer line. They had been made aware of the log earlier in the day, but as they neared the log, they saw that there was a line already blown around it. Seeing this path, they made the decision to drive around the log. The UTV successfully navigated the slope but then rolled upon reentry to the dozer line. There were no injuries and the UTV was successfully righted with no damage.
incidents.quote: Unspoken human factors may have contributed: a desire not to miss a burn window and pressure to get all the prep work done

incidents.name: South Carolina Truck Backing
incidents.summary: After stopping for a break during travel home from a fire assignment, the driver asked a visiting crewmember to be their backer. The driver had noted the adjacent bollards (short posts to divert traffic) before selecting the parking site. During backing, there was a miscommunication of distance, due to which the driver accelerated and struck a bollard.
incidents.quote: The backer began with large beckoning arm motions, which the driver was familiar with as an indication that there is a long distance between the vehicle and a backing hazard.

incidents.name: Dry Creek Sawyer Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: While felling a 15-inch diameter, 33-foot tall ponderosa pine snag on the Plumas National Forest, the tree broke and fell 180 degrees off its intended lay. The sawyer escaped the stump straight back, and was struck by the falling stob when he had made it about 17 feet away from the stump. Though briefly pinned to the ground, he did not sustain major injuries.
incidents.quote: “Trees can do crazy things in a split second. I was trained to establish and use one of two escape routes at 45’s. But I panicked and blindly ran toward my other crewmate."

incidents.name: Black Cove Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: A North Carolina Forest Service firefighter was seriously injured on the Black Cove Fire when a crawler tractor disturbed the roots of a dead snag, causing it to fall and pin the firefighter’s legs. Crews on scene quickly freed the firefighter and initiated the Incident Within an Incident protocol. Additional personnel arrived within minutes to assist, and due to the severity of injuries and remote location, a NCHART hoist helicopter extracted the firefighter, who was then transported by air ambulance to the nearest trauma center.
incidents.quote: He was unable to reach his radio, so he yelled for help. The equipment operator could not hear his call for help over the sound of his equipment.

incidents.name: Salt Flats Fire UTV Burn Damage
incidents.summary: Texas A&M Forest Service resources were requested to assist with a wildfire exhibiting very active fire behavior, having already crossed a four-lane highway, and threatening structures with evacuations in progress. During structure protection operations, a Polaris XP900 UTV experienced mechanical failure. The operator was unable to move the UTV from the path of the fire and was forced to abandon it. The UTV was burned over, resulting in total loss of the equipment. The operator safely escaped with no injuries.
incidents.quote: “When I pressed the gas, and it didn’t go, my stomach dropped.” The UTV Operator tried working with the UTV to get it engaged. He looked back and saw the fire had gotten into the crowns of the 20’ oaks, and he made the decision to abandon the UTV and retreat on foot, approximately 500’, to the road. “I don’t have time to mess with this. I grabbed my pack and hightailed it out.”

incidents.name: Lynne Fire Tractor Plow Lessons
incidents.summary: A tractor plow was following his swamper and the fire edge around to the west. The mixed fuel of slash pine and oak required the dozer to maneuver extensively, involving a lot of reversing and repositioning. While backing up to improve his angle on the fire, the plow (attached by an articulating hitch) struck an oak tree and tipped over.
incidents.quote: Local personnel need to support a training period including hands on practice for visiting resources.

incidents.name: Arizona Backing-Parking Incident
incidents.summary: While parking a vehicle and attempting to avoid awning support posts and not block a road, a driver accidentally backed a vehicle into a post he could not see.
incidents.quote: If I need to back in, I will ask for help if it is available

incidents.name: Pennsylvania DCNR Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: Supervisor David L. Warfel led training exercises as part of the Wildland Fire Academy at Shippensburg University. During classroom training the following day, Forest Maintenance Supervisor Warfel reported feeling ill. Later that evening at approximately 5:45 p.m. on Thursday, May 29, he was found deceased in his quarters from a cardiac event.
incidents.quote: He reported feeling ill. Later that evening, he was found deceased in his quarters from a cardiac event.

incidents.name: Ayers Road Fire UTV Accident
incidents.summary: The UTV caught a steep edge and tipped over onto the driver’s side. A dozer assigned to the fire was used to pull the UTV upright and then pull it to a flat spot. During the UTV recovery effort, the UTV again rolled over, this time rolling one full rotation and coming to rest on its wheels.
incidents.quote: The UTV once during operations and once during recovery.

incidents.name: Skell Prescribed Fire Pile Burn Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: At the time of the escape, local agencies had not yet transition to fire season schedules, leaving few resources available on weekends. An air attack platform from Northern California was the first on scene and initiated a swift response utilizing nearby aerial resources. Ground crews followed within two hours and contained the fire at 43 acres. Upon investigation, it was determined that the fire originated from a smoldering landing pile from the previous winter, and the Telephone Fire was declared a wildfire as a result of the Skell Prescribed Pile Burn.
incidents.quote: Ultimately on June 10, nine days after the initial report of the incident, the Skell Rx was declared a wildfire.

incidents.name: Woodworth Station Prescribed Fire UTV Accident
incidents.fire: Woodworth Station Pasture E Prescribed Fire
incidents.summary: While returning to ignite the interior strip fire, a UTV struck a large rock obscured by tall grass, causing the UTV to roll over on its driver’s side. A medical response was initiated immediately, and both driver and passenger were transported to the hospital. The passenger suffered a laceration to the scalp requiring nine staples, the driver had a bruised left arm.
incidents.quote: Neither driver nor passenger of UTV A were wearing seatbelts when this rock strike occurred. Both passengers were wearing helmets—but were not using chin straps.

incidents.name: Barksdale Air Force Base Pile Burn UTV Fire
incidents.summary: On June 5, our crew of 5 USFWS, 1 BLM, and 2 US Air Force active duty was using the Terra Torch UTV to burn piles on Barksdale Air Force Base, Louisiana. Between 1330 and 1340 hours, while working on our ninth pile of the day, the UTV caught fire. The UTV was put out with multiple fire extinguishers and water from another UTV. One firefighter suffered first degree burns to his nose and ear. He was treated and released from the hospital and returned to work the next day.
incidents.quote: Everything was running smoothly—until Firefighter #1radioed: “Terra Torch on fire.”

incidents.name: Oregon Chainsaw Chaps Strike
incidents.summary: Sawyer had just started cutting for the day, after felling a small tree, they stood up from a crouched position while the chain was still spinning. It made contact with their chaps, pulled out some of the kevlar lining and was subsequently stopped without any harm to the sawyer.
incidents.quote: They stood up from a crouched position while the chain was still spinning. It made contact with their chaps.

incidents.name: Texas Storm Damage Chainsaw Chaps Cut
incidents.summary: On June 9, 2025, a saw team of 4 sawyers was dispatched to the area of Bonham, Texas to assist with the cleanup from a tornado that hit the town the night before. Sawyer 1 was making cuts on one end of a pile of downed trees while Sawyer 2 was working on the other side of the pile to clear the road faster. During Sawyer 1’s second cut on a limb, a 4-inch diameter limb pushed the saw onto their leg at an unknown throttle position. The chaps worked exactly as designed, and no injuries resulted.
incidents.quote: When the chainsaw bar hit my chaps, I immediately stopped and realized I struck my chaps and got really irritated with myself.

incidents.name: West Yellowstone Smokejumper Accident
incidents.summary: The jumpers who had landed uninjured located their injured colleague and initiated care, and EMS crews arrived at the injury location approximately one hour after the accident. The jumper was loaded onto an air ambulance for medevac to a hospital a little less than two hours after the accident.
incidents.quote: During a proficiency jump east of Hebgen Lake, two smokejumpers were pushed backwards by strong winds and landed a considerable distance from the identified jump spot. One smokejumper landed uninjured, while the other landed hard in a stand of young lodgepole pine trees and broke his leg.

incidents.name: Kaibab NF Chainsaw Kickback Laceration
incidents.summary: On June 16th a severity engine was doing project chainsaw work on the Kaibab National Forest. At around 1400 hours a new sawyer experienced kickback while limbing a downed ponderosa pine and cut through his left boot and into his foot, creating a three-inch laceration.
incidents.quote: He was doing good. He’s a new sawyer and I was giving him a couple of pointers about limbing and safety. Prior to the accident nothing was out of the norma

incidents.name: Trout Fire Dozer Entrapment
incidents.summary: Seeking a safer environment after a sudden increase in fire behavior, the dozer operator decided to exit the open cab dozer and run to a safety zone. While doing so, the dozer operator was exposed to flame and radiant heat and sustained burns to his hands, face, and ear. This incident initiated a rapid medical response that included paramedic and EMT personnel assigned to the area.
incidents.quote: The dozer is still in gear and disappears into the smoke, with nobody in control. A Field Medical Unit Leader (MEDL) was very close by and reacted immediately to the Incident-Withinand-Incident (IWI) call. He looked on his digital Ops map for the location he heard on the radio—Soldier Canyon—and couldn’t find it.

incidents.name: Controller Bay Airboat Incident
incidents.summary: The Cordova Ranger District (CRD) Fish Crew was conducting field work in the Controller Bay area on June 17th, 2025. The crew visited several pre-determined field sites throughout the afternoon and returned downriver at approximately 1700. The waves and sea state had increased from what they experienced when they left Controller Bay around noon. The airboat operator reduced power and came off step to moor up for the night. The reduction of power and coming off step caused the bow to dip, allowing an initial wave and bow wake to inundate the airboat. This initial wave caused the airboat to become very heavy and further reduce the freeboard (the height of a vessel’s side between the waterline and the top rail). A second wave came over the bow which pitched the airboat to the starboard side, dumping all five passengers into the water. The airboat proceeded to sink and was entirely under the water within 15 seconds of taking the first wave.

incidents.name: Pomas Fire Helicopter Cargo Load Release
incidents.summary: When transitioning from forward to vertical flying. When the pilot adjusted to the top of the collective, some part of his hand or glove bumped the release switch, causing the load to release from the hook.
incidents.quote: While delivering a cargo net full of structure protection supplies to a backcountry trail bridge, the helicopter load release was inadvertently triggered and the net dropped on part of the bridge, damaging it.

incidents.name: Conner Fire Burn Injury
incidents.summary: A firefighter sustained second-degree burn injuries to the hands, wrists and face while suppressing the Conner Fire. At the time of the incident, the engine crew was assigned to hold and secure the fire edge along a mountain road when erratic, high winds caused a sudden and dramatic increase in fire behavior, exposing one crewmember to flame and radiant heat.
incidents.quote: Erratic, high winds caused a sudden and dramatic increase in fire behavior, exposing one crewmember to flame and radiant heat

incidents.name: Ninetyeight Fire Boating Accident
incidents.summary: Five firefighters working on the Ninetyeight Fire were injured in a boating incident. Three were transported to the Fairbanks Memorial Hospital and two firefighters were released. Two firefighters did not go to the hospital but were treated on scene.
incidents.quote: All the passengers were ejected into the river.

incidents.name: Laguna Fire Dozer Entrapment
incidents.summary: Strong outflow winds from a passing thunderstorm caused rapid fire growth in the area where a dozer was working, and two firefighters, the dozer Operator and the Heavy Equipment Boss (HEQB), became entrapped. Due to fire behavior, the firefighters deployed their fire shelters and remained inside until they deemed that it was safe to come out.

incidents.name: Deer Creek Fire Pyro-Vortex Incident
incidents.summary: A pyro-vortex occurred on July 12, 2025, at approximately 1250. This pyro-vortex was large enough with enough damage for the National Weather Service to classify the incident as an EF2 tornado. Fire personnel were located at numerous locations in and around the fire tornado area—in vehicles, helicopter and on the ground—when it began forming and making the fire behavior more intense
incidents.quote: The TFLD from the Structure Group began driving south from the north side of Hang Dog Road, noting the “flame lengths coming off the main column were about 250-300 feet tall.”

incidents.name: Green Fire Head Injury Extraction
incidents.summary: A tool propped up against a tree, with the working end up, was accidentally knocked over. This tool ended up falling approximately one foot, striking the firefighter with a glancing blow to the firefighter’s unprotected head. Initially, the injured firefighter said she was okay but was experiencing some head pain. After 5 minutes of evaluation, she was able to continue the hike up the steep, nearly inaccessible ridgeline. After approximately 3/8th of a mile she started vomiting with a severe headache. Extraction of the injured firefighter was a complex operation and involved coordination of multiple resources including REMS, Helicopters, crews, a dozer and an ambulance.
incidents.quote: It took multiple hours to extract and transport the injured firefighter off the incident.

incidents.name: Toonerville Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On Incident #95 (the Toonerville Fire), two Department of Natural Resource (DNR) Crews were gridding approximately 50 feet off a road in a timber stand. One crew member had just finished attaching a hose to a wye fitting and had just begun putting their fire pack back on when an unexpected event occurred. A green Douglas-fir, approximately 12 inches DBH (bole diameter at 4.5 feet from the ground), fell on its own—without warning. There were no visible signs of burn-out or instability on this tree. The firefighter heard the tree beginning to fall, shouted a warning, and tried to move clear. The falling tree knocked the fire pack off the firefighter but resulted in no injuries or equipment damage.
incidents.quote: Working in timber stands always carries risk, even when trees appear uncompromised.

incidents.name: Fire 227 Gas Pipeline Rupture
incidents.summary: FlexSteel pipe(s)...are commonly used in petroleum transportation and have a good safety record. However, the maximum heat threshold they are designed for is 185 F. Once this pipe was exposed to the high temperatures of the passing wildfire, the outer polyurethane melted away, exposing the steel middle section. This resulted in a natural gas leak and subsequent gas line fire.
incidents.quote: On public land there are regulations requiring oil and gas lines to be buried. The same rules do not apply on private land.

incidents.name: Orleans Complex Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: The crew was engaged in direct attack working up hill, adjacent to the black. As the crew boss was working their way up the line with supplies, he “bumped by” a crew member and started to see a tree in the black falling towards the crew. As he yelled “tree!” several fire fighters rushed out of the way, however the tree directly struck a crew member.
incidents.quote: As he yelled “tree!” several fire fighters rushed out of the way, however the tree directly struck a crew member.

incidents.name: South Rim Fire Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: The sawyer, who was not directly working with a swamper, reached forward to move the limb to free the bar from the tree while maintaining his right hand on the trigger handle. As he reached forward, he inadvertently activated the throttle. The sawyer’s left hand contacted the top of the chain while it was running at cutting speed, causing severe injury to the sawyer’s hand.
incidents.quote: The sawyer’s left hand contacted the top of the chain while it was running at cutting speed, causing severe injury to the sawyer’s hand.

incidents.name: California Work Capacity Test Compartment Syndrome
incidents.summary: The employee, a seasonal firefighter, was completing the arduous pack test when they completed the test they had severe leg cramps. The EMT on site recommended the staff take the employee to the ER for further diagnosis. The employee spent the night in the ER at Mercy Medical in Redding. They were diagnosed with compartment syndrome and the medical team performed a surgical procedure to release the pressure from swelling. The employee is expected to stay in the hospital 2-3 days.
incidents.quote: The employee, a seasonal firefighter, was completing the arduous pack test when they completed the test they had severe leg cramps.

incidents.name: Pomas Fire Fall Injury Extraction 2025
incidents.summary: A water tender operator exited the water tender’s cab and fell resulting in an injury that required immediate medical intervention. The response involved a medical assessment on-site, followed by transport to a helispot where the injured party was transferred to an agency Type 3 Helicopter. The helicopter then flew to the helibase, where the individual was transferred to an air ambulance. The total elapsed time from initial notification to the patient’s transfer to the air ambulance was approximately two hours.
incidents.quote: The incident map did not identify the accident location (fill site) with a specific name or designated drop point. The important landmark was inadvertently obscured with pump symbols or field site icons, which hindered navigation and coordination.

incidents.name: Aggie Creek Fire Spike Camp Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: In the early morning of July 25, at 0406, the crew was awakened by a loud series of popping sounds, followed by a large crash as the snag and the green tree’s dead top fell and came to rest in the camping area. One individual was struck in the foot by a 2-inch by 4-foot piece from the top of the green tree when it clipped the corner of a tent. In total, 12 individuals were camping in the area, with five tents positioned immediately adjacent to the downed tree. The injured individual was attended to by on-scene medical personnel, who communicated with the incident Medical Unit Leader. No lost time was recorded.
incidents.quote: In the early morning of July 25, at 0406, the crew was awakened by a loud series of popping sounds, followed by a large crash as the snag and the green tree’s dead top fell and came to rest in the camping area.

incidents.name: War Creek Fire Water Tender Accident Fatality
incidents.summary: While responding to the War Creek Fire (Jones County, South Dakota) in a 2,000gallon tender, Captain Nicholas Van Dam was involved in a motor vehicle accident. Captain Van Dam was ejected from the vehicle as it left the roadway and rolled. Captain Van Dam sustained fatal injuries and was pronounced deceased at the scene.

incidents.name: Oregon Mop Up Electric Shock
incidents.summary: While he was close to the pole, the Engine Boss observed the water boiling around the base of the pole, with some arcing and buzzing. At this moment he started to realize electricity was involved in the situation—and the hazardous spot they were all standing in. He went to stand up from a crouch, put his right knee on the ground, braced his right hand against the pole and received a significant shock when his hand made contact with the pole. The electrical shock was brief. As soon as he pulled his hand away it was over. The Engine Boss was then extremely agitated, but was still focused on the incident. He gathered himself together and remained on scene.
incidents.quote: He went to stand up from a crouch, put his right knee on the ground, braced his right hand against the pole and received a significant shock when his hand made contact with the pole.

incidents.name: Canyon Fire Vehicle Rollover
incidents.summary: While attempting to position the vehicle, P1 left the dozer line and rolled approximately five times down into a canyon. The vehicle ultimately came to rest on its four wheels on a mid-slope knob. D1 was ejected from P1 as it rolled down the canyon.
incidents.quote: A utility pickup truck driven by a single individual lost traction while ascending a dozer line during wildfire suppression operations. The vehicle subsequently left the dozer line and rolled down a steep canyon slope.

incidents.name: Billy Fire UTV Accident
incidents.summary: Positioning themselves for quick egress, the UTV driver (Engine Boss Trainee) backed toward the road embankment. The rear tires sunk off the roadbed’s steep edge. Unable to gain traction, the UTV tilted, slid, and impacted something hard. The UTV and crew somersaulted backward down into the drainage.
incidents.quote: The UTV and crew somersaulted backward down into the drainage—the crew, all wearing hardhats, hit the UTV ceiling as unrestrained bodies and gear tumbled in different directions.

incidents.name: Rock Fire Radio Battery Overheat
incidents.summary: When they opened the battery pack to try replacing the batteries, they noticed that on one side the batteries were placed opposite of their required positioning. This caused the batteries to overheat and leak, melting parts of the internal clamshell and expanding the batteries on the other side. Fortunately, this was noticed prior to going to the line and only the clamshell was damaged.
incidents.quote: This caused the batteries to overheat and leak, melting parts of the internal clamshell and expanding the batteries on the other side.

incidents.name: Squeezer Fire Smokejumper Accident
incidents.summary: Jumper 1 continued to have trouble with up air as they turned base to final...[their] left-hand turn continued around for approximately 270 degrees which put them impacting rising terrain upon landing...[t]he injured jumper was oriented face up, head pointing downslope, parachute piled loosely on top. The jumpers attempted to use the knife from a reserve parachute container to cut away gear, but ended up having more success with pocketknives and trauma kit shears. It was evident that both upper legs were fractured. A traction device located in the trauma kit was used to pull traction on the right leg and a tree branch was used to splint and support the left leg.
incidents.quote: Unfortunately, the first call from the ground was from Jumper 2: “[They’re] not in good shape. I need help!”

incidents.name: Three Creeks Fire Electrical Shock
incidents.summary: While inspecting a hollow, smoking tree that was in contact with overhead powerlines, a firefighter inserted a hand inside the hollow cavity to check for residual heat. At that moment, the firefighter felt an electrical jolt from finger to elbow. The firefighter immediately withdrew, reported the shock, and stepped back. Crews halted work until the power company confirmed that power was shut down. The firefighter experienced some tingling, but, otherwise, felt stable. He was diagnosed with an electrical burn to his hand.
incidents.quote: At that moment, the firefighter felt an electrical jolt from finger to elbow.

incidents.name: Bivens Creek Fire Medical Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter/Sawyer Ruben Romero was serving as a sawyer on a Type 2 crew with TJ Forestry Contracting LLC. While actively involved in suppression of the Bivens Creek Fire in Montana, Firefighter/Sawyer Romero suffered a cardiovascular event. Rapid medical assistance was rendered from a line paramedic. Resuscitation attempts, however, were unsuccessful and Firefighter/Sawyer Romero passed away.
incidents.quote: While actively involved in suppression of the Bivens Creek Fire in Montana, Firefighter/Sawyer Romero suffered a cardiovascular event.

incidents.name: Emigrant Fire Limb Strike Medical Response
incidents.summary: A firefighter on the Emigrant Fire was struck by a falling tree limb during tree felling operations. Although the firefighter followed proper escape procedures, the tree he cut hit another tree while falling and caused that tree to shed a branch, which struck him on the head and shoulder. The patient was initially reported to have lost consciousness. The incident was originally assessed as a “Green” injury by the crew. After assessment by advanced medical personnel, the incident was upgraded to a “Red” and reported to Emigrant Communications through the IWI Process. An immediate, multi-layered medical response was initiated.
incidents.quote: [T]he tree he cut hit another tree while falling and caused that tree to shed a branch, which struck him on the head and shoulder.

incidents.name: Goose Fire Vehicle Fuel Tank Puncture Incident
incidents.summary: On August 31, 2025, at approximately 1815 hours, while departing the Goose Fire, the driver was operating the assigned 2023 RAM 2500 when they attempted to avoid a pothole and ran over an object/stick that punctured its fuel tank. Once the leak was discovered, the driver shut off the vehicle and all occupants exited. A temporary fix using earplugs, towels and tape halted the leak until the tank could be emptied with a hand pump.
incidents.quote: Unbeknownst to the operator at the time, this object shifted upward and punctured the vehicle’s fuel tank.

incidents.name: Stampede Ridge Fire Smokejumper Incident
incidents.summary: This is an excellent example of doing what makes sense and empowering employees to take care of each other without getting balled-up by official titles they may or may not have. It is a common theme throughout this incident that decision-makers evaluated their choices based on “what is in the best interest of patient care and makes the most sense given our location and situation.”
incidents.quote: As he attempted to move his feet, his tone changed: “No, I’m not fine.” When the stinging pain persisted, Jumper #3 suspected that he likely had bone fractures in both his feet.

incidents.name: TCU Lightning Complex Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: At approximately 0800 hours, the engine was involved in a single-vehicle rollover while traveling on State Highway 49, approximately 2.2 miles south of the Angels Camp Incident Base. The engine, staffed with a Fire Captain and two Firefighter I’s, lost control while negotiating a sharp "S" curve. It struck the hillside, rolled onto its passenger side, and came to rest. One firefighter sustained minor lacerations and was transported to a local area hospital, where they were evaluated and released.
incidents.quote: During the turn, the rear tires lost traction, and the engine began to “fishtail”. FC1 attempted to regain control to avoid driving off a steep embankment on the right side of the road. The engine then struck the opposing hillside, causing it to roll onto its passenger side.

incidents.name: Oregon Project Work Chainsaw Cut
incidents.summary: While performing felling operations on a prescribed burn unit, a sawyer off an engine crew was putting a backcut into the tree they were falling when the tip of the bar contacted a hammerhead wedge (a wedge with a mechanical steel insert on its end). This caused the saw to kick back onto the sawyer's shoulder, resulting in a large laceration. The sawyer was transported to the hospital where the hospital staff treated their wound and released the patient the same day.
incidents.quote: The force of the blow “rocked [him] sideways.” He dropped the saw and grabbed his arm.

incidents.name: Emigrant Fire Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On September 8, 2025, the Region 6 Zigzag IHC was working on the Emigrant Fire on the Willamette National Forest. The crew was engaged in firefighting efforts on Division M when a crewmember sustained significant injuries from a tree strike.
incidents.quote: The crew was engaged in firefighting efforts on Division M when a crewmember sustained significant injuries from a tree strike.

incidents.name: Dragon Bravo Fire Medical Emergency Fatality
incidents.summary: On the afternoon of September 8, 2025, Firefighter/Equipment Operator J. Hank Hester collapsed while performing suppression repair at the Dragon Bravo Fire near the Grand Canyon North Rim in Arizona. Line paramedics performed CPR at the scene, but Firefighter/Equipment Operator Hester could not be resuscitated. The suspected cause of death is a cardiovascular emergency.

incidents.name: Garnet Fire Hit by Tree Limb
incidents.summary: On September 16, 2025, a spotter with a falling team mitigating hazard trees on the Garnet Fire (Sierra National Forest) was struck by a falling limb. The limb fell from the falling pine tree just as the sawyer completed the backcut. The spotter suffered a broken left forearm and finger degloving. A quick extraction by a REMS team and hotshot crew led to a medevac by Army helicopter.
incidents.quote: Both the sawyer and spotter began to utilize their pre-identified escape routes. But after only a few steps, the spotter was struck in the arm by a falling branch.

incidents.name: Tinker Bugs Rx Fire Hit by Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Isabella Oscarson, who was a seasonal employee from Minnesota working for the Idaho Department of Lands, was struck by a falling tree while assisting with the U.S. Forest Service’s Tinker Bugs prescribed fire in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. Rapid medical assistance was rendered, and Firefighter Oscarson was flown to a hospital in Grangeville, Idaho, where she later passed away.
incidents.quote: Oscarson was evacuated from the scene and flown to Grangeville, where she succumbed to her injuries.

incidents.name: Dragon Bravo Water Tender Rollover
incidents.summary: A water tender working the Dragon Bravo Fire was involved in a single vehicle rollover. While driving a recently maintained road, the north bound water tender moved to the right side of the road to provide room for another vehicle to pass southbound. The rear wheels of the tender began to sink into the soft shoulder. The driver felt the sinking and began steering the vehicle out of the soft road material. The tender crossed the dirt road and entered the opposite ditch where it began to roll onto the drivers side.
incidents.quote: The momentum of the vehicle caused it to roll onto its drivers side and the deep borrow ditch on the opposite side of the road caused it to roll completely onto its top.

incidents.name: Labor Mountain Fire Tree Strike
incidents.summary: While scouting direct line for a one-acre spot fire east of the 511-road system, a firefighter on an interagency hotshot crew sustained an injury from a falling tree in Division November on the Labor Mountain Fire. The patient was found pinned face-down under the tree, which was lying across the thoracic spine and line gear. A Rapid Extraction Module Support (REMS) team arrived on scene, [and] by 1802, the patient was confirmed at the hospital. Fortunately, the firefighter’s injuries were limited to bruising and minor abrasions.
incidents.quote: The patient was found pinned face-down under the tree, which was lying across the thoracic spine and line gear.

incidents.name: Blackburn Canyon Fire Engine Crewmember Broken Arm
incidents.summary: On Saturday, October 11, 2025, Texas A&M Forest Service resources responded to the Blackburn Canyon Fire in Randall County, Texas. During initial attack pump-and-roll operations, an engine crewmember suffered a broken arm after the hose he was holding snagged vegetation during mobile attack. The patient was driven back to the staging area and transported to the hospital by ambulance.
incidents.quote: Cameron was holding his arm and said: “Jeff, I need to go to the hospital.”

incidents.name: Crown Creek Fire Dozer Rollover
incidents.summary: During dozer operations on the Crown Creek Fire, a dozer operator was constructing line around a structure. After several unsuccessful attempts to remove a stump from the line, the operator attempted to maneuver around it. As this maneuver was being made, the slope gave way beneath the machine. The dozer slid downslope and rolled onto its left side. The operator was wearing a seatbelt and the Roll Over Protective Structure (ROPS) performed as designed. Because of these factors, the operator was not injured.
incidents.quote: As this maneuver was being made, the slope gave way beneath the machine. The dozer slid downslope and rolled onto its left side.

incidents.name: Sugar Rush Timber Sale Pile Burning Slip-and-Fall Incident
incidents.fire: Sugar Rush Timber Sale Pile Burn
incidents.summary: During a prescribed pile burn on the Sugar Rush Timber Sale, located in the Coos Bay Unit, Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Oregon, a firefighter suffered a closed posterior malleolus fracture of the right tibia after a slip-and-fall incident while traversing a 40 percent slope. The firefighter self-extricated, was transported for medical care, then later released with follow-up orthopedic instructions.
incidents.quote: The crewmember was unprepared for the lost footing and began to fall to their right side when the calks regained traction and all the force of the fall was transferred to the ankle.

incidents.name: Olympic NF Hazard Tree Mitigation Hit by Tree
incidents.summary: On December 17, 2025, two U.S. Forest Service employees were conducting hazard tree mitigation work at Big Creek Campground on the Olympic National Forest. The work was intended to reduce identified hazards and support employee and public safety within the campground. During hand falling of a dead Douglas-fir approximately 10 inches in diameter at breast height (DBH) and 70 feet tall, several cutting actions at the stump resulted in the tree pulling to the left of the intended lay. As the tree began to commit to the fall, the top of the snag contacted a lower branch of an adjacent fir tree. This contact caused the upper portion of the dead snag to break and fold back toward the stump. As the top collapsed backward, it broke apart and a 3-inch DBH and 1 ½-foot-long piece of the broken top struck the sawyer on the left forearm, resulting in a fracture.
incidents.quote: As the snag continued to fall, the top portion of the tree flexed under compression and fractured approximately onethird of the way up the bole. The broken section folded backward and broke into several pieces as it fell toward the stump and struck Technician 1, resulting in a fracture to the left forearm.

incidents.name: A6 Fire Tree Felling Burn Injury
incidents.summary: Two North Carolina Forest Service firefighters were measuring the 193-acre A6 Fire’s perimeter when they discovered a tree near the fireline that was burning. This was a 70-foot-tall loblolly pine, approximately 14 inches in diameter. Because this tree was dropping fire brands across the line, suppression action was required. The two firefighters, both FAL3 qualified, decided to fell the tree. During the felling sequence, a burning limb struck the sawyer on the helmet, causing 1st and 2nd degree burns on the head, neck and ears. The injured sawyer was treated on site and evacuated to medical care, and has since made a full recovery.
incidents.quote: When the branch hit the full brimmed helmet, it broke into multiple burning pieces—burning the faller’s head, neck, and ears.

incidents.name: California Type 3 Engine Rollover
incidents.summary: On December 23, 2025, at approximately 1015 hours, a CAL FIRE Type 3 fire engine was enroute to the CAL FIRE station in the community of Patterson, California. While traveling on Del Puerto Canyon Road approximately six miles west of Interstate 5, the fire engine was involved in a rollover. The Fire Captain (FC) and two Fire Apparatus Engineers (FAE) of the engine company were evaluated at a local hospital for minor injuries and then released.

incidents.name: Dozer Overheating Rapid Lesson Sharing
incidents.summary: The John Deere J Series Dozer has overheated during fire operations. When the engine overheats it goes into a limp mode, limiting the dozer’s speed and effectiveness. Because the dozer could go into this limp mode during critical times of fire operations, this situation represents a key safety concern. Multiple federal and state land management agencies have worked together with the manufacturer to remedy this problem. After various modifications to the engine cooling system, a design has been developed that fixes this overheating dilemma.

incidents.name: Bahia Grande Unit 10 Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: On the morning of January 7th, 2026, while conducting prescribed fire operations on Unit 10 of the Baha Grande tract of the Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge (NWR), a slopover onto private land was declared a wildfire that spread to 188 acres in size. The escaped fire burned approx. 95 acres of private land and approx. 93 acres of refuge land outside the planned burn unit. Resources from several local departments and the Texas Forest Service responded and aided in suppressing the wildfire within the initial operational period.
incidents.quote: Due to the increased winds and thick smoke, fire quickly become established in the adjacent heavy fuels.

incidents.name: Little Snowies Pile Burn Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: The Judith‑Musselshell Ranger District conducted hand‑pile burning in early December 2025 under favorable conditions, but later warm, dry, and windy weather caused lingering heat sources to persist. On January 11, a rekindle led to the 5.1‑acre South Fork Fire, of which 1.16 acres burned onto private land before being contained.

incidents.name: Missouri IA Response Engine Vehicle Fire
incidents.summary: On January 12, 2026, a Hiawatha National Forest engine traveling to assist on the Sligo Fire experienced a growing vibration that rapidly escalated into a mechanical failure. Before the crew could reach the next exit, the engine produced several loud bangs, jolted violently, and filled with black smoke, prompting the driver to stop along a busy highway. A chase truck following behind observed debris falling from beneath the engine, along with smoke and flames. The chase truck’s fire extinguisher was used to put out the fire under the engine, while additional burning material ignited a small roadside fire that was quickly contained by the local fire department and Forest Service personnel. Investigation revealed that the driveshaft had separated from the transfer case, entangling wiring that created sparks, which then ignited hot transmission fluid and fuel, causing the fire.
incidents.quote: As the driver pulled the engine over to the side of the highway, he noticed his brakes weren’t working correctly.

incidents.name: Havasu Piles Declared Wildfire
incidents.summary: The Havasu Fire on Havasu National Wildlife Refuge began on the morning of January 19, 2026, as a result of a prescribed fire that extended beyond the designated project area into adjacent receptive fuels, consuming 4,084 acres of refuge lands. The planned prescribed fire area involved 185 acres of previously constructed mechanical piles of salt cedar, which were ignited under an approved program of work, prescribed fire plan, and fire management plan. The wildfire was declared and managed as a Type 3 Incident with 88 firefighters engaged and resulted in minimal damage to infrastructure but consumed multiple habitats for threatened and endangered species. The wildfire remained within the boundaries of the refuge but threatened the community and infrastructure of Topock, AZ and impacted the local area with dense concentrations of smoke.
incidents.quote: With limited firefighting resources and few natural or prepared barriers that could be defended, the fire progressed rapidly to the south through the refuge.

incidents.name: East Fork Scott Pile Burn Response
incidents.summary: On January 14, 2026, ignition operations were completed on the East Fork Scott pile burn unit on the Scott River Ranger District, Klamath National Forest. The unit transitioned into patrol status. On January 27, a frontal wind event developed across the burn unit, with sustained winds of approximately 20 mph and gusts up to 38 mph from roughly the Southeast recorded at a nearby Remote Automatic Weather Station (RAWS). Under these conditions, residual heat sources within the unit became active and resulted in fire spread beyond the project boundary onto adjacent private lands. Based on observed fire behavior, time of day, available and responding resources, and probability of success, the individual in charge determined that containment would be achieved by the end of the operational period and that declaration of the prescribed fire as a wildfire was not warranted under the burn plan and applicable policy.
incidents.quote: As fire behavior intensified with increasing winds, command transitioned to the responding highest-qualified personnel.

incidents.name: Mississippi Fuels Reduction Project Work Marsh Master Rollover
incidents.summary: On February 7, 2026, a firefighter was deployed to Grand Bay National Wildlife Refuge, located in Moss Point, Mississippi. Operations consisted of mastication preparation (mowing) of firelines for upcoming planned hazardous fuels reduction prescribed fire projects. The firefighter parked and unloaded the Marsh Master Type 2 (MM2) with a hydraulic mower implement at the Goat Farm Road Parking Area. They proceeded to mow firelines for several hours and remained in contact with the Duty Officer (DO) at several points throughout the day. At approximately 1650, the firefighter texted the DO that the MM2 with mower implement was loaded and they were returning to the Fire Center located in Gautier, Mississippi. At approximately 1700, the DO received a call from the firefighter stating they had been in an accident on Interstate 10 westbound just west of the Exit 75 onramp. There were no injuries, but the trailer had overturned and both the truck and Marsh Master sustained damage.
incidents.quote: The fishtailing amplified almost immediately—causing full loss of vehicle control. The violent movement of the trailer forced the vehicle to veer into the left lane of traffic heading toward the cable barrier of the median.

incidents.name: West End Prescribed Fire ATV Rollover
incidents.summary: During prescribed fire operations on February 18, 2026, personnel from BLM, USFWS, and LRAFB completed the Pollinator Unit burn before moving to the West End unit, where the Firing Boss Trainee rolled an ATV on a steep slope and became briefly trapped.
