Crews freed the trainee, who was evaluated on-site, transported to a hospital, and released the same day with no limitations.
incidents.quote: The Burn Boss sees the Holding Boss moving quickly behind this structure located west of DP#4, yelling: “Rollover!” The Burn Boss immediately radioed nearby units to converge on this location and informed FES to: “Send EMS ASAP.”

incidents.name: Texas Dozer Transport Rollover
incidents.summary: During a period of heightened wildfire danger in the Texas Panhandle in February of 2026, multiple Texas A&M Forest Service resources from other areas of the state were sent to that area to preposition. After several days, the fire danger decreased, and many resources were sent back to their home units. While en route back to their home unit in Montgomery County, a Texas A&M Forest Service transport hauling a Type 4 tractor plow overturned when it exited Interstate 45 on an exit ramp with a sharp curve. Both occupants of the transport were taken to the hospital, treated and released. They were back to full duty less than a week later.
incidents.quote: As she took the turn, the tires slid and the truck rolled over, making two complete revolutions.

incidents.name: Tri-Lakes Volunteer Fire Department Entrapment Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter Jeffery Derrick responded with the Tri-Lakes Volunteer Fire Department to a grass fire. While battling the blaze, shifting winds changed the fire’s direction and the fire spread into high grass and pastureland where firefighters were working the fire lines. Firefighter Derrick tried to make his way back to the fire department vehicle but became disoriented and was overcome by the fire.
incidents.quote: Firefighter Derrick was pronounced deceased at the scene.

incidents.name: National Chainsaw Workshop Kickback Injury
incidents.summary: A very experienced C-Faller had his chainsaw kick back while cutting a 55-inch DBH “pistol-butted” Douglas-fir on a steep slope.
incidents.quote: With 100 deaths per 100,000 workers, the most dangerous occupation in the United States is logging.

incidents.name: Butler County Fire Protection Response Fatality
incidents.summary: While responding to a brush fire, Shift Commander Jackson Warren was fatally injured when the fire apparatus he was driving ran off the right side of the road and overturned. Shift Commander Warren was pronounced deceased at the scene.

incidents.name: Compartment 75 Prescribed Fire Vehicle Tree Strike
incidents.summary: Engine 603 firefighters identified a burning hazard tree and requested a more experienced sawyer, but before further mitigation could occur, the tree unexpectedly fell, prompting personnel to retreat just as it struck and significantly damaged the engine. Notifications were made promptly through agency channels, and no injuries occurred as firefighters escaped in time.
incidents.quote: He yelled: “Tree’s coming down!” to the Holding Boss who was standing directly beside him. Both the Holding Boss and the driver quickly ran up the embankment—just in time to look over and see the tree strike Engine 603.

incidents.name: Morrill and Cottonwood Fires IWI Communications
incidents.summary: There were communication challenges on the Morrill and Cottonwood fires due to the vast geographic areas that these fires encompassed and the flat terrain in which they were burning.
incidents.quote: Not any one single communication system is effective in all situations.

incidents.name: Interagency Natural Resource Center Overcharged Diesel Truck Battery
incidents.summary: A recently transferred vehicle, a 2012 Dodge Ram 2500 with reoccurring battery issues, was left to charge inside a closed vehicle bay overnight. The following day, the Dispatch Center and CIO radio employees reported a strong “rotten egg” odor. This smell was so strong that the Dispatch Center Manager had employees leave the building and the CIO employees self-evacuated.
incidents.quote: Don’t hesitate to call the 911 line to help with unidentified smells or uncertain levels of gases.

incidents.name: East Ute Plaza Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: During the East Ute Plaza Fire on March 17, 2026, shifting winds and increased fire activity during burnout operations caused an igniter to slip on an embankment and become overrun by flames, igniting their protective clothing. Crews quickly extinguished the flames on the firefighter, who was then transported to a hospital and treated for second‑ and third‑degree burns covering seven percent of their body.
incidents.quote: The Firing Boss heard a “blood-curdling scream” and started moving along the road to get a better view through the smoke.The screaming stopped and the smoke opened up enough for the Firing Boss to see the igniter was on fire.

incidents.name: NIFC Cache Van Incident
incidents.summary: On March 18, 2026, an employee of the Great Basin Fire Cache at NIFC in Boise, Idaho, was returning from an offsite storage facility and found that the truck entrance to the NIFC campus was closed. He drove around to the main vehicle entrance, which is intended primarily for passenger vehicles but is large enough to allow a tractor-trailer to pass through. While passing through this smaller entrance, a rear cargo door swung open and contacted signage next to the guard's station. Both the signage and the rear door were damaged in the minor accident.
incidents.quote: Taking a little extra time to double-check the details can make a significant difference.

incidents.name: Blue Buck Prescribed Fire Tree Strike Incident
incidents.summary: A snag struck a sawyer during attempted mitigation efforts as part of prescribed fire operations on the Blue Buck Unit on the Mark Twain National Forest.
incidents.quote: The scope of work expanded beyond initial expectations.

incidents.name: Cottonwood Fire Burned Vehicles Incident
incidents.summary: On March 21, a Type 2 Initial Attack crew parked three trucks in previously burned “good black” before hiking 15–20 minutes away to secure fireline around nearby unburned cedar patches. By mid‑afternoon, fire behavior intensified in a large island of unburned fuel near the parking area, and when crews returned, they found all three trucks fully engulfed in flames.
incidents.quote: Several of the crewmembers stated that they believed this fire event was a “freak of nature.”

incidents.name: Ouachita National Forest Prescribed Burn Slopover Dozer Fire
incidents.summary: While working a slopover on a prescribed fire on the Ouachita National Forest, a dozer operator made the decision to disengage due to the number of spot fires in the area. As he was backing the dozer, it died. Upon exiting the dozer, the operator noticed a small fire under the machine. He engaged the fire with a fire extinguisher, but meanwhile noticed more fire inside the engine compartment. He emptied the rest of the first fire extinguisher at this fire, and used another fire extinguisher from a nearby UTV, but to no avail. The fire quickly grew and the operator moved to a safe location as the dozer burned. It is thought that the fire in the engine compartment was ignited by embers sucked into the air cleaner system, which is comprised of flammable paper filters and plastic housing components.
incidents.quote: “It was very humbling that we were three grown men with 77 years of combined experience and there was nothing we could do.”

incidents.name: Faulty Engine Battery Medical Incident
incidents.summary: For several days starting on March 21, 2026, crewmembers on an out of area fire assignment using a spare holdover fire engine experienced a bad smell emanating from the driver side vent. Smoke was also noted, but an inspection under the hood did not reveal any obvious issues. The following day, nearly all the crewmembers experienced headaches, disorientation, and a sandpaper feeling in the throat. Six of the eight were taken to the hospital, where they were treated for sulfuric acid fumes and carbon monoxide exposure and released. They made a full recovery after an a few additional days of lingering symptoms. Towed to a mechanic, the engine was examined and the cause of the toxic fume exposure was determined to be a faulty battery.
incidents.quote: Later that evening, after the burn, crew members were experiencing scratchy throats and nose bleeds.

incidents.name: Bald Knob Prescribed Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: While returning from prescribed fire activities on the Bald Knob South RX in the Big South Fork NRA, a vehicle accident occurred on the Beech Grove Road, a county road. The driver was the sole occupant of the pickup pulling a utility trailer with a UTV when the vehicle left the edge of the road and rolled onto its side. The driver was injured. Following extrication by other fire personnel, the individual was transferred to the hospital for care.

incidents.name: Cedar Canyon Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: A member of the Okeene Volunteer Fire Department sustained burns when the engine he was operating shut down, forcing him and another member of the fire department to escape on foot when gusting winds increased fire behavior. The firefighter was treated at a local hospital for 2nd and 3rd degree burns and was later transferred to Baptist Medical center in Oklahoma City.

incidents.name: Cedar Canyon Fire Vehicle Accident
incidents.summary: A member of the Okeene Volunteer Fire Department was injured when the heavy brush truck he was operating ran off into a ravine. The sudden drop caused the driver’s head to impact the roof of the truck, resulting in head and neck injuries. The firefighter was treated at a local hospital for a concussion and compression injury to his neck.

incidents.name: Cedar Canyon Fire Heart Attack
incidents.summary: A member of the Loyal Volunteer Fire Department suffered a heart attack after responding to the Cedar Canyon Fire in NW Oklahoma. The firefighter was transferred via Life Flight to Baptist Medical Center in Oklahoma City where he is in stable but critical condition. At approximately 1712, a Loyal VFD brush truck was providing structure protection which included a firing operation to secure the values at risk. At completion of the firing operation, one of the firefighters asked to go to a rehab station setup at the incident. After his vitals were taken, it was decided to immediately transport via ambulance to Baptist Medical Center. Enroute the patient started to complain about chest pains and the heart attack occurred. EMS was able to revive patient near Kingfisher, OK and stabilize him enough for Life Flight transport to Oklahoma City.

incidents.name: Hwy 1498 Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: At 1330 hours on 29 March 2026, a significant fire broke out on Hwy 1498 near Wheelwright, Kentucky, on the Floyd/Knott County line. During the intense firefighting operations, two Kentucky Division of Forestry firefighters were tragically entrapped. The Incident Commander Type 5 and the fire crew, demonstrating exceptional teamwork, assisted the injured firefighters, who bravely walked off the mountain from the burn scene under their own power. After a thorough assessment by the EMTs, it was deemed necessary to request a life-flight helicopter for one of the two firefighters' urgent transport to the burn unit to treat the severe burns covering their body
incidents.quote: Injured firefighter 1 was trying their best to run through the fire, but the heat was slowing them down! I started hearing HELP! HELP! ME!

incidents.name: Superior National Forest Linseed Oil Rags Close Call
incidents.summary: During preseason tool maintenance on March 31, 2026, an oil‑soaked linseed rag was discarded in a 21‑gallon oily waste can inside the Kawishiwi Ranger Station’s wood and paint shop. Two days later, smoldering rags were discovered in the can and moved outside, after which ventilation cleared the shop and staff held an impromptu safety discussion.

incidents.name: Washington and Jefferson National Forests Initial Attack Fire Fuel Geyser
incidents.summary: After felling a 16-inch diameter-at-breast-height (DBH) burning snag and bumping up the line, the sawyer was unable to restart his saw. The sawyer moved about 20 feet away from the fire to investigate the issue. Unsure of how long it had been since he last refueled, he popped the cap off the saw, notably failing to first check the fuel window. Fuel immediately sprayed out of the saw, splashing his chaps, leg, chest and arm.
incidents.quote: We hadn’t talked about it yet this year…but we need to get people thinking, when that saw stops, don’t just pop the top.” —Sawyer

incidents.name: Westover Air Reserve Base Declared Wildfire Review
incidents.summary: The Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst Wildland Support Module conducted a 31-acre prescribed burn on Westover Air Reserve Base in Chicopee, MA that escaped containment lines and burned one acre of private property that caused significant property loss.
incidents.quote: Security protocols on USAF installations limited the ability of crews to openly and freely patrol on private property.

incidents.name: Washington and Jefferson National Forests Engine Wheel Stud Failure
incidents.summary: While in support of prescribed fire and fuels management activities on the George Washington & Jefferson National Forests (GWJ) in Virginia, a U.S. Wildland Fire Service (USWFS) Type-6 engine experienced a wheel stud failure. Due to the crew’s situational awareness, the issue was detected before it could lead to a catastrophic outcome.
incidents.quote: The transition from forest to paved road is an important checkpoint.

incidents.name: Gunstock Fire Heavy Equipment Incident
incidents.summary: On April 15, 2026, a county crew was building containment line around a 4-5 acre fire burning in timber. While constructing line, a dozer became high centered on a rock, which caused it to skid downhill. Once the dozer was off the rock, the tracks on the dozer took hold, tipping it onto its side. The operator was able to exit the dozer with only minor injuries. The fire moved toward the tipped over dozer, which had started to leak fuel due to its position on its side. Despite the crew trying to put in line around the dozer, the dozer ended up engulfed in flames and is a total loss. The rollover occurred due to the unknown depth of the rock under the leaf/debris and soil during the construction of the containment line.
incidents.quote: The fire moved toward the dozer, and with the dozer in position, fuel started to leak. The dozer ended up engulfed in flames.

incidents.name: Idaho Panhandle National Forest Rhabdomyolysis
incidents.summary: A squad leader participated in rappel recertification during the week of April 13 to April 19, 2026, returning to their home unit on Monday April 20. Over the next few days, they participated in two-a-day workouts with their crew. Starting on April 22, the squad leader felt very sore from the previous day's workouts. Despite feeling sore, they participated in a crew PT run on the 23rd and felt unusually tired. After the workout, they noticed their urine was a concerningly dark color. Soon there after, the squad boss decided to seek medical care.
incidents.quote: You should be aware of its symptoms: severe muscle cramping and/or dark-colored urine.

incidents.name: Hilliard Volunteer Fire Department Fatality
incidents.summary: Firefighter James Kevin Crews experienced a medical emergency while fighting a brushfire. Fellow responders administered lifesaving measures and transported Firefighter Crews to a local hospital where he was pronounced deceased. The cause of death has not been determined.

incidents.name: Covelo South Incident Prescribed Fire Burn Injuries
incidents.summary: Four CAL FIRE employees sustained superficial burn injuries while conducting firing operations on the Covelo South Vegetation Management Project (VMP) in Mendocino County, California.
incidents.quote: Four personnel were above the firing location and impacted by advancing fire.

incidents.name: Mapes Fire Dozer Incident
incidents.summary: During direct line construction, the operator noticed flames originating from a small gap between the dozer hood cowling and the windshield. The operator extinguished the fire with the onboard fire extinguisher and proceeded with fire suppression operations with no further issues. The gap between the windshield and hood collected pine needles and other debris which created a receptive fuelbed for embers.
incidents.quote: Moving forward, placing a filler piece on the outside of the hood cowl sealing against the windshield will help keep woody material from collecting in this cavity and mitigate the potential for the dozer catching fire when constructing fireline.

incidents.name: Knowles Fire Entrapment
incidents.summary: Five firefighters from the interagency Rifle Helitack crew staffed by both USWFS and USFS employees were involved in a burnover event while providing an initial attack response to the Gore and Knowles fires. Firefighters from the crew deployed fire shelters.
incidents.quote: Rifle Helitack crewmembers Emily Barker, Nicholas "Nick" Hutcherson, and Sydney Watson perished during the entrapment. Crewmember Nathan "Nate" Matthews passed away on July 24, 2026, from injuries he sustained during the entrapment.

incidents.name: Austin Fire Hit by Tree Fatality
incidents.summary: A member of a contract Falling Module assigned to the Austin fire was critically injured while conducting hazard tree mitigation. The sawyer was cutting a snag, when the top portion broke off, fell back toward him and struck him in the head and back.
incidents.quote: Critical incident stress management, peer support and related mental health resources will continue to be provided to those that have been impacted by the incident

incidents.name: Lucas Fire Engine Burn Damage
incidents.summary: A CAL FIRE Type 3 fire engine was impacted by radiant heat and direct flame. The engine was traveling on a fire access road to the top of a ridge on the incident to support fire suppression efforts. The engine became stuck and could not continue, so personnel evacuated and traveled on foot to a safe location. The engine was a complete loss; there were no injuries to the engine personnel.
incidents.quote: Utilize a spotter or have personnel scout incident access to ensure the viability of use by equipment.
